verses.text: ¶ And the Lord spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thine hand upon the waters of Egypt, upon their streams, upon their rivers, and upon their ponds, and upon all their pools of water, that they may become blood; and <hi type="italic">that</hi> there may be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in <hi type="italic">vessels of</hi> wood, and in <hi type="italic">vessels of</hi> stone.

verses.name: Exodus 7:20
verses.text: And Moses and Aaron did so, as the Lord commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and smote the waters that <hi type="italic">were</hi> in the river, in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters that <hi type="italic">were</hi> in the river were turned to blood.

verses.name: Exodus 7:21
verses.text: And the fish that <hi type="italic">was</hi> in the river died; and the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink of the water of the river; and there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 7:22
verses.text: And the magicians of Egypt did so with their enchantments: and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, neither did he hearken unto them; as the Lord had said.

verses.name: Exodus 7:23
verses.text: And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, neither did he set his heart to this also.

verses.name: Exodus 7:24
verses.text: And all the Egyptians digged round about the river for water to drink; for they could not drink of the water of the river.

verses.name: Exodus 7:25
verses.text: And seven days were fulfilled, after that the Lord had smitten the river.  <chapter eID="Exod.7"/><div eID="gen60" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 8:1
verses.text: AND the Lord spake unto Moses, Go unto Pharaoh, and say unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Let my people go, that they may serve me.

verses.name: Exodus 8:2
verses.text: And if thou refuse to let <hi type="italic">them</hi> go, behold, I will smite all thy borders with frogs:

verses.name: Exodus 8:3
verses.text: And the river shall bring forth frogs abundantly, which shall go up and come into thine house, and into thy bedchamber, and upon thy bed, and into the house of thy servants, and upon thy people, and into thine ovens, and into thy kneadingtroughs:

verses.name: Exodus 8:4
verses.text: And the frogs shall come up both on thee, and upon thy people, and upon all thy servants.

verses.name: Exodus 8:5
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch forth thine hand with thy rod over the streams, over the rivers, and over the ponds, and cause frogs to come up upon the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 8:6
verses.text: And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 8:7
verses.text: And the magicians did so with their enchantments, and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 8:8
verses.text: ¶ Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said, Intreat the Lord, that he may take away the frogs from me, and from my people; and I will let the people go, that they may do sacrifice unto the Lord.

verses.name: Exodus 8:9
verses.text: And Moses said unto Pharaoh, Glory over me: when shall I intreat for thee, and for thy servants, and for thy people, to destroy the frogs from thee and thy houses, <hi type="italic">that</hi> they may remain in the river only?

verses.name: Exodus 8:10
verses.text: And he said, To morrow. And he said, <hi type="italic">Be it</hi> according to thy word: that thou mayest know that <hi type="italic">there is</hi> none like unto the Lord our God.

verses.name: Exodus 8:11
verses.text: And the frogs shall depart from thee, and from thy houses, and from thy servants, and from thy people; they shall remain in the river only.

verses.name: Exodus 8:12
verses.text: And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh: and Moses cried unto the Lord because of the frogs which he had brought against Pharaoh.

verses.name: Exodus 8:13
verses.text: And the Lord did according to the word of Moses; and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the villages, and out of the fields.

verses.name: Exodus 8:14
verses.text: And they gathered them together upon heaps: and the land stank.

verses.name: Exodus 8:15
verses.text: But when Pharaoh saw that there was respite, he hardened his heart, and hearkened not unto them; as the Lord had said.

verses.name: Exodus 8:16
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 8:17
verses.text: And they did so; for Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and smote the dust of the earth, and it became lice in man, and in beast; all the dust of the land became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 8:18
verses.text: And the magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not: so there were lice upon man, and upon beast.

verses.name: Exodus 8:19
verses.text: Then the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the finger of God: and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as the Lord had said.

verses.name: Exodus 8:20
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh; lo, he cometh forth to the water; and say unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Let my people go, that they may serve me.

verses.name: Exodus 8:21
verses.text: Else, if thou wilt not let my people go, behold, I will send swarms <hi type="italic">of flies</hi> upon thee, and upon thy servants, and upon thy people, and into thy houses: and the houses of the Egyptians shall be full of swarms <hi type="italic">of flies</hi>, and also the ground whereon they <hi type="italic">are</hi>.

verses.name: Exodus 8:22
verses.text: And I will sever in that day the land of Goshen, in which my people dwell, that no swarms <hi type="italic">of flies</hi> shall be there; to the end thou mayest know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord in the midst of the earth.

verses.name: Exodus 8:23
verses.text: And I will put a division between my people and thy people: to morrow shall this sign be.

verses.name: Exodus 8:24
verses.text: And the Lord did so; and there came a grievous swarm <hi type="italic">of flies</hi> into the house of Pharaoh, and <hi type="italic">into</hi> his servants’ houses, and into all the land of Egypt: the land was corrupted by reason of the swarm <hi type="italic">of flies</hi>.

verses.name: Exodus 8:25
verses.text: ¶ And Pharaoh called for Moses and for Aaron, and said, Go ye, sacrifice to your God in the land.

verses.name: Exodus 8:26
verses.text: And Moses said, It is not meet so to do; for we shall sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians to the Lord our God: lo, shall we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone us?

verses.name: Exodus 8:27
verses.text: We will go three days’ journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to the Lord our God, as he shall command us.

verses.name: Exodus 8:28
verses.text: And Pharaoh said, I will let you go, that ye may sacrifice to the Lord your God in the wilderness; only ye shall not go very far away: intreat for me.

verses.name: Exodus 8:29
verses.text: And Moses said, Behold, I go out from thee, and I will intreat the Lord that the swarms <hi type="italic">of flies</hi> may depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people, to morrow: but let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more in not letting the people go to sacrifice to the Lord.

verses.name: Exodus 8:30
verses.text: And Moses went out from Pharaoh, and intreated the Lord.

verses.name: Exodus 8:31
verses.text: And the Lord did according to the word of Moses; and he removed the swarms <hi type="italic">of flies</hi> from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people; there remained not one.

verses.name: Exodus 8:32
verses.text: And Pharaoh hardened his heart at this time also, neither would he let the people go.  <chapter eID="Exod.8"/><div eID="gen61" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 9:1
verses.text: THEN the Lord said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh, and tell him, Thus saith the Lord God of the Hebrews, Let my people go, that they may serve me.

verses.name: Exodus 9:2
verses.text: For if thou refuse to let <hi type="italic">them</hi> go, and wilt hold them still,

verses.name: Exodus 9:3
verses.text: Behold, the hand of the Lord is upon thy cattle which <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the field, upon the horses, upon the asses, upon the camels, upon the oxen, and upon the sheep: <hi type="italic">there shall be</hi> a very grievous murrain.

verses.name: Exodus 9:4
verses.text: And the Lord shall sever between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt: and there shall nothing die of all <hi type="italic">that is</hi> the children’s of Israel.

verses.name: Exodus 9:5
verses.text: And the Lord appointed a set time, saying, To morrow the Lord shall do this thing in the land.

verses.name: Exodus 9:6
verses.text: And the Lord did that thing on the morrow, and all the cattle of Egypt died: but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one.

verses.name: Exodus 9:7
verses.text: And Pharaoh sent, and, behold, there was not one of the cattle of the Israelites dead. And the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he did not let the people go.

verses.name: Exodus 9:8
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Moses and unto Aaron, Take to you handfuls of ashes of the furnace, and let Moses sprinkle it toward the heaven in the sight of Pharaoh.

verses.name: Exodus 9:9
verses.text: And it shall become small dust in all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boil breaking forth <hi type="italic">with</hi> blains upon man, and upon beast, throughout all the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 9:10
verses.text: And they took ashes of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses sprinkled it up toward heaven; and it became a boil breaking forth <hi type="italic">with</hi> blains upon man, and upon beast.

verses.name: Exodus 9:11
verses.text: And the magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils; for the boil was upon the magicians, and upon all the Egyptians.

verses.name: Exodus 9:12
verses.text: And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he hearkened not unto them; as the Lord had spoken unto Moses.

verses.name: Exodus 9:13
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and say unto him, Thus saith the Lord God of the Hebrews, Let my people go, that they may serve me.

verses.name: Exodus 9:14
verses.text: For I will at this time send all my plagues upon thine heart, and upon thy servants, and upon thy people; that thou mayest know that <hi type="italic">there is</hi> none like me in all the earth.

verses.name: Exodus 9:15
verses.text: For now I will stretch out my hand, that I may smite thee and thy people with pestilence; and thou shalt be cut off from the earth.

verses.name: Exodus 9:16
verses.text: And in very deed for this <hi type="italic">cause</hi> have I raised thee up, for to shew <hi type="italic">in</hi> thee my power; and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth.

verses.name: Exodus 9:17
verses.text: As yet exaltest thou thyself against my people, that thou wilt not let them go?

verses.name: Exodus 9:18
verses.text: Behold, to morrow about this time I will cause it to rain a very grievous hail, such as hath not been in Egypt since the foundation thereof even until now.

verses.name: Exodus 9:19
verses.text: Send therefore now, <hi type="italic">and</hi> gather thy cattle, and all that thou hast in the field; <hi type="italic">for upon</hi> every man and beast which shall be found in the field, and shall not be brought home, the hail shall come down upon them, and they shall die.

verses.name: Exodus 9:20
verses.text: He that feared the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh made his servants and his cattle flee into the houses:

verses.name: Exodus 9:21
verses.text: And he that regarded not the word of the Lord left his servants and his cattle in the field.

verses.name: Exodus 9:22
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Moses, Stretch forth thine hand toward heaven, that there may be hail in all the land of Egypt, upon man, and upon beast, and upon every herb of the field, throughout the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 9:23
verses.text: And Moses stretched forth his rod toward heaven: and the Lord sent thunder and hail, and the fire ran along upon the ground; and the Lord rained hail upon the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 9:24
verses.text: So there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.

verses.name: Exodus 9:25
verses.text: And the hail smote throughout all the land of Egypt all that <hi type="italic">was</hi> in the field, both man and beast; and the hail smote every herb of the field, and brake every tree of the field.

verses.name: Exodus 9:26
verses.text: Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel <hi type="italic">were</hi>, was there no hail.

verses.name: Exodus 9:27
verses.text: ¶ And Pharaoh sent, and called for Moses and Aaron, and said unto them, I have sinned this time: the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> righteous, and I and my people <hi type="italic">are</hi> wicked.

verses.name: Exodus 9:28
verses.text: Intreat the Lord (for <hi type="italic">it is</hi> enough) that there be no <hi type="italic">more</hi> mighty thunderings and hail; and I will let you go, and ye shall stay no longer.

verses.name: Exodus 9:29
verses.text: And Moses said unto him, As soon as I am gone out of the city, I will spread abroad my hands unto the Lord; <hi type="italic">and</hi> the thunder shall cease, neither shall there be any more hail; that thou mayest know how that the earth <hi type="italic">is</hi> the Lord’s.

verses.name: Exodus 9:30
verses.text: But as for thee and thy servants, I know that ye will not yet fear the Lord God.

verses.name: Exodus 9:31
verses.text: And the flax and the barley was smitten: for the barley <hi type="italic">was</hi> in the ear, and the flax <hi type="italic">was</hi> bolled.

verses.name: Exodus 9:32
verses.text: But the wheat and the rie were not smitten: for they <hi type="italic">were</hi> not grown up.

verses.name: Exodus 9:33
verses.text: And Moses went out of the city from Pharaoh, and spread abroad his hands unto the Lord: and the thunders and hail ceased, and the rain was not poured upon the earth.

verses.name: Exodus 9:34
verses.text: And when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders were ceased, he sinned yet more, and hardened his heart, he and his servants.

verses.name: Exodus 9:35
verses.text: And the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, neither would he let the children of Israel go; as the Lord had spoken by Moses.  <chapter eID="Exod.9"/><div eID="gen62" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 10:1
verses.text: AND the Lord said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh: for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants, that I might shew these my signs before him:

verses.name: Exodus 10:2
verses.text: And that thou mayest tell in the ears of thy son, and of thy son’s son, what things I have wrought in Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them; that ye may know how that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord.

verses.name: Exodus 10:3
verses.text: And Moses and Aaron came in unto Pharaoh, and said unto him, Thus saith the Lord God of the Hebrews, How long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself before me? let my people go, that they may serve me.

verses.name: Exodus 10:4
verses.text: Else, if thou refuse to let my people go, behold, to morrow will I bring the locusts into thy coast:

verses.name: Exodus 10:5
verses.text: And they shall cover the face of the earth, that one cannot be able to see the earth: and they shall eat the residue of that which is escaped, which remaineth unto you from the hail, and shall eat every tree which groweth for you out of the field:

verses.name: Exodus 10:6
verses.text: And they shall fill thy houses, and the houses of all thy servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians; which neither thy fathers, nor thy fathers’ fathers have seen, since the day that they were upon the earth unto this day. And he turned himself, and went out from Pharaoh.

verses.name: Exodus 10:7
verses.text: And Pharaoh’s servants said unto him, How long shall this man be a snare unto us? let the men go, that they may serve the Lord their God: knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?

verses.name: Exodus 10:8
verses.text: And Moses and Aaron were brought again unto Pharaoh: and he said unto them, Go, serve the Lord your God: <hi type="italic">but</hi> who <hi type="italic">are</hi> they that shall go?

verses.name: Exodus 10:9
verses.text: And Moses said, We will go with our young and with our old, with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds will we go; for we <hi type="italic">must hold</hi> a feast unto the Lord.

verses.name: Exodus 10:10
verses.text: And he said unto them, Let the Lord be so with you, as I will let you go, and your little ones: look <hi type="italic">to it;</hi> for evil <hi type="italic">is</hi> before you.

verses.name: Exodus 10:11
verses.text: Not so: go now ye <hi type="italic">that are</hi> men, and serve the Lord; for that ye did desire. And they were driven out from Pharaoh’s presence.

verses.name: Exodus 10:12
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up upon the land of Egypt, and eat every herb of the land, <hi type="italic">even</hi> all that the hail hath left.

verses.name: Exodus 10:13
verses.text: And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt, and the Lord brought an east wind upon the land all that day, and all <hi type="italic">that</hi> night; <hi type="italic">and</hi> when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts.

verses.name: Exodus 10:14
verses.text: And the locusts went up over all the land of Egypt, and rested in all the coasts of Egypt: very grievous <hi type="italic">were they;</hi> before them there were no such locusts as they, neither after them shall be such.

verses.name: Exodus 10:15
verses.text: For they covered the face of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened; and they did eat every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees which the hail had left: and there remained not any green thing in the trees, or in the herbs of the field, through all the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 10:16
verses.text: ¶ Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste; and he said, I have sinned against the Lord your God, and against you.

verses.name: Exodus 10:17
verses.text: Now therefore forgive, I pray thee, my sin only this once, and intreat the Lord your God, that he may take away from me this death only.

verses.name: Exodus 10:18
verses.text: And he went out from Pharaoh, and intreated the Lord.

verses.name: Exodus 10:19
verses.text: And the Lord turned a mighty strong west wind, which took away the locusts, and cast them into the Red sea; there remained not one locust in all the coasts of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 10:20
verses.text: But the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, so that he would not let the children of Israel go.

verses.name: Exodus 10:21
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness <hi type="italic">which</hi> may be felt.

verses.name: Exodus 10:22
verses.text: And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven; and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days:

verses.name: Exodus 10:23
verses.text: They saw not one another, neither rose any from his place for three days: but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.

verses.name: Exodus 10:24
verses.text: ¶ And Pharaoh called unto Moses, and said, Go ye, serve the Lord; only let your flocks and your herds be stayed: let your little ones also go with you.

verses.name: Exodus 10:25
verses.text: And Moses said, Thou must give us also sacrifices and burnt offerings, that we may sacrifice unto the Lord our God.

verses.name: Exodus 10:26
verses.text: Our cattle also shall go with us; there shall not an hoof be left behind; for thereof must we take to serve the Lord our God; and we know not with what we must serve the Lord, until we come thither.

verses.name: Exodus 10:27
verses.text: ¶ But the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let them go.

verses.name: Exodus 10:28
verses.text: And Pharaoh said unto him, Get thee from me, take heed to thyself, see my face no more; for in <hi type="italic">that</hi> day thou seest my face thou shalt die.

verses.name: Exodus 10:29
verses.text: And Moses said, Thou hast spoken well, I will see thy face again no more.  <chapter eID="Exod.10"/><div eID="gen63" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 11:1
verses.text: AND the Lord said unto Moses, Yet will I bring one plague <hi type="italic">more</hi> upon Pharaoh, and upon Egypt; afterwards he will let you go hence: when he shall let <hi type="italic">you</hi> go, he shall surely thrust you out hence altogether.

verses.name: Exodus 11:2
verses.text: Speak now in the ears of the people, and let every man borrow of his neighbour, and every woman of her neighbour, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold.

verses.name: Exodus 11:3
verses.text: And the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover the man Moses <hi type="italic">was</hi> very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh’s servants, and in the sight of the people.

verses.name: Exodus 11:4
verses.text: And Moses said, Thus saith the Lord, About midnight will I go out into the midst of Egypt:

verses.name: Exodus 11:5
verses.text: And all the firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sitteth upon his throne, even unto the firstborn of the maidservant that <hi type="italic">is</hi> behind the mill; and all the firstborn of beasts.

verses.name: Exodus 11:6
verses.text: And there shall be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as there was none like it, nor shall be like it any more.

verses.name: Exodus 11:7
verses.text: But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.

verses.name: Exodus 11:8
verses.text: And all these thy servants shall come down unto me, and bow down themselves unto me, saying, Get thee out, and all the people that follow thee: and after that I will go out. And he went out from Pharaoh in a great anger.

verses.name: Exodus 11:9
verses.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you; that my wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 11:10
verses.text: And Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh: and the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, so that he would not let the children of Israel go out of his land.  <chapter eID="Exod.11"/><div eID="gen64" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 12:1
verses.text: AND the Lord spake unto Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 12:2
verses.text: This month <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> unto you the beginning of months: it <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> the first month of the year to you.

verses.name: Exodus 12:3
verses.text: ¶ Speak ye unto all the congregation of Israel, saying, In the tenth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to the house of <hi type="italic">their</hi> fathers, a lamb for an house:

verses.name: Exodus 12:4
verses.text: And if the household be too little for the lamb, let him and his neighbour next unto his house take <hi type="italic">it</hi> according to the number of the souls; every man according to his eating shall make your count for the lamb.

verses.name: Exodus 12:5
verses.text: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take <hi type="italic">it</hi> out from the sheep, or from the goats:

verses.name: Exodus 12:6
verses.text: And ye shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it in the evening.

verses.name: Exodus 12:7
verses.text: And they shall take of the blood, and strike <hi type="italic">it</hi> on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses, wherein they shall eat it.

verses.name: Exodus 12:8
verses.text: And they shall eat the flesh in that night, roast with fire, and unleavened bread; <hi type="italic">and</hi> with bitter <hi type="italic">herbs</hi> they shall eat it.

verses.name: Exodus 12:9
verses.text: Eat not of it raw, nor sodden at all with water, but roast <hi type="italic">with</hi> fire; his head with his legs, and with the purtenance thereof.

verses.name: Exodus 12:10
verses.text: And ye shall let nothing of it remain until the morning; and that which remaineth of it until the morning ye shall burn with fire.

verses.name: Exodus 12:11
verses.text: ¶ And thus shall ye eat it; <hi type="italic">with</hi> your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it <hi type="italic">is</hi> the Lord’s passover.

verses.name: Exodus 12:12
verses.text: For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord.

verses.name: Exodus 12:13
verses.text: And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye <hi type="italic">are:</hi> and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy <hi type="italic">you</hi>, when I smite the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 12:14
verses.text: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the Lord throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.

verses.name: Exodus 12:15
verses.text: Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses: for whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.

verses.name: Exodus 12:16
verses.text: And in the first day <hi type="italic">there shall be</hi> an holy convocation, and in the seventh day there shall be an holy convocation to you; no manner of work shall be done in them, save <hi type="italic">that</hi> which every man must eat, that only may be done of you.

verses.name: Exodus 12:17
verses.text: And ye shall observe <hi type="italic">the feast of</hi> unleavened bread; for in this selfsame day have I brought your armies out of the land of Egypt: therefore shall ye observe this day in your generations by an ordinance for ever.

verses.name: Exodus 12:18
verses.text: ¶ In the first <hi type="italic">month</hi>, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even.

verses.name: Exodus 12:19
verses.text: Seven days shall there be no leaven found in your houses: for whosoever eateth that which is leavened, even that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he be a stranger, or born in the land.

verses.name: Exodus 12:20
verses.text: Ye shall eat nothing leavened; in all your habitations shall ye eat unleavened bread.

verses.name: Exodus 12:21
verses.text: ¶ Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said unto them, Draw out and take you a lamb according to your families, and kill the passover.

verses.name: Exodus 12:22
verses.text: And ye shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip <hi type="italic">it</hi> in the blood that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the bason, and strike the lintel and the two side posts with the blood that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the bason; and none of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning.

verses.name: Exodus 12:23
verses.text: For the Lord will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side posts, the Lord will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite <hi type="italic">you</hi>.

verses.name: Exodus 12:24
verses.text: And ye shall observe this thing for an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever.

verses.name: Exodus 12:25
verses.text: And it shall come to pass, when ye be come to the land which the Lord will give you, according as he hath promised, that ye shall keep this service.

verses.name: Exodus 12:26
verses.text: And it shall come to pass, when your children shall say unto you, What mean ye by this service?

verses.name: Exodus 12:27
verses.text: That ye shall say, It <hi type="italic">is</hi> the sacrifice of the Lord’s passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he smote the Egyptians, and delivered our houses. And the people bowed the head and worshipped.

verses.name: Exodus 12:28
verses.text: And the children of Israel went away, and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they.

verses.name: Exodus 12:29
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass, that at midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that <hi type="italic">was</hi> in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.

verses.name: Exodus 12:30
verses.text: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for <hi type="italic">there was</hi> not a house where <hi type="italic">there was</hi> not one dead.

verses.name: Exodus 12:31
verses.text: ¶ And he called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Rise up, <hi type="italic">and</hi> get you forth from among my people, both ye and the children of Israel; and go, serve the Lord, as ye have said.

verses.name: Exodus 12:32
verses.text: Also take your flocks and your herds, as ye have said, and be gone; and bless me also.

verses.name: Exodus 12:33
verses.text: And the Egyptians were urgent upon the people, that they might send them out of the land in haste; for they said, We <hi type="italic">be</hi> all dead <hi type="italic">men</hi>.

verses.name: Exodus 12:34
verses.text: And the people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneadingtroughs being bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.

verses.name: Exodus 12:35
verses.text: And the children of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and they borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment:

verses.name: Exodus 12:36
verses.text: And the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them <hi type="italic">such things as they required</hi>. And they spoiled the Egyptians.

verses.name: Exodus 12:37
verses.text: ¶ And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot <hi type="italic">that were</hi> men, beside children.

verses.name: Exodus 12:38
verses.text: And a mixed multitude went up also with them; and flocks, and herds, <hi type="italic">even</hi> very much cattle.

verses.name: Exodus 12:39
verses.text: And they baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought forth out of Egypt, for it was not leavened; because they were thrust out of Egypt, and could not tarry, neither had they prepared for themselves any victual.

verses.name: Exodus 12:40
verses.text: ¶ Now the sojourning of the children of Israel, who dwelt in Egypt, <hi type="italic">was</hi> four hundred and thirty years.

verses.name: Exodus 12:41
verses.text: And it came to pass at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 12:42
verses.text: It <hi type="italic">is</hi> a night to be much observed unto the Lord for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this <hi type="italic">is</hi> that night of the Lord to be observed of all the children of Israel in their generations.

verses.name: Exodus 12:43
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Moses and Aaron, This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the ordinance of the passover: There shall no stranger eat thereof:

verses.name: Exodus 12:44
verses.text: But every man’s servant that is bought for money, when thou hast circumcised him, then shall he eat thereof.

verses.name: Exodus 12:45
verses.text: A foreigner and an hired servant shall not eat thereof.

verses.name: Exodus 12:46
verses.text: In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth ought of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.

verses.name: Exodus 12:47
verses.text: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.

verses.name: Exodus 12:48
verses.text: And when a stranger shall sojourn with thee, and will keep the passover to the Lord, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it; and he shall be as one that is born in the land: for no uncircumcised person shall eat thereof.

verses.name: Exodus 12:49
verses.text: One law shall be to him that is homeborn, and unto the stranger that sojourneth among you.

verses.name: Exodus 12:50
verses.text: Thus did all the children of Israel; as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they.

verses.name: Exodus 12:51
verses.text: And it came to pass the selfsame day, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the Lord did bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their armies.  <chapter eID="Exod.12"/><div eID="gen65" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 13:1
verses.text: AND the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 13:2
verses.text: Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, <hi type="italic">both</hi> of man and of beast: it <hi type="italic">is</hi> mine.

verses.name: Exodus 13:3
verses.text: ¶ And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this <hi type="italic">place:</hi> there shall no leavened bread be eaten.

verses.name: Exodus 13:4
verses.text: This day came ye out in the month Abib.

verses.name: Exodus 13:5
verses.text: ¶ And it shall be when the Lord shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, which he sware unto thy fathers to give thee, a land flowing with milk and honey, that thou shalt keep this service in this month.

verses.name: Exodus 13:6
verses.text: Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and in the seventh day <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> a feast to the Lord.

verses.name: Exodus 13:7
verses.text: Unleavened bread shall be eaten seven days; and there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters.

verses.name: Exodus 13:8
verses.text: ¶ And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, <hi type="italic">This is done</hi> because of that <hi type="italic">which</hi> the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 13:9
verses.text: And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the Lord’s law may be in thy mouth: for with a strong hand hath the Lord brought thee out of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 13:10
verses.text: Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in his season from year to year.

verses.name: Exodus 13:11
verses.text: ¶ And it shall be when the Lord shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanites, as he sware unto thee and to thy fathers, and shall give it thee,

verses.name: Exodus 13:12
verses.text: That thou shalt set apart unto the Lord all that openeth the matrix, and every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> the Lord’s.

verses.name: Exodus 13:13
verses.text: And every firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a lamb; and if thou wilt not redeem it, then thou shalt break his neck: and all the firstborn of man among thy children shalt thou redeem.

verses.name: Exodus 13:14
verses.text: ¶ And it shall be when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What <hi type="italic">is</hi> this? that thou shalt say unto him, By strength of hand the Lord brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage:

verses.name: Exodus 13:15
verses.text: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh would hardly let us go, that the Lord slew all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of beast: therefore I sacrifice to the Lord all that openeth the matrix, being males; but all the firstborn of my children I redeem.

verses.name: Exodus 13:16
verses.text: And it shall be for a token upon thine hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes: for by strength of hand the Lord brought us forth out of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 13:17
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not <hi type="italic">through</hi> the way of the land of the Philistines, although that <hi type="italic">was</hi> near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt:

verses.name: Exodus 13:18
verses.text: But God led the people about, <hi type="italic">through</hi> the way of the wilderness of the Red sea: and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 13:19
verses.text: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

verses.name: Exodus 13:20
verses.text: ¶ And they took their journey from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness.

verses.name: Exodus 13:21
verses.text: And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:

verses.name: Exodus 13:22
verses.text: He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, <hi type="italic">from</hi> before the people.  <chapter eID="Exod.13"/><div eID="gen66" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 14:1
verses.text: AND the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 14:2
verses.text: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they turn and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, over against Baal-zephon: before it shall ye encamp by the sea.

verses.name: Exodus 14:3
verses.text: For Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, They <hi type="italic">are</hi> entangled in the land, the wilderness hath shut them in.

verses.name: Exodus 14:4
verses.text: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, that he shall follow after them; and I will be honoured upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host; that the Egyptians may know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord. And they did so.

verses.name: Exodus 14:5
verses.text: ¶ And it was told the king of Egypt that the people fled: and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was turned against the people, and they said, Why have we done this, that we have let Israel go from serving us?

verses.name: Exodus 14:6
verses.text: And he made ready his chariot, and took his people with him:

verses.name: Exodus 14:7
verses.text: And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt, and captains over every one of them.

verses.name: Exodus 14:8
verses.text: And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after the children of Israel: and the children of Israel went out with an high hand.

verses.name: Exodus 14:9
verses.text: But the Egyptians pursued after them, all the horses <hi type="italic">and</hi> chariots of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his army, and overtook them encamping by the sea, beside Pi-hahiroth, before Baal-zephon.

verses.name: Exodus 14:10
verses.text: ¶ And when Pharaoh drew nigh, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and, behold, the Egyptians marched after them; and they were sore afraid: and the children of Israel cried out unto the Lord.

verses.name: Exodus 14:11
verses.text: And they said unto Moses, Because <hi type="italic">there were</hi> no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? wherefore hast thou dealt thus with us, to carry us forth out of Egypt?

verses.name: Exodus 14:12
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is</hi> not this the word that we did tell thee in Egypt, saying, Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? For <hi type="italic">it had been</hi> better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.

verses.name: Exodus 14:13
verses.text: ¶ And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.

verses.name: Exodus 14:14
verses.text: The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.

verses.name: Exodus 14:15
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Moses, Wherefore criest thou unto me? speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward:

verses.name: Exodus 14:16
verses.text: But lift thou up thy rod, and stretch out thine hand over the sea, and divide it: and the children of Israel shall go on dry <hi type="italic">ground</hi> through the midst of the sea.

verses.name: Exodus 14:17
verses.text: And I, behold, I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and they shall follow them: and I will get me honour upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.

verses.name: Exodus 14:18
verses.text: And the Egyptians shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord, when I have gotten me honour upon Pharaoh, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.

verses.name: Exodus 14:19
verses.text: ¶ And the angel of God, which went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them:

verses.name: Exodus 14:20
verses.text: And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and it was a cloud and darkness <hi type="italic">to them</hi>, but it gave light by night <hi type="italic">to these:</hi> so that the one came not near the other all the night.

verses.name: Exodus 14:21
verses.text: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the Lord caused the sea to go <hi type="italic">back</hi> by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry <hi type="italic">land</hi>, and the waters were divided.

verses.name: Exodus 14:22
verses.text: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry <hi type="italic">ground:</hi> and the waters <hi type="italic">were</hi> a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.

verses.name: Exodus 14:23
verses.text: ¶ And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them to the midst of the sea, <hi type="italic">even</hi> all Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.

verses.name: Exodus 14:24
verses.text: And it came to pass, that in the morning watch the Lord looked unto the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of the cloud, and troubled the host of the Egyptians,

verses.name: Exodus 14:25
verses.text: And took off their chariot wheels, that they drave them heavily: so that the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Israel; for the Lord fighteth for them against the Egyptians.

verses.name: Exodus 14:26
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand over the sea, that the waters may come again upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen.

verses.name: Exodus 14:27
verses.text: And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and the Lord overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.

verses.name: Exodus 14:28
verses.text: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, <hi type="italic">and</hi> all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.

verses.name: Exodus 14:29
verses.text: But the children of Israel walked upon dry <hi type="italic">land</hi> in the midst of the sea; and the waters <hi type="italic">were</hi> a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.

verses.name: Exodus 14:30
verses.text: Thus the Lord saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore.

verses.name: Exodus 14:31
verses.text: And Israel saw that great work which the Lord did upon the Egyptians: and the people feared the Lord, and believed the Lord, and his servant Moses.  <chapter eID="Exod.14"/><div eID="gen67" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 15:1
verses.text: THEN sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the Lord, and spake, saying, I will sing unto the Lord, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.

verses.name: Exodus 15:2
verses.text: The Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he <hi type="italic">is</hi> my God, and I will prepare him an habitation; my father’s God, and I will exalt him.

verses.name: Exodus 15:3
verses.text: The Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> a man of war: the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> his name.

verses.name: Exodus 15:4
verses.text: Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red sea.

verses.name: Exodus 15:5
verses.text: The depths have covered them: they sank into the bottom as a stone.

verses.name: Exodus 15:6
verses.text: Thy right hand, O Lord, is become glorious in power: thy right hand, O Lord, hath dashed in pieces the enemy.

verses.name: Exodus 15:7
verses.text: And in the greatness of thine excellency thou hast overthrown them that rose up against thee: thou sentest forth thy wrath, <hi type="italic">which</hi> consumed them as stubble.

verses.name: Exodus 15:8
verses.text: And with the blast of thy nostrils the waters were gathered together, the floods stood upright as an heap, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the depths were congealed in the heart of the sea.

verses.name: Exodus 15:9
verses.text: The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil; my lust shall be satisfied upon them; I will draw my sword, my hand shall destroy them.

verses.name: Exodus 15:10
verses.text: Thou didst blow with thy wind, the sea covered them: they sank as lead in the mighty waters.

verses.name: Exodus 15:11
verses.text: Who <hi type="italic">is</hi> like unto thee, O Lord, among the gods? who <hi type="italic">is</hi> like thee, glorious in holiness, fearful <hi type="italic">in</hi> praises, doing wonders?

verses.name: Exodus 15:12
verses.text: Thou stretchedst out thy right hand, the earth swallowed them.

verses.name: Exodus 15:13
verses.text: Thou in thy mercy hast led forth the people <hi type="italic">which</hi> thou hast redeemed: thou hast guided <hi type="italic">them</hi> in thy strength unto thy holy habitation.

verses.name: Exodus 15:14
verses.text: The people shall hear, <hi type="italic">and</hi> be afraid: sorrow shall take hold on the inhabitants of Palestina.

verses.name: Exodus 15:15
verses.text: Then the dukes of Edom shall be amazed; the mighty men of Moab, trembling shall take hold upon them; all the inhabitants of Canaan shall melt away.

verses.name: Exodus 15:16
verses.text: Fear and dread shall fall upon them; by the greatness of thine arm they shall be <hi type="italic">as</hi> still as a stone; till thy people pass over, O Lord, till the people pass over, <hi type="italic">which</hi> thou hast purchased.

verses.name: Exodus 15:17
verses.text: Thou shalt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thine inheritance, <hi type="italic">in</hi> the place, O Lord, <hi type="italic">which</hi> thou hast made for thee to dwell in, <hi type="italic">in</hi> the Sanctuary, O Lord, <hi type="italic">which</hi> thy hands have established.

verses.name: Exodus 15:18
verses.text: The Lord shall reign for ever and ever.

verses.name: Exodus 15:19
verses.text: For the horse of Pharaoh went in with his chariots and with his horsemen into the sea, and the Lord brought again the waters of the sea upon them; but the children of Israel went on dry <hi type="italic">land</hi> in the midst of the sea.

verses.name: Exodus 15:20
verses.text: ¶ And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.

verses.name: Exodus 15:21
verses.text: And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to the Lord, for he hath triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.

verses.name: Exodus 15:22
verses.text: So Moses brought Israel from the Red sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.

verses.name: Exodus 15:23
verses.text: ¶ And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they <hi type="italic">were</hi> bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah.

verses.name: Exodus 15:24
verses.text: And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?

verses.name: Exodus 15:25
verses.text: And he cried unto the Lord; and the Lord shewed him a tree, <hi type="italic">which</hi> when he had cast into the waters, the waters were made sweet: there he made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there he proved them,

verses.name: Exodus 15:26
verses.text: And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the Lord thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord that healeth thee.

verses.name: Exodus 15:27
verses.text: ¶ And they came to Elim, where <hi type="italic">were</hi> twelve wells of water, and threescore and ten palm trees: and they encamped there by the waters.  <chapter eID="Exod.15"/><div eID="gen68" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 16:1
verses.text: AND they took their journey from Elim, and all the congregation of the children of Israel came unto the wilderness of Sin, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departing out of the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 16:2
verses.text: And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness:

verses.name: Exodus 16:3
verses.text: And the children of Israel said unto them, Would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, <hi type="italic">and</hi> when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.

verses.name: Exodus 16:4
verses.text: ¶ Then said the Lord unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.

verses.name: Exodus 16:5
verses.text: And it shall come to pass, that on the sixth day they shall prepare <hi type="italic">that</hi> which they bring in; and it shall be twice as much as they gather daily.

verses.name: Exodus 16:6
verses.text: And Moses and Aaron said unto all the children of Israel, At even, then ye shall know that the Lord hath brought you out from the land of Egypt:

verses.name: Exodus 16:7
verses.text: And in the morning, then ye shall see the glory of the Lord; for that he heareth your murmurings against the Lord: and what <hi type="italic">are</hi> we, that ye murmur against us?

verses.name: Exodus 16:8
verses.text: And Moses said, <hi type="italic">This shall be</hi>, when the Lord shall give you in the evening flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to the full; for that the Lord heareth your murmurings which ye murmur against him: and what <hi type="italic">are</hi> we? your murmurings <hi type="italic">are</hi> not against us, but against the Lord.

verses.name: Exodus 16:9
verses.text: ¶ And Moses spake unto Aaron, Say unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, Come near before the Lord: for he hath heard your murmurings.

verses.name: Exodus 16:10
verses.text: And it came to pass, as Aaron spake unto the whole congregation of the children of Israel, that they looked toward the wilderness, and, behold, the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud.

verses.name: Exodus 16:11
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 16:12
verses.text: I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel: speak unto them, saying, At even ye shall eat flesh, and in the morning ye shall be filled with bread; and ye shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord your God.

verses.name: Exodus 16:13
verses.text: And it came to pass, that at even the quails came up, and covered the camp: and in the morning the dew lay round about the host.

verses.name: Exodus 16:14
verses.text: And when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness <hi type="italic">there lay</hi> a small round thing, <hi type="italic">as</hi> small as the hoar frost on the ground.

verses.name: Exodus 16:15
verses.text: And when the children of Israel saw <hi type="italic">it</hi>, they said one to another, It <hi type="italic">is</hi> manna: for they wist not what it <hi type="italic">was</hi>. And Moses said unto them, This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the bread which the Lord hath given you to eat.

verses.name: Exodus 16:16
verses.text: ¶ This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the thing which the Lord hath commanded, Gather of it every man according to his eating, an omer for every man, <hi type="italic">according to</hi> the number of your persons; take ye every man for <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">are</hi> in his tents.

verses.name: Exodus 16:17
verses.text: And the children of Israel did so, and gathered, some more, some less.

verses.name: Exodus 16:18
verses.text: And when they did mete <hi type="italic">it</hi> with an omer, he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack; they gathered every man according to his eating.

verses.name: Exodus 16:19
verses.text: And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning.

verses.name: Exodus 16:20
verses.text: Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.

verses.name: Exodus 16:21
verses.text: And they gathered it every morning, every man according to his eating: and when the sun waxed hot, it melted.

verses.name: Exodus 16:22
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass, <hi type="italic">that</hi> on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for one <hi type="italic">man:</hi> and all the rulers of the congregation came and told Moses.

verses.name: Exodus 16:23
verses.text: And he said unto them, This <hi type="italic">is that</hi> which the Lord hath said, To morrow <hi type="italic">is</hi> the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake <hi type="italic">that</hi> which ye will bake <hi type="italic">to day</hi>, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.

verses.name: Exodus 16:24
verses.text: And they laid it up till the morning, as Moses bade: and it did not stink, neither was there any worm therein.

verses.name: Exodus 16:25
verses.text: And Moses said, Eat that to day; for to day <hi type="italic">is</hi> a sabbath unto the Lord: to day ye shall not find it in the field.

verses.name: Exodus 16:26
verses.text: Six days ye shall gather it; but on the seventh day, <hi type="italic">which is</hi> the sabbath, in it there shall be none.

verses.name: Exodus 16:27
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass, <hi type="italic">that</hi> there went out <hi type="italic">some</hi> of the people on the seventh day for to gather, and they found none.

verses.name: Exodus 16:28
verses.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws?

verses.name: Exodus 16:29
verses.text: See, for that the Lord hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.

verses.name: Exodus 16:30
verses.text: So the people rested on the seventh day.

verses.name: Exodus 16:31
verses.text: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it <hi type="italic">was</hi> like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it <hi type="italic">was</hi> like wafers <hi type="italic">made</hi> with honey.

verses.name: Exodus 16:32
verses.text: ¶ And Moses said, This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the thing which the Lord commandeth, Fill an omer of it to be kept for your generations; that they may see the bread wherewith I have fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you forth from the land of Egypt.

verses.name: Exodus 16:33
verses.text: And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a pot, and put an omer full of manna therein, and lay it up before the Lord, to be kept for your generations.

verses.name: Exodus 16:34
verses.text: As the Lord commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept.

verses.name: Exodus 16:35
verses.text: And the children of Israel did eat manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited; they did eat manna, until they came unto the borders of the land of Canaan.

verses.name: Exodus 16:36
verses.text: Now an omer <hi type="italic">is</hi> the tenth <hi type="italic">part</hi> of an ephah.  <chapter eID="Exod.16"/><div eID="gen69" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 17:1
verses.text: AND all the congregation of the children of Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, after their journeys, according to the commandment of the Lord, and pitched in Rephidim: and <hi type="italic">there was</hi> no water for the people to drink.

verses.name: Exodus 17:2
verses.text: Wherefore the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And Moses said unto them, Why chide ye with me? wherefore do ye tempt the Lord?

verses.name: Exodus 17:3
verses.text: And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore <hi type="italic">is</hi> this <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?

verses.name: Exodus 17:4
verses.text: And Moses cried unto the Lord, saying, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me.

verses.name: Exodus 17:5
verses.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, Go on before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel; and thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thine hand, and go.

verses.name: Exodus 17:6
verses.text: Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.

verses.name: Exodus 17:7
verses.text: And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not?

verses.name: Exodus 17:8
verses.text: ¶ Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.

verses.name: Exodus 17:9
verses.text: And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in mine hand.

verses.name: Exodus 17:10
verses.text: So Joshua did as Moses had said to him, and fought with Amalek: and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

verses.name: Exodus 17:11
verses.text: And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

verses.name: Exodus 17:12
verses.text: But Moses’ hands <hi type="italic">were</hi> heavy; and they took a stone, and put <hi type="italic">it</hi> under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.

verses.name: Exodus 17:13
verses.text: And Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.

verses.name: Exodus 17:14
verses.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, Write this <hi type="italic">for</hi> a memorial in a book, and rehearse <hi type="italic">it</hi> in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.

verses.name: Exodus 17:15
verses.text: And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it Jehovah-nissi:

verses.name: Exodus 17:16
verses.text: For he said, Because the Lord hath sworn <hi type="italic">that</hi> the Lord <hi type="italic">will have</hi> war with Amalek from generation to generation.  <chapter eID="Exod.17"/><div eID="gen70" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 18:1
verses.text: WHEN Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father in law, heard of all that God had done for Moses, and for Israel his people, <hi type="italic">and</hi> that the Lord had brought Israel out of Egypt;

verses.name: Exodus 18:2
verses.text: Then Jethro, Moses’ father in law, took Zipporah, Moses’ wife, after he had sent her back,

verses.name: Exodus 18:3
verses.text: And her two sons; of which the name of the one <hi type="italic">was</hi> Gershom; for he said, I have been an alien in a strange land:

verses.name: Exodus 18:4
verses.text: And the name of the other <hi type="italic">was</hi> Eliezer; for the God of my father, <hi type="italic">said he</hi>, <hi type="italic">was</hi> mine help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh:

verses.name: Exodus 18:5
verses.text: And Jethro, Moses’ father in law, came with his sons and his wife unto Moses into the wilderness, where he encamped at the mount of God:

verses.name: Exodus 18:6
verses.text: And he said unto Moses, I thy father in law Jethro am come unto thee, and thy wife, and her two sons with her.

verses.name: Exodus 18:7
verses.text: ¶ And Moses went out to meet his father in law, and did obeisance, and kissed him; and they asked each other of <hi type="italic">their</hi> welfare; and they came into the tent.

verses.name: Exodus 18:8
verses.text: And Moses told his father in law all that the Lord had done unto Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, <hi type="italic">and</hi> all the travail that had come upon them by the way, and <hi type="italic">how</hi> the Lord delivered them.

verses.name: Exodus 18:9
verses.text: And Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness which the Lord had done to Israel, whom he had delivered out of the hand of the Egyptians.

verses.name: Exodus 18:10
verses.text: And Jethro said, Blessed <hi type="italic">be</hi> the Lord, who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh, who hath delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.

verses.name: Exodus 18:11
verses.text: Now I know that the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> greater than all gods: for in the thing wherein they dealt proudly <hi type="italic">he was</hi> above them.

verses.name: Exodus 18:12
verses.text: And Jethro, Moses’ father in law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God: and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses’ father in law before God.

verses.name: Exodus 18:13
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses sat to judge the people: and the people stood by Moses from the morning unto the evening.

verses.name: Exodus 18:14
verses.text: And when Moses’ father in law saw all that he did to the people, he said, What <hi type="italic">is</hi> this thing that thou doest to the people? why sittest thou thyself alone, and all the people stand by thee from morning unto even?

verses.name: Exodus 18:15
verses.text: And Moses said unto his father in law, Because the people come unto me to inquire of God:

verses.name: Exodus 18:16
verses.text: When they have a matter, they come unto me; and I judge between one and another, and I do make <hi type="italic">them</hi> know the statutes of God, and his laws.

verses.name: Exodus 18:17
verses.text: And Moses’ father in law said unto him, The thing that thou doest <hi type="italic">is</hi> not good.

verses.name: Exodus 18:18
verses.text: Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that <hi type="italic">is</hi> with thee: for this thing <hi type="italic">is</hi> too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.

verses.name: Exodus 18:19
verses.text: Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God:

verses.name: Exodus 18:20
verses.text: And thou shalt teach them ordinances and laws, and shalt shew them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do.

verses.name: Exodus 18:21
verses.text: Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place <hi type="italic">such</hi> over them, <hi type="italic">to be</hi> rulers of thousands, <hi type="italic">and</hi> rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens:

verses.name: Exodus 18:22
verses.text: And let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, <hi type="italic">that</hi> every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear <hi type="italic">the burden</hi> with thee.

verses.name: Exodus 18:23
verses.text: If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee <hi type="italic">so</hi>, then thou shalt be able to endure, and all this people shall also go to their place in peace.

verses.name: Exodus 18:24
verses.text: So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father in law, and did all that he had said.

verses.name: Exodus 18:25
verses.text: And Moses chose able men out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.

verses.name: Exodus 18:26
verses.text: And they judged the people at all seasons: the hard causes they brought unto Moses, but every small matter they judged themselves.

verses.name: Exodus 18:27
verses.text: ¶ And Moses let his father in law depart; and he went his way into his own land.  <chapter eID="Exod.18"/><div eID="gen71" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 19:1
verses.text: IN the third month, when the children of Israel were gone forth out of the land of Egypt, the same day came they <hi type="italic">into</hi> the wilderness of Sinai.

verses.name: Exodus 19:2
verses.text: For they were departed from Rephidim, and were come <hi type="italic">to</hi> the desert of Sinai, and had pitched in the wilderness; and there Israel camped before the mount.

verses.name: Exodus 19:3
verses.text: And Moses went up unto God, and the Lord called unto him out of the mountain, saying, Thus shalt thou say to the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel;

verses.name: Exodus 19:4
verses.text: Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and <hi type="italic">how</hi> I bare you on eagles’ wings, and brought you unto myself.

verses.name: Exodus 19:5
verses.text: Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth <hi type="italic">is</hi> mine:

verses.name: Exodus 19:6
verses.text: And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These <hi type="italic">are</hi> the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.

verses.name: Exodus 19:7
verses.text: ¶ And Moses came and called for the elders of the people, and laid before their faces all these words which the Lord commanded him.

verses.name: Exodus 19:8
verses.text: And all the people answered together, and said, All that the Lord hath spoken we will do. And Moses returned the words of the people unto the Lord.

verses.name: Exodus 19:9
verses.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, Lo, I come unto thee in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with thee, and believe thee for ever. And Moses told the words of the people unto the Lord.

verses.name: Exodus 19:10
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Moses, Go unto the people, and sanctify them to day and to morrow, and let them wash their clothes,

verses.name: Exodus 19:11
verses.text: And be ready against the third day: for the third day the Lord will come down in the sight of all the people upon mount Sinai.

verses.name: Exodus 19:12
verses.text: And thou shalt set bounds unto the people round about, saying, Take heed to yourselves, <hi type="italic">that ye</hi> go <hi type="italic">not</hi> up into the mount, or touch the border of it: whosoever toucheth the mount shall be surely put to death:

verses.name: Exodus 19:13
verses.text: There shall not an hand touch it, but he shall surely be stoned, or shot through; whether <hi type="italic">it be</hi> beast or man, it shall not live: when the trumpet soundeth long, they shall come up to the mount.

verses.name: Exodus 19:14
verses.text: ¶ And Moses went down from the mount unto the people, and sanctified the people; and they washed their clothes.

verses.name: Exodus 19:15
verses.text: And he said unto the people, Be ready against the third day: come not at <hi type="italic">your</hi> wives.

verses.name: Exodus 19:16
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass on the third day in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud; so that all the people that <hi type="italic">was</hi> in the camp trembled.

verses.name: Exodus 19:17
verses.text: And Moses brought forth the people out of the camp to meet with God; and they stood at the nether part of the mount.

verses.name: Exodus 19:18
verses.text: And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the Lord descended upon it in fire: and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mount quaked greatly.

verses.name: Exodus 19:19
verses.text: And when the voice of the trumpet sounded long, and waxed louder and louder, Moses spake, and God answered him by a voice.

verses.name: Exodus 19:20
verses.text: And the Lord came down upon mount Sinai, on the top of the mount: and the Lord called Moses <hi type="italic">up</hi> to the top of the mount; and Moses went up.

verses.name: Exodus 19:21
verses.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, Go down, charge the people, lest they break through unto the Lord to gaze, and many of them perish.

verses.name: Exodus 19:22
verses.text: And let the priests also, which come near to the Lord, sanctify themselves, lest the Lord break forth upon them.

verses.name: Exodus 19:23
verses.text: And Moses said unto the Lord, The people cannot come up to mount Sinai: for thou chargedst us, saying, Set bounds about the mount, and sanctify it.

verses.name: Exodus 19:24
verses.text: And the Lord said unto him, Away, get thee down, and thou shalt come up, thou, and Aaron with thee: but let not the priests and the people break through to come up unto the Lord, lest he break forth upon them.

verses.name: Exodus 19:25
verses.text: So Moses went down unto the people, and spake unto them.  <chapter eID="Exod.19"/><div eID="gen72" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 20:1
verses.text: AND God spake all these words, saying,

verses.name: Exodus 20:2
verses.text: I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

verses.name: Exodus 20:3
verses.text: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

verses.name: Exodus 20:4
verses.text: Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness <hi type="italic">of any thing</hi> that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in heaven above, or that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the earth beneath, or that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the water under the earth:

verses.name: Exodus 20:5
verses.text: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God <hi type="italic">am</hi> a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth <hi type="italic">generation</hi> of them that hate me;

verses.name: Exodus 20:6
verses.text: And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.

verses.name: Exodus 20:7
verses.text: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

verses.name: Exodus 20:8
verses.text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.

verses.name: Exodus 20:9
verses.text: Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work:

verses.name: Exodus 20:10
verses.text: But the seventh day <hi type="italic">is</hi> the sabbath of the Lord thy God: <hi type="italic">in it</hi> thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that <hi type="italic">is</hi> within thy gates:

verses.name: Exodus 20:11
verses.text: For <hi type="italic">in</hi> six days the Lord made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them <hi type="italic">is</hi>, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the Lord blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.

verses.name: Exodus 20:12
verses.text: ¶ Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

verses.name: Exodus 20:13
verses.text: Thou shalt not kill.

verses.name: Exodus 20:14
verses.text: Thou shalt not commit adultery.

verses.name: Exodus 20:15
verses.text: Thou shalt not steal.

verses.name: Exodus 20:16
verses.text: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.

verses.name: Exodus 20:17
verses.text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy neighbour’s.

verses.name: Exodus 20:18
verses.text: ¶ And all the people saw the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the noise of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking: and when the people saw <hi type="italic">it</hi>, they removed, and stood afar off.

verses.name: Exodus 20:19
verses.text: And they said unto Moses, Speak thou with us, and we will hear: but let not God speak with us, lest we die.

verses.name: Exodus 20:20
verses.text: And Moses said unto the people, Fear not: for God is come to prove you, and that his fear may be before your faces, that ye sin not.

verses.name: Exodus 20:21
verses.text: And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where God <hi type="italic">was</hi>.

verses.name: Exodus 20:22
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Moses, Thus thou shalt say unto the children of Israel, Ye have seen that I have talked with you from heaven.

verses.name: Exodus 20:23
verses.text: Ye shall not make with me gods of silver, neither shall ye make unto you gods of gold.

verses.name: Exodus 20:24
verses.text: ¶ An altar of earth thou shalt make unto me, and shalt sacrifice thereon thy burnt offerings, and thy peace offerings, thy sheep, and thine oxen: in all places where I record my name I will come unto thee, and I will bless thee.

verses.name: Exodus 20:25
verses.text: And if thou wilt make me an altar of stone, thou shalt not build it of hewn stone: for if thou lift up thy tool upon it, thou hast polluted it.

verses.name: Exodus 20:26
verses.text: Neither shalt thou go up by steps unto mine altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon.  <chapter eID="Exod.20"/><div eID="gen73" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Exodus 21:1
verses.text: NOW these <hi type="italic">are</hi> the judgments which thou shalt set before them.

verses.name: Exodus 21:2
verses.text: If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.

verses.name: Exodus 21:3
verses.text: If he came in by himself, he shall go out by himself: if he were married, then his wife shall go out with him.

verses.name: Exodus 21:4
verses.text: If his master have given him a wife, and she have born him sons or daughters; the wife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself.

verses.name: Exodus 21:5
verses.text: And if the servant shall plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free:

verses.name: Exodus 21:6
verses.text: Then his master shall bring him unto the judges; he shall also bring him to the door, or unto the door post; and his master shall bore his ear through with an aul; and he shall serve him for ever.

verses.name: Exodus 21:7
verses.text: ¶ And if a man sell his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do.

verses.name: Exodus 21:8
verses.text: If she please not her master, who hath betrothed her to himself, then shall he let her be redeemed: to sell her unto a strange nation he shall have no power, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her.

verses.name: Exodus 21:9
verses.text: And if he have betrothed her unto his son, he shall deal with her after the manner of daughters.

verses.name: Exodus 21:10
verses.text: If he take him another <hi type="italic">wife;</hi> her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish.

verses.name: Exodus 21:11
verses.text: And if he do not these three unto her, then shall she go out free without money.

verses.name: Exodus 21:12
verses.text: ¶ He that smiteth a man, so that he die, shall be surely put to death.

verses.name: Exodus 21:13
verses.text: And if a man lie not in wait, but God deliver <hi type="italic">him</hi> into his hand; then I will appoint thee a place whither he shall flee.

verses.name: Exodus 21:14
verses.text: But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour, to slay him with guile; thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.

verses.name: Exodus 21:15
verses.text: ¶ And he that smiteth his father, or his mother, shall be surely put to death.

verses.name: Exodus 21:16
verses.text: ¶ And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.

verses.name: Exodus 21:17
verses.text: ¶ And he that curseth his father, or his mother, shall surely be put to death.

verses.name: Exodus 21:18
verses.text: ¶ And if men strive together, and one smite another with a stone, or with <hi type="italic">his</hi> fist, and he die not, but keepeth <hi type="italic">his</hi> bed:

verses.name: Exodus 21:19
verses.text: If he rise again, and walk abroad upon his staff, then shall he that smote <hi type="italic">him</hi> be quit: only he shall pay <hi type="italic">for</hi> the loss of his time, and shall cause <hi type="italic">him</hi> to be thoroughly healed.

verses.name: Exodus 21:20
verses.text: ¶ And if a man smite his servant, or his maid, with a rod, and he die under his hand; he shall be surely punished.

verses.name: Exodus 21:21
verses.text: Notwithstanding, if he continue a day or two, he shall not be punished: for he <hi type="italic">is</hi> his money.
