verses.text: Let not my lord, I pray thee, regard this man of Belial, <hi type="italic">even</hi> Nabal: for as his name <hi type="italic">is</hi>, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> he; Nabal <hi type="italic">is</hi> his name, and folly <hi type="italic">is</hi> with him: but I thine handmaid saw not the young men of my lord, whom thou didst send.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:26
verses.text: Now therefore, my lord, <hi type="italic">as</hi> the Lord liveth, and <hi type="italic">as</hi> thy soul liveth, seeing the Lord hath withholden thee from coming to <hi type="italic">shed</hi> blood, and from avenging thyself with thine own hand, now let thine enemies, and they that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:27
verses.text: And now this blessing which thine handmaid hath brought unto my lord, let it even be given unto the young men that follow my lord.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:28
verses.text: I pray thee, forgive the trespass of thine handmaid: for the Lord will certainly make my lord a sure house; because my lord fighteth the battles of the Lord, and evil hath not been found in thee <hi type="italic">all</hi> thy days.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:29
verses.text: Yet a man is risen to pursue thee, and to seek thy soul: but the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord thy God; and the souls of thine enemies, them shall he sling out, <hi type="italic">as out</hi> of the middle of a sling.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:30
verses.text: And it shall come to pass, when the Lord shall have done to my lord according to all the good that he hath spoken concerning thee, and shall have appointed thee ruler over Israel;

verses.name: I Samuel 25:31
verses.text: That this shall be no grief unto thee, nor offence of heart unto my lord, either that thou hast shed blood causeless, or that my lord hath avenged himself: but when the Lord shall have dealt well with my lord, then remember thine handmaid.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:32
verses.text: ¶ And David said to Abigail, Blessed <hi type="italic">be</hi> the Lord God of Israel, which sent thee this day to meet me:

verses.name: I Samuel 25:33
verses.text: And blessed <hi type="italic">be</hi> thy advice, and blessed <hi type="italic">be</hi> thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to <hi type="italic">shed</hi> blood, and from avenging myself with mine own hand.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:34
verses.text: For in very deed, <hi type="italic">as</hi> the Lord God of Israel liveth, which hath kept me back from hurting thee, except thou hadst hasted and come to meet me, surely there had not been left unto Nabal by the morning light any that pisseth against the wall.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:35
verses.text: So David received of her hand <hi type="italic">that</hi> which she had brought him, and said unto her, Go up in peace to thine house; see, I have hearkened to thy voice, and have accepted thy person.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:36
verses.text: ¶ And Abigail came to Nabal; and, behold, he held a feast in his house, like the feast of a king; and Nabal’s heart <hi type="italic">was</hi> merry within him, for he <hi type="italic">was</hi> very drunken: wherefore she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:37
verses.text: But it came to pass in the morning, when the wine was gone out of Nabal, and his wife had told him these things, that his heart died within him, and he became <hi type="italic">as</hi> a stone.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:38
verses.text: And it came to pass about ten days <hi type="italic">after</hi>, that the Lord smote Nabal, that he died.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:39
verses.text: ¶ And when David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, Blessed <hi type="italic">be</hi> the Lord, that hath pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and hath kept his servant from evil: for the Lord hath returned the wickedness of Nabal upon his own head. And David sent and communed with Abigail, to take her to him to wife.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:40
verses.text: And when the servants of David were come to Abigail to Carmel, they spake unto her, saying, David sent us unto thee, to take thee to him to wife.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:41
verses.text: And she arose, and bowed herself on <hi type="italic">her</hi> face to the earth, and said, Behold, <hi type="italic">let</hi> thine handmaid <hi type="italic">be</hi> a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:42
verses.text: And Abigail hasted, and arose, and rode upon an ass, with five damsels of hers that went after her; and she went after the messengers of David, and became his wife.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:43
verses.text: David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel; and they were also both of them his wives.

verses.name: I Samuel 25:44
verses.text: ¶ But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David’s wife, to Phalti the son of Laish, which <hi type="italic">was</hi> of Gallim.  <chapter eID="1Sam.25"/><div eID="gen271" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 26:1
verses.text: AND the Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, <hi type="italic">which is</hi> before Jeshimon?

verses.name: I Samuel 26:2
verses.text: Then Saul arose, and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:3
verses.text: And Saul pitched in the hill of Hachilah, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> before Jeshimon, by the way. But David abode in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul came after him into the wilderness.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:4
verses.text: David therefore sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:5
verses.text: ¶ And David arose, and came to the place where Saul had pitched: and David beheld the place where Saul lay, and Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host: and Saul lay in the trench, and the people pitched round about him.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:6
verses.text: Then answered David and said to Ahimelech the Hittite, and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother to Joab, saying, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? And Abishai said, I will go down with thee.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:7
verses.text: So David and Abishai came to the people by night: and, behold, Saul lay sleeping within the trench, and his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster: but Abner and the people lay round about him.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:8
verses.text: Then said Abishai to David, God hath delivered thine enemy into thine hand this day: now therefore let me smite him, I pray thee, with the spear even to the earth at once, and I will not <hi type="italic">smite</hi> him the second time.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:9
verses.text: And David said to Abishai, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the Lord’s anointed, and be guiltless?

verses.name: I Samuel 26:10
verses.text: David said furthermore, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord liveth, the Lord shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and perish.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:11
verses.text: The Lord forbid that I should stretch forth mine hand against the Lord’s anointed: but, I pray thee, take thou now the spear that <hi type="italic">is</hi> at his bolster, and the cruse of water, and let us go.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:12
verses.text: So David took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul’s bolster; and they gat them away, and no man saw <hi type="italic">it</hi>, nor knew <hi type="italic">it</hi>, neither awaked: for they <hi type="italic">were</hi> all asleep; because a deep sleep from the Lord was fallen upon them.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:13
verses.text: ¶ Then David went over to the other side, and stood on the top of an hill afar off; a great space <hi type="italic">being</hi> between them:

verses.name: I Samuel 26:14
verses.text: And David cried to the people, and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, Answerest thou not, Abner? Then Abner answered and said, Who <hi type="italic">art</hi> thou <hi type="italic">that</hi> criest to the king?

verses.name: I Samuel 26:15
verses.text: And David said to Abner, <hi type="italic">Art</hi> not thou a <hi type="italic">valiant</hi> man? and who <hi type="italic">is</hi> like to thee in Israel? wherefore then hast thou not kept thy lord the king? for there came one of the people in to destroy the king thy lord.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:16
verses.text: This thing <hi type="italic">is</hi> not good that thou hast done. <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord liveth, ye <hi type="italic">are</hi> worthy to die, because ye have not kept your master, the Lord’s anointed. And now see where the king’s spear <hi type="italic">is</hi>, and the cruse of water that <hi type="italic">was</hi> at his bolster.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:17
verses.text: And Saul knew David’s voice, and said, <hi type="italic">Is</hi> this thy voice, my son David? And David said, <hi type="italic">It is</hi> my voice, my lord, O king.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:18
verses.text: And he said, Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil <hi type="italic">is</hi> in mine hand?

verses.name: I Samuel 26:19
verses.text: Now therefore, I pray thee, let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the Lord have stirred thee up against me, let him accept an offering: but if <hi type="italic">they be</hi> the children of men, cursed <hi type="italic">be</hi> they before the Lord; for they have driven me out this day from abiding in the inheritance of the Lord, saying, Go, serve other gods.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:20
verses.text: Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the Lord: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:21
verses.text: ¶ Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David: for I will no more do thee harm, because my soul was precious in thine eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:22
verses.text: And David answered and said, Behold the king’s spear! and let one of the young men come over and fetch it.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:23
verses.text: The Lord render to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness: for the Lord delivered thee into <hi type="italic">my</hi> hand to day, but I would not stretch forth mine hand against the Lord’s anointed.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:24
verses.text: And, behold, as thy life was much set by this day in mine eyes, so let my life be much set by in the eyes of the Lord, and let him deliver me out of all tribulation.

verses.name: I Samuel 26:25
verses.text: Then Saul said to David, Blessed <hi type="italic">be</hi> thou, my son David: thou shalt both do great <hi type="italic">things</hi>, and also shalt still prevail. So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.  <chapter eID="1Sam.26"/><div eID="gen272" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 27:1
verses.text: AND David said in his heart, I shall now perish one day by the hand of Saul: <hi type="italic">there is</hi> nothing better for me than that I should speedily escape into the land of the Philistines; and Saul shall despair of me, to seek me any more in any coast of Israel: so shall I escape out of his hand.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:2
verses.text: And David arose, and he passed over with the six hundred men that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him unto Achish, the son of Maoch, king of Gath.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:3
verses.text: And David dwelt with Achish at Gath, he and his men, every man with his household, <hi type="italic">even</hi> David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal’s wife.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:4
verses.text: And it was told Saul that David was fled to Gath: and he sought no more again for him.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:5
verses.text: ¶ And David said unto Achish, If I have now found grace in thine eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country, that I may dwell there: for why should thy servant dwell in the royal city with thee?

verses.name: I Samuel 27:6
verses.text: Then Achish gave him Ziklag that day: wherefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:7
verses.text: And the time that David dwelt in the country of the Philistines was a full year and four months.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:8
verses.text: ¶ And David and his men went up, and invaded the Geshurites, and the Gezrites, and the Amalekites: for those <hi type="italic">nations were</hi> of old the inhabitants of the land, as thou goest to Shur, even unto the land of Egypt.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:9
verses.text: And David smote the land, and left neither man nor woman alive, and took away the sheep, and the oxen, and the asses, and the camels, and the apparel, and returned, and came to Achish.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:10
verses.text: And Achish said, Whither have ye made a road to day? And David said, Against the south of Judah, and against the south of the Jerahmeelites, and against the south of the Kenites.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:11
verses.text: And David saved neither man nor woman alive, to bring <hi type="italic">tidings</hi> to Gath, saying, Lest they should tell on us, saying, So did David, and so <hi type="italic">will be</hi> his manner all the while he dwelleth in the country of the Philistines.

verses.name: I Samuel 27:12
verses.text: And Achish believed David, saying, He hath made his people Israel utterly to abhor him; therefore he shall be my servant for ever.  <chapter eID="1Sam.27"/><div eID="gen273" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 28:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass in those days, that the Philistines gathered their armies together for warfare, to fight with Israel. And Achish said unto David, Know thou assuredly, that thou shalt go out with me to battle, thou and thy men.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:2
verses.text: And David said to Achish, Surely thou shalt know what thy servant can do. And Achish said to David, Therefore will I make thee keeper of mine head for ever.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:3
verses.text: ¶ Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had lamented him, and buried him in Ramah, even in his own city. And Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:4
verses.text: And the Philistines gathered themselves together, and came and pitched in Shunem: and Saul gathered all Israel together, and they pitched in Gilboa.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:5
verses.text: And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:6
verses.text: And when Saul inquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:7
verses.text: ¶ Then said Saul unto his servants, Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and inquire of her. And his servants said to him, Behold, <hi type="italic">there is</hi> a woman that hath a familiar spirit at En-dor.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:8
verses.text: And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and he went, and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night: and he said, I pray thee, divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me <hi type="italic">him</hi> up, whom I shall name unto thee.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:9
verses.text: And the woman said unto him, Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?

verses.name: I Samuel 28:10
verses.text: And Saul sware to her by the Lord, saying, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord liveth, there shall no punishment happen to thee for this thing.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:11
verses.text: Then said the woman, Whom shall I bring up unto thee? And he said, Bring me up Samuel.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:12
verses.text: And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried with a loud voice: and the woman spake to Saul, saying, Why hast thou deceived me? for thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> Saul.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:13
verses.text: And the king said unto her, Be not afraid: for what sawest thou? And the woman said unto Saul, I saw gods ascending out of the earth.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:14
verses.text: And he said unto her, What form <hi type="italic">is</hi> he of? And she said, An old man cometh up; and he <hi type="italic">is</hi> covered with a mantle. And Saul perceived that it <hi type="italic">was</hi> Samuel, and he stooped with <hi type="italic">his</hi> face to the ground, and bowed himself.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:15
verses.text: ¶ And Samuel said to Saul, Why hast thou disquieted me, to bring me up? And Saul answered, I am sore distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God is departed from me, and answereth me no more, neither by prophets, nor by dreams: therefore I have called thee, that thou mayest make known unto me what I shall do.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:16
verses.text: Then said Samuel, Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy?

verses.name: I Samuel 28:17
verses.text: And the Lord hath done to him, as he spake by me: for the Lord hath rent the kingdom out of thine hand, and given it to thy neighbour, <hi type="italic">even</hi> to David:

verses.name: I Samuel 28:18
verses.text: Because thou obeyedst not the voice of the Lord, nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore hath the Lord done this thing unto thee this day.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:19
verses.text: Moreover the Lord will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow <hi type="italic">shalt</hi> thou and thy sons <hi type="italic">be</hi> with me: the Lord also shall deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:20
verses.text: Then Saul fell straightway all along on the earth, and was sore afraid, because of the words of Samuel: and there was no strength in him; for he had eaten no bread all the day, nor all the night.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:21
verses.text: ¶ And the woman came unto Saul, and saw that he was sore troubled, and said unto him, Behold, thine handmaid hath obeyed thy voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have hearkened unto thy words which thou spakest unto me.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:22
verses.text: Now therefore, I pray thee, hearken thou also unto the voice of thine handmaid, and let me set a morsel of bread before thee; and eat, that thou mayest have strength, when thou goest on thy way.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:23
verses.text: But he refused, and said, I will not eat. But his servants, together with the woman, compelled him; and he hearkened unto their voice. So he arose from the earth, and sat upon the bed.

verses.name: I Samuel 28:24
verses.text: And the woman had a fat calf in the house; and she hasted, and killed it, and took flour, and kneaded <hi type="italic">it</hi>, and did bake unleavened bread thereof:

verses.name: I Samuel 28:25
verses.text: And she brought <hi type="italic">it</hi> before Saul, and before his servants; and they did eat. Then they rose up, and went away that night.  <chapter eID="1Sam.28"/><div eID="gen274" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 29:1
verses.text: NOW the Philistines gathered together all their armies to Aphek: and the Israelites pitched by a fountain which <hi type="italic">is</hi> in Jezreel.

verses.name: I Samuel 29:2
verses.text: And the lords of the Philistines passed on by hundreds, and by thousands: but David and his men passed on in the rereward with Achish.

verses.name: I Samuel 29:3
verses.text: Then said the princes of the Philistines, What <hi type="italic">do</hi> these Hebrews <hi type="italic">here?</hi> And Achish said unto the princes of the Philistines, <hi type="italic">Is</hi> not this David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, which hath been with me these days, or these years, and I have found no fault in him since he fell <hi type="italic">unto me</hi> unto this day?

verses.name: I Samuel 29:4
verses.text: And the princes of the Philistines were wroth with him; and the princes of the Philistines said unto him, Make this fellow return, that he may go again to his place which thou hast appointed him, and let him not go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he be an adversary to us: for wherewith should he reconcile himself unto his master? <hi type="italic">should it</hi> not <hi type="italic">be</hi> with the heads of these men?

verses.name: I Samuel 29:5
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is</hi> not this David, of whom they sang one to another in dances, saying, Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands?

verses.name: I Samuel 29:6
verses.text: ¶ Then Achish called David, and said unto him, Surely, <hi type="italic">as</hi> the Lord liveth, thou hast been upright, and thy going out and thy coming in with me in the host <hi type="italic">is</hi> good in my sight: for I have not found evil in thee since the day of thy coming unto me unto this day: nevertheless the lords favour thee not.

verses.name: I Samuel 29:7
verses.text: Wherefore now return, and go in peace, that thou displease not the lords of the Philistines.

verses.name: I Samuel 29:8
verses.text: ¶ And David said unto Achish, But what have I done? and what hast thou found in thy servant so long as I have been with thee unto this day, that I may not go fight against the enemies of my lord the king?

verses.name: I Samuel 29:9
verses.text: And Achish answered and said to David, I know that thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> good in my sight, as an angel of God: notwithstanding the princes of the Philistines have said, He shall not go up with us to the battle.

verses.name: I Samuel 29:10
verses.text: Wherefore now rise up early in the morning with thy master’s servants that are come with thee: and as soon as ye be up early in the morning, and have light, depart.

verses.name: I Samuel 29:11
verses.text: So David and his men rose up early to depart in the morning, to return into the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.  <chapter eID="1Sam.29"/><div eID="gen275" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 30:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass, when David and his men were come to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had invaded the south, and Ziklag, and smitten Ziklag, and burned it with fire;

verses.name: I Samuel 30:2
verses.text: And had taken the women captives, that <hi type="italic">were</hi> therein: they slew not any, either great or small, but carried <hi type="italic">them</hi> away, and went on their way.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:3
verses.text: ¶ So David and his men came to the city, and, behold, <hi type="italic">it was</hi> burned with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, were taken captives.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:4
verses.text: Then David and the people that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him lifted up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:5
verses.text: And David’s two wives were taken captives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:6
verses.text: And David was greatly distressed; for the people spake of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters: but David encouraged himself in the Lord his God.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:7
verses.text: And David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech’s son, I pray thee, bring me hither the ephod. And Abiathar brought thither the ephod to David.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:8
verses.text: And David inquired at the Lord, saying, Shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? And he answered him, Pursue: for thou shalt surely overtake <hi type="italic">them</hi>, and without fail recover <hi type="italic">all</hi>.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:9
verses.text: So David went, he and the six hundred men that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left behind stayed.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:10
verses.text: But David pursued, he and four hundred men: for two hundred abode behind, which were so faint that they could not go over the brook Besor.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:11
verses.text: ¶ And they found an Egyptian in the field, and brought him to David, and gave him bread, and he did eat; and they made him drink water;

verses.name: I Samuel 30:12
verses.text: And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins: and when he had eaten, his spirit came again to him: for he had eaten no bread, nor drunk <hi type="italic">any</hi> water, three days and three nights.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:13
verses.text: And David said unto him, To whom <hi type="italic">belongest</hi> thou? and whence <hi type="italic">art</hi> thou? And he said, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite; and my master left me, because three days agone I fell sick.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:14
verses.text: We made an invasion <hi type="italic">upon</hi> the south of the Cherethites, and upon <hi type="italic">the coast</hi> which <hi type="italic">belongeth</hi> to Judah, and upon the south of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:15
verses.text: And David said to him, Canst thou bring me down to this company? And he said, Swear unto me by God, that thou wilt neither kill me, nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring thee down to this company.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:16
verses.text: ¶ And when he had brought him down, behold, <hi type="italic">they were</hi> spread abroad upon all the earth, eating and drinking, and dancing, because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:17
verses.text: And David smote them from the twilight even unto the evening of the next day: and there escaped not a man of them, save four hundred young men, which rode upon camels, and fled.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:18
verses.text: And David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away: and David rescued his two wives.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:19
verses.text: And there was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil, nor any <hi type="italic">thing</hi> that they had taken to them: David recovered all.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:20
verses.text: And David took all the flocks and the herds, <hi type="italic">which</hi> they drave before those <hi type="italic">other</hi> cattle, and said, This <hi type="italic">is</hi> David’s spoil.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:21
verses.text: ¶ And David came to the two hundred men, which were so faint that they could not follow David, whom they had made also to abide at the brook Besor: and they went forth to meet David, and to meet the people that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him: and when David came near to the people, he saluted them.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:22
verses.text: Then answered all the wicked men and <hi type="italic">men</hi> of Belial, of those that went with David, and said, Because they went not with us, we will not give them <hi type="italic">ought</hi> of the spoil that we have recovered, save to every man his wife and his children, that they may lead <hi type="italic">them</hi> away, and depart.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:23
verses.text: Then said David, Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the Lord hath given us, who hath preserved us, and delivered the company that came against us into our hand.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:24
verses.text: For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part <hi type="italic">is</hi> that goeth down to the battle, so <hi type="italic">shall</hi> his part <hi type="italic">be</hi> that tarrieth by the stuff: they shall part alike.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:25
verses.text: And it was <hi type="italic">so</hi> from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel unto this day.

verses.name: I Samuel 30:26
verses.text: ¶ And when David came to Ziklag, he sent of the spoil unto the elders of Judah, <hi type="italic">even</hi> to his friends, saying, Behold a present for you of the spoil of the enemies of the Lord;

verses.name: I Samuel 30:27
verses.text: To <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Beth-el, and to <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in south Ramoth, and to <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Jattir,

verses.name: I Samuel 30:28
verses.text: And to <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Aroer, and to <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Siphmoth, and to <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Eshtemoa,

verses.name: I Samuel 30:29
verses.text: And to <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Rachal, and to <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in the cities of the Kenites,

verses.name: I Samuel 30:30
verses.text: And to <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Hormah, and to <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Chor-ashan, and to <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Athach,

verses.name: I Samuel 30:31
verses.text: And to <hi type="italic">them</hi> which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men were wont to haunt.  <chapter eID="1Sam.30"/><div eID="gen276" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Samuel 31:1
verses.text: NOW the Philistines fought against Israel: and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:2
verses.text: And the Philistines followed hard upon Saul and upon his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, Saul’s sons.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:3
verses.text: And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him; and he was sore wounded of the archers.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:4
verses.text: Then said Saul unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:5
verses.text: And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword, and died with him.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:6
verses.text: So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:7
verses.text: ¶ And when the men of Israel that <hi type="italic">were</hi> on the other side of the valley, and <hi type="italic">they</hi> that <hi type="italic">were</hi> on the other side Jordan, saw that the men of Israel fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, they forsook the cities, and fled; and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:8
verses.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen in mount Gilboa.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:9
verses.text: And they cut off his head, and stripped off his armour, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to publish <hi type="italic">it in</hi> the house of their idols, and among the people.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:10
verses.text: And they put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth: and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:11
verses.text: ¶ And when the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard of that which the Philistines had done to Saul;

verses.name: I Samuel 31:12
verses.text: All the valiant men arose, and went all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan, and came to Jabesh, and burnt them there.

verses.name: I Samuel 31:13
verses.text: And they took their bones, and buried <hi type="italic">them</hi> under a tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days.  <chapter eID="1Sam.31"/><div eID="gen277" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen246" osisID="1Sam" type="book"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 1:1
verses.text: NOW it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag;

verses.name: II Samuel 1:2
verses.text: It came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and <hi type="italic">so</hi> it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:3
verses.text: And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:4
verses.text: And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:5
verses.text: And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son be dead?

verses.name: II Samuel 1:6
verses.text: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:7
verses.text: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here <hi type="italic">am</hi> I.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:8
verses.text: And he said unto me, Who <hi type="italic">art</hi> thou? And I answered him, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> an Amalekite.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:9
verses.text: He said unto me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life <hi type="italic">is</hi> yet whole in me.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:10
verses.text: So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that <hi type="italic">was</hi> upon his head, and the bracelet that <hi type="italic">was</hi> on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:11
verses.text: Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him:

verses.name: II Samuel 1:12
verses.text: And they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the Lord, and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:13
verses.text: ¶ And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence <hi type="italic">art</hi> thou? And he answered, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:14
verses.text: And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the Lord’s anointed?

verses.name: II Samuel 1:15
verses.text: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, <hi type="italic">and</hi> fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:16
verses.text: And David said unto him, Thy blood <hi type="italic">be</hi> upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain the Lord’s anointed.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:17
verses.text: ¶ And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son:

verses.name: II Samuel 1:18
verses.text: (Also he bade them teach the children of Judah <hi type="italic">the use of</hi> the bow: behold, <hi type="italic">it is</hi> written in the book of Jasher.)

verses.name: II Samuel 1:19
verses.text: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!

verses.name: II Samuel 1:20
verses.text: Tell <hi type="italic">it</hi> not in Gath, publish <hi type="italic">it</hi> not in the streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:21
verses.text: Ye mountains of Gilboa, <hi type="italic">let there be</hi> no dew, neither <hi type="italic">let there be</hi> rain, upon you, nor fields of offerings: for there the shield of the mighty is vilely cast away, the shield of Saul, <hi type="italic">as though he had</hi> not <hi type="italic">been</hi> anointed with oil.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:22
verses.text: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not empty.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:23
verses.text: Saul and Jonathan <hi type="italic">were</hi> lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:24
verses.text: Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet, with <hi type="italic">other</hi> delights, who put on ornaments of gold upon your apparel.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:25
verses.text: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, <hi type="italic">thou wast</hi> slain in thine high places.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:26
verses.text: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.

verses.name: II Samuel 1:27
verses.text: How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!  <chapter eID="2Sam.1"/><div eID="gen279" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 2:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass after this, that David inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And the Lord said unto him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? And he said, Unto Hebron.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:2
verses.text: So David went up thither, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail Nabal’s wife the Carmelite.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:3
verses.text: And his men that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him did David bring up, every man with his household: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:4
verses.text: And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, <hi type="italic">That</hi> the men of Jabesh-gilead <hi type="italic">were they</hi> that buried Saul.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:5
verses.text: ¶ And David sent messengers unto the men of Jabesh-gilead, and said unto them, Blessed <hi type="italic">be</hi> ye of the Lord, that ye have shewed this kindness unto your lord, <hi type="italic">even</hi> unto Saul, and have buried him.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:6
verses.text: And now the Lord shew kindness and truth unto you: and I also will requite you this kindness, because ye have done this thing.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:7
verses.text: Therefore now let your hands be strengthened, and be ye valiant: for your master Saul is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:8
verses.text: ¶ But Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul’s host, took Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;

verses.name: II Samuel 2:9
verses.text: And made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:10
verses.text: Ish-bosheth Saul’s son <hi type="italic">was</hi> forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:11
verses.text: And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:12
verses.text: ¶ And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:13
verses.text: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out, and met together by the pool of Gibeon: and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:14
verses.text: And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men now arise, and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:15
verses.text: Then there arose and went over by number twelve of Benjamin, which <hi type="italic">pertained</hi> to Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:16
verses.text: And they caught every one his fellow by the head, and <hi type="italic">thrust</hi> his sword in his fellow’s side; so they fell down together: wherefore that place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> in Gibeon.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:17
verses.text: And there was a very sore battle that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:18
verses.text: ¶ And there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel <hi type="italic">was as</hi> light of foot as a wild roe.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:19
verses.text: And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:20
verses.text: Then Abner looked behind him, and said, <hi type="italic">Art</hi> thou Asahel? And he answered, I <hi type="italic">am</hi>.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:21
verses.text: And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take thee his armour. But Asahel would not turn aside from following of him.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:22
verses.text: And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from following me: wherefore should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?

verses.name: II Samuel 2:23
verses.text: Howbeit he refused to turn aside: wherefore Abner with the hinder end of the spear smote him under the fifth <hi type="italic">rib</hi>, that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, <hi type="italic">that</hi> as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:24
verses.text: Joab also and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun went down when they were come to the hill of Ammah, that <hi type="italic">lieth</hi> before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:25
verses.text: ¶ And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one troop, and stood on the top of an hill.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:26
verses.text: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter end? how long shall it be then, ere thou bid the people return from following their brethren?

verses.name: II Samuel 2:27
verses.text: And Joab said, <hi type="italic">As</hi> God liveth, unless thou hadst spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone up every one from following his brother.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:28
verses.text: So Joab blew a trumpet, and all the people stood still, and pursued after Israel no more, neither fought they any more.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:29
verses.text: And Abner and his men walked all that night through the plain, and passed over Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and they came to Mahanaim.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:30
verses.text: And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had gathered all the people together, there lacked of David’s servants nineteen men and Asahel.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:31
verses.text: But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner’s men, <hi type="italic">so that</hi> three hundred and threescore men died.

verses.name: II Samuel 2:32
verses.text: ¶ And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulchre of his father, which <hi type="italic">was in</hi> Beth-lehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and they came to Hebron at break of day.  <chapter eID="2Sam.2"/><div eID="gen280" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 3:1
verses.text: NOW there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David: but David waxed stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul waxed weaker and weaker.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:2
verses.text: ¶ And unto David were sons born in Hebron: and his firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;

verses.name: II Samuel 3:3
verses.text: And his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;

verses.name: II Samuel 3:4
verses.text: And the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;

verses.name: II Samuel 3:5
verses.text: And the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:6
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:7
verses.text: And Saul had a concubine, whose name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and <hi type="italic">Ish</hi>-<hi type="italic">bosheth</hi> said to Abner, Wherefore hast thou gone in unto my father’s concubine?

verses.name: II Samuel 3:8
verses.text: Then was Abner very wroth for the words of Ish-bosheth, and said, <hi type="italic">Am</hi> I a dog’s head, which against Judah do shew kindness this day unto the house of Saul thy father, to his brethren, and to his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David, that thou chargest me to day with a fault concerning this woman?

verses.name: II Samuel 3:9
verses.text: So do God to Abner, and more also, except, as the Lord hath sworn to David, even so I do to him;

verses.name: II Samuel 3:10
verses.text: To translate the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beer-sheba.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:11
verses.text: And he could not answer Abner a word again, because he feared him.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:12
verses.text: ¶ And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose <hi type="italic">is</hi> the land? saying <hi type="italic">also</hi>, Make thy league with me, and, behold, my hand <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> with thee, to bring about all Israel unto thee.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:13
verses.text: ¶ And he said, Well; I will make a league with thee: but one thing I require of thee, that is, Thou shalt not see my face, except thou first bring Michal Saul’s daughter, when thou comest to see my face.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:14
verses.text: And David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth Saul’s son, saying, Deliver <hi type="italic">me</hi> my wife Michal, which I espoused to me for an hundred foreskins of the Philistines.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:15
verses.text: And Ish-bosheth sent, and took her from <hi type="italic">her</hi> husband, <hi type="italic">even</hi> from Phaltiel the son of Laish.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:16
verses.text: And her husband went with her along weeping behind her to Bahurim. Then said Abner unto him, Go, return. And he returned.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:17
verses.text: ¶ And Abner had communication with the elders of Israel, saying, Ye sought for David in times past <hi type="italic">to be</hi> king over you:

verses.name: II Samuel 3:18
verses.text: Now then do <hi type="italic">it:</hi> for the Lord hath spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:19
verses.text: And Abner also spake in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and that seemed good to the whole house of Benjamin.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:20
verses.text: So Abner came to David to Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made Abner and the men that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him a feast.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:21
verses.text: And Abner said unto David, I will arise and go, and will gather all Israel unto my lord the king, that they may make a league with thee, and that thou mayest reign over all that thine heart desireth. And David sent Abner away; and he went in peace.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:22
verses.text: ¶ And, behold, the servants of David and Joab came from <hi type="italic">pursuing</hi> a troop, and brought in a great spoil with them: but Abner <hi type="italic">was</hi> not with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he was gone in peace.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:23
verses.text: When Joab and all the host that <hi type="italic">was</hi> with him were come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he hath sent him away, and he is gone in peace.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:24
verses.text: Then Joab came to the king, and said, What hast thou done? behold, Abner came unto thee; why <hi type="italic">is</hi> it <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou hast sent him away, and he is quite gone?

verses.name: II Samuel 3:25
verses.text: Thou knowest Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive thee, and to know thy going out and thy coming in, and to know all that thou doest.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:26
verses.text: And when Joab was come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, which brought him again from the well of Sirah: but David knew <hi type="italic">it</hi> not.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:27
verses.text: And when Abner was returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside in the gate to speak with him quietly, and smote him there under the fifth <hi type="italic">rib</hi>, that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:28
verses.text: ¶ And afterward when David heard <hi type="italic">it</hi>, he said, I and my kingdom <hi type="italic">are</hi> guiltless before the Lord for ever from the blood of Abner the son of Ner:

verses.name: II Samuel 3:29
verses.text: Let it rest on the head of Joab, and on all his father’s house; and let there not fail from the house of Joab one that hath an issue, or that is a leper, or that leaneth on a staff, or that falleth on the sword, or that lacketh bread.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:30
verses.text: So Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner, because he had slain their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:31
verses.text: ¶ And David said to Joab, and to all the people that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him, Rend your clothes, and gird you with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David <hi type="italic">himself</hi> followed the bier.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:32
verses.text: And they buried Abner in Hebron: and the king lifted up his voice, and wept at the grave of Abner; and all the people wept.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:33
verses.text: And the king lamented over Abner, and said, Died Abner as a fool dieth?

verses.name: II Samuel 3:34
verses.text: Thy hands <hi type="italic">were</hi> not bound, nor thy feet put into fetters: as a man falleth before wicked men, <hi type="italic">so</hi> fellest thou. And all the people wept again over him.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:35
verses.text: And when all the people came to cause David to eat meat while it was yet day, David sware, saying, So do God to me, and more also, if I taste bread, or ought else, till the sun be down.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:36
verses.text: And all the people took notice <hi type="italic">of it</hi>, and it pleased them: as whatsoever the king did pleased all the people.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:37
verses.text: For all the people and all Israel understood that day that it was not of the king to slay Abner the son of Ner.

verses.name: II Samuel 3:38
verses.text: And the king said unto his servants, Know ye not that there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel?

verses.name: II Samuel 3:39
verses.text: And I <hi type="italic">am</hi> this day weak, though anointed king; and these men the sons of Zeruiah <hi type="italic">be</hi> too hard for me: the Lord shall reward the doer of evil according to his wickedness.  <chapter eID="2Sam.3"/><div eID="gen281" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 4:1
verses.text: AND when Saul’s son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.

verses.name: II Samuel 4:2
verses.text: And Saul’s son had two men <hi type="italic">that were</hi> captains of bands: the name of the one <hi type="italic">was</hi> Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin: (for Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin:

verses.name: II Samuel 4:3
verses.text: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and were sojourners there until this day.)

verses.name: II Samuel 4:4
verses.text: And Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son <hi type="italic">that was</hi> lame of <hi type="italic">his</hi> feet. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Mephibosheth.

verses.name: II Samuel 4:5
verses.text: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, who lay on a bed at noon.

verses.name: II Samuel 4:6
verses.text: And they came thither into the midst of the house, <hi type="italic">as though</hi> they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him under the fifth <hi type="italic">rib:</hi> and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

verses.name: II Samuel 4:7
verses.text: For when they came into the house, he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, and they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and gat them away through the plain all night.

verses.name: II Samuel 4:8
verses.text: And they brought the head of Ish-bosheth unto David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold the head of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul thine enemy, which sought thy life; and the Lord hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.

verses.name: II Samuel 4:9
verses.text: ¶ And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,

verses.name: II Samuel 4:10
verses.text: When one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, who <hi type="italic">thought</hi> that I would have given him a reward for his tidings:

verses.name: II Samuel 4:11
verses.text: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?

verses.name: II Samuel 4:12
verses.text: And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged <hi type="italic">them</hi> up over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth, and buried <hi type="italic">it</hi> in the sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.  <chapter eID="2Sam.4"/><div eID="gen282" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 5:1
verses.text: THEN came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, we <hi type="italic">are</hi> thy bone and thy flesh.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:2
verses.text: Also in time past, when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and the Lord said to thee, Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:3
verses.text: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and king David made a league with them in Hebron before the Lord: and they anointed David king over Israel.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:4
verses.text: ¶ David <hi type="italic">was</hi> thirty years old when he began to reign, <hi type="italic">and</hi> he reigned forty years.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:5
verses.text: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:6
verses.text: ¶ And the king and his men went to Jerusalem unto the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land: which spake unto David, saying, Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither: thinking, David cannot come in hither.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:7
verses.text: Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion: the same <hi type="italic">is</hi> the city of David.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:8
verses.text: And David said on that day, Whosoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind, <hi type="italic">that are</hi> hated of David’s soul, <hi type="italic">he shall be chief and captain</hi>. Wherefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:9
verses.text: So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David. And David built round about from Millo and inward.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:10
verses.text: And David went on, and grew great, and the Lord God of hosts <hi type="italic">was</hi> with him.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:11
verses.text: ¶ And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, and carpenters, and masons: and they built David an house.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:12
verses.text: And David perceived that the Lord had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel’s sake.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:13
verses.text: ¶ And David took <hi type="italic">him</hi> more concubines and wives out of Jerusalem, after he was come from Hebron: and there were yet sons and daughters born to David.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:14
verses.text: And these <hi type="italic">be</hi> the names of those that were born unto him in Jerusalem; Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,

verses.name: II Samuel 5:15
verses.text: Ibhar also, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,

verses.name: II Samuel 5:16
verses.text: And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:17
verses.text: ¶ But when the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines came up to seek David; and David heard <hi type="italic">of it</hi>, and went down to the hold.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:18
verses.text: The Philistines also came and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:19
verses.text: And David inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go up to the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into mine hand? And the Lord said unto David, Go up: for I will doubtless deliver the Philistines into thine hand.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:20
verses.text: And David came to Baal-perazim, and David smote them there, and said, The Lord hath broken forth upon mine enemies before me, as the breach of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baal-perazim.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:21
verses.text: And there they left their images, and David and his men burned them.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:22
verses.text: ¶ And the Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:23
verses.text: And when David inquired of the Lord, he said, Thou shalt not go up; <hi type="italic">but</hi> fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:24
verses.text: And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the Lord go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.

verses.name: II Samuel 5:25
verses.text: And David did so, as the Lord had commanded him; and smote the Philistines from Geba until thou come to Gazer.  <chapter eID="2Sam.5"/><div eID="gen283" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 6:1
verses.text: AGAIN, David gathered together all <hi type="italic">the</hi> chosen <hi type="italic">men</hi> of Israel, thirty thousand.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:2
verses.text: And David arose, and went with all the people that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him from Baale of Judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the Lord of hosts that dwelleth <hi type="italic">between</hi> the cherubims.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:3
verses.text: And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that <hi type="italic">was</hi> in Gibeah: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drave the new cart.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:4
verses.text: And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab which <hi type="italic">was</hi> at Gibeah, accompanying the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:5
verses.text: And David and all the house of Israel played before the Lord on all manner of <hi type="italic">instruments made of</hi> fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets, and on cymbals.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:6
verses.text: ¶ And when they came to Nachon’s threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth <hi type="italic">his hand</hi> to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:7
verses.text: And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for <hi type="italic">his</hi> error; and there he died by the ark of God.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:8
verses.text: And David was displeased, because the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah: and he called the name of the place Perez-uzzah to this day.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:9
verses.text: And David was afraid of the Lord that day, and said, How shall the ark of the Lord come to me?

verses.name: II Samuel 6:10
verses.text: So David would not remove the ark of the Lord unto him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:11
verses.text: And the ark of the Lord continued in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months: and the Lord blessed Obed-edom, and all his household.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:12
verses.text: ¶ And it was told king David, saying, The Lord hath blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that <hi type="italic">pertaineth</hi> unto him, because of the ark of God. So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the city of David with gladness.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:13
verses.text: And it was <hi type="italic">so</hi>, that when they that bare the ark of the Lord had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:14
verses.text: And David danced before the Lord with all <hi type="italic">his</hi> might; and David <hi type="italic">was</hi> girded with a linen ephod.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:15
verses.text: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the Lord with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:16
verses.text: And as the ark of the Lord came into the city of David, Michal Saul’s daughter looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the Lord; and she despised him in her heart.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:17
verses.text: ¶ And they brought in the ark of the Lord, and set it in his place, in the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it: and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Lord.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:18
verses.text: And as soon as David had made an end of offering burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:19
verses.text: And he dealt among all the people, <hi type="italic">even</hi> among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece <hi type="italic">of flesh</hi>, and a flagon <hi type="italic">of wine</hi>. So all the people departed every one to his house.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:20
verses.text: ¶ Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, How glorious was the king of Israel to day, who uncovered himself to day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!

verses.name: II Samuel 6:21
verses.text: And David said unto Michal, <hi type="italic">It was</hi> before the Lord, which chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the Lord, over Israel: therefore will I play before the Lord.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:22
verses.text: And I will yet be more vile than thus, and will be base in mine own sight: and of the maidservants which thou hast spoken of, of them shall I be had in honour.

verses.name: II Samuel 6:23
verses.text: Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.  <chapter eID="2Sam.6"/><div eID="gen284" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 7:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass, when the king sat in his house, and the Lord had given him rest round about from all his enemies;

verses.name: II Samuel 7:2
verses.text: That the king said unto Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in an house of cedar, but the ark of God dwelleth within curtains.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:3
verses.text: And Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in thine heart; for the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> with thee.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:4
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass that night, that the word of the Lord came unto Nathan, saying,

verses.name: II Samuel 7:5
verses.text: Go and tell my servant David, Thus saith the Lord, Shalt thou build me an house for me to dwell in?

verses.name: II Samuel 7:6
verses.text: Whereas I have not dwelt in <hi type="italic">any</hi> house since the time that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:7
verses.text: In all <hi type="italic">the places</hi> wherein I have walked with all the children of Israel spake I a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, Why build ye not me an house of cedar?

verses.name: II Samuel 7:8
verses.text: Now therefore so shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith the Lord of hosts, I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel:

verses.name: II Samuel 7:9
verses.text: And I was with thee whithersoever thou wentest, and have cut off all thine enemies out of thy sight, and have made thee a great name, like unto the name of the great <hi type="italic">men</hi> that <hi type="italic">are</hi> in the earth.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:10
verses.text: Moreover I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in a place of their own, and move no more; neither shall the children of wickedness afflict them any more, as beforetime,

verses.name: II Samuel 7:11
verses.text: And as since the time that I commanded judges <hi type="italic">to be</hi> over my people Israel, and have caused thee to rest from all thine enemies. Also the Lord telleth thee that he will make thee an house.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:12
verses.text: ¶ And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:13
verses.text: He shall build an house for my name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:14
verses.text: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men:

verses.name: II Samuel 7:15
verses.text: But my mercy shall not depart away from him, as I took <hi type="italic">it</hi> from Saul, whom I put away before thee.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:16
verses.text: And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:17
verses.text: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak unto David.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:18
verses.text: ¶ Then went king David in, and sat before the Lord, and he said, Who <hi type="italic">am</hi> I, O Lord God? and what <hi type="italic">is</hi> my house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?

verses.name: II Samuel 7:19
verses.text: And this was yet a small thing in thy sight, O Lord God; but thou hast spoken also of thy servant’s house for a great while to come. And <hi type="italic">is</hi> this the manner of man, O Lord God?

verses.name: II Samuel 7:20
verses.text: And what can David say more unto thee? for thou, Lord God, knowest thy servant.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:21
verses.text: For thy word’s sake, and according to thine own heart, hast thou done all these great things, to make thy servant know <hi type="italic">them</hi>.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:22
verses.text: Wherefore thou art great, O Lord God: for <hi type="italic">there is</hi> none like thee, neither <hi type="italic">is there any</hi> God beside thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:23
verses.text: And what one nation in the earth <hi type="italic">is</hi> like thy people, <hi type="italic">even</hi> like Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to himself, and to make him a name, and to do for you great things and terrible, for thy land, before thy people, which thou redeemedst to thee from Egypt, <hi type="italic">from</hi> the nations and their gods?

verses.name: II Samuel 7:24
verses.text: For thou hast confirmed to thyself thy people Israel <hi type="italic">to be</hi> a people unto thee for ever: and thou, Lord, art become their God.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:25
verses.text: And now, O Lord God, the word that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant, and concerning his house, establish <hi type="italic">it</hi> for ever, and do as thou hast said.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:26
verses.text: And let thy name be magnified for ever, saying, The Lord of hosts <hi type="italic">is</hi> the God over Israel: and let the house of thy servant David be established before thee.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:27
verses.text: For thou, O Lord of hosts, God of Israel, hast revealed to thy servant, saying, I will build thee an house: therefore hath thy servant found in his heart to pray this prayer unto thee.

verses.name: II Samuel 7:28
verses.text: And now, O Lord God, thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> that God, and thy words be true, and thou hast promised this goodness unto thy servant:

verses.name: II Samuel 7:29
verses.text: Therefore now let it please thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue for ever before thee: for thou, O Lord God, hast spoken <hi type="italic">it:</hi> and with thy blessing let the house of thy servant be blessed for ever.  <chapter eID="2Sam.7"/><div eID="gen285" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 8:1
verses.text: AND after this it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them: and David took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:2
verses.text: And he smote Moab, and measured them with a line, casting them down to the ground; even with two lines measured he to put to death, and with one full line to keep alive. And <hi type="italic">so</hi> the Moabites became David’s servants, <hi type="italic">and</hi> brought gifts.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:3
verses.text: ¶ David smote also Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:4
verses.text: And David took from him a thousand <hi type="italic">chariots</hi>, and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: and David houghed all the chariot <hi type="italic">horses</hi>, but reserved of them <hi type="italic">for</hi> an hundred chariots.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:5
verses.text: And when the Syrians of Damascus came to succour Hadadezer king of Zobah, David slew of the Syrians two and twenty thousand men.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:6
verses.text: Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus: and the Syrians became servants to David, <hi type="italic">and</hi> brought gifts. And the Lord preserved David whithersoever he went.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:7
verses.text: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:8
verses.text: And from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took exceeding much brass.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:9
verses.text: ¶ When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer,

verses.name: II Samuel 8:10
verses.text: Then Toi sent Joram his son unto king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer, and smitten him: for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. And <hi type="italic">Joram</hi> brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:

verses.name: II Samuel 8:11
verses.text: Which also king David did dedicate unto the Lord, with the silver and gold that he had dedicated of all nations which he subdued;

verses.name: II Samuel 8:12
verses.text: Of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:13
verses.text: And David gat <hi type="italic">him</hi> a name when he returned from smiting of the Syrians in the valley of salt, <hi type="italic">being</hi> eighteen thousand <hi type="italic">men</hi>.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:14
verses.text: ¶ And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom put he garrisons, and all they of Edom became David’s servants. And the Lord preserved David whithersoever he went.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:15
verses.text: And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed judgment and justice unto all his people.

verses.name: II Samuel 8:16
verses.text: And Joab the son of Zeruiah <hi type="italic">was</hi> over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud <hi type="italic">was</hi> recorder;

verses.name: II Samuel 8:17
verses.text: And Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, <hi type="italic">were</hi> the priests; and Seraiah <hi type="italic">was</hi> the scribe;

verses.name: II Samuel 8:18
verses.text: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada <hi type="italic">was over</hi> both the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons were chief rulers.  <chapter eID="2Sam.8"/><div eID="gen286" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 9:1
verses.text: AND David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?

verses.name: II Samuel 9:2
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">there was</hi> of the house of Saul a servant whose name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Ziba. And when they had called him unto David, the king said unto him, <hi type="italic">Art</hi> thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant <hi type="italic">is he</hi>.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:3
verses.text: And the king said, <hi type="italic">Is</hi> there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may shew the kindness of God unto him? And Ziba said unto the king, Jonathan hath yet a son, <hi type="italic">which is</hi> lame on <hi type="italic">his</hi> feet.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:4
verses.text: And the king said unto him, Where <hi type="italic">is</hi> he? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:5
verses.text: ¶ Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:6
verses.text: Now when Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, was come unto David, he fell on his face, and did reverence. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold thy servant!

verses.name: II Samuel 9:7
verses.text: ¶ And David said unto him, Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father’s sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:8
verses.text: And he bowed himself, and said, What <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy servant, that thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I <hi type="italic">am?</hi>

verses.name: II Samuel 9:9
verses.text: ¶ Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said unto him, I have given unto thy master’s son all that pertained to Saul and to all his house.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:10
verses.text: Thou therefore, and thy sons, and thy servants, shall till the land for him, and thou shalt bring in <hi type="italic">the fruits</hi>, that thy master’s son may have food to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master’s son shall eat bread alway at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:11
verses.text: Then said Ziba unto the king, According to all that my lord the king hath commanded his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth, <hi type="italic">said the king</hi>, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king’s sons.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:12
verses.text: And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Micha. And all that dwelt in the house of Ziba <hi type="italic">were</hi> servants unto Mephibosheth.

verses.name: II Samuel 9:13
verses.text: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king’s table; and was lame on both his feet.  <chapter eID="2Sam.9"/><div eID="gen287" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Samuel 10:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:2
verses.text: Then said David, I will shew kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father shewed kindness unto me. And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants for his father. And David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:3
verses.text: And the princes of the children of Ammon said unto Hanun their lord, Thinkest thou that David doth honour thy father, that he hath sent comforters unto thee? hath not David <hi type="italic">rather</hi> sent his servants unto thee, to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?

verses.name: II Samuel 10:4
verses.text: Wherefore Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, <hi type="italic">even</hi> to their buttocks, and sent them away.

verses.name: II Samuel 10:5
