verses.text: THEN Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the children of Israel, unto king Solomon in Jerusalem, that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> Zion.

verses.name: I Kings 8:2
verses.text: And all the men of Israel assembled themselves unto king Solomon at the feast in the month Ethanim, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> the seventh month.

verses.name: I Kings 8:3
verses.text: And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark.

verses.name: I Kings 8:4
verses.text: And they brought up the ark of the Lord, and the tabernacle of the congregation, and all the holy vessels that <hi type="italic">were</hi> in the tabernacle, even those did the priests and the Levites bring up.

verses.name: I Kings 8:5
verses.text: And king Solomon, and all the congregation of Israel, that were assembled unto him, <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen, that could not be told nor numbered for multitude.

verses.name: I Kings 8:6
verses.text: And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the Lord unto his place, into the oracle of the house, to the most holy <hi type="italic">place</hi>, <hi type="italic">even</hi> under the wings of the cherubims.

verses.name: I Kings 8:7
verses.text: For the cherubims spread forth <hi type="italic">their</hi> two wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubims covered the ark and the staves thereof above.

verses.name: I Kings 8:8
verses.text: And they drew out the staves, that the ends of the staves were seen out in the holy <hi type="italic">place</hi> before the oracle, and they were not seen without: and there they are unto this day.

verses.name: I Kings 8:9
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There was</hi> nothing in the ark save the two tables of stone, which Moses put there at Horeb, when the Lord made <hi type="italic">a covenant</hi> with the children of Israel, when they came out of the land of Egypt.

verses.name: I Kings 8:10
verses.text: And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the holy <hi type="italic">place</hi>, that the cloud filled the house of the Lord,

verses.name: I Kings 8:11
verses.text: So that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud: for the glory of the Lord had filled the house of the Lord.

verses.name: I Kings 8:12
verses.text: ¶ Then spake Solomon, The Lord said that he would dwell in the thick darkness.

verses.name: I Kings 8:13
verses.text: I have surely built thee an house to dwell in, a settled place for thee to abide in for ever.

verses.name: I Kings 8:14
verses.text: And the king turned his face about, and blessed all the congregation of Israel: (and all the congregation of Israel stood;)

verses.name: I Kings 8:15
verses.text: And he said, Blessed <hi type="italic">be</hi> the Lord God of Israel, which spake with his mouth unto David my father, and hath with his hand fulfilled <hi type="italic">it</hi>, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 8:16
verses.text: Since the day that I brought forth my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build an house, that my name might be therein; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 8:17
verses.text: And it was in the heart of David my father to build an house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 8:18
verses.text: And the Lord said unto David my father, Whereas it was in thine heart to build an house unto my name, thou didst well that it was in thine heart.

verses.name: I Kings 8:19
verses.text: Nevertheless thou shalt not build the house; but thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house unto my name.

verses.name: I Kings 8:20
verses.text: And the Lord hath performed his word that he spake, and I am risen up in the room of David my father, and sit on the throne of Israel, as the Lord promised, and have built an house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 8:21
verses.text: And I have set there a place for the ark, wherein <hi type="italic">is</hi> the covenant of the Lord, which he made with our fathers, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.

verses.name: I Kings 8:22
verses.text: ¶ And Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord in the presence of all the congregation of Israel, and spread forth his hands toward heaven:

verses.name: I Kings 8:23
verses.text: And he said, Lord God of Israel, <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no God like thee, in heaven above, or on earth beneath, who keepest covenant and mercy with thy servants that walk before thee with all their heart:

verses.name: I Kings 8:24
verses.text: Who hast kept with thy servant David my father that thou promisedst him: thou spakest also with thy mouth, and hast fulfilled <hi type="italic">it</hi> with thine hand, as <hi type="italic">it is</hi> this day.

verses.name: I Kings 8:25
verses.text: Therefore now, Lord God of Israel, keep with thy servant David my father that thou promisedst him, saying, There shall not fail thee a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel; so that thy children take heed to their way, that they walk before me as thou hast walked before me.

verses.name: I Kings 8:26
verses.text: And now, O God of Israel, let thy word, I pray thee, be verified, which thou spakest unto thy servant David my father.

verses.name: I Kings 8:27
verses.text: But will God indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?

verses.name: I Kings 8:28
verses.text: Yet have thou respect unto the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplication, O Lord my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer, which thy servant prayeth before thee to day:

verses.name: I Kings 8:29
verses.text: That thine eyes may be open toward this house night and day, <hi type="italic">even</hi> toward the place of which thou hast said, My name shall be there: that thou mayest hearken unto the prayer which thy servant shall make toward this place.

verses.name: I Kings 8:30
verses.text: And hearken thou to the supplication of thy servant, and of thy people Israel, when they shall pray toward this place: and hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place: and when thou hearest, forgive.

verses.name: I Kings 8:31
verses.text: ¶ If any man trespass against his neighbour, and an oath be laid upon him to cause him to swear, and the oath come before thine altar in this house:

verses.name: I Kings 8:32
verses.text: Then hear thou in heaven, and do, and judge thy servants, condemning the wicked, to bring his way upon his head; and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.

verses.name: I Kings 8:33
verses.text: ¶ When thy people Israel be smitten down before the enemy, because they have sinned against thee, and shall turn again to thee, and confess thy name, and pray, and make supplication unto thee in this house:

verses.name: I Kings 8:34
verses.text: Then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy people Israel, and bring them again unto the land which thou gavest unto their fathers.

verses.name: I Kings 8:35
verses.text: ¶ When heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against thee; if they pray toward this place, and confess thy name, and turn from their sin, when thou afflictest them:

verses.name: I Kings 8:36
verses.text: Then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy servants, and of thy people Israel, that thou teach them the good way wherein they should walk, and give rain upon thy land, which thou hast given to thy people for an inheritance.

verses.name: I Kings 8:37
verses.text: ¶ If there be in the land famine, if there be pestilence, blasting, mildew, locust, <hi type="italic">or</hi> if there be caterpiller; if their enemy besiege them in the land of their cities; whatsoever plague, whatsoever sickness <hi type="italic">there be;</hi>

verses.name: I Kings 8:38
verses.text: What prayer and supplication soever be <hi type="italic">made</hi> by any man, <hi type="italic">or</hi> by all thy people Israel, which shall know every man the plague of his own heart, and spread forth his hands toward this house:

verses.name: I Kings 8:39
verses.text: Then hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place, and forgive, and do, and give to every man according to his ways, whose heart thou knowest; (for thou, <hi type="italic">even</hi> thou only, knowest the hearts of all the children of men;)

verses.name: I Kings 8:40
verses.text: That they may fear thee all the days that they live in the land which thou gavest unto our fathers.

verses.name: I Kings 8:41
verses.text: Moreover concerning a stranger, that <hi type="italic">is</hi> not of thy people Israel, but cometh out of a far country for thy name’s sake;

verses.name: I Kings 8:42
verses.text: (For they shall hear of thy great name, and of thy strong hand, and of thy stretched out arm;) when he shall come and pray toward this house;

verses.name: I Kings 8:43
verses.text: Hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place, and do according to all that the stranger calleth to thee for: that all people of the earth may know thy name, to fear thee, as <hi type="italic">do</hi> thy people Israel; and that they may know that this house, which I have builded, is called by thy name.

verses.name: I Kings 8:44
verses.text: ¶ If thy people go out to battle against their enemy, whithersoever thou shalt send them, and shall pray unto the Lord toward the city which thou hast chosen, and <hi type="italic">toward</hi> the house that I have built for thy name:

verses.name: I Kings 8:45
verses.text: Then hear thou in heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.

verses.name: I Kings 8:46
verses.text: If they sin against thee, (for <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near;

verses.name: I Kings 8:47
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Yet</hi> if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness;

verses.name: I Kings 8:48
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">so</hi> return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies, which led them away captive, and pray unto thee toward their land, which thou gavest unto their fathers, the city which thou hast chosen, and the house which I have built for thy name:

verses.name: I Kings 8:49
verses.text: Then hear thou their prayer and their supplication in heaven thy dwelling place, and maintain their cause,

verses.name: I Kings 8:50
verses.text: And forgive thy people that have sinned against thee, and all their transgressions wherein they have transgressed against thee, and give them compassion before them who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them:

verses.name: I Kings 8:51
verses.text: For they <hi type="italic">be</hi> thy people, and thine inheritance, which thou broughtest forth out of Egypt, from the midst of the furnace of iron:

verses.name: I Kings 8:52
verses.text: That thine eyes may be open unto the supplication of thy servant, and unto the supplication of thy people Israel, to hearken unto them in all that they call for unto thee.

verses.name: I Kings 8:53
verses.text: For thou didst separate them from among all the people of the earth, <hi type="italic">to be</hi> thine inheritance, as thou spakest by the hand of Moses thy servant, when thou broughtest our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord God.

verses.name: I Kings 8:54
verses.text: And it was <hi type="italic">so</hi>, that when Solomon had made an end of praying all this prayer and supplication unto the Lord, he arose from before the altar of the Lord, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread up to heaven.

verses.name: I Kings 8:55
verses.text: And he stood, and blessed all the congregation of Israel with a loud voice, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 8:56
verses.text: Blessed <hi type="italic">be</hi> the Lord, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.

verses.name: I Kings 8:57
verses.text: The Lord our God be with us, as he was with our fathers: let him not leave us, nor forsake us:

verses.name: I Kings 8:58
verses.text: That he may incline our hearts unto him, to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and his statutes, and his judgments, which he commanded our fathers.

verses.name: I Kings 8:59
verses.text: And let these my words, wherewith I have made supplication before the Lord, be nigh unto the Lord our God day and night, that he maintain the cause of his servant, and the cause of his people Israel at all times, as the matter shall require:

verses.name: I Kings 8:60
verses.text: That all the people of the earth may know that the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> God, <hi type="italic">and that there is</hi> none else.

verses.name: I Kings 8:61
verses.text: Let your heart therefore be perfect with the Lord our God, to walk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments, as at this day.

verses.name: I Kings 8:62
verses.text: ¶ And the king, and all Israel with him, offered sacrifice before the Lord.

verses.name: I Kings 8:63
verses.text: And Solomon offered a sacrifice of peace offerings, which he offered unto the Lord, two and twenty thousand oxen, and an hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Israel dedicated the house of the Lord.

verses.name: I Kings 8:64
verses.text: The same day did the king hallow the middle of the court that <hi type="italic">was</hi> before the house of the Lord: for there he offered burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings: because the brasen altar that <hi type="italic">was</hi> before the Lord <hi type="italic">was</hi> too little to receive the burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings.

verses.name: I Kings 8:65
verses.text: And at that time Solomon held a feast, and all Israel with him, a great congregation, from the entering in of Hamath unto the river of Egypt, before the Lord our God, seven days and seven days, <hi type="italic">even</hi> fourteen days.

verses.name: I Kings 8:66
verses.text: On the eighth day he sent the people away: and they blessed the king, and went unto their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness that the Lord had done for David his servant, and for Israel his people.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.8"/><div eID="gen311" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 9:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass, when Solomon had finished the building of the house of the Lord, and the king’s house, and all Solomon’s desire which he was pleased to do,

verses.name: I Kings 9:2
verses.text: That the Lord appeared to Solomon the second time, as he had appeared unto him at Gibeon.

verses.name: I Kings 9:3
verses.text: And the Lord said unto him, I have heard thy prayer and thy supplication, that thou hast made before me: I have hallowed this house, which thou hast built, to put my name there for ever; and mine eyes and mine heart shall be there perpetually.

verses.name: I Kings 9:4
verses.text: And if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked, in integrity of heart, and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded thee, <hi type="italic">and</hi> wilt keep my statutes and my judgments:

verses.name: I Kings 9:5
verses.text: Then I will establish the throne of thy kingdom upon Israel for ever, as I promised to David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man upon the throne of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 9:6
verses.text: <hi type="italic">But</hi> if ye shall at all turn from following me, ye or your children, and will not keep my commandments <hi type="italic">and</hi> my statutes which I have set before you, but go and serve other gods, and worship them:

verses.name: I Kings 9:7
verses.text: Then will I cut off Israel out of the land which I have given them; and this house, which I have hallowed for my name, will I cast out of my sight; and Israel shall be a proverb and a byword among all people:

verses.name: I Kings 9:8
verses.text: And at this house, <hi type="italic">which</hi> is high, every one that passeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss; and they shall say, Why hath the Lord done thus unto this land, and to this house?

verses.name: I Kings 9:9
verses.text: And they shall answer, Because they forsook the Lord their God, who brought forth their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have taken hold upon other gods, and have worshipped them, and served them: therefore hath the Lord brought upon them all this evil.

verses.name: I Kings 9:10
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, when Solomon had built the two houses, the house of the Lord, and the king’s house,

verses.name: I Kings 9:11
verses.text: (<hi type="italic">Now</hi> Hiram the king of Tyre had furnished Solomon with cedar trees and fir trees, and with gold, according to all his desire,) that then king Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.

verses.name: I Kings 9:12
verses.text: And Hiram came out from Tyre to see the cities which Solomon had given him; and they pleased him not.

verses.name: I Kings 9:13
verses.text: And he said, What cities <hi type="italic">are</hi> these which thou hast given me, my brother? And he called them the land of Cabul unto this day.

verses.name: I Kings 9:14
verses.text: And Hiram sent to the king sixscore talents of gold.

verses.name: I Kings 9:15
verses.text: ¶ And this <hi type="italic">is</hi> the reason of the levy which king Solomon raised; for to build the house of the Lord, and his own house, and Millo, and the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, and Megiddo, and Gezer.

verses.name: I Kings 9:16
verses.text: <hi type="italic">For</hi> Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up, and taken Gezer, and burnt it with fire, and slain the Canaanites that dwelt in the city, and given it <hi type="italic">for</hi> a present unto his daughter, Solomon’s wife.

verses.name: I Kings 9:17
verses.text: And Solomon built Gezer, and Beth-horon the nether,

verses.name: I Kings 9:18
verses.text: And Baalath, and Tadmor in the wilderness, in the land,

verses.name: I Kings 9:19
verses.text: And all the cities of store that Solomon had, and cities for his chariots, and cities for his horsemen, and that which Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.

verses.name: I Kings 9:20
verses.text: <hi type="italic">And</hi> all the people <hi type="italic">that were</hi> left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, which <hi type="italic">were</hi> not of the children of Israel,

verses.name: I Kings 9:21
verses.text: Their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel also were not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day.

verses.name: I Kings 9:22
verses.text: But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondmen: but they <hi type="italic">were</hi> men of war, and his servants, and his princes, and his captains, and rulers of his chariots, and his horsemen.

verses.name: I Kings 9:23
verses.text: These <hi type="italic">were</hi> the chief of the officers that <hi type="italic">were</hi> over Solomon’s work, five hundred and fifty, which bare rule over the people that wrought in the work.

verses.name: I Kings 9:24
verses.text: ¶ But Pharaoh’s daughter came up out of the city of David unto her house which <hi type="italic">Solomon</hi> had built for her: then did he build Millo.

verses.name: I Kings 9:25
verses.text: ¶ And three times in a year did Solomon offer burnt offerings and peace offerings upon the altar which he built unto the Lord, and he burnt incense upon the altar that <hi type="italic">was</hi> before the Lord. So he finished the house.

verses.name: I Kings 9:26
verses.text: ¶ And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion-geber, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea, in the land of Edom.

verses.name: I Kings 9:27
verses.text: And Hiram sent in the navy his servants, shipmen that had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.

verses.name: I Kings 9:28
verses.text: And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought <hi type="italic">it</hi> to king Solomon.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.9"/><div eID="gen312" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 10:1
verses.text: AND when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Lord, she came to prove him with hard questions.

verses.name: I Kings 10:2
verses.text: And she came to Jerusalem with a very great train, with camels that bare spices, and very much gold, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.

verses.name: I Kings 10:3
verses.text: And Solomon told her all her questions: there was not <hi type="italic">any</hi> thing hid from the king, which he told her not.

verses.name: I Kings 10:4
verses.text: And when the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon’s wisdom, and the house that he had built,

verses.name: I Kings 10:5
verses.text: And the meat of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel, and his cupbearers, and his ascent by which he went up unto the house of the Lord; there was no more spirit in her.

verses.name: I Kings 10:6
verses.text: And she said to the king, It was a true report that I heard in mine own land of thy acts and of thy wisdom.

verses.name: I Kings 10:7
verses.text: Howbeit I believed not the words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen <hi type="italic">it:</hi> and, behold, the half was not told me: thy wisdom and prosperity exceedeth the fame which I heard.

verses.name: I Kings 10:8
verses.text: Happy <hi type="italic">are</hi> thy men, happy <hi type="italic">are</hi> these thy servants, which stand continually before thee, <hi type="italic">and</hi> that hear thy wisdom.

verses.name: I Kings 10:9
verses.text: Blessed be the Lord thy God, which delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel: because the Lord loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king, to do judgment and justice.

verses.name: I Kings 10:10
verses.text: And she gave the king an hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices very great store, and precious stones: there came no more such abundance of spices as these which the queen of Sheba gave to king Solomon.

verses.name: I Kings 10:11
verses.text: And the navy also of Hiram, that brought gold from Ophir, brought in from Ophir great plenty of almug trees, and precious stones.

verses.name: I Kings 10:12
verses.text: And the king made of the almug trees pillars for the house of the Lord, and for the king’s house, harps also and psalteries for singers: there came no such almug trees, nor were seen unto this day.

verses.name: I Kings 10:13
verses.text: And king Solomon gave unto the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked, beside <hi type="italic">that</hi> which Solomon gave her of his royal bounty. So she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants.

verses.name: I Kings 10:14
verses.text: ¶ Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred threescore and six talents of gold,

verses.name: I Kings 10:15
verses.text: Beside <hi type="italic">that he had</hi> of the merchantmen, and of the traffick of the spice merchants, and of all the kings of Arabia, and of the governors of the country.

verses.name: I Kings 10:16
verses.text: ¶ And king Solomon made two hundred targets <hi type="italic">of</hi> beaten gold: six hundred <hi type="italic">shekels</hi> of gold went to one target.

verses.name: I Kings 10:17
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">he made</hi> three hundred shields <hi type="italic">of</hi> beaten gold; three pound of gold went to one shield: and the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.

verses.name: I Kings 10:18
verses.text: ¶ Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with the best gold.

verses.name: I Kings 10:19
verses.text: The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne <hi type="italic">was</hi> round behind: and <hi type="italic">there were</hi> stays on either side on the place of the seat, and two lions stood beside the stays.

verses.name: I Kings 10:20
verses.text: And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps: there was not the like made in any kingdom.

verses.name: I Kings 10:21
verses.text: ¶ And all king Solomon’s drinking vessels <hi type="italic">were of</hi> gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon <hi type="italic">were of</hi> pure gold; none <hi type="italic">were of</hi> silver: it was nothing accounted of in the days of Solomon.

verses.name: I Kings 10:22
verses.text: For the king had at sea a navy of Tharshish with the navy of Hiram: once in three years came the navy of Tharshish, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.

verses.name: I Kings 10:23
verses.text: So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and for wisdom.

verses.name: I Kings 10:24
verses.text: ¶ And all the earth sought to Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.

verses.name: I Kings 10:25
verses.text: And they brought every man his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and armour, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year.

verses.name: I Kings 10:26
verses.text: ¶ And Solomon gathered together chariots and horsemen: and he had a thousand and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he bestowed in the cities for chariots, and with the king at Jerusalem.

verses.name: I Kings 10:27
verses.text: And the king made silver <hi type="italic">to be</hi> in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars made he <hi type="italic">to be</hi> as the sycomore trees that <hi type="italic">are</hi> in the vale, for abundance.

verses.name: I Kings 10:28
verses.text: ¶ And Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king’s merchants received the linen yarn at a price.

verses.name: I Kings 10:29
verses.text: And a chariot came up and went out of Egypt for six hundred <hi type="italic">shekels</hi> of silver, and an horse for an hundred and fifty: and so for all the kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, did they bring <hi type="italic">them</hi> out by their means.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.10"/><div eID="gen313" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 11:1
verses.text: BUT king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, <hi type="italic">and</hi> Hittites;

verses.name: I Kings 11:2
verses.text: Of the nations <hi type="italic">concerning</hi> which the Lord said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: <hi type="italic">for</hi> surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon clave unto these in love.

verses.name: I Kings 11:3
verses.text: And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart.

verses.name: I Kings 11:4
verses.text: For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, <hi type="italic">that</hi> his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as <hi type="italic">was</hi> the heart of David his father.

verses.name: I Kings 11:5
verses.text: For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.

verses.name: I Kings 11:6
verses.text: And Solomon did evil in the sight of the Lord, and went not fully after the Lord, as <hi type="italic">did</hi> David his father.

verses.name: I Kings 11:7
verses.text: Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that <hi type="italic">is</hi> before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.

verses.name: I Kings 11:8
verses.text: And likewise did he for all his strange wives, which burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.

verses.name: I Kings 11:9
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel, which had appeared unto him twice,

verses.name: I Kings 11:10
verses.text: And had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods: but he kept not that which the Lord commanded.

verses.name: I Kings 11:11
verses.text: Wherefore the Lord said unto Solomon, Forasmuch as this is done of thee, and thou hast not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded thee, I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant.

verses.name: I Kings 11:12
verses.text: Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father’s sake: <hi type="italic">but</hi> I will rend it out of the hand of thy son.

verses.name: I Kings 11:13
verses.text: Howbeit I will not rend away all the kingdom; <hi type="italic">but</hi> will give one tribe to thy son for David my servant’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake which I have chosen.

verses.name: I Kings 11:14
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord stirred up an adversary unto Solomon, Hadad the Edomite: he <hi type="italic">was</hi> of the king’s seed in Edom.

verses.name: I Kings 11:15
verses.text: For it came to pass, when David was in Edom, and Joab the captain of the host was gone up to bury the slain, after he had smitten every male in Edom;

verses.name: I Kings 11:16
verses.text: (For six months did Joab remain there with all Israel, until he had cut off every male in Edom:)

verses.name: I Kings 11:17
verses.text: That Hadad fled, he and certain Edomites of his father’s servants with him, to go into Egypt; Hadad <hi type="italic">being</hi> yet a little child.

verses.name: I Kings 11:18
verses.text: And they arose out of Midian, and came to Paran: and they took men with them out of Paran, and they came to Egypt, unto Pharaoh king of Egypt; which gave him an house, and appointed him victuals, and gave him land.

verses.name: I Kings 11:19
verses.text: And Hadad found great favour in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him to wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.

verses.name: I Kings 11:20
verses.text: And the sister of Tahpenes bare him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh’s house: and Genubath was in Pharaoh’s household among the sons of Pharaoh.

verses.name: I Kings 11:21
verses.text: And when Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the host was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, Let me depart, that I may go to mine own country.

verses.name: I Kings 11:22
verses.text: Then Pharaoh said unto him, But what hast thou lacked with me, that, behold, thou seekest to go to thine own country? And he answered, Nothing: howbeit let me go in any wise.

verses.name: I Kings 11:23
verses.text: ¶ And God stirred him up <hi type="italic">another</hi> adversary, Rezon the son of Eliadah, which fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah:

verses.name: I Kings 11:24
verses.text: And he gathered men unto him, and became captain over a band, when David slew them <hi type="italic">of Zobah:</hi> and they went to Damascus, and dwelt therein, and reigned in Damascus.

verses.name: I Kings 11:25
verses.text: And he was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, beside the mischief that Hadad <hi type="italic">did:</hi> and he abhorred Israel, and reigned over Syria.

verses.name: I Kings 11:26
verses.text: ¶ And Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite of Zereda, Solomon’s servant, whose mother’s name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Zeruah, a widow woman, even he lifted up <hi type="italic">his</hi> hand against the king.

verses.name: I Kings 11:27
verses.text: And this <hi type="italic">was</hi> the cause that he lifted up <hi type="italic">his</hi> hand against the king: Solomon built Millo, <hi type="italic">and</hi> repaired the breaches of the city of David his father.

verses.name: I Kings 11:28
verses.text: And the man Jeroboam <hi type="italic">was</hi> a mighty man of valour: and Solomon seeing the young man that he was industrious, he made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph.

verses.name: I Kings 11:29
verses.text: And it came to pass at that time when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, that the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the way; and he had clad himself with a new garment; and they two <hi type="italic">were</hi> alone in the field:

verses.name: I Kings 11:30
verses.text: And Ahijah caught the new garment that <hi type="italic">was</hi> on him, and rent it <hi type="italic">in</hi> twelve pieces:

verses.name: I Kings 11:31
verses.text: And he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee:

verses.name: I Kings 11:32
verses.text: (But he shall have one tribe for my servant David’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel:)

verses.name: I Kings 11:33
verses.text: Because that they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in my ways, to do <hi type="italic">that which is</hi> right in mine eyes, and <hi type="italic">to keep</hi> my statutes and my judgments, as <hi type="italic">did</hi> David his father.

verses.name: I Kings 11:34
verses.text: Howbeit I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand: but I will make him prince all the days of his life for David my servant’s sake, whom I chose, because he kept my commandments and my statutes:

verses.name: I Kings 11:35
verses.text: But I will take the kingdom out of his son’s hand, and will give it unto thee, <hi type="italic">even</hi> ten tribes.

verses.name: I Kings 11:36
verses.text: And unto his son will I give one tribe, that David my servant may have a light alway before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen me to put my name there.

verses.name: I Kings 11:37
verses.text: And I will take thee, and thou shalt reign according to all that thy soul desireth, and shalt be king over Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 11:38
verses.text: And it shall be, if thou wilt hearken unto all that I command thee, and wilt walk in my ways, and do <hi type="italic">that is</hi> right in my sight, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did; that I will be with thee, and build thee a sure house, as I built for David, and will give Israel unto thee.

verses.name: I Kings 11:39
verses.text: And I will for this afflict the seed of David, but not for ever.

verses.name: I Kings 11:40
verses.text: Solomon sought therefore to kill Jeroboam. And Jeroboam arose, and fled into Egypt, unto Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.

verses.name: I Kings 11:41
verses.text: ¶ And the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?

verses.name: I Kings 11:42
verses.text: And the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel <hi type="italic">was</hi> forty years.

verses.name: I Kings 11:43
verses.text: And Solomon slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David his father: and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.11"/><div eID="gen314" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 12:1
verses.text: AND Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king.

verses.name: I Kings 12:2
verses.text: And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who was yet in Egypt, heard <hi type="italic">of it</hi>, (for he was fled from the presence of king Solomon, and Jeroboam dwelt in Egypt;)

verses.name: I Kings 12:3
verses.text: That they sent and called him. And Jeroboam and all the congregation of Israel came, and spake unto Rehoboam, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 12:4
verses.text: Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make thou the grievous service of thy father, and his heavy yoke which he put upon us, lighter, and we will serve thee.

verses.name: I Kings 12:5
verses.text: And he said unto them, Depart yet <hi type="italic">for</hi> three days, then come again to me. And the people departed.

verses.name: I Kings 12:6
verses.text: ¶ And king Rehoboam consulted with the old men, that stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, and said, How do ye advise that I may answer this people?

verses.name: I Kings 12:7
verses.text: And they spake unto him, saying, If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.

verses.name: I Kings 12:8
verses.text: But he forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him, <hi type="italic">and</hi> which stood before him:

verses.name: I Kings 12:9
verses.text: And he said unto them, What counsel give ye that we may answer this people, who have spoken to me, saying, Make the yoke which thy father did put upon us lighter?

verses.name: I Kings 12:10
verses.text: And the young men that were grown up with him spake unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou speak unto this people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou <hi type="italic">it</hi> lighter unto us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little <hi type="italic">finger</hi> shall be thicker than my father’s loins.

verses.name: I Kings 12:11
verses.text: And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.

verses.name: I Kings 12:12
verses.text: ¶ So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king had appointed, saying, Come to me again the third day.

verses.name: I Kings 12:13
verses.text: And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men’s counsel that they gave him;

verses.name: I Kings 12:14
verses.text: And spake to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke: my father <hi type="italic">also</hi> chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.

verses.name: I Kings 12:15
verses.text: Wherefore the king hearkened not unto the people; for the cause was from the Lord, that he might perform his saying, which the Lord spake by Ahijah the Shilonite unto Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

verses.name: I Kings 12:16
verses.text: ¶ So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither <hi type="italic">have we</hi> inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.

verses.name: I Kings 12:17
verses.text: But <hi type="italic">as for</hi> the children of Israel which dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.

verses.name: I Kings 12:18
verses.text: Then king Rehoboam sent Adoram, who <hi type="italic">was</hi> over the tribute; and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died. Therefore king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.

verses.name: I Kings 12:19
verses.text: So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

verses.name: I Kings 12:20
verses.text: And it came to pass, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam was come again, that they sent and called him unto the congregation, and made him king over all Israel: there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only.

verses.name: I Kings 12:21
verses.text: ¶ And when Rehoboam was come to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah, with the tribe of Benjamin, an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men, which were warriors, to fight against the house of Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.

verses.name: I Kings 12:22
verses.text: But the word of God came unto Shemaiah the man of God, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 12:23
verses.text: Speak unto Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and unto all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the remnant of the people, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 12:24
verses.text: Thus saith the Lord, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel: return every man to his house; for this thing is from me. They hearkened therefore to the word of the Lord, and returned to depart, according to the word of the Lord.

verses.name: I Kings 12:25
verses.text: ¶ Then Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim, and dwelt therein; and went out from thence, and built Penuel.

verses.name: I Kings 12:26
verses.text: And Jeroboam said in his heart, Now shall the kingdom return to the house of David:

verses.name: I Kings 12:27
verses.text: If this people go up to do sacrifice in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again unto their lord, <hi type="italic">even</hi> unto Rehoboam king of Judah, and they shall kill me, and go again to Rehoboam king of Judah.

verses.name: I Kings 12:28
verses.text: Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves <hi type="italic">of</hi> gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

verses.name: I Kings 12:29
verses.text: And he set the one in Beth-el, and the other put he in Dan.

verses.name: I Kings 12:30
verses.text: And this thing became a sin: for the people went <hi type="italic">to worship</hi> before the one, <hi type="italic">even</hi> unto Dan.

verses.name: I Kings 12:31
verses.text: And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.

verses.name: I Kings 12:32
verses.text: And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in Judah, and he offered upon the altar. So did he in Beth-el, sacrificing unto the calves that he had made: and he placed in Beth-el the priests of the high places which he had made.

verses.name: I Kings 12:33
verses.text: So he offered upon the altar which he had made in Beth-el the fifteenth day of the eighth month, <hi type="italic">even</hi> in the month which he had devised of his own heart; and ordained a feast unto the children of Israel: and he offered upon the altar, and burnt incense.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.12"/><div eID="gen315" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 13:1
verses.text: AND, behold, there came a man of God out of Judah by the word of the Lord unto Beth-el: and Jeroboam stood by the altar to burn incense.

verses.name: I Kings 13:2
verses.text: And he cried against the altar in the word of the Lord, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith the Lord; Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men’s bones shall be burnt upon thee.

verses.name: I Kings 13:3
verses.text: And he gave a sign the same day, saying, This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the sign which the Lord hath spoken; Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that <hi type="italic">are</hi> upon it shall be poured out.

verses.name: I Kings 13:4
verses.text: And it came to pass, when king Jeroboam heard the saying of the man of God, which had cried against the altar in Beth-el, that he put forth his hand from the altar, saying, Lay hold on him. And his hand, which he put forth against him, dried up, so that he could not pull it in again to him.

verses.name: I Kings 13:5
verses.text: The altar also was rent, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the Lord.

verses.name: I Kings 13:6
verses.text: And the king answered and said unto the man of God, Intreat now the face of the Lord thy God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored me again. And the man of God besought the Lord, and the king’s hand was restored him again, and became as <hi type="italic">it was</hi> before.

verses.name: I Kings 13:7
verses.text: And the king said unto the man of God, Come home with me, and refresh thyself, and I will give thee a reward.

verses.name: I Kings 13:8
verses.text: And the man of God said unto the king, If thou wilt give me half thine house, I will not go in with thee, neither will I eat bread nor drink water in this place:

verses.name: I Kings 13:9
verses.text: For so was it charged me by the word of the Lord, saying, Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor turn again by the same way that thou camest.

verses.name: I Kings 13:10
verses.text: So he went another way, and returned not by the way that he came to Beth-el.

verses.name: I Kings 13:11
verses.text: ¶ Now there dwelt an old prophet in Beth-el; and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Beth-el: the words which he had spoken unto the king, them they told also to their father.

verses.name: I Kings 13:12
verses.text: And their father said unto them, What way went he? For his sons had seen what way the man of God went, which came from Judah.

verses.name: I Kings 13:13
verses.text: And he said unto his sons, Saddle me the ass. So they saddled him the ass: and he rode thereon,

verses.name: I Kings 13:14
verses.text: And went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak: and he said unto him, <hi type="italic">Art</hi> thou the man of God that camest from Judah? And he said, I <hi type="italic">am</hi>.

verses.name: I Kings 13:15
verses.text: Then he said unto him, Come home with me, and eat bread.

verses.name: I Kings 13:16
verses.text: And he said, I may not return with thee, nor go in with thee: neither will I eat bread nor drink water with thee in this place:

verses.name: I Kings 13:17
verses.text: For it was said to me by the word of the Lord, Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest.

verses.name: I Kings 13:18
verses.text: He said unto him, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> a prophet also as thou <hi type="italic">art;</hi> and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. <hi type="italic">But</hi> he lied unto him.

verses.name: I Kings 13:19
verses.text: So he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.

verses.name: I Kings 13:20
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of the Lord came unto the prophet that brought him back:

verses.name: I Kings 13:21
verses.text: And he cried unto the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Forasmuch as thou hast disobeyed the mouth of the Lord, and hast not kept the commandment which the Lord thy God commanded thee,

verses.name: I Kings 13:22
verses.text: But camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk water in the place, of the which <hi type="italic">the L</hi><hi type="italic">ord</hi> did say to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no water; thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers.

verses.name: I Kings 13:23
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that he saddled for him the ass, <hi type="italic">to wit</hi>, for the prophet whom he had brought back.

verses.name: I Kings 13:24
verses.text: And when he was gone, a lion met him by the way, and slew him: and his carcase was cast in the way, and the ass stood by it, the lion also stood by the carcase.

verses.name: I Kings 13:25
verses.text: And, behold, men passed by, and saw the carcase cast in the way, and the lion standing by the carcase: and they came and told <hi type="italic">it</hi> in the city where the old prophet dwelt.

verses.name: I Kings 13:26
verses.text: And when the prophet that brought him back from the way heard <hi type="italic">thereof</hi>, he said, It <hi type="italic">is</hi> the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the Lord: therefore the Lord hath delivered him unto the lion, which hath torn him, and slain him, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake unto him.

verses.name: I Kings 13:27
verses.text: And he spake to his sons, saying, Saddle me the ass. And they saddled <hi type="italic">him</hi>.

verses.name: I Kings 13:28
verses.text: And he went and found his carcase cast in the way, and the ass and the lion standing by the carcase: the lion had not eaten the carcase, nor torn the ass.

verses.name: I Kings 13:29
verses.text: And the prophet took up the carcase of the man of God, and laid it upon the ass, and brought it back: and the old prophet came to the city, to mourn and to bury him.

verses.name: I Kings 13:30
verses.text: And he laid his carcase in his own grave; and they mourned over him, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, Alas, my brother!

verses.name: I Kings 13:31
verses.text: And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he spake to his sons, saying, When I am dead, then bury me in the sepulchre wherein the man of God <hi type="italic">is</hi> buried; lay my bones beside his bones:

verses.name: I Kings 13:32
verses.text: For the saying which he cried by the word of the Lord against the altar in Beth-el, and against all the houses of the high places which <hi type="italic">are</hi> in the cities of Samaria, shall surely come to pass.

verses.name: I Kings 13:33
verses.text: ¶ After this thing Jeroboam returned not from his evil way, but made again of the lowest of the people priests of the high places: whosoever would, he consecrated him, and he became <hi type="italic">one</hi> of the priests of the high places.

verses.name: I Kings 13:34
verses.text: And this thing became sin unto the house of Jeroboam, even to cut <hi type="italic">it</hi> off, and to destroy <hi type="italic">it</hi> from off the face of the earth.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.13"/><div eID="gen316" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 14:1
verses.text: AT that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.

verses.name: I Kings 14:2
verses.text: And Jeroboam said to his wife, Arise, I pray thee, and disguise thyself, that thou be not known to be the wife of Jeroboam; and get thee to Shiloh: behold, there <hi type="italic">is</hi> Ahijah the prophet, which told me that <hi type="italic">I should be</hi> king over this people.

verses.name: I Kings 14:3
verses.text: And take with thee ten loaves, and cracknels, and a cruse of honey, and go to him: he shall tell thee what shall become of the child.

verses.name: I Kings 14:4
verses.text: And Jeroboam’s wife did so, and arose, and went to Shiloh, and came to the house of Ahijah. But Ahijah could not see; for his eyes were set by reason of his age.

verses.name: I Kings 14:5
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord said unto Ahijah, Behold, the wife of Jeroboam cometh to ask a thing of thee for her son; for he <hi type="italic">is</hi> sick: thus and thus shalt thou say unto her: for it shall be, when she cometh in, that she shall feign herself <hi type="italic">to be</hi> another <hi type="italic">woman</hi>.

verses.name: I Kings 14:6
verses.text: And it was <hi type="italic">so</hi>, when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet, as she came in at the door, that he said, Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam; why feignest thou thyself <hi type="italic">to be</hi> another? for I <hi type="italic">am</hi> sent to thee <hi type="italic">with</hi> heavy <hi type="italic">tidings</hi>.

verses.name: I Kings 14:7
verses.text: Go, tell Jeroboam, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Forasmuch as I exalted thee from among the people, and made thee prince over my people Israel,

verses.name: I Kings 14:8
verses.text: And rent the kingdom away from the house of David, and gave it thee: and <hi type="italic">yet</hi> thou hast not been as my servant David, who kept my commandments, and who followed me with all his heart, to do <hi type="italic">that</hi> only <hi type="italic">which was</hi> right in mine eyes;

verses.name: I Kings 14:9
verses.text: But hast done evil above all that were before thee: for thou hast gone and made thee other gods, and molten images, to provoke me to anger, and hast cast me behind thy back:

verses.name: I Kings 14:10
verses.text: Therefore, behold, I will bring evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam him that pisseth against the wall, <hi type="italic">and</hi> him that is shut up and left in Israel, and will take away the remnant of the house of Jeroboam, as a man taketh away dung, till it be all gone.

verses.name: I Kings 14:11
verses.text: Him that dieth of Jeroboam in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth in the field shall the fowls of the air eat: for the Lord hath spoken <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: I Kings 14:12
verses.text: Arise thou therefore, get thee to thine own house: <hi type="italic">and</hi> when thy feet enter into the city, the child shall die.

verses.name: I Kings 14:13
verses.text: And all Israel shall mourn for him, and bury him: for he only of Jeroboam shall come to the grave, because in him there is found <hi type="italic">some</hi> good thing toward the Lord God of Israel in the house of Jeroboam.

verses.name: I Kings 14:14
verses.text: Moreover the Lord shall raise him up a king over Israel, who shall cut off the house of Jeroboam that day: but what? even now.

verses.name: I Kings 14:15
verses.text: For the Lord shall smite Israel, as a reed is shaken in the water, and he shall root up Israel out of this good land, which he gave to their fathers, and shall scatter them beyond the river, because they have made their groves, provoking the Lord to anger.

verses.name: I Kings 14:16
verses.text: And he shall give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, who did sin, and who made Israel to sin.

verses.name: I Kings 14:17
verses.text: ¶ And Jeroboam’s wife arose, and departed, and came to Tirzah: <hi type="italic">and</hi> when she came to the threshold of the door, the child died;

verses.name: I Kings 14:18
verses.text: And they buried him; and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by the hand of his servant Ahijah the prophet.

verses.name: I Kings 14:19
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred, and how he reigned, behold, they <hi type="italic">are</hi> written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 14:20
verses.text: And the days which Jeroboam reigned <hi type="italic">were</hi> two and twenty years: and he slept with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his stead.

verses.name: I Kings 14:21
verses.text: ¶ And Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam <hi type="italic">was</hi> forty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the Lord did choose out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. And his mother’s name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Naamah an Ammonitess.

verses.name: I Kings 14:22
verses.text: And Judah did evil in the sight of the Lord, and they provoked him to jealousy with their sins which they had committed, above all that their fathers had done.

verses.name: I Kings 14:23
verses.text: For they also built them high places, and images, and groves, on every high hill, and under every green tree.

verses.name: I Kings 14:24
verses.text: And there were also sodomites in the land: <hi type="italic">and</hi> they did according to all the abominations of the nations which the Lord cast out before the children of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 14:25
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass in the fifth year of king Rehoboam, <hi type="italic">that</hi> Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem:

verses.name: I Kings 14:26
verses.text: And he took away the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house; he even took away all: and he took away all the shields of gold which Solomon had made.

verses.name: I Kings 14:27
verses.text: And king Rehoboam made in their stead brasen shields, and committed <hi type="italic">them</hi> unto the hands of the chief of the guard, which kept the door of the king’s house.

verses.name: I Kings 14:28
verses.text: And it was <hi type="italic">so</hi>, when the king went into the house of the Lord, that the guard bare them, and brought them back into the guard chamber.

verses.name: I Kings 14:29
verses.text: ¶ Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: I Kings 14:30
verses.text: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all <hi type="italic">their</hi> days.

verses.name: I Kings 14:31
verses.text: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And his mother’s name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Naamah an Ammonitess. And Abijam his son reigned in his stead.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.14"/><div eID="gen317" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 15:1
verses.text: NOW in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam the son of Nebat reigned Abijam over Judah.

verses.name: I Kings 15:2
verses.text: Three years reigned he in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom.

verses.name: I Kings 15:3
verses.text: And he walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as the heart of David his father.

verses.name: I Kings 15:4
verses.text: Nevertheless for David’s sake did the Lord his God give him a lamp in Jerusalem, to set up his son after him, and to establish Jerusalem:

verses.name: I Kings 15:5
verses.text: Because David did <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> right in the eyes of the Lord, and turned not aside from any <hi type="italic">thing</hi> that he commanded him all the days of his life, save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

verses.name: I Kings 15:6
verses.text: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.

verses.name: I Kings 15:7
verses.text: Now the rest of the acts of Abijam, and all that he did, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

verses.name: I Kings 15:8
verses.text: And Abijam slept with his fathers; and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his stead.

verses.name: I Kings 15:9
verses.text: ¶ And in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel reigned Asa over Judah.

verses.name: I Kings 15:10
verses.text: And forty and one years reigned he in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom.

verses.name: I Kings 15:11
verses.text: And Asa did <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> right in the eyes of the Lord, as <hi type="italic">did</hi> David his father.

verses.name: I Kings 15:12
verses.text: And he took away the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.

verses.name: I Kings 15:13
verses.text: And also Maachah his mother, even her he removed from <hi type="italic">being</hi> queen, because she had made an idol in a grove; and Asa destroyed her idol, and burnt <hi type="italic">it</hi> by the brook Kidron.

verses.name: I Kings 15:14
verses.text: But the high places were not removed: nevertheless Asa’s heart was perfect with the Lord all his days.

verses.name: I Kings 15:15
verses.text: And he brought in the things which his father had dedicated, and the things which himself had dedicated, into the house of the Lord, silver, and gold, and vessels.

verses.name: I Kings 15:16
verses.text: ¶ And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

verses.name: I Kings 15:17
verses.text: And Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and built Ramah, that he might not suffer any to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

verses.name: I Kings 15:18
verses.text: Then Asa took all the silver and the gold <hi type="italic">that were</hi> left in the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house, and delivered them into the hand of his servants: and king Asa sent them to Ben-hadad, the son of Tabrimon, the son of Hezion, king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 15:19
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> a league between me and thee, <hi type="italic">and</hi> between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent unto thee a present of silver and gold; come and break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.

verses.name: I Kings 15:20
verses.text: So Ben-hadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of the hosts which he had against the cities of Israel, and smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abel-beth-maachah, and all Cinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali.

verses.name: I Kings 15:21
verses.text: And it came to pass, when Baasha heard <hi type="italic">thereof</hi>, that he left off building of Ramah, and dwelt in Tirzah.

verses.name: I Kings 15:22
verses.text: Then king Asa made a proclamation throughout all Judah; none <hi type="italic">was</hi> exempted: and they took away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha had builded; and king Asa built with them Geba of Benjamin, and Mizpah.

verses.name: I Kings 15:23
verses.text: The rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities which he built, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? Nevertheless in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.

verses.name: I Kings 15:24
verses.text: And Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father: and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead.

verses.name: I Kings 15:25
verses.text: ¶ And Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned over Israel two years.

verses.name: I Kings 15:26
verses.text: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of his father, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin.

verses.name: I Kings 15:27
verses.text: ¶ And Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him; and Baasha smote him at Gibbethon, which <hi type="italic">belonged</hi> to the Philistines; for Nadab and all Israel laid siege to Gibbethon.

verses.name: I Kings 15:28
verses.text: Even in the third year of Asa king of Judah did Baasha slay him, and reigned in his stead.

verses.name: I Kings 15:29
verses.text: And it came to pass, when he reigned, <hi type="italic">that</hi> he smote all the house of Jeroboam; he left not to Jeroboam any that breathed, until he had destroyed him, according unto the saying of the Lord, which he spake by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite:

verses.name: I Kings 15:30
verses.text: Because of the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned, and which he made Israel sin, by his provocation wherewith he provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger.

verses.name: I Kings 15:31
verses.text: ¶ Now the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: I Kings 15:32
verses.text: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

verses.name: I Kings 15:33
verses.text: In the third year of Asa king of Judah began Baasha the son of Ahijah to reign over all Israel in Tirzah, twenty and four years.

verses.name: I Kings 15:34
verses.text: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.15"/><div eID="gen318" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 16:1
verses.text: THEN the word of the Lord came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 16:2
verses.text: Forasmuch as I exalted thee out of the dust, and made thee prince over my people Israel; and thou hast walked in the way of Jeroboam, and hast made my people Israel to sin, to provoke me to anger with their sins;

verses.name: I Kings 16:3
verses.text: Behold, I will take away the posterity of Baasha, and the posterity of his house; and will make thy house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

verses.name: I Kings 16:4
verses.text: Him that dieth of Baasha in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth of his in the fields shall the fowls of the air eat.

verses.name: I Kings 16:5
verses.text: Now the rest of the acts of Baasha, and what he did, and his might, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: I Kings 16:6
verses.text: So Baasha slept with his fathers, and was buried in Tirzah: and Elah his son reigned in his stead.

verses.name: I Kings 16:7
verses.text: And also by the hand of the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani came the word of the Lord against Baasha, and against his house, even for all the evil that he did in the sight of the Lord, in provoking him to anger with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam; and because he killed him.

verses.name: I Kings 16:8
verses.text: ¶ In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, two years.

verses.name: I Kings 16:9
verses.text: And his servant Zimri, captain of half <hi type="italic">his</hi> chariots, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of <hi type="italic">his</hi> house in Tirzah.

verses.name: I Kings 16:10
verses.text: And Zimri went in and smote him, and killed him, in the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead.

verses.name: I Kings 16:11
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, <hi type="italic">that</hi> he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.

verses.name: I Kings 16:12
verses.text: Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,

verses.name: I Kings 16:13
verses.text: For all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned, and by which they made Israel to sin, in provoking the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.

verses.name: I Kings 16:14
verses.text: Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: I Kings 16:15
verses.text: ¶ In the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah did Zimri reign seven days in Tirzah. And the people <hi type="italic">were</hi> encamped against Gibbethon, which <hi type="italic">belonged</hi> to the Philistines.

verses.name: I Kings 16:16
verses.text: And the people <hi type="italic">that were</hi> encamped heard say, Zimri hath conspired, and hath also slain the king: wherefore all Israel made Omri, the captain of the host, king over Israel that day in the camp.

verses.name: I Kings 16:17
verses.text: And Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.

verses.name: I Kings 16:18
verses.text: And it came to pass, when Zimri saw that the city was taken, that he went into the palace of the king’s house, and burnt the king’s house over him with fire, and died,

verses.name: I Kings 16:19
verses.text: For his sins which he sinned in doing evil in the sight of the Lord, in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin which he did, to make Israel to sin.

verses.name: I Kings 16:20
verses.text: Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and his treason that he wrought, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: I Kings 16:21
verses.text: ¶ Then were the people of Israel divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king; and half followed Omri.

verses.name: I Kings 16:22
verses.text: But the people that followed Omri prevailed against the people that followed Tibni the son of Ginath: so Tibni died, and Omri reigned.

verses.name: I Kings 16:23
verses.text: ¶ In the thirty and first year of Asa king of Judah began Omri to reign over Israel, twelve years: six years reigned he in Tirzah.

verses.name: I Kings 16:24
verses.text: And he bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver, and built on the hill, and called the name of the city which he built, after the name of Shemer, owner of the hill, Samaria.

verses.name: I Kings 16:25
verses.text: ¶ But Omri wrought evil in the eyes of the Lord, and did worse than all that <hi type="italic">were</hi> before him.

verses.name: I Kings 16:26
verses.text: For he walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.

verses.name: I Kings 16:27
verses.text: Now the rest of the acts of Omri which he did, and his might that he shewed, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: I Kings 16:28
verses.text: So Omri slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria: and Ahab his son reigned in his stead.

verses.name: I Kings 16:29
verses.text: ¶ And in the thirty and eighth year of Asa king of Judah began Ahab the son of Omri to reign over Israel: and Ahab the son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty and two years.

verses.name: I Kings 16:30
verses.text: And Ahab the son of Omri did evil in the sight of the Lord above all that <hi type="italic">were</hi> before him.

verses.name: I Kings 16:31
verses.text: And it came to pass, as if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, that he took to wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him.

verses.name: I Kings 16:32
verses.text: And he reared up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal, which he had built in Samaria.

verses.name: I Kings 16:33
verses.text: And Ahab made a grove; and Ahab did more to provoke the Lord God of Israel to anger than all the kings of Israel that were before him.

verses.name: I Kings 16:34
verses.text: ¶ In his days did Hiel the Beth-elite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest <hi type="italic">son</hi> Segub, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.16"/><div eID="gen319" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 17:1
verses.text: AND Elijah the Tishbite, <hi type="italic">who was</hi> of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.

verses.name: I Kings 17:2
verses.text: And the word of the Lord came unto him, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 17:3
verses.text: Get thee hence, and turn thee eastward, and hide thyself by the brook Cherith, that <hi type="italic">is</hi> before Jordan.

verses.name: I Kings 17:4
verses.text: And it shall be, <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou shalt drink of the brook; and I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.

verses.name: I Kings 17:5
verses.text: So he went and did according unto the word of the Lord: for he went and dwelt by the brook Cherith, that <hi type="italic">is</hi> before Jordan.

verses.name: I Kings 17:6
verses.text: And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook.

verses.name: I Kings 17:7
verses.text: And it came to pass after a while, that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.

verses.name: I Kings 17:8
verses.text: ¶ And the word of the Lord came unto him, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 17:9
verses.text: Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which <hi type="italic">belongeth</hi> to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee.

verses.name: I Kings 17:10
verses.text: So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman <hi type="italic">was</hi> there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.

verses.name: I Kings 17:11
verses.text: And as she was going to fetch <hi type="italic">it</hi>, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thine hand.

verses.name: I Kings 17:12
verses.text: And she said, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.

verses.name: I Kings 17:13
verses.text: And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go <hi type="italic">and</hi> do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring <hi type="italic">it</hi> unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son.

verses.name: I Kings 17:14
verses.text: For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day <hi type="italic">that</hi> the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth.

verses.name: I Kings 17:15
verses.text: And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat <hi type="italic">many</hi> days.

verses.name: I Kings 17:16
verses.text: <hi type="italic">And</hi> the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Elijah.

verses.name: I Kings 17:17
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass after these things, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick; and his sickness was so sore, that there was no breath left in him.

verses.name: I Kings 17:18
verses.text: And she said unto Elijah, What have I to do with thee, O thou man of God? art thou come unto me to call my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son?

verses.name: I Kings 17:19
verses.text: And he said unto her, Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into a loft, where he abode, and laid him upon his own bed.

verses.name: I Kings 17:20
verses.text: And he cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, hast thou also brought evil upon the widow with whom I sojourn, by slaying her son?

verses.name: I Kings 17:21
verses.text: And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, I pray thee, let this child’s soul come into him again.

verses.name: I Kings 17:22
verses.text: And the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.

verses.name: I Kings 17:23
verses.text: And Elijah took the child, and brought him down out of the chamber into the house, and delivered him unto his mother: and Elijah said, See, thy son liveth.

verses.name: I Kings 17:24
verses.text: ¶ And the woman said to Elijah, Now by this I know that thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> a man of God, <hi type="italic">and</hi> that the word of the Lord in thy mouth <hi type="italic">is</hi> truth.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.17"/><div eID="gen320" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 18:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass <hi type="italic">after</hi> many days, that the word of the Lord came to Elijah in the third year, saying, Go, shew thyself unto Ahab; and I will send rain upon the earth.

verses.name: I Kings 18:2
verses.text: And Elijah went to shew himself unto Ahab. And <hi type="italic">there was</hi> a sore famine in Samaria.

verses.name: I Kings 18:3
verses.text: And Ahab called Obadiah, which <hi type="italic">was</hi> the governor of <hi type="italic">his</hi> house. (Now Obadiah feared the Lord greatly:

verses.name: I Kings 18:4
verses.text: For it was <hi type="italic">so</hi>, when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the Lord, that Obadiah took an hundred prophets, and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water.)

verses.name: I Kings 18:5
verses.text: And Ahab said unto Obadiah, Go into the land, unto all fountains of water, and unto all brooks: peradventure we may find grass to save the horses and mules alive, that we lose not all the beasts.

verses.name: I Kings 18:6
verses.text: So they divided the land between them to pass throughout it: Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.

verses.name: I Kings 18:7
verses.text: ¶ And as Obadiah was in the way, behold, Elijah met him: and he knew him, and fell on his face, and said, <hi type="italic">Art</hi> thou that my lord Elijah?

verses.name: I Kings 18:8
verses.text: And he answered him, I <hi type="italic">am:</hi> go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah <hi type="italic">is here</hi>.

verses.name: I Kings 18:9
verses.text: And he said, What have I sinned, that thou wouldest deliver thy servant into the hand of Ahab, to slay me?

verses.name: I Kings 18:10
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord thy God liveth, there is no nation or kingdom, whither my lord hath not sent to seek thee: and when they said, <hi type="italic">He is</hi> not <hi type="italic">there;</hi> he took an oath of the kingdom and nation, that they found thee not.

verses.name: I Kings 18:11
verses.text: And now thou sayest, Go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah <hi type="italic">is here</hi>.

verses.name: I Kings 18:12
verses.text: And it shall come to pass, <hi type="italic">as soon as</hi> I am gone from thee, that the Spirit of the Lord shall carry thee whither I know not; and <hi type="italic">so</hi> when I come and tell Ahab, and he cannot find thee, he shall slay me: but I thy servant fear the Lord from my youth.

verses.name: I Kings 18:13
verses.text: Was it not told my lord what I did when Jezebel slew the prophets of the Lord, how I hid an hundred men of the Lord’s prophets by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water?

verses.name: I Kings 18:14
verses.text: And now thou sayest, Go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah <hi type="italic">is here:</hi> and he shall slay me.

verses.name: I Kings 18:15
verses.text: And Elijah said, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord of hosts liveth, before whom I stand, I will surely shew myself unto him to day.

verses.name: I Kings 18:16
verses.text: So Obadiah went to meet Ahab, and told him: and Ahab went to meet Elijah.

verses.name: I Kings 18:17
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, <hi type="italic">Art</hi> thou he that troubleth Israel?

verses.name: I Kings 18:18
