verses.text: And he answered, I have not troubled Israel; but thou, and thy father’s house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the Lord, and thou hast followed Baalim.

verses.name: I Kings 18:19
verses.text: Now therefore send, <hi type="italic">and</hi> gather to me all Israel unto mount Carmel, and the prophets of Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the groves four hundred, which eat at Jezebel’s table.

verses.name: I Kings 18:20
verses.text: So Ahab sent unto all the children of Israel, and gathered the prophets together unto mount Carmel.

verses.name: I Kings 18:21
verses.text: And Elijah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if the Lord <hi type="italic">be</hi> God, follow him: but if Baal, <hi type="italic">then</hi> follow him. And the people answered him not a word.

verses.name: I Kings 18:22
verses.text: Then said Elijah unto the people, I, <hi type="italic">even</hi> I only, remain a prophet of the Lord; but Baal’s prophets <hi type="italic">are</hi> four hundred and fifty men.

verses.name: I Kings 18:23
verses.text: Let them therefore give us two bullocks; and let them choose one bullock for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and lay <hi type="italic">it</hi> on wood, and put no fire <hi type="italic">under:</hi> and I will dress the other bullock, and lay <hi type="italic">it</hi> on wood, and put no fire <hi type="italic">under:</hi>

verses.name: I Kings 18:24
verses.text: And call ye on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the Lord: and the God that answereth by fire, let him be God. And all the people answered and said, It is well spoken.

verses.name: I Kings 18:25
verses.text: And Elijah said unto the prophets of Baal, Choose you one bullock for yourselves, and dress <hi type="italic">it</hi> first; for ye <hi type="italic">are</hi> many; and call on the name of your gods, but put no fire <hi type="italic">under</hi>.

verses.name: I Kings 18:26
verses.text: And they took the bullock which was given them, and they dressed <hi type="italic">it</hi>, and called on the name of Baal from morning even until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us. But <hi type="italic">there was</hi> no voice, nor any that answered. And they leaped upon the altar which was made.

verses.name: I Kings 18:27
verses.text: And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud: for he <hi type="italic">is</hi> a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, <hi type="italic">or</hi> peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked.

verses.name: I Kings 18:28
verses.text: And they cried aloud, and cut themselves after their manner with knives and lancets, till the blood gushed out upon them.

verses.name: I Kings 18:29
verses.text: And it came to pass, when midday was past, and they prophesied until the <hi type="italic">time</hi> of the offering of the <hi type="italic">evening</hi> sacrifice, that <hi type="italic">there was</hi> neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded.

verses.name: I Kings 18:30
verses.text: And Elijah said unto all the people, Come near unto me. And all the people came near unto him. And he repaired the altar of the Lord <hi type="italic">that was</hi> broken down.

verses.name: I Kings 18:31
verses.text: And Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, unto whom the word of the Lord came, saying, Israel shall be thy name:

verses.name: I Kings 18:32
verses.text: And with the stones he built an altar in the name of the Lord: and he made a trench about the altar, as great as would contain two measures of seed.

verses.name: I Kings 18:33
verses.text: And he put the wood in order, and cut the bullock in pieces, and laid <hi type="italic">him</hi> on the wood, and said, Fill four barrels with water, and pour <hi type="italic">it</hi> on the burnt sacrifice, and on the wood.

verses.name: I Kings 18:34
verses.text: And he said, Do <hi type="italic">it</hi> the second time. And they did <hi type="italic">it</hi> the second time. And he said, Do <hi type="italic">it</hi> the third time. And they did <hi type="italic">it</hi> the third time.

verses.name: I Kings 18:35
verses.text: And the water ran round about the altar; and he filled the trench also with water.

verses.name: I Kings 18:36
verses.text: And it came to pass at <hi type="italic">the time of</hi> the offering of the <hi type="italic">evening</hi> sacrifice, that Elijah the prophet came near, and said, Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> God in Israel, and <hi type="italic">that</hi> I <hi type="italic">am</hi> thy servant, and <hi type="italic">that</hi> I have done all these things at thy word.

verses.name: I Kings 18:37
verses.text: Hear me, O Lord, hear me, that this people may know that thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> the Lord God, and <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou hast turned their heart back again.

verses.name: I Kings 18:38
verses.text: Then the fire of the Lord fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that <hi type="italic">was</hi> in the trench.

verses.name: I Kings 18:39
verses.text: And when all the people saw <hi type="italic">it</hi>, they fell on their faces: and they said, The Lord, he <hi type="italic">is</hi> the God; the Lord, he <hi type="italic">is</hi> the God.

verses.name: I Kings 18:40
verses.text: And Elijah said unto them, Take the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape. And they took them: and Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon, and slew them there.

verses.name: I Kings 18:41
verses.text: ¶ And Elijah said unto Ahab, Get thee up, eat and drink; for <hi type="italic">there is</hi> a sound of abundance of rain.

verses.name: I Kings 18:42
verses.text: So Ahab went up to eat and to drink. And Elijah went up to the top of Carmel; and he cast himself down upon the earth, and put his face between his knees,

verses.name: I Kings 18:43
verses.text: And said to his servant, Go up now, look toward the sea. And he went up, and looked, and said, <hi type="italic">There is</hi> nothing. And he said, Go again seven times.

verses.name: I Kings 18:44
verses.text: And it came to pass at the seventh time, that he said, Behold, there ariseth a little cloud out of the sea, like a man’s hand. And he said, Go up, say unto Ahab, Prepare <hi type="italic">thy chariot</hi>, and get thee down, that the rain stop thee not.

verses.name: I Kings 18:45
verses.text: And it came to pass in the mean while, that the heaven was black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. And Ahab rode, and went to Jezreel.

verses.name: I Kings 18:46
verses.text: And the hand of the Lord was on Elijah; and he girded up his loins, and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.18"/><div eID="gen321" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 19:1
verses.text: AND Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and withal how he had slain all the prophets with the sword.

verses.name: I Kings 19:2
verses.text: Then Jezebel sent a messenger unto Elijah, saying, So let the gods do <hi type="italic">to me</hi>, and more also, if I make not thy life as the life of one of them by to morrow about this time.

verses.name: I Kings 19:3
verses.text: And when he saw <hi type="italic">that</hi>, he arose, and went for his life, and came to Beer-sheba, which <hi type="italic">belongeth</hi> to Judah, and left his servant there.

verses.name: I Kings 19:4
verses.text: ¶ But he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a juniper tree: and he requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O Lord, take away my life; for I <hi type="italic">am</hi> not better than my fathers.

verses.name: I Kings 19:5
verses.text: And as he lay and slept under a juniper tree, behold, then an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise <hi type="italic">and</hi> eat.

verses.name: I Kings 19:6
verses.text: And he looked, and, behold, <hi type="italic">there was</hi> a cake baken on the coals, and a cruse of water at his head. And he did eat and drink, and laid him down again.

verses.name: I Kings 19:7
verses.text: And the angel of the Lord came again the second time, and touched him, and said, Arise <hi type="italic">and</hi> eat; because the journey <hi type="italic">is</hi> too great for thee.

verses.name: I Kings 19:8
verses.text: And he arose, and did eat and drink, and went in the strength of that meat forty days and forty nights unto Horeb the mount of God.

verses.name: I Kings 19:9
verses.text: ¶ And he came thither unto a cave, and lodged there; and, behold, the word of the Lord <hi type="italic">came</hi> to him, and he said unto him, What doest thou here, Elijah?

verses.name: I Kings 19:10
verses.text: And he said, I have been very jealous for the Lord God of hosts: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, <hi type="italic">even</hi> I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.

verses.name: I Kings 19:11
verses.text: And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the Lord; <hi type="italic">but</hi> the Lord <hi type="italic">was</hi> not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; <hi type="italic">but</hi> the Lord <hi type="italic">was</hi> not in the earthquake:

verses.name: I Kings 19:12
verses.text: And after the earthquake a fire; <hi type="italic">but</hi> the Lord <hi type="italic">was</hi> not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.

verses.name: I Kings 19:13
verses.text: And it was <hi type="italic">so</hi>, when Elijah heard <hi type="italic">it</hi>, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out, and stood in the entering in of the cave. And, behold, <hi type="italic">there came</hi> a voice unto him, and said, What doest thou here, Elijah?

verses.name: I Kings 19:14
verses.text: And he said, I have been very jealous for the Lord God of hosts: because the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, <hi type="italic">even</hi> I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.

verses.name: I Kings 19:15
verses.text: And the Lord said unto him, Go, return on thy way to the wilderness of Damascus: and when thou comest, anoint Hazael <hi type="italic">to be</hi> king over Syria:

verses.name: I Kings 19:16
verses.text: And Jehu the son of Nimshi shalt thou anoint <hi type="italic">to be</hi> king over Israel: and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah shalt thou anoint <hi type="italic">to be</hi> prophet in thy room.

verses.name: I Kings 19:17
verses.text: And it shall come to pass, <hi type="italic">that</hi> him that escapeth the sword of Hazael shall Jehu slay: and him that escapeth from the sword of Jehu shall Elisha slay.

verses.name: I Kings 19:18
verses.text: Yet I have left <hi type="italic">me</hi> seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him.

verses.name: I Kings 19:19
verses.text: ¶ So he departed thence, and found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who <hi type="italic">was</hi> plowing <hi type="italic">with</hi> twelve yoke <hi type="italic">of oxen</hi> before him, and he with the twelfth: and Elijah passed by him, and cast his mantle upon him.

verses.name: I Kings 19:20
verses.text: And he left the oxen, and ran after Elijah, and said, Let me, I pray thee, kiss my father and my mother, and <hi type="italic">then</hi> I will follow thee. And he said unto him, Go back again: for what have I done to thee?

verses.name: I Kings 19:21
verses.text: And he returned back from him, and took a yoke of oxen, and slew them, and boiled their flesh with the instruments of the oxen, and gave unto the people, and they did eat. Then he arose, and went after Elijah, and ministered unto him.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.19"/><div eID="gen322" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 20:1
verses.text: AND Ben-hadad the king of Syria gathered all his host together: and <hi type="italic">there were</hi> thirty and two kings with him, and horses, and chariots: and he went up and besieged Samaria, and warred against it.

verses.name: I Kings 20:2
verses.text: And he sent messengers to Ahab king of Israel into the city, and said unto him, Thus saith Ben-hadad,

verses.name: I Kings 20:3
verses.text: Thy silver and thy gold <hi type="italic">is</hi> mine; thy wives also and thy children, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the goodliest, <hi type="italic">are</hi> mine.

verses.name: I Kings 20:4
verses.text: And the king of Israel answered and said, My lord, O king, according to thy saying, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> thine, and all that I have.

verses.name: I Kings 20:5
verses.text: And the messengers came again, and said, Thus speaketh Ben-hadad, saying, Although I have sent unto thee, saying, Thou shalt deliver me thy silver, and thy gold, and thy wives, and thy children;

verses.name: I Kings 20:6
verses.text: Yet I will send my servants unto thee to morrow about this time, and they shall search thine house, and the houses of thy servants; and it shall be, <hi type="italic">that</hi> whatsoever is pleasant in thine eyes, they shall put <hi type="italic">it</hi> in their hand, and take <hi type="italic">it</hi> away.

verses.name: I Kings 20:7
verses.text: Then the king of Israel called all the elders of the land, and said, Mark, I pray you, and see how this <hi type="italic">man</hi> seeketh mischief: for he sent unto me for my wives, and for my children, and for my silver, and for my gold; and I denied him not.

verses.name: I Kings 20:8
verses.text: And all the elders and all the people said unto him, Hearken not <hi type="italic">unto him</hi>, nor consent.

verses.name: I Kings 20:9
verses.text: Wherefore he said unto the messengers of Ben-hadad, Tell my lord the king, All that thou didst send for to thy servant at the first I will do: but this thing I may not do. And the messengers departed, and brought him word again.

verses.name: I Kings 20:10
verses.text: And Ben-hadad sent unto him, and said, The gods do so unto me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for handfuls for all the people that follow me.

verses.name: I Kings 20:11
verses.text: And the king of Israel answered and said, Tell <hi type="italic">him</hi>, Let not him that girdeth on <hi type="italic">his harness</hi> boast himself as he that putteth it off.

verses.name: I Kings 20:12
verses.text: And it came to pass, when <hi type="italic">Ben</hi>-<hi type="italic">hadad</hi> heard this message, as he <hi type="italic">was</hi> drinking, he and the kings in the pavilions, that he said unto his servants, Set <hi type="italic">yourselves in array</hi>. And they set <hi type="italic">themselves in array</hi> against the city.

verses.name: I Kings 20:13
verses.text: ¶ And, behold, there came a prophet unto Ahab king of Israel, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Hast thou seen all this great multitude? behold, I will deliver it into thine hand this day; and thou shalt know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord.

verses.name: I Kings 20:14
verses.text: And Ahab said, By whom? And he said, Thus saith the Lord, <hi type="italic">Even</hi> by the young men of the princes of the provinces. Then he said, Who shall order the battle? And he answered, Thou.

verses.name: I Kings 20:15
verses.text: Then he numbered the young men of the princes of the provinces, and they were two hundred and thirty two: and after them he numbered all the people, <hi type="italic">even</hi> all the children of Israel, <hi type="italic">being</hi> seven thousand.

verses.name: I Kings 20:16
verses.text: And they went out at noon. But Ben-hadad <hi type="italic">was</hi> drinking himself drunk in the pavilions, he and the kings, the thirty and two kings that helped him.

verses.name: I Kings 20:17
verses.text: And the young men of the princes of the provinces went out first; and Ben-hadad sent out, and they told him, saying, There are men come out of Samaria.

verses.name: I Kings 20:18
verses.text: And he said, Whether they be come out for peace, take them alive; or whether they be come out for war, take them alive.

verses.name: I Kings 20:19
verses.text: So these young men of the princes of the provinces came out of the city, and the army which followed them.

verses.name: I Kings 20:20
verses.text: And they slew every one his man: and the Syrians fled; and Israel pursued them: and Ben-hadad the king of Syria escaped on an horse with the horsemen.

verses.name: I Kings 20:21
verses.text: And the king of Israel went out, and smote the horses and chariots, and slew the Syrians with a great slaughter.

verses.name: I Kings 20:22
verses.text: ¶ And the prophet came to the king of Israel, and said unto him, Go, strengthen thyself, and mark, and see what thou doest: for at the return of the year the king of Syria will come up against thee.

verses.name: I Kings 20:23
verses.text: And the servants of the king of Syria said unto him, Their gods <hi type="italic">are</hi> gods of the hills; therefore they were stronger than we; but let us fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they.

verses.name: I Kings 20:24
verses.text: And do this thing, Take the kings away, every man out of his place, and put captains in their rooms:

verses.name: I Kings 20:25
verses.text: And number thee an army, like the army that thou hast lost, horse for horse, and chariot for chariot: and we will fight against them in the plain, <hi type="italic">and</hi> surely we shall be stronger than they. And he hearkened unto their voice, and did so.

verses.name: I Kings 20:26
verses.text: And it came to pass at the return of the year, that Ben-hadad numbered the Syrians, and went up to Aphek, to fight against Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 20:27
verses.text: And the children of Israel were numbered, and were all present, and went against them: and the children of Israel pitched before them like two little flocks of kids; but the Syrians filled the country.

verses.name: I Kings 20:28
verses.text: ¶ And there came a man of God, and spake unto the king of Israel, and said, Thus saith the Lord, Because the Syrians have said, The Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> God of the hills, but he <hi type="italic">is</hi> not God of the valleys, therefore will I deliver all this great multitude into thine hand, and ye shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord.

verses.name: I Kings 20:29
verses.text: And they pitched one over against the other seven days. And <hi type="italic">so</hi> it was, that in the seventh day the battle was joined: and the children of Israel slew of the Syrians an hundred thousand footmen in one day.

verses.name: I Kings 20:30
verses.text: But the rest fled to Aphek, into the city; and <hi type="italic">there</hi> a wall fell upon twenty and seven thousand of the men <hi type="italic">that were</hi> left. And Ben-hadad fled, and came into the city, into an inner chamber.

verses.name: I Kings 20:31
verses.text: ¶ And his servants said unto him, Behold now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel <hi type="italic">are</hi> merciful kings: let us, I pray thee, put sackcloth on our loins, and ropes upon our heads, and go out to the king of Israel: peradventure he will save thy life.

verses.name: I Kings 20:32
verses.text: So they girded sackcloth on their loins, and <hi type="italic">put</hi> ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel, and said, Thy servant Ben-hadad saith, I pray thee, let me live. And he said, <hi type="italic">Is</hi> he yet alive? he <hi type="italic">is</hi> my brother.

verses.name: I Kings 20:33
verses.text: Now the men did diligently observe whether <hi type="italic">any thing would come</hi> from him, and did hastily catch <hi type="italic">it:</hi> and they said, Thy brother Ben-hadad. Then he said, Go ye, bring him. Then Ben-hadad came forth to him; and he caused him to come up into the chariot.

verses.name: I Kings 20:34
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">Ben</hi>-<hi type="italic">hadad</hi> said unto him, The cities, which my father took from thy father, I will restore; and thou shalt make streets for thee in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria. Then <hi type="italic">said Ahab</hi>, I will send thee away with this covenant. So he made a covenant with him, and sent him away.

verses.name: I Kings 20:35
verses.text: ¶ And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said unto his neighbour in the word of the Lord, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man refused to smite him.

verses.name: I Kings 20:36
verses.text: Then said he unto him, Because thou hast not obeyed the voice of the Lord, behold, as soon as thou art departed from me, a lion shall slay thee. And as soon as he was departed from him, a lion found him, and slew him.

verses.name: I Kings 20:37
verses.text: Then he found another man, and said, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man smote him, so that in smiting he wounded <hi type="italic">him</hi>.

verses.name: I Kings 20:38
verses.text: So the prophet departed, and waited for the king by the way, and disguised himself with ashes upon his face.

verses.name: I Kings 20:39
verses.text: And as the king passed by, he cried unto the king: and he said, Thy servant went out into the midst of the battle; and, behold, a man turned aside, and brought a man unto me, and said, Keep this man: if by any means he be missing, then shall thy life be for his life, or else thou shalt pay a talent of silver.

verses.name: I Kings 20:40
verses.text: And as thy servant was busy here and there, he was gone. And the king of Israel said unto him, So <hi type="italic">shall</hi> thy judgment <hi type="italic">be;</hi> thyself hast decided <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: I Kings 20:41
verses.text: And he hasted, and took the ashes away from his face; and the king of Israel discerned him that he <hi type="italic">was</hi> of the prophets.

verses.name: I Kings 20:42
verses.text: And he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Because thou hast let go out of <hi type="italic">thy</hi> hand a man whom I appointed to utter destruction, therefore thy life shall go for his life, and thy people for his people.

verses.name: I Kings 20:43
verses.text: And the king of Israel went to his house heavy and displeased, and came to Samaria.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.20"/><div eID="gen323" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 21:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass after these things, <hi type="italic">that</hi> Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard, which <hi type="italic">was</hi> in Jezreel, hard by the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

verses.name: I Kings 21:2
verses.text: And Ahab spake unto Naboth, saying, Give me thy vineyard, that I may have it for a garden of herbs, because it <hi type="italic">is</hi> near unto my house: and I will give thee for it a better vineyard than it; <hi type="italic">or</hi>, if it seem good to thee, I will give thee the worth of it in money.

verses.name: I Kings 21:3
verses.text: And Naboth said to Ahab, The Lord forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee.

verses.name: I Kings 21:4
verses.text: And Ahab came into his house heavy and displeased because of the word which Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him: for he had said, I will not give thee the inheritance of my fathers. And he laid him down upon his bed, and turned away his face, and would eat no bread.

verses.name: I Kings 21:5
verses.text: ¶ But Jezebel his wife came to him, and said unto him, Why is thy spirit so sad, that thou eatest no bread?

verses.name: I Kings 21:6
verses.text: And he said unto her, Because I spake unto Naboth the Jezreelite, and said unto him, Give me thy vineyard for money; or else, if it please thee, I will give thee <hi type="italic">another</hi> vineyard for it: and he answered, I will not give thee my vineyard.

verses.name: I Kings 21:7
verses.text: And Jezebel his wife said unto him, Dost thou now govern the kingdom of Israel? arise, <hi type="italic">and</hi> eat bread, and let thine heart be merry: I will give thee the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.

verses.name: I Kings 21:8
verses.text: So she wrote letters in Ahab’s name, and sealed <hi type="italic">them</hi> with his seal, and sent the letters unto the elders and to the nobles that <hi type="italic">were</hi> in his city, dwelling with Naboth.

verses.name: I Kings 21:9
verses.text: And she wrote in the letters, saying, Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people:

verses.name: I Kings 21:10
verses.text: And set two men, sons of Belial, before him, to bear witness against him, saying, Thou didst blaspheme God and the king. And <hi type="italic">then</hi> carry him out, and stone him, that he may die.

verses.name: I Kings 21:11
verses.text: And the men of his city, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the elders and the nobles who were the inhabitants in his city, did as Jezebel had sent unto them, <hi type="italic">and</hi> as it <hi type="italic">was</hi> written in the letters which she had sent unto them.

verses.name: I Kings 21:12
verses.text: They proclaimed a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people.

verses.name: I Kings 21:13
verses.text: And there came in two men, children of Belial, and sat before him: and the men of Belial witnessed against him, <hi type="italic">even</hi> against Naboth, in the presence of the people, saying, Naboth did blaspheme God and the king. Then they carried him forth out of the city, and stoned him with stones, that he died.

verses.name: I Kings 21:14
verses.text: Then they sent to Jezebel, saying, Naboth is stoned, and is dead.

verses.name: I Kings 21:15
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass, when Jezebel heard that Naboth was stoned, and was dead, that Jezebel said to Ahab, Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give thee for money: for Naboth is not alive, but dead.

verses.name: I Kings 21:16
verses.text: And it came to pass, when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, that Ahab rose up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.

verses.name: I Kings 21:17
verses.text: ¶ And the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 21:18
verses.text: Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> in Samaria: behold, <hi type="italic">he is</hi> in the vineyard of Naboth, whither he is gone down to possess it.

verses.name: I Kings 21:19
verses.text: And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Hast thou killed, and also taken possession? And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the Lord, In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.

verses.name: I Kings 21:20
verses.text: And Ahab said to Elijah, Hast thou found me, O mine enemy? And he answered, I have found <hi type="italic">thee:</hi> because thou hast sold thyself to work evil in the sight of the Lord.

verses.name: I Kings 21:21
verses.text: Behold, I will bring evil upon thee, and will take away thy posterity, and will cut off from Ahab him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel,

verses.name: I Kings 21:22
verses.text: And will make thine house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah, for the provocation wherewith thou hast provoked <hi type="italic">me</hi> to anger, and made Israel to sin.

verses.name: I Kings 21:23
verses.text: And of Jezebel also spake the Lord, saying, The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.

verses.name: I Kings 21:24
verses.text: Him that dieth of Ahab in the city the dogs shall eat; and him that dieth in the field shall the fowls of the air eat.

verses.name: I Kings 21:25
verses.text: ¶ But there was none like unto Ahab, which did sell himself to work wickedness in the sight of the Lord, whom Jezebel his wife stirred up.

verses.name: I Kings 21:26
verses.text: And he did very abominably in following idols, according to all <hi type="italic">things</hi> as did the Amorites, whom the Lord cast out before the children of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 21:27
verses.text: And it came to pass, when Ahab heard those words, that he rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon his flesh, and fasted, and lay in sackcloth, and went softly.

verses.name: I Kings 21:28
verses.text: And the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

verses.name: I Kings 21:29
verses.text: Seest thou how Ahab humbleth himself before me? because he humbleth himself before me, I will not bring the evil in his days: <hi type="italic">but</hi> in his son’s days will I bring the evil upon his house.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.21"/><div eID="gen324" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: I Kings 22:1
verses.text: AND they continued three years without war between Syria and Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 22:2
verses.text: And it came to pass in the third year, that Jehoshaphat the king of Judah came down to the king of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 22:3
verses.text: And the king of Israel said unto his servants, Know ye that Ramoth in Gilead <hi type="italic">is</hi> ours, and we <hi type="italic">be</hi> still, <hi type="italic">and</hi> take it not out of the hand of the king of Syria?

verses.name: I Kings 22:4
verses.text: And he said unto Jehoshaphat, Wilt thou go with me to battle to Ramoth-gilead? And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> as thou <hi type="italic">art</hi>, my people as thy people, my horses as thy horses.

verses.name: I Kings 22:5
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat said unto the king of Israel, Inquire, I pray thee, at the word of the Lord to day.

verses.name: I Kings 22:6
verses.text: Then the king of Israel gathered the prophets together, about four hundred men, and said unto them, Shall I go against Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And they said, Go up; for the Lord shall deliver <hi type="italic">it</hi> into the hand of the king.

verses.name: I Kings 22:7
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat said, <hi type="italic">Is there</hi> not here a prophet of the Lord besides, that we might inquire of him?

verses.name: I Kings 22:8
verses.text: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, <hi type="italic">There is</hi> yet one man, Micaiah the son of Imlah, by whom we may inquire of the Lord: but I hate him; for he doth not prophesy good concerning me, but evil. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.

verses.name: I Kings 22:9
verses.text: Then the king of Israel called an officer, and said, Hasten <hi type="italic">hither</hi> Micaiah the son of Imlah.

verses.name: I Kings 22:10
verses.text: And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah sat each on his throne, having put on their robes, in a void place in the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets prophesied before them.

verses.name: I Kings 22:11
verses.text: And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made him horns of iron: and he said, Thus saith the Lord, With these shalt thou push the Syrians, until thou have consumed them.

verses.name: I Kings 22:12
verses.text: And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and prosper: for the Lord shall deliver <hi type="italic">it</hi> into the king’s hand.

verses.name: I Kings 22:13
verses.text: And the messenger that was gone to call Micaiah spake unto him, saying, Behold now, the words of the prophets <hi type="italic">declare</hi> good unto the king with one mouth: let thy word, I pray thee, be like the word of one of them, and speak <hi type="italic">that which is</hi> good.

verses.name: I Kings 22:14
verses.text: And Micaiah said, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord liveth, what the Lord saith unto me, that will I speak.

verses.name: I Kings 22:15
verses.text: ¶ So he came to the king. And the king said unto him, Micaiah, shall we go against Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall we forbear? And he answered him, Go, and prosper: for the Lord shall deliver <hi type="italic">it</hi> into the hand of the king.

verses.name: I Kings 22:16
verses.text: And the king said unto him, How many times shall I adjure thee that thou tell me nothing but <hi type="italic">that which is</hi> true in the name of the Lord?

verses.name: I Kings 22:17
verses.text: And he said, I saw all Israel scattered upon the hills, as sheep that have not a shepherd: and the Lord said, These have no master: let them return every man to his house in peace.

verses.name: I Kings 22:18
verses.text: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, Did I not tell thee that he would prophesy no good concerning me, but evil?

verses.name: I Kings 22:19
verses.text: And he said, Hear thou therefore the word of the Lord: I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.

verses.name: I Kings 22:20
verses.text: And the Lord said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead? And one said on this manner, and another said on that manner.

verses.name: I Kings 22:21
verses.text: And there came forth a spirit, and stood before the Lord, and said, I will persuade him.

verses.name: I Kings 22:22
verses.text: And the Lord said unto him, Wherewith? And he said, I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade <hi type="italic">him</hi>, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.

verses.name: I Kings 22:23
verses.text: Now therefore, behold, the Lord hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets, and the Lord hath spoken evil concerning thee.

verses.name: I Kings 22:24
verses.text: But Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah went near, and smote Micaiah on the cheek, and said, Which way went the Spirit of the Lord from me to speak unto thee?

verses.name: I Kings 22:25
verses.text: And Micaiah said, Behold, thou shalt see in that day, when thou shalt go into an inner chamber to hide thyself.

verses.name: I Kings 22:26
verses.text: And the king of Israel said, Take Micaiah, and carry him back unto Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son;

verses.name: I Kings 22:27
verses.text: And say, Thus saith the king, Put this <hi type="italic">fellow</hi> in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I come in peace.

verses.name: I Kings 22:28
verses.text: And Micaiah said, If thou return at all in peace, the Lord hath not spoken by me. And he said, Hearken, O people, every one of you.

verses.name: I Kings 22:29
verses.text: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.

verses.name: I Kings 22:30
verses.text: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, I will disguise myself, and enter into the battle; but put thou on thy robes. And the king of Israel disguised himself, and went into the battle.

verses.name: I Kings 22:31
verses.text: But the king of Syria commanded his thirty and two captains that had rule over his chariots, saying, Fight neither with small nor great, save only with the king of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 22:32
verses.text: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, Surely it <hi type="italic">is</hi> the king of Israel. And they turned aside to fight against him: and Jehoshaphat cried out.

verses.name: I Kings 22:33
verses.text: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots perceived that it <hi type="italic">was</hi> not the king of Israel, that they turned back from pursuing him.

verses.name: I Kings 22:34
verses.text: And a <hi type="italic">certain</hi> man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness: wherefore he said unto the driver of his chariot, Turn thine hand, and carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.

verses.name: I Kings 22:35
verses.text: And the battle increased that day: and the king was stayed up in his chariot against the Syrians, and died at even: and the blood ran out of the wound into the midst of the chariot.

verses.name: I Kings 22:36
verses.text: And there went a proclamation throughout the host about the going down of the sun, saying, Every man to his city, and every man to his own country.

verses.name: I Kings 22:37
verses.text: ¶ So the king died, and was brought to Samaria; and they buried the king in Samaria.

verses.name: I Kings 22:38
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">one</hi> washed the chariot in the pool of Samaria; and the dogs licked up his blood; and they washed his armour; according unto the word of the Lord which he spake.

verses.name: I Kings 22:39
verses.text: Now the rest of the acts of Ahab, and all that he did, and the ivory house which he made, and all the cities that he built, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.name: I Kings 22:40
verses.text: So Ahab slept with his fathers; and Ahaziah his son reigned in his stead.

verses.name: I Kings 22:41
verses.text: ¶ And Jehoshaphat the son of Asa began to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 22:42
verses.text: Jehoshaphat <hi type="italic">was</hi> thirty and five years old when he began to reign; and he reigned twenty and five years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.

verses.name: I Kings 22:43
verses.text: And he walked in all the ways of Asa his father; he turned not aside from it, doing <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> right in the eyes of the Lord: nevertheless the high places were not taken away; <hi type="italic">for</hi> the people offered and burnt incense yet in the high places.

verses.name: I Kings 22:44
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 22:45
verses.text: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he shewed, and how he warred, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

verses.name: I Kings 22:46
verses.text: And the remnant of the sodomites, which remained in the days of his father Asa, he took out of the land.

verses.name: I Kings 22:47
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There was</hi> then no king in Edom: a deputy <hi type="italic">was</hi> king.

verses.name: I Kings 22:48
verses.text: Jehoshaphat made ships of Tharshish to go to Ophir for gold: but they went not; for the ships were broken at Ezion-geber.

verses.name: I Kings 22:49
verses.text: Then said Ahaziah the son of Ahab unto Jehoshaphat, Let my servants go with thy servants in the ships. But Jehoshaphat would not.

verses.name: I Kings 22:50
verses.text: ¶ And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father: and Jehoram his son reigned in his stead.

verses.name: I Kings 22:51
verses.text: ¶ Ahaziah the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigned two years over Israel.

verses.name: I Kings 22:52
verses.text: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin:

verses.name: I Kings 22:53
verses.text: For he served Baal, and worshipped him, and provoked to anger the Lord God of Israel, according to all that his father had done.  <chapter eID="1Kgs.22"/><div eID="gen325" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen303" osisID="1Kgs" type="book"/>

verses.name: II Kings 1:1
verses.text: THEN Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.

verses.name: II Kings 1:2
verses.text: And Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber that <hi type="italic">was</hi> in Samaria, and was sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, inquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease.

verses.name: II Kings 1:3
verses.text: But the angel of the Lord said to Elijah the Tishbite, Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say unto them, <hi type="italic">Is it</hi> not because <hi type="italic">there is</hi> not a God in Israel, <hi type="italic">that</hi> ye go to inquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron?

verses.name: II Kings 1:4
verses.text: Now therefore thus saith the Lord, Thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die. And Elijah departed.

verses.name: II Kings 1:5
verses.text: ¶ And when the messengers turned back unto him, he said unto them, Why are ye now turned back?

verses.name: II Kings 1:6
verses.text: And they said unto him, There came a man up to meet us, and said unto us, Go, turn again unto the king that sent you, and say unto him, Thus saith the Lord, <hi type="italic">Is it</hi> not because <hi type="italic">there is</hi> not a God in Israel, <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou sendest to inquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron? therefore thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.

verses.name: II Kings 1:7
verses.text: And he said unto them, What manner of man <hi type="italic">was he</hi> which came up to meet you, and told you these words?

verses.name: II Kings 1:8
verses.text: And they answered him, <hi type="italic">He was</hi> an hairy man, and girt with a girdle of leather about his loins. And he said, It <hi type="italic">is</hi> Elijah the Tishbite.

verses.name: II Kings 1:9
verses.text: Then the king sent unto him a captain of fifty with his fifty. And he went up to him: and, behold, he sat on the top of an hill. And he spake unto him, Thou man of God, the king hath said, Come down.

verses.name: II Kings 1:10
verses.text: And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, If I <hi type="italic">be</hi> a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.

verses.name: II Kings 1:11
verses.text: Again also he sent unto him another captain of fifty with his fifty. And he answered and said unto him, O man of God, thus hath the king said, Come down quickly.

verses.name: II Kings 1:12
verses.text: And Elijah answered and said unto them, If I <hi type="italic">be</hi> a man of God, let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And the fire of God came down from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.

verses.name: II Kings 1:13
verses.text: ¶ And he sent again a captain of the third fifty with his fifty. And the third captain of fifty went up, and came and fell on his knees before Elijah, and besought him, and said unto him, O man of God, I pray thee, let my life, and the life of these fifty thy servants, be precious in thy sight.

verses.name: II Kings 1:14
verses.text: Behold, there came fire down from heaven, and burnt up the two captains of the former fifties with their fifties: therefore let my life now be precious in thy sight.

verses.name: II Kings 1:15
verses.text: And the angel of the Lord said unto Elijah, Go down with him: be not afraid of him. And he arose, and went down with him unto the king.

verses.name: II Kings 1:16
verses.text: And he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Forasmuch as thou hast sent messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron, <hi type="italic">is it</hi> not because <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no God in Israel to inquire of his word? therefore thou shalt not come down off that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.

verses.name: II Kings 1:17
verses.text: ¶ So he died according to the word of the Lord which Elijah had spoken. And Jehoram reigned in his stead in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah; because he had no son.

verses.name: II Kings 1:18
verses.text: Now the rest of the acts of Ahaziah which he did, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?  <chapter eID="2Kgs.1"/><div eID="gen327" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 2:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass, when the Lord would take up Elijah into heaven by a whirlwind, that Elijah went with Elisha from Gilgal.

verses.name: II Kings 2:2
verses.text: And Elijah said unto Elisha, Tarry here, I pray thee; for the Lord hath sent me to Beth-el. And Elisha said <hi type="italic">unto him</hi>, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord liveth, and <hi type="italic">as</hi> thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. So they went down to Beth-el.

verses.name: II Kings 2:3
verses.text: And the sons of the prophets that <hi type="italic">were</hi> at Beth-el came forth to Elisha, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the Lord will take away thy master from thy head to day? And he said, Yea, I know <hi type="italic">it;</hi> hold ye your peace.

verses.name: II Kings 2:4
verses.text: And Elijah said unto him, Elisha, tarry here, I pray thee; for the Lord hath sent me to Jericho. And he said, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord liveth, and <hi type="italic">as</hi> thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. So they came to Jericho.

verses.name: II Kings 2:5
verses.text: And the sons of the prophets that <hi type="italic">were</hi> at Jericho came to Elisha, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the Lord will take away thy master from thy head to day? And he answered, Yea, I know <hi type="italic">it;</hi> hold ye your peace.

verses.name: II Kings 2:6
verses.text: And Elijah said unto him, Tarry, I pray thee, here; for the Lord hath sent me to Jordan. And he said, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord liveth, and <hi type="italic">as</hi> thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. And they two went on.

verses.name: II Kings 2:7
verses.text: And fifty men of the sons of the prophets went, and stood to view afar off: and they two stood by Jordan.

verses.name: II Kings 2:8
verses.text: And Elijah took his mantle, and wrapped <hi type="italic">it</hi> together, and smote the waters, and they were divided hither and thither, so that they two went over on dry ground.

verses.name: II Kings 2:9
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass, when they were gone over, that Elijah said unto Elisha, Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee. And Elisha said, I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.

verses.name: II Kings 2:10
verses.text: And he said, Thou hast asked a hard thing: <hi type="italic">nevertheless</hi>, if thou see me <hi type="italic">when I am</hi> taken from thee, it shall be so unto thee; but if not, it shall not be <hi type="italic">so</hi>.

verses.name: II Kings 2:11
verses.text: And it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, <hi type="italic">there appeared</hi> a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

verses.name: II Kings 2:12
verses.text: ¶ And Elisha saw <hi type="italic">it</hi>, and he cried, My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof. And he saw him no more: and he took hold of his own clothes, and rent them in two pieces.

verses.name: II Kings 2:13
verses.text: He took up also the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and went back, and stood by the bank of Jordan;

verses.name: II Kings 2:14
verses.text: And he took the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and smote the waters, and said, Where <hi type="italic">is</hi> the Lord God of Elijah? and when he also had smitten the waters, they parted hither and thither: and Elisha went over.

verses.name: II Kings 2:15
verses.text: And when the sons of the prophets which <hi type="italic">were</hi> to view at Jericho saw him, they said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. And they came to meet him, and bowed themselves to the ground before him.

verses.name: II Kings 2:16
verses.text: ¶ And they said unto him, Behold now, there be with thy servants fifty strong men; let them go, we pray thee, and seek thy master: lest peradventure the Spirit of the Lord hath taken him up, and cast him upon some mountain, or into some valley. And he said, Ye shall not send.

verses.name: II Kings 2:17
verses.text: And when they urged him till he was ashamed, he said, Send. They sent therefore fifty men; and they sought three days, but found him not.

verses.name: II Kings 2:18
verses.text: And when they came again to him, (for he tarried at Jericho,) he said unto them, Did I not say unto you, Go not?

verses.name: II Kings 2:19
verses.text: ¶ And the men of the city said unto Elisha, Behold, I pray thee, the situation of this city <hi type="italic">is</hi> pleasant, as my lord seeth: but the water <hi type="italic">is</hi> naught, and the ground barren.

verses.name: II Kings 2:20
verses.text: And he said, Bring me a new cruse, and put salt therein. And they brought <hi type="italic">it</hi> to him.

verses.name: II Kings 2:21
verses.text: And he went forth unto the spring of the waters, and cast the salt in there, and said, Thus saith the Lord, I have healed these waters; there shall not be from thence any more death or barren <hi type="italic">land</hi>.

verses.name: II Kings 2:22
verses.text: So the waters were healed unto this day, according to the saying of Elisha which he spake.

verses.name: II Kings 2:23
verses.text: ¶ And he went up from thence unto Beth-el: and as he was going up by the way, there came forth little children out of the city, and mocked him, and said unto him, Go up, thou bald head; go up, thou bald head.

verses.name: II Kings 2:24
verses.text: And he turned back, and looked on them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord. And there came forth two she bears out of the wood, and tare forty and two children of them.

verses.name: II Kings 2:25
verses.text: And he went from thence to mount Carmel, and from thence he returned to Samaria.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.2"/><div eID="gen328" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 3:1
verses.text: NOW Jehoram the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigned twelve years.

verses.name: II Kings 3:2
verses.text: And he wrought evil in the sight of the Lord; but not like his father, and like his mother: for he put away the image of Baal that his father had made.

verses.name: II Kings 3:3
verses.text: Nevertheless he cleaved unto the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which made Israel to sin; he departed not therefrom.

verses.name: II Kings 3:4
verses.text: ¶ And Mesha king of Moab was a sheepmaster, and rendered unto the king of Israel an hundred thousand lambs, and an hundred thousand rams, with the wool.

verses.name: II Kings 3:5
verses.text: But it came to pass, when Ahab was dead, that the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 3:6
verses.text: ¶ And king Jehoram went out of Samaria the same time, and numbered all Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 3:7
verses.text: And he went and sent to Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, saying, The king of Moab hath rebelled against me: wilt thou go with me against Moab to battle? And he said, I will go up: I <hi type="italic">am</hi> as thou <hi type="italic">art</hi>, my people as thy people, <hi type="italic">and</hi> my horses as thy horses.

verses.name: II Kings 3:8
verses.text: And he said, Which way shall we go up? And he answered, The way through the wilderness of Edom.

verses.name: II Kings 3:9
verses.text: So the king of Israel went, and the king of Judah, and the king of Edom: and they fetched a compass of seven days’ journey: and there was no water for the host, and for the cattle that followed them.

verses.name: II Kings 3:10
verses.text: And the king of Israel said, Alas! that the Lord hath called these three kings together, to deliver them into the hand of Moab!

verses.name: II Kings 3:11
verses.text: But Jehoshaphat said, <hi type="italic">Is there</hi> not here a prophet of the Lord, that we may inquire of the Lord by him? And one of the king of Israel’s servants answered and said, Here <hi type="italic">is</hi> Elisha the son of Shaphat, which poured water on the hands of Elijah.

verses.name: II Kings 3:12
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat said, The word of the Lord is with him. So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.

verses.name: II Kings 3:13
verses.text: And Elisha said unto the king of Israel, What have I to do with thee? get thee to the prophets of thy father, and to the prophets of thy mother. And the king of Israel said unto him, Nay: for the Lord hath called these three kings together, to deliver them into the hand of Moab.

verses.name: II Kings 3:14
verses.text: And Elisha said, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord of hosts liveth, before whom I stand, surely, were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look toward thee, nor see thee.

verses.name: II Kings 3:15
verses.text: But now bring me a minstrel. And it came to pass, when the minstrel played, that the hand of the Lord came upon him.

verses.name: II Kings 3:16
verses.text: And he said, Thus saith the Lord, Make this valley full of ditches.

verses.name: II Kings 3:17
verses.text: For thus saith the Lord, Ye shall not see wind, neither shall ye see rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water, that ye may drink, both ye, and your cattle, and your beasts.

verses.name: II Kings 3:18
verses.text: And this is <hi type="italic">but</hi> a light thing in the sight of the Lord: he will deliver the Moabites also into your hand.

verses.name: II Kings 3:19
verses.text: And ye shall smite every fenced city, and every choice city, and shall fell every good tree, and stop all wells of water, and mar every good piece of land with stones.

verses.name: II Kings 3:20
verses.text: And it came to pass in the morning, when the meat offering was offered, that, behold, there came water by the way of Edom, and the country was filled with water.

verses.name: II Kings 3:21
verses.text: ¶ And when all the Moabites heard that the kings were come up to fight against them, they gathered all that were able to put on armour, and upward, and stood in the border.

verses.name: II Kings 3:22
verses.text: And they rose up early in the morning, and the sun shone upon the water, and the Moabites saw the water on the other side <hi type="italic">as</hi> red as blood:

verses.name: II Kings 3:23
verses.text: And they said, This <hi type="italic">is</hi> blood: the kings are surely slain, and they have smitten one another: now therefore, Moab, to the spoil.

verses.name: II Kings 3:24
verses.text: And when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and smote the Moabites, so that they fled before them: but they went forward smiting the Moabites, even in <hi type="italic">their</hi> country.

verses.name: II Kings 3:25
verses.text: And they beat down the cities, and on every good piece of land cast every man his stone, and filled it; and they stopped all the wells of water, and felled all the good trees: only in Kir-haraseth left they the stones thereof; howbeit the slingers went about <hi type="italic">it</hi>, and smote it.

verses.name: II Kings 3:26
verses.text: ¶ And when the king of Moab saw that the battle was too sore for him, he took with him seven hundred men that drew swords, to break through <hi type="italic">even</hi> unto the king of Edom: but they could not.

verses.name: II Kings 3:27
verses.text: Then he took his eldest son that should have reigned in his stead, and offered him <hi type="italic">for</hi> a burnt offering upon the wall. And there was great indignation against Israel: and they departed from him, and returned to <hi type="italic">their own</hi> land.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.3"/><div eID="gen329" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 4:1
verses.text: NOW there cried a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets unto Elisha, saying, Thy servant my husband is dead; and thou knowest that thy servant did fear the Lord: and the creditor is come to take unto him my two sons to be bondmen.

verses.name: II Kings 4:2
verses.text: And Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil.

verses.name: II Kings 4:3
verses.text: Then he said, Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, <hi type="italic">even</hi> empty vessels; borrow not a few.

verses.name: II Kings 4:4
verses.text: And when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and shalt pour out into all those vessels, and thou shalt set aside that which is full.

verses.name: II Kings 4:5
verses.text: So she went from him, and shut the door upon her and upon her sons, who brought <hi type="italic">the vessels</hi> to her; and she poured out.

verses.name: II Kings 4:6
verses.text: And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her, <hi type="italic">There is</hi> not a vessel more. And the oil stayed.

verses.name: II Kings 4:7
verses.text: Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest.

verses.name: II Kings 4:8
verses.text: ¶ And it fell on a day, that Elisha passed to Shunem, where <hi type="italic">was</hi> a great woman; and she constrained him to eat bread. And <hi type="italic">so</hi> it was, <hi type="italic">that</hi> as oft as he passed by, he turned in thither to eat bread.

verses.name: II Kings 4:9
verses.text: And she said unto her husband, Behold now, I perceive that this <hi type="italic">is</hi> an holy man of God, which passeth by us continually.

verses.name: II Kings 4:10
verses.text: Let us make a little chamber, I pray thee, on the wall; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick: and it shall be, when he cometh to us, that he shall turn in thither.

verses.name: II Kings 4:11
verses.text: And it fell on a day, that he came thither, and he turned into the chamber, and lay there.

verses.name: II Kings 4:12
verses.text: And he said to Gehazi his servant, Call this Shunammite. And when he had called her, she stood before him.

verses.name: II Kings 4:13
verses.text: And he said unto him, Say now unto her, Behold, thou hast been careful for us with all this care; what <hi type="italic">is</hi> to be done for thee? wouldest thou be spoken for to the king, or to the captain of the host? And she answered, I dwell among mine own people.

verses.name: II Kings 4:14
verses.text: And he said, What then <hi type="italic">is</hi> to be done for her? And Gehazi answered, Verily she hath no child, and her husband is old.

verses.name: II Kings 4:15
verses.text: And he said, Call her. And when he had called her, she stood in the door.

verses.name: II Kings 4:16
verses.text: And he said, About this season, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a son. And she said, Nay, my lord, <hi type="italic">thou</hi> man of God, do not lie unto thine handmaid.

verses.name: II Kings 4:17
verses.text: And the woman conceived, and bare a son at that season that Elisha had said unto her, according to the time of life.

verses.name: II Kings 4:18
verses.text: ¶ And when the child was grown, it fell on a day, that he went out to his father to the reapers.

verses.name: II Kings 4:19
verses.text: And he said unto his father, My head, my head. And he said to a lad, Carry him to his mother.

verses.name: II Kings 4:20
verses.text: And when he had taken him, and brought him to his mother, he sat on her knees till noon, and <hi type="italic">then</hi> died.

verses.name: II Kings 4:21
verses.text: And she went up, and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and shut <hi type="italic">the door</hi> upon him, and went out.

verses.name: II Kings 4:22
verses.text: And she called unto her husband, and said, Send me, I pray thee, one of the young men, and one of the asses, that I may run to the man of God, and come again.

verses.name: II Kings 4:23
verses.text: And he said, Wherefore wilt thou go to him to day? <hi type="italic">it is</hi> neither new moon, nor sabbath. And she said, <hi type="italic">It shall be</hi> well.

verses.name: II Kings 4:24
verses.text: Then she saddled an ass, and said to her servant, Drive, and go forward; slack not <hi type="italic">thy</hi> riding for me, except I bid thee.

verses.name: II Kings 4:25
verses.text: So she went and came unto the man of God to mount Carmel. And it came to pass, when the man of God saw her afar off, that he said to Gehazi his servant, Behold, <hi type="italic">yonder is</hi> that Shunammite:

verses.name: II Kings 4:26
verses.text: Run now, I pray thee, to meet her, and say unto her, <hi type="italic">Is it</hi> well with thee? <hi type="italic">is it</hi> well with thy husband? <hi type="italic">is it</hi> well with the child? And she answered, <hi type="italic">It is</hi> well.

verses.name: II Kings 4:27
verses.text: And when she came to the man of God to the hill, she caught him by the feet: but Gehazi came near to thrust her away. And the man of God said, Let her alone; for her soul <hi type="italic">is</hi> vexed within her: and the Lord hath hid <hi type="italic">it</hi> from me, and hath not told me.

verses.name: II Kings 4:28
verses.text: Then she said, Did I desire a son of my lord? did I not say, Do not deceive me?

verses.name: II Kings 4:29
verses.text: Then he said to Gehazi, Gird up thy loins, and take my staff in thine hand, and go thy way: if thou meet any man, salute him not; and if any salute thee, answer him not again: and lay my staff upon the face of the child.

verses.name: II Kings 4:30
verses.text: And the mother of the child said, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord liveth, and <hi type="italic">as</hi> thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. And he arose, and followed her.

verses.name: II Kings 4:31
verses.text: And Gehazi passed on before them, and laid the staff upon the face of the child; but <hi type="italic">there was</hi> neither voice, nor hearing. Wherefore he went again to meet him, and told him, saying, The child is not awaked.

verses.name: II Kings 4:32
verses.text: And when Elisha was come into the house, behold, the child was dead, <hi type="italic">and</hi> laid upon his bed.

verses.name: II Kings 4:33
verses.text: He went in therefore, and shut the door upon them twain, and prayed unto the Lord.

verses.name: II Kings 4:34
verses.text: And he went up, and lay upon the child, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands: and he stretched himself upon the child; and the flesh of the child waxed warm.

verses.name: II Kings 4:35
verses.text: Then he returned, and walked in the house to and fro; and went up, and stretched himself upon him: and the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.

verses.name: II Kings 4:36
verses.text: And he called Gehazi, and said, Call this Shunammite. So he called her. And when she was come in unto him, he said, Take up thy son.

verses.name: II Kings 4:37
verses.text: Then she went in, and fell at his feet, and bowed herself to the ground, and took up her son, and went out.

verses.name: II Kings 4:38
verses.text: ¶ And Elisha came again to Gilgal: and <hi type="italic">there was</hi> a dearth in the land; and the sons of the prophets <hi type="italic">were</hi> sitting before him: and he said unto his servant, Set on the great pot, and seethe pottage for the sons of the prophets.

verses.name: II Kings 4:39
verses.text: And one went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered thereof wild gourds his lap full, and came and shred <hi type="italic">them</hi> into the pot of pottage: for they knew <hi type="italic">them</hi> not.

verses.name: II Kings 4:40
verses.text: So they poured out for the men to eat. And it came to pass, as they were eating of the pottage, that they cried out, and said, O <hi type="italic">thou</hi> man of God, <hi type="italic">there is</hi> death in the pot. And they could not eat <hi type="italic">thereof</hi>.

verses.name: II Kings 4:41
verses.text: But he said, Then bring meal. And he cast <hi type="italic">it</hi> into the pot; and he said, Pour out for the people, that they may eat. And there was no harm in the pot.

verses.name: II Kings 4:42
verses.text: ¶ And there came a man from Baal-shalisha, and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and full ears of corn in the husk thereof. And he said, Give unto the people, that they may eat.

verses.name: II Kings 4:43
verses.text: And his servitor said, What, should I set this before an hundred men? He said again, Give the people, that they may eat: for thus saith the Lord, They shall eat, and shall leave <hi type="italic">thereof</hi>.

verses.name: II Kings 4:44
verses.text: So he set <hi type="italic">it</hi> before them, and they did eat, and left <hi type="italic">thereof</hi>, according to the word of the Lord.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.4"/><div eID="gen330" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 5:1
verses.text: NOW Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honourable, because by him the Lord had given deliverance unto Syria: he was also a mighty man in valour, <hi type="italic">but he was</hi> a leper.

verses.name: II Kings 5:2
verses.text: And the Syrians had gone out by companies, and had brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little maid; and she waited on Naaman’s wife.

verses.name: II Kings 5:3
verses.text: And she said unto her mistress, Would God my lord <hi type="italic">were</hi> with the prophet that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy.

verses.name: II Kings 5:4
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">one</hi> went in, and told his lord, saying, Thus and thus said the maid that <hi type="italic">is</hi> of the land of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 5:5
verses.text: And the king of Syria said, Go to, go, and I will send a letter unto the king of Israel. And he departed, and took with him ten talents of silver, and six thousand <hi type="italic">pieces</hi> of gold, and ten changes of raiment.

verses.name: II Kings 5:6
verses.text: And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, Now when this letter is come unto thee, behold, I have <hi type="italic">therewith</hi> sent Naaman my servant to thee, that thou mayest recover him of his leprosy.

verses.name: II Kings 5:7
verses.text: And it came to pass, when the king of Israel had read the letter, that he rent his clothes, and said, <hi type="italic">Am</hi> I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man doth send unto me to recover a man of his leprosy? wherefore consider, I pray you, and see how he seeketh a quarrel against me.

verses.name: II Kings 5:8
verses.text: ¶ And it was <hi type="italic">so</hi>, when Elisha the man of God had heard that the king of Israel had rent his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, Wherefore hast thou rent thy clothes? let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 5:9
verses.text: So Naaman came with his horses and with his chariot, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha.

verses.name: II Kings 5:10
verses.text: And Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying, Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

verses.name: II Kings 5:11
verses.text: But Naaman was wroth, and went away, and said, Behold, I thought, He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the Lord his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper.

verses.name: II Kings 5:12
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Are</hi> not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? may I not wash in them, and be clean? So he turned and went away in a rage.

verses.name: II Kings 5:13
verses.text: And his servants came near, and spake unto him, and said, My father, <hi type="italic">if</hi> the prophet had bid thee <hi type="italic">do some</hi> great thing, wouldest thou not have done <hi type="italic">it?</hi> how much rather then, when he saith to thee, Wash, and be clean?

verses.name: II Kings 5:14
verses.text: Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

verses.name: II Kings 5:15
verses.text: ¶ And he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him: and he said, Behold, now I know that <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no God in all the earth, but in Israel: now therefore, I pray thee, take a blessing of thy servant.

verses.name: II Kings 5:16
verses.text: But he said, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord liveth, before whom I stand, I will receive none. And he urged him to take <hi type="italic">it;</hi> but he refused.

verses.name: II Kings 5:17
verses.text: And Naaman said, Shall there not then, I pray thee, be given to thy servant two mules’ burden of earth? for thy servant will henceforth offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice unto other gods, but unto the Lord.

verses.name: II Kings 5:18
verses.text: In this thing the Lord pardon thy servant, <hi type="italic">that</hi> when my master goeth into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leaneth on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon: when I bow down myself in the house of Rimmon, the Lord pardon thy servant in this thing.

verses.name: II Kings 5:19
verses.text: And he said unto him, Go in peace. So he departed from him a little way.

verses.name: II Kings 5:20
verses.text: ¶ But Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, Behold, my master hath spared Naaman this Syrian, in not receiving at his hands that which he brought: but, <hi type="italic">as</hi> the Lord liveth, I will run after him, and take somewhat of him.

verses.name: II Kings 5:21
verses.text: So Gehazi followed after Naaman. And when Naaman saw <hi type="italic">him</hi> running after him, he lighted down from the chariot to meet him, and said, <hi type="italic">Is</hi> all well?

verses.name: II Kings 5:22
verses.text: And he said, All <hi type="italic">is</hi> well. My master hath sent me, saying, Behold, even now there be come to me from mount Ephraim two young men of the sons of the prophets: give them, I pray thee, a talent of silver, and two changes of garments.

verses.name: II Kings 5:23
verses.text: And Naaman said, Be content, take two talents. And he urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of garments, and laid <hi type="italic">them</hi> upon two of his servants; and they bare <hi type="italic">them</hi> before him.

verses.name: II Kings 5:24
verses.text: And when he came to the tower, he took <hi type="italic">them</hi> from their hand, and bestowed <hi type="italic">them</hi> in the house: and he let the men go, and they departed.

verses.name: II Kings 5:25
verses.text: But he went in, and stood before his master. And Elisha said unto him, Whence <hi type="italic">comest thou</hi>, Gehazi? And he said, Thy servant went no whither.

verses.name: II Kings 5:26
verses.text: And he said unto him, Went not mine heart <hi type="italic">with thee</hi>, when the man turned again from his chariot to meet thee? <hi type="italic">Is it</hi> a time to receive money, and to receive garments, and oliveyards, and vineyards, and sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and maidservants?

verses.name: II Kings 5:27
verses.text: The leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee, and unto thy seed for ever. And he went out from his presence a leper <hi type="italic">as white</hi> as snow.  <chapter eID="2Kgs.5"/><div eID="gen331" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 6:1
verses.text: AND the sons of the prophets said unto Elisha, Behold now, the place where we dwell with thee is too strait for us.

verses.name: II Kings 6:2
verses.text: Let us go, we pray thee, unto Jordan, and take thence every man a beam, and let us make us a place there, where we may dwell. And he answered, Go ye.

verses.name: II Kings 6:3
verses.text: And one said, Be content, I pray thee, and go with thy servants. And he answered, I will go.

verses.name: II Kings 6:4
verses.text: So he went with them. And when they came to Jordan, they cut down wood.

verses.name: II Kings 6:5
verses.text: But as one was felling a beam, the axe head fell into the water: and he cried, and said, Alas, master! for it was borrowed.

verses.name: II Kings 6:6
verses.text: And the man of God said, Where fell it? And he shewed him the place. And he cut down a stick, and cast <hi type="italic">it</hi> in thither; and the iron did swim.

verses.name: II Kings 6:7
verses.text: Therefore said he, Take <hi type="italic">it</hi> up to thee. And he put out his hand, and took it.

verses.name: II Kings 6:8
verses.text: ¶ Then the king of Syria warred against Israel, and took counsel with his servants, saying, In such and such a place <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> my camp.

verses.name: II Kings 6:9
verses.text: And the man of God sent unto the king of Israel, saying, Beware that thou pass not such a place; for thither the Syrians are come down.

verses.name: II Kings 6:10
verses.text: And the king of Israel sent to the place which the man of God told him and warned him of, and saved himself there, not once nor twice.

verses.name: II Kings 6:11
verses.text: Therefore the heart of the king of Syria was sore troubled for this thing; and he called his servants, and said unto them, Will ye not shew me which of us <hi type="italic">is</hi> for the king of Israel?

verses.name: II Kings 6:12
verses.text: And one of his servants said, None, my lord, O king: but Elisha, the prophet that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in Israel, telleth the king of Israel the words that thou speakest in thy bedchamber.

verses.name: II Kings 6:13
verses.text: ¶ And he said, Go and spy where he <hi type="italic">is</hi>, that I may send and fetch him. And it was told him, saying, Behold, <hi type="italic">he is</hi> in Dothan.

verses.name: II Kings 6:14
verses.text: Therefore sent he thither horses, and chariots, and a great host: and they came by night, and compassed the city about.

verses.name: II Kings 6:15
verses.text: And when the servant of the man of God was risen early, and gone forth, behold, an host compassed the city both with horses and chariots. And his servant said unto him, Alas, my master! how shall we do?

verses.name: II Kings 6:16
verses.text: And he answered, Fear not: for they that <hi type="italic">be</hi> with us <hi type="italic">are</hi> more than they that <hi type="italic">be</hi> with them.

verses.name: II Kings 6:17
verses.text: And Elisha prayed, and said, Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain <hi type="italic">was</hi> full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.

verses.name: II Kings 6:18
verses.text: And when they came down to him, Elisha prayed unto the Lord, and said, Smite this people, I pray thee, with blindness. And he smote them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.

verses.name: II Kings 6:19
verses.text: ¶ And Elisha said unto them, This <hi type="italic">is</hi> not the way, neither <hi type="italic">is</hi> this the city: follow me, and I will bring you to the man whom ye seek. But he led them to Samaria.

verses.name: II Kings 6:20
verses.text: And it came to pass, when they were come into Samaria, that Elisha said, Lord, open the eyes of these <hi type="italic">men</hi>, that they may see. And the Lord opened their eyes, and they saw; and, behold, <hi type="italic">they were</hi> in the midst of Samaria.

verses.name: II Kings 6:21
verses.text: And the king of Israel said unto Elisha, when he saw them, My father, shall I smite <hi type="italic">them?</hi> shall I smite <hi type="italic">them?</hi>

verses.name: II Kings 6:22
verses.text: And he answered, Thou shalt not smite <hi type="italic">them:</hi> wouldest thou smite those whom thou hast taken captive with thy sword and with thy bow? set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink, and go to their master.

verses.name: II Kings 6:23
verses.text: And he prepared great provision for them: and when they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they went to their master. So the bands of Syria came no more into the land of Israel.

verses.name: II Kings 6:24
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass after this, that Ben-hadad king of Syria gathered all his host, and went up, and besieged Samaria.

verses.name: II Kings 6:25
verses.text: And there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass’s head was <hi type="italic">sold</hi> for fourscore <hi type="italic">pieces</hi> of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove’s dung for five <hi type="italic">pieces</hi> of silver.

verses.name: II Kings 6:26
verses.text: And as the king of Israel was passing by upon the wall, there cried a woman unto him, saying, Help, my lord, O king.

verses.name: II Kings 6:27
verses.text: And he said, If the Lord do not help thee, whence shall I help thee? out of the barnfloor, or out of the winepress?

verses.name: II Kings 6:28
verses.text: And the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered, This woman said unto me, Give thy son, that we may eat him to day, and we will eat my son to morrow.

verses.name: II Kings 6:29
verses.text: So we boiled my son, and did eat him: and I said unto her on the next day, Give thy son, that we may eat him: and she hath hid her son.

verses.name: II Kings 6:30
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the woman, that he rent his clothes; and he passed by upon the wall, and the people looked, and, behold, <hi type="italic">he had</hi> sackcloth within upon his flesh.

verses.name: II Kings 6:31
verses.text: Then he said, God do so and more also to me, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat shall stand on him this day.

verses.name: II Kings 6:32
verses.text: But Elisha sat in his house, and the elders sat with him; and <hi type="italic">the king</hi> sent a man from before him: but ere the messenger came to him, he said to the elders, See ye how this son of a murderer hath sent to take away mine head? look, when the messenger cometh, shut the door, and hold him fast at the door: <hi type="italic">is</hi> not the sound of his master’s feet behind him?

verses.name: II Kings 6:33
verses.text: And while he yet talked with them, behold, the messenger came down unto him: and he said, Behold, this evil <hi type="italic">is</hi> of the Lord; what should I wait for the Lord any longer?  <chapter eID="2Kgs.6"/><div eID="gen332" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Kings 7:1
verses.text: THEN Elisha said, Hear ye the word of the Lord; Thus saith the Lord, To morrow about this time <hi type="italic">shall</hi> a measure of fine flour <hi type="italic">be sold</hi> for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, in the gate of Samaria.

verses.name: II Kings 7:2
verses.text: Then a lord on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God, and said, Behold, <hi type="italic">if</hi> the Lord would make windows in heaven, might this thing be? And he said, Behold, thou shalt see <hi type="italic">it</hi> with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof.

verses.name: II Kings 7:3
