verses.text: But I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there; and have chosen David to be over my people Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:7
verses.text: Now it was in the heart of David my father to build an house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:8
verses.text: But the Lord said to David my father, Forasmuch as it was in thine heart to build an house for my name, thou didst well in that it was in thine heart:

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:9
verses.text: Notwithstanding thou shalt not build the house; but thy son which shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house for my name.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:10
verses.text: The Lord therefore hath performed his word that he hath spoken: for I am risen up in the room of David my father, and am set on the throne of Israel, as the Lord promised, and have built the house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:11
verses.text: And in it have I put the ark, wherein <hi type="italic">is</hi> the covenant of the Lord, that he made with the children of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:12
verses.text: ¶ And he stood before the altar of the Lord in the presence of all the congregation of Israel, and spread forth his hands:

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:13
verses.text: For Solomon had made a brasen scaffold, of five cubits long, and five cubits broad, and three cubits high, and had set it in the midst of the court: and upon it he stood, and kneeled down upon his knees before all the congregation of Israel, and spread forth his hands toward heaven,

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:14
verses.text: And said, O Lord God of Israel, <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no God like thee in the heaven, nor in the earth; which keepest covenant, and <hi type="italic">shewest</hi> mercy unto thy servants, that walk before thee with all their hearts:

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:15
verses.text: Thou which hast kept with thy servant David my father that which thou hast promised him; and spakest with thy mouth, and hast fulfilled <hi type="italic">it</hi> with thine hand, as <hi type="italic">it is</hi> this day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:16
verses.text: Now therefore, O Lord God of Israel, keep with thy servant David my father that which thou hast promised him, saying, There shall not fail thee a man in my sight to sit upon the throne of Israel; yet so that thy children take heed to their way to walk in my law, as thou hast walked before me.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:17
verses.text: Now then, O Lord God of Israel, let thy word be verified, which thou hast spoken unto thy servant David.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:18
verses.text: But will God in very deed dwell with men on the earth? behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house which I have built!

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:19
verses.text: Have respect therefore to the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplication, O Lord my God, to hearken unto the cry and the prayer which thy servant prayeth before thee:

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:20
verses.text: That thine eyes may be open upon this house day and night, upon the place whereof thou hast said that thou wouldest put thy name there; to hearken unto the prayer which thy servant prayeth toward this place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:21
verses.text: Hearken therefore unto the supplications of thy servant, and of thy people Israel, which they shall make toward this place: hear thou from thy dwelling place, <hi type="italic">even</hi> from heaven; and when thou hearest, forgive.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:22
verses.text: ¶ If a man sin against his neighbour, and an oath be laid upon him to make him swear, and the oath come before thine altar in this house;

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:23
verses.text: Then hear thou from heaven, and do, and judge thy servants, by requiting the wicked, by recompensing his way upon his own head; and by justifying the righteous, by giving him according to his righteousness.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:24
verses.text: ¶ And if thy people Israel be put to the worse before the enemy, because they have sinned against thee; and shall return and confess thy name, and pray and make supplication before thee in this house;

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:25
verses.text: Then hear thou from the heavens, and forgive the sin of thy people Israel, and bring them again unto the land which thou gavest to them and to their fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:26
verses.text: ¶ When the heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against thee; <hi type="italic">yet</hi> if they pray toward this place, and confess thy name, and turn from their sin, when thou dost afflict them;

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:27
verses.text: Then hear thou from heaven, and forgive the sin of thy servants, and of thy people Israel, when thou hast taught them the good way, wherein they should walk; and send rain upon thy land, which thou hast given unto thy people for an inheritance.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:28
verses.text: ¶ If there be dearth in the land, if there be pestilence, if there be blasting, or mildew, locusts, or caterpillers; if their enemies besiege them in the cities of their land; whatsoever sore or whatsoever sickness <hi type="italic">there be:</hi>

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:29
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Then</hi> what prayer <hi type="italic">or</hi> what supplication soever shall be made of any man, or of all thy people Israel, when every one shall know his own sore and his own grief, and shall spread forth his hands in this house:

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:30
verses.text: Then hear thou from heaven thy dwelling place, and forgive, and render unto every man according unto all his ways, whose heart thou knowest; (for thou only knowest the hearts of the children of men:)

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:31
verses.text: That they may fear thee, to walk in thy ways, so long as they live in the land which thou gavest unto our fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:32
verses.text: ¶ Moreover concerning the stranger, which is not of thy people Israel, but is come from a far country for thy great name’s sake, and thy mighty hand, and thy stretched out arm; if they come and pray in this house;

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:33
verses.text: Then hear thou from the heavens, <hi type="italic">even</hi> from thy dwelling place, and do according to all that the stranger calleth to thee for; that all people of the earth may know thy name, and fear thee, as <hi type="italic">doth</hi> thy people Israel, and may know that this house which I have built is called by thy name.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:34
verses.text: If thy people go out to war against their enemies by the way that thou shalt send them, and they pray unto thee toward this city which thou hast chosen, and the house which I have built for thy name;

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:35
verses.text: Then hear thou from the heavens their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:36
verses.text: If they sin against thee, (for <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no man which sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them over before <hi type="italic">their</hi> enemies, and they carry them away captives unto a land far off or near;

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:37
verses.text: Yet <hi type="italic">if</hi> they bethink themselves in the land whither they are carried captive, and turn and pray unto thee in the land of their captivity, saying, We have sinned, we have done amiss, and have dealt wickedly;

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:38
verses.text: If they return to thee with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their captivity, whither they have carried them captives, and pray toward their land, which thou gavest unto their fathers, and <hi type="italic">toward</hi> the city which thou hast chosen, and toward the house which I have built for thy name:

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:39
verses.text: Then hear thou from the heavens, <hi type="italic">even</hi> from thy dwelling place, their prayer and their supplications, and maintain their cause, and forgive thy people which have sinned against thee.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:40
verses.text: Now, my God, let, I beseech thee, thine eyes be open, and <hi type="italic">let</hi> thine ears <hi type="italic">be</hi> attent unto the prayer <hi type="italic">that is made</hi> in this place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:41
verses.text: Now therefore arise, O Lord God, into thy resting place, thou, and the ark of thy strength: let thy priests, O Lord God, be clothed with salvation, and let thy saints rejoice in goodness.

verses.name: II Chronicles 6:42
verses.text: O Lord God, turn not away the face of thine anointed: remember the mercies of David thy servant.  <chapter eID="2Chr.6"/><div eID="gen388" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:1
verses.text: NOW when Solomon had made an end of praying, the fire came down from heaven, and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices; and the glory of the Lord filled the house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:2
verses.text: And the priests could not enter into the house of the Lord, because the glory of the Lord had filled the Lord’s house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:3
verses.text: And when all the children of Israel saw how the fire came down, and the glory of the Lord upon the house, they bowed themselves with their faces to the ground upon the pavement, and worshipped, and praised the Lord, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, For <hi type="italic">he is</hi> good; for his mercy <hi type="italic">endureth</hi> for ever.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:4
verses.text: ¶ Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:5
verses.text: And king Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty and two thousand oxen, and an hundred and twenty thousand sheep: so the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:6
verses.text: And the priests waited on their offices: the Levites also with instruments of musick of the Lord, which David the king had made to praise the Lord, because his mercy <hi type="italic">endureth</hi> for ever, when David praised by their ministry; and the priests sounded trumpets before them, and all Israel stood.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:7
verses.text: Moreover Solomon hallowed the middle of the court that <hi type="italic">was</hi> before the house of the Lord: for there he offered burnt offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings, because the brasen altar which Solomon had made was not able to receive the burnt offerings, and the meat offerings, and the fat.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:8
verses.text: ¶ Also at the same time Solomon kept the feast seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great congregation, from the entering in of Hamath unto the river of Egypt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:9
verses.text: And in the eighth day they made a solemn assembly: for they kept the dedication of the altar seven days, and the feast seven days.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:10
verses.text: And on the three and twentieth day of the seventh month he sent the people away into their tents, glad and merry in heart for the goodness that the Lord had shewed unto David, and to Solomon, and to Israel his people.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:11
verses.text: Thus Solomon finished the house of the Lord, and the king’s house: and all that came into Solomon’s heart to make in the house of the Lord, and in his own house, he prosperously effected.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:12
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord appeared to Solomon by night, and said unto him, I have heard thy prayer, and have chosen this place to myself for an house of sacrifice.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:13
verses.text: If I shut up heaven that there be no rain, or if I command the locusts to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among my people;

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:14
verses.text: If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:15
verses.text: Now mine eyes shall be open, and mine ears attent unto the prayer <hi type="italic">that is made</hi> in this place.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:16
verses.text: For now have I chosen and sanctified this house, that my name may be there for ever: and mine eyes and mine heart shall be there perpetually.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:17
verses.text: And as for thee, if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked, and do according to all that I have commanded thee, and shalt observe my statutes and my judgments;

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:18
verses.text: Then will I stablish the throne of thy kingdom, according as I have covenanted with David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man <hi type="italic">to be</hi> ruler in Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:19
verses.text: But if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes and my commandments, which I have set before you, and shall go and serve other gods, and worship them;

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:20
verses.text: Then will I pluck them up by the roots out of my land which I have given them; and this house, which I have sanctified for my name, will I cast out of my sight, and will make it <hi type="italic">to be</hi> a proverb and a byword among all nations.

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:21
verses.text: And this house, which is high, shall be an astonishment to every one that passeth by it; so that he shall say, Why hath the Lord done thus unto this land, and unto this house?

verses.name: II Chronicles 7:22
verses.text: And it shall be answered, Because they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, which brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold on other gods, and worshipped them, and served them: therefore hath he brought all this evil upon them.  <chapter eID="2Chr.7"/><div eID="gen389" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass at the end of twenty years, wherein Solomon had built the house of the Lord, and his own house,

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:2
verses.text: That the cities which Huram had restored to Solomon, Solomon built them, and caused the children of Israel to dwell there.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:3
verses.text: And Solomon went to Hamath-zobah, and prevailed against it.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:4
verses.text: And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the store cities, which he built in Hamath.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:5
verses.text: Also he built Beth-horon the upper, and Beth-horon the nether, fenced cities, with walls, gates, and bars;

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:6
verses.text: And Baalath, and all the store cities that Solomon had, and all the chariot cities, and the cities of the horsemen, and all that Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and throughout all the land of his dominion.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:7
verses.text: ¶ <hi type="italic">As for</hi> all the people <hi type="italic">that were</hi> left of the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, which <hi type="italic">were</hi> not of Israel,

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:8
verses.text: <hi type="italic">But</hi> of their children, who were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel consumed not, them did Solomon make to pay tribute until this day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:9
verses.text: But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no servants for his work; but they <hi type="italic">were</hi> men of war, and chief of his captains, and captains of his chariots and horsemen.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:10
verses.text: And these <hi type="italic">were</hi> the chief of king Solomon’s officers, <hi type="italic">even</hi> two hundred and fifty, that bare rule over the people.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:11
verses.text: ¶ And Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh out of the city of David unto the house that he had built for her: for he said, My wife shall not dwell in the house of David king of Israel, because <hi type="italic">the places are</hi> holy, whereunto the ark of the Lord hath come.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:12
verses.text: ¶ Then Solomon offered burnt offerings unto the Lord on the altar of the Lord, which he had built before the porch,

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:13
verses.text: Even after a certain rate every day, offering according to the commandment of Moses, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts, three times in the year, <hi type="italic">even</hi> in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:14
verses.text: ¶ And he appointed, according to the order of David his father, the courses of the priests to their service, and the Levites to their charges, to praise and minister before the priests, as the duty of every day required: the porters also by their courses at every gate: for so had David the man of God commanded.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:15
verses.text: And they departed not from the commandment of the king unto the priests and Levites concerning any matter, or concerning the treasures.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:16
verses.text: Now all the work of Solomon was prepared unto the day of the foundation of the house of the Lord, and until it was finished. <hi type="italic">So</hi> the house of the Lord was perfected.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:17
verses.text: ¶ Then went Solomon to Ezion-geber, and to Eloth, at the sea side in the land of Edom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 8:18
verses.text: And Huram sent him by the hands of his servants ships, and servants that had knowledge of the sea; and they went with the servants of Solomon to Ophir, and took thence four hundred and fifty talents of gold, and brought <hi type="italic">them</hi> to king Solomon.  <chapter eID="2Chr.8"/><div eID="gen390" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:1
verses.text: AND when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to prove Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great company, and camels that bare spices, and gold in abundance, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:2
verses.text: And Solomon told her all her questions: and there was nothing hid from Solomon which he told her not.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:3
verses.text: And when the queen of Sheba had seen the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:4
verses.text: And the meat of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel; his cupbearers also, and their apparel; and his ascent by which he went up into the house of the Lord; there was no more spirit in her.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:5
verses.text: And she said to the king, <hi type="italic">It was</hi> a true report which I heard in mine own land of thine acts, and of thy wisdom:

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:6
verses.text: Howbeit I believed not their words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen <hi type="italic">it:</hi> and, behold, the one half of the greatness of thy wisdom was not told me: <hi type="italic">for</hi> thou exceedest the fame that I heard.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:7
verses.text: Happy <hi type="italic">are</hi> thy men, and happy <hi type="italic">are</hi> these thy servants, which stand continually before thee, and hear thy wisdom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:8
verses.text: Blessed be the Lord thy God, which delighted in thee to set thee on his throne, <hi type="italic">to be</hi> king for the Lord thy God: because thy God loved Israel, to establish them for ever, therefore made he thee king over them, to do judgment and justice.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:9
verses.text: And she gave the king an hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices great abundance, and precious stones: neither was there any such spice as the queen of Sheba gave king Solomon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:10
verses.text: And the servants also of Huram, and the servants of Solomon, which brought gold from Ophir, brought algum trees and precious stones.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:11
verses.text: And the king made <hi type="italic">of</hi> the algum trees terraces to the house of the Lord, and to the king’s palace, and harps and psalteries for singers: and there were none such seen before in the land of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:12
verses.text: And king Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked, beside <hi type="italic">that</hi> which she had brought unto the king. So she turned, and went away to her own land, she and her servants.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:13
verses.text: ¶ Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and threescore and six talents of gold;

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:14
verses.text: Beside <hi type="italic">that which</hi> chapmen and merchants brought. And all the kings of Arabia and governors of the country brought gold and silver to Solomon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:15
verses.text: ¶ And king Solomon made two hundred targets <hi type="italic">of</hi> beaten gold: six hundred <hi type="italic">shekels</hi> of beaten gold went to one target.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:16
verses.text: And three hundred shields <hi type="italic">made he of</hi> beaten gold: three hundred <hi type="italic">shekels</hi> of gold went to one shield. And the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:17
verses.text: Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with pure gold.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:18
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">there were</hi> six steps to the throne, with a footstool of gold, <hi type="italic">which were</hi> fastened to the throne, and stays on each side of the sitting place, and two lions standing by the stays:

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:19
verses.text: And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps. There was not the like made in any kingdom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:20
verses.text: ¶ And all the drinking vessels of king Solomon <hi type="italic">were of</hi> gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon <hi type="italic">were of</hi> pure gold: none <hi type="italic">were of</hi> silver; it was <hi type="italic">not</hi> any thing accounted of in the days of Solomon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:21
verses.text: For the king’s ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Huram: every three years once came the ships of Tarshish bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:22
verses.text: And king Solomon passed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:23
verses.text: ¶ And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, that God had put in his heart.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:24
verses.text: And they brought every man his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and raiment, harness, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:25
verses.text: ¶ And Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen; whom he bestowed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:26
verses.text: ¶ And he reigned over all the kings from the river even unto the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:27
verses.text: And the king made silver in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar trees made he as the sycomore trees that <hi type="italic">are</hi> in the low plains in abundance.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:28
verses.text: And they brought unto Solomon horses out of Egypt, and out of all lands.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:29
verses.text: ¶ Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat?

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:30
verses.text: And Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.

verses.name: II Chronicles 9:31
verses.text: And Solomon slept with his fathers, and he was buried in the city of David his father: and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.  <chapter eID="2Chr.9"/><div eID="gen391" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:1
verses.text: AND Rehoboam went to Shechem: for to Shechem were all Israel come to make him king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:2
verses.text: And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who <hi type="italic">was</hi> in Egypt, whither he had fled from the presence of Solomon the king, heard <hi type="italic">it</hi>, that Jeroboam returned out of Egypt.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:3
verses.text: And they sent and called him. So Jeroboam and all Israel came and spake to Rehoboam, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:4
verses.text: Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore ease thou somewhat the grievous servitude of thy father, and his heavy yoke that he put upon us, and we will serve thee.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:5
verses.text: And he said unto them, Come again unto me after three days. And the people departed.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:6
verses.text: ¶ And king Rehoboam took counsel with the old men that had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, What counsel give ye <hi type="italic">me</hi> to return answer to this people?

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:7
verses.text: And they spake unto him, saying, If thou be kind to this people, and please them, and speak good words to them, they will be thy servants for ever.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:8
verses.text: But he forsook the counsel which the old men gave him, and took counsel with the young men that were brought up with him, that stood before him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:9
verses.text: And he said unto them, What advice give ye that we may return answer to this people, which have spoken to me, saying, Ease somewhat the yoke that thy father did put upon us?

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:10
verses.text: And the young men that were brought up with him spake unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou answer the people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou <hi type="italic">it</hi> somewhat lighter for us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little <hi type="italic">finger</hi> shall be thicker than my father’s loins.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:11
verses.text: For whereas my father put a heavy yoke upon you, I will put more to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I <hi type="italic">will chastise you</hi> with scorpions.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:12
verses.text: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king bade, saying, Come again to me on the third day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:13
verses.text: And the king answered them roughly; and king Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men,

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:14
verses.text: And answered them after the advice of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add thereto: my father chastised you with whips, but I <hi type="italic">will chastise you</hi> with scorpions.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:15
verses.text: So the king hearkened not unto the people: for the cause was of God, that the Lord might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:16
verses.text: ¶ And when all Israel <hi type="italic">saw</hi> that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? and <hi type="italic">we have</hi> none inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to your tents, O Israel: <hi type="italic">and</hi> now, David, see to thine own house. So all Israel went to their tents.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:17
verses.text: But <hi type="italic">as for</hi> the children of Israel that dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:18
verses.text: Then king Rehoboam sent Hadoram that <hi type="italic">was</hi> over the tribute; and the children of Israel stoned him with stones, that he died. But king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to <hi type="italic">his</hi> chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 10:19
verses.text: And Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.  <chapter eID="2Chr.10"/><div eID="gen392" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:1
verses.text: AND when Rehoboam was come to Jerusalem, he gathered of the house of Judah and Benjamin an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen <hi type="italic">men</hi>, which were warriors, to fight against Israel, that he might bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:2
verses.text: But the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:3
verses.text: Speak unto Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:4
verses.text: Thus saith the Lord, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren: return every man to his house: for this thing is done of me. And they obeyed the words of the Lord, and returned from going against Jeroboam.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:5
verses.text: ¶ And Rehoboam dwelt in Jerusalem, and built cities for defence in Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:6
verses.text: He built even Beth-lehem, and Etam, and Tekoa,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:7
verses.text: And Beth-zur, and Shoco, and Adullam,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:8
verses.text: And Gath, and Mareshah, and Ziph,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:9
verses.text: And Adoraim, and Lachish, and Azekah,

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:10
verses.text: And Zorah, and Aijalon, and Hebron, which <hi type="italic">are</hi> in Judah and in Benjamin fenced cities.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:11
verses.text: And he fortified the strong holds, and put captains in them, and store of victual, and of oil and wine.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:12
verses.text: And in every several city <hi type="italic">he put</hi> shields and spears, and made them exceeding strong, having Judah and Benjamin on his side.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:13
verses.text: ¶ And the priests and the Levites that <hi type="italic">were</hi> in all Israel resorted to him out of all their coasts.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:14
verses.text: For the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem: for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest’s office unto the Lord:

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:15
verses.text: And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:16
verses.text: And after them out of all the tribes of Israel such as set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem, to sacrifice unto the Lord God of their fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:17
verses.text: So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong, three years: for three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:18
verses.text: ¶ And Rehoboam took him Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David to wife, <hi type="italic">and</hi> Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse;

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:19
verses.text: Which bare him children; Jeush, and Shamariah, and Zaham.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:20
verses.text: And after her he took Maachah the daughter of Absalom; which bare him Abijah, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:21
verses.text: And Rehoboam loved Maachah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines: (for he took eighteen wives, and threescore concubines; and begat twenty and eight sons, and threescore daughters.)

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:22
verses.text: And Rehoboam made Abijah the son of Maachah the chief, <hi type="italic">to be</hi> ruler among his brethren: for <hi type="italic">he thought</hi> to make him king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 11:23
verses.text: And he dealt wisely, and dispersed of all his children throughout all the countries of Judah and Benjamin, unto every fenced city: and he gave them victual in abundance. And he desired many wives.  <chapter eID="2Chr.11"/><div eID="gen393" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:2
verses.text: And it came to pass, <hi type="italic">that</hi> in the fifth year of king Rehoboam Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had transgressed against the Lord,

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:3
verses.text: With twelve hundred chariots, and threescore thousand horsemen: and the people <hi type="italic">were</hi> without number that came with him out of Egypt; the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:4
verses.text: And he took the fenced cities which <hi type="italic">pertained</hi> to Judah, and came to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:5
verses.text: ¶ Then came Shemaiah the prophet to Rehoboam, and <hi type="italic">to</hi> the princes of Judah, that were gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said unto them, Thus saith the Lord, Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:6
verses.text: Whereupon the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, The Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> righteous.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:7
verses.text: And when the Lord saw that they humbled themselves, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying, They have humbled themselves; <hi type="italic">therefore</hi> I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance; and my wrath shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:8
verses.text: Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:9
verses.text: So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, and took away the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house; he took all: he carried away also the shields of gold which Solomon had made.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:10
verses.text: Instead of which king Rehoboam made shields of brass, and committed <hi type="italic">them</hi> to the hands of the chief of the guard, that kept the entrance of the king’s house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:11
verses.text: And when the king entered into the house of the Lord, the guard came and fetched them, and brought them again into the guard chamber.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:12
verses.text: And when he humbled himself, the wrath of the Lord turned from him, that he would not destroy <hi type="italic">him</hi> altogether: and also in Judah things went well.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:13
verses.text: ¶ So king Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem, and reigned: for Rehoboam <hi type="italic">was</hi> one and forty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the Lord had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. And his mother’s name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Naamah an Ammonitess.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:14
verses.text: And he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:15
verses.text: Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet, and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies? And <hi type="italic">there were</hi> wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.

verses.name: II Chronicles 12:16
verses.text: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David: and Abijah his son reigned in his stead.  <chapter eID="2Chr.12"/><div eID="gen394" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:1
verses.text: NOW in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam began Abijah to reign over Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:2
verses.text: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also <hi type="italic">was</hi> Michaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:3
verses.text: And Abijah set the battle in array with an army of valiant men of war, <hi type="italic">even</hi> four hundred thousand chosen men: Jeroboam also set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, <hi type="italic">being</hi> mighty men of valour.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:4
verses.text: ¶ And Abijah stood up upon mount Zemaraim, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> in mount Ephraim, and said, Hear me, thou Jeroboam, and all Israel;

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:5
verses.text: Ought ye not to know that the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, <hi type="italic">even</hi> to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:6
verses.text: Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, is risen up, and hath rebelled against his lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:7
verses.text: And there are gathered unto him vain men, the children of Belial, and have strengthened themselves against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and tenderhearted, and could not withstand them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:8
verses.text: And now ye think to withstand the kingdom of the Lord in the hand of the sons of David; and ye <hi type="italic">be</hi> a great multitude, and <hi type="italic">there are</hi> with you golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:9
verses.text: Have ye not cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made you priests after the manner of the nations of <hi type="italic">other</hi> lands? so that whosoever cometh to consecrate himself with a young bullock and seven rams, <hi type="italic">the same</hi> may be a priest of <hi type="italic">them that are</hi> no gods.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:10
verses.text: But as for us, the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> our God, and we have not forsaken him; and the priests, which minister unto the Lord, <hi type="italic">are</hi> the sons of Aaron, and the Levites <hi type="italic">wait</hi> upon <hi type="italic">their</hi> business:

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:11
verses.text: And they burn unto the Lord every morning and every evening burnt sacrifices and sweet incense: the shewbread also <hi type="italic">set they in order</hi> upon the pure table; and the candlestick of gold with the lamps thereof, to burn every evening: for we keep the charge of the Lord our God; but ye have forsaken him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:12
verses.text: And, behold, God himself <hi type="italic">is</hi> with us for <hi type="italic">our</hi> captain, and his priests with sounding trumpets to cry alarm against you. O children of Israel, fight ye not against the Lord God of your fathers; for ye shall not prosper.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:13
verses.text: ¶ But Jeroboam caused an ambushment to come about behind them: so they were before Judah, and the ambushment <hi type="italic">was</hi> behind them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:14
verses.text: And when Judah looked back, behold, the battle <hi type="italic">was</hi> before and behind: and they cried unto the Lord, and the priests sounded with the trumpets.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:15
verses.text: Then the men of Judah gave a shout: and as the men of Judah shouted, it came to pass, that God smote Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:16
verses.text: And the children of Israel fled before Judah: and God delivered them into their hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:17
verses.text: And Abijah and his people slew them with a great slaughter: so there fell down slain of Israel five hundred thousand chosen men.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:18
verses.text: Thus the children of Israel were brought under at that time, and the children of Judah prevailed, because they relied upon the Lord God of their fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:19
verses.text: And Abijah pursued after Jeroboam, and took cities from him, Beth-el with the towns thereof, and Jeshanah with the towns thereof, and Ephrain with the towns thereof.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:20
verses.text: Neither did Jeroboam recover strength again in the days of Abijah: and the Lord struck him, and he died.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:21
verses.text: ¶ But Abijah waxed mighty, and married fourteen wives, and begat twenty and two sons, and sixteen daughters.

verses.name: II Chronicles 13:22
verses.text: And the rest of the acts of Abijah, and his ways, and his sayings, <hi type="italic">are</hi> written in the story of the prophet Iddo.  <chapter eID="2Chr.13"/><div eID="gen395" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:1
verses.text: SO Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his stead. In his days the land was quiet ten years.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:2
verses.text: And Asa did <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> good and right in the eyes of the Lord his God:

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:3
verses.text: For he took away the altars of the strange <hi type="italic">gods</hi>, and the high places, and brake down the images, and cut down the groves:

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:4
verses.text: And commanded Judah to seek the Lord God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:5
verses.text: Also he took away out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the images: and the kingdom was quiet before him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:6
verses.text: ¶ And he built fenced cities in Judah: for the land had rest, and he had no war in those years; because the Lord had given him rest.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:7
verses.text: Therefore he said unto Judah, Let us build these cities, and make about <hi type="italic">them</hi> walls, and towers, gates, and bars, <hi type="italic">while</hi> the land <hi type="italic">is</hi> yet before us; because we have sought the Lord our God, we have sought <hi type="italic">him</hi>, and he hath given us rest on every side. So they built and prospered.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:8
verses.text: And Asa had an army <hi type="italic">of men</hi> that bare targets and spears, out of Judah three hundred thousand; and out of Benjamin, that bare shields and drew bows, two hundred and fourscore thousand: all these <hi type="italic">were</hi> mighty men of valour.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:9
verses.text: ¶ And there came out against them Zerah the Ethiopian with an host of a thousand thousand, and three hundred chariots; and came unto Mareshah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:10
verses.text: Then Asa went out against him, and they set the battle in array in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:11
verses.text: And Asa cried unto the Lord his God, and said, Lord, <hi type="italic">it is</hi> nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Lord our God; for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude. O Lord, thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> our God; let not man prevail against thee.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:12
verses.text: So the Lord smote the Ethiopians before Asa, and before Judah; and the Ethiopians fled.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:13
verses.text: And Asa and the people that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him pursued them unto Gerar: and the Ethiopians were overthrown, that they could not recover themselves; for they were destroyed before the Lord, and before his host; and they carried away very much spoil.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:14
verses.text: And they smote all the cities round about Gerar; for the fear of the Lord came upon them: and they spoiled all the cities; for there was exceeding much spoil in them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 14:15
verses.text: They smote also the tents of cattle, and carried away sheep and camels in abundance, and returned to Jerusalem.  <chapter eID="2Chr.14"/><div eID="gen396" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:1
verses.text: AND the Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded:

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:2
verses.text: And he went out to meet Asa, and said unto him, Hear ye me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin; The Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:3
verses.text: Now for a long season Israel <hi type="italic">hath been</hi> without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:4
verses.text: But when they in their trouble did turn unto the Lord God of Israel, and sought him, he was found of them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:5
verses.text: And in those times <hi type="italic">there was</hi> no peace to him that went out, nor to him that came in, but great vexations <hi type="italic">were</hi> upon all the inhabitants of the countries.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:6
verses.text: And nation was destroyed of nation, and city of city: for God did vex them with all adversity.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:7
verses.text: Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:8
verses.text: And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim, and renewed the altar of the Lord, that <hi type="italic">was</hi> before the porch of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:9
verses.text: And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God <hi type="italic">was</hi> with him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:10
verses.text: So they gathered themselves together at Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:11
verses.text: And they offered unto the Lord the same time, of the spoil <hi type="italic">which</hi> they had brought, seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:12
verses.text: And they entered into a covenant to seek the Lord God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul;

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:13
verses.text: That whosoever would not seek the Lord God of Israel should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:14
verses.text: And they sware unto the Lord with a loud voice, and with shouting, and with trumpets, and with cornets.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:15
verses.text: And all Judah rejoiced at the oath: for they had sworn with all their heart, and sought him with their whole desire; and he was found of them: and the Lord gave them rest round about.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:16
verses.text: ¶ And also <hi type="italic">concerning</hi> Maachah the mother of Asa the king, he removed her from <hi type="italic">being</hi> queen, because she had made an idol in a grove: and Asa cut down her idol, and stamped <hi type="italic">it</hi>, and burnt <hi type="italic">it</hi> at the brook Kidron.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:17
verses.text: But the high places were not taken away out of Israel: nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:18
verses.text: ¶ And he brought into the house of God the things that his father had dedicated, and that he himself had dedicated, silver, and gold, and vessels.

verses.name: II Chronicles 15:19
verses.text: And there was no <hi type="italic">more</hi> war unto the five and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa.  <chapter eID="2Chr.15"/><div eID="gen397" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:1
verses.text: IN the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah, and built Ramah, to the intent that he might let none go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:2
verses.text: Then Asa brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king’s house, and sent to Ben-hadad king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:3
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> a league between me and thee, as <hi type="italic">there was</hi> between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent thee silver and gold; go, break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:4
verses.text: And Ben-hadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel; and they smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:5
verses.text: And it came to pass, when Baasha heard <hi type="italic">it</hi>, that he left off building of Ramah, and let his work cease.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:6
verses.text: Then Asa the king took all Judah; and they carried away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha was building; and he built therewith Geba and Mizpah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:7
verses.text: ¶ And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah, and said unto him, Because thou hast relied on the king of Syria, and not relied on the Lord thy God, therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of thine hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:8
verses.text: Were not the Ethiopians and the Lubims a huge host, with very many chariots and horsemen? yet, because thou didst rely on the Lord, he delivered them into thine hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:9
verses.text: For the eyes of the Lord run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of <hi type="italic">them</hi> whose heart <hi type="italic">is</hi> perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:10
verses.text: Then Asa was wroth with the seer, and put him in a prison house; for <hi type="italic">he was</hi> in a rage with him because of this <hi type="italic">thing</hi>. And Asa oppressed <hi type="italic">some</hi> of the people the same time.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:11
verses.text: ¶ And, behold, the acts of Asa, first and last, lo, they <hi type="italic">are</hi> written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:12
verses.text: And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease <hi type="italic">was</hi> exceeding <hi type="italic">great:</hi> yet in his disease he sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:13
verses.text: ¶ And Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the one and fortieth year of his reign.

verses.name: II Chronicles 16:14
verses.text: And they buried him in his own sepulchres, which he had made for himself in the city of David, and laid him in the bed which was filled with sweet odours and divers kinds <hi type="italic">of spices</hi> prepared by the apothecaries’ art: and they made a very great burning for him.  <chapter eID="2Chr.16"/><div eID="gen398" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:1
verses.text: AND Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead, and strengthened himself against Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:2
verses.text: And he placed forces in all the fenced cities of Judah, and set garrisons in the land of Judah, and in the cities of Ephraim, which Asa his father had taken.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:3
verses.text: And the Lord was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father David, and sought not unto Baalim;

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:4
verses.text: But sought to the <hi type="italic">L</hi><hi type="italic">ord</hi> God of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:5
verses.text: Therefore the Lord stablished the kingdom in his hand; and all Judah brought to Jehoshaphat presents; and he had riches and honour in abundance.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:6
verses.text: And his heart was lifted up in the ways of the Lord: moreover he took away the high places and groves out of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:7
verses.text: ¶ Also in the third year of his reign he sent to his princes, <hi type="italic">even</hi> to Ben-hail, and to Obadiah, and to Zechariah, and to Nethaneel, and to Michaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:8
verses.text: And with them <hi type="italic">he sent</hi> Levites, <hi type="italic">even</hi> Shemaiah, and Nethaniah, and Zebadiah, and Asahel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehonathan, and Adonijah, and Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah, Levites; and with them Elishama and Jehoram, priests.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:9
verses.text: And they taught in Judah, and <hi type="italic">had</hi> the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:10
verses.text: ¶ And the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that <hi type="italic">were</hi> round about Judah, so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:11
verses.text: Also <hi type="italic">some</hi> of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat presents, and tribute silver; and the Arabians brought him flocks, seven thousand and seven hundred rams, and seven thousand and seven hundred he goats.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:12
verses.text: ¶ And Jehoshaphat waxed great exceedingly; and he built in Judah castles, and cities of store.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:13
verses.text: And he had much business in the cities of Judah: and the men of war, mighty men of valour, <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:14
verses.text: And these <hi type="italic">are</hi> the numbers of them according to the house of their fathers: Of Judah, the captains of thousands; Adnah the chief, and with him mighty men of valour three hundred thousand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:15
verses.text: And next to him <hi type="italic">was</hi> Jehohanan the captain, and with him two hundred and fourscore thousand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:16
verses.text: And next him <hi type="italic">was</hi> Amasiah the son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself unto the Lord; and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valour.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:17
verses.text: And of Benjamin; Eliada a mighty man of valour, and with him armed men with bow and shield two hundred thousand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:18
verses.text: And next him <hi type="italic">was</hi> Jehozabad, and with him an hundred and fourscore thousand ready prepared for the war.

verses.name: II Chronicles 17:19
verses.text: These waited on the king, beside <hi type="italic">those</hi> whom the king put in the fenced cities throughout all Judah.  <chapter eID="2Chr.17"/><div eID="gen399" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:1
verses.text: NOW Jehoshaphat had riches and honour in abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:2
verses.text: And after <hi type="italic">certain</hi> years he went down to Ahab to Samaria. And Ahab killed sheep and oxen for him in abundance, and for the people that <hi type="italic">he had</hi> with him, and persuaded him to go up <hi type="italic">with him</hi> to Ramoth-gilead.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:3
verses.text: And Ahab king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Wilt thou go with me to Ramoth-gilead? And he answered him, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> as thou <hi type="italic">art</hi>, and my people as thy people; and <hi type="italic">we will be</hi> with thee in the war.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:4
verses.text: ¶ And Jehoshaphat said unto the king of Israel, Inquire, I pray thee, at the word of the Lord to day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:5
verses.text: Therefore the king of Israel gathered together of prophets four hundred men, and said unto them, Shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And they said, Go up; for God will deliver <hi type="italic">it</hi> into the king’s hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:6
verses.text: But Jehoshaphat said, <hi type="italic">Is there</hi> not here a prophet of the Lord besides, that we might inquire of him?

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:7
verses.text: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, <hi type="italic">There is</hi> yet one man, by whom we may inquire of the Lord: but I hate him; for he never prophesied good unto me, but always evil: the same <hi type="italic">is</hi> Micaiah the son of Imla. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:8
verses.text: And the king of Israel called for one <hi type="italic">of his</hi> officers, and said, Fetch quickly Micaiah the son of Imla.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:9
verses.text: And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah sat either of them on his throne, clothed in <hi type="italic">their</hi> robes, and they sat in a void place at the entering in of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets prophesied before them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:10
verses.text: And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah had made him horns of iron, and said, Thus saith the Lord, With these thou shalt push Syria until they be consumed.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:11
verses.text: And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and prosper: for the Lord shall deliver <hi type="italic">it</hi> into the hand of the king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:12
verses.text: And the messenger that went to call Micaiah spake to him, saying, Behold, the words of the prophets <hi type="italic">declare</hi> good to the king with one assent; let thy word therefore, I pray thee, be like one of theirs, and speak thou good.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:13
verses.text: And Micaiah said, <hi type="italic">As</hi> the Lord liveth, even what my God saith, that will I speak.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:14
verses.text: And when he was come to the king, the king said unto him, Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And he said, Go ye up, and prosper, and they shall be delivered into your hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:15
verses.text: And the king said to him, How many times shall I adjure thee that thou say nothing but the truth to me in the name of the Lord?

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:16
verses.text: Then he said, I did see all Israel scattered upon the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd: and the Lord said, These have no master; let them return <hi type="italic">therefore</hi> every man to his house in peace.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:17
verses.text: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, Did I not tell thee <hi type="italic">that</hi> he would not prophesy good unto me, but evil?

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:18
verses.text: Again he said, Therefore hear the word of the Lord; I saw the Lord sitting upon his throne, and all the host of heaven standing on his right hand and <hi type="italic">on</hi> his left.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:19
verses.text: And the Lord said, Who shall entice Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead? And one spake saying after this manner, and another saying after that manner.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:20
verses.text: Then there came out a spirit, and stood before the Lord, and said, I will entice him. And the Lord said unto him, Wherewith?

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:21
verses.text: And he said, I will go out, and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And <hi type="italic">the L</hi><hi type="italic">ord</hi> said, Thou shalt entice <hi type="italic">him</hi>, and thou shalt also prevail: go out, and do <hi type="italic">even</hi> so.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:22
verses.text: Now therefore, behold, the Lord hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of these thy prophets, and the Lord hath spoken evil against thee.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:23
verses.text: Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah came near, and smote Micaiah upon the cheek, and said, Which way went the Spirit of the Lord from me to speak unto thee?

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:24
verses.text: And Micaiah said, Behold, thou shalt see on that day when thou shalt go into an inner chamber to hide thyself.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:25
verses.text: Then the king of Israel said, Take ye Micaiah, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son;

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:26
verses.text: And say, Thus saith the king, Put this <hi type="italic">fellow</hi> in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I return in peace.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:27
verses.text: And Micaiah said, If thou certainly return in peace, <hi type="italic">then</hi> hath not the Lord spoken by me. And he said, Hearken, all ye people.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:28
verses.text: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:29
verses.text: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, I will disguise myself, and will go to the battle; but put thou on thy robes. So the king of Israel disguised himself; and they went to the battle.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:30
verses.text: Now the king of Syria had commanded the captains of the chariots that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him, saying, Fight ye not with small or great, save only with the king of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:31
verses.text: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, It <hi type="italic">is</hi> the king of Israel. Therefore they compassed about him to fight: but Jehoshaphat cried out, and the Lord helped him; and God moved them <hi type="italic">to depart</hi> from him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:32
verses.text: For it came to pass, that, when the captains of the chariots perceived that it was not the king of Israel, they turned back again from pursuing him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:33
verses.text: And a <hi type="italic">certain</hi> man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness: therefore he said to his chariot man, Turn thine hand, that thou mayest carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.

verses.name: II Chronicles 18:34
verses.text: And the battle increased that day: howbeit the king of Israel stayed <hi type="italic">himself</hi> up in <hi type="italic">his</hi> chariot against the Syrians until the even: and about the time of the sun going down he died.  <chapter eID="2Chr.18"/><div eID="gen400" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:1
verses.text: AND Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returned to his house in peace to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:2
verses.text: And Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him, and said to king Jehoshaphat, Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the Lord? therefore <hi type="italic">is</hi> wrath upon thee from before the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:3
verses.text: Nevertheless there are good things found in thee, in that thou hast taken away the groves out of the land, and hast prepared thine heart to seek God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:4
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat dwelt at Jerusalem: and he went out again through the people from Beer-sheba to mount Ephraim, and brought them back unto the Lord God of their fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:5
verses.text: ¶ And he set judges in the land throughout all the fenced cities of Judah, city by city,

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:6
verses.text: And said to the judges, Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the Lord, who <hi type="italic">is</hi> with you in the judgment.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:7
verses.text: Wherefore now let the fear of the Lord be upon you; take heed and do <hi type="italic">it:</hi> for <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:8
verses.text: ¶ Moreover in Jerusalem did Jehoshaphat set of the Levites, and <hi type="italic">of</hi> the priests, and of the chief of the fathers of Israel, for the judgment of the Lord, and for controversies, when they returned to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:9
verses.text: And he charged them, saying, Thus shall ye do in the fear of the Lord, faithfully, and with a perfect heart.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:10
verses.text: And what cause soever shall come to you of your brethren that dwell in their cities, between blood and blood, between law and commandment, statutes and judgments, ye shall even warn them that they trespass not against the Lord, and <hi type="italic">so</hi> wrath come upon you, and upon your brethren: this do, and ye shall not trespass.

verses.name: II Chronicles 19:11
verses.text: And, behold, Amariah the chief priest <hi type="italic">is</hi> over you in all matters of the Lord; and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, for all the king’s matters: also the Levites <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> officers before you. Deal courageously, and the Lord shall be with the good.  <chapter eID="2Chr.19"/><div eID="gen401" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:1
verses.text: IT came to pass after this also, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the children of Moab, and the children of Ammon, and with them <hi type="italic">other</hi> beside the Ammonites, came against Jehoshaphat to battle.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:2
verses.text: Then there came some that told Jehoshaphat, saying, There cometh a great multitude against thee from beyond the sea on this side Syria; and, behold, they <hi type="italic">be</hi> in Hazazon-tamar, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> En-gedi.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:3
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat feared, and set himself to seek the Lord, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:4
verses.text: And Judah gathered themselves together, to ask <hi type="italic">help</hi> of the Lord: even out of all the cities of Judah they came to seek the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:5
verses.text: ¶ And Jehoshaphat stood in the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the Lord, before the new court,

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:6
verses.text: And said, O Lord God of our fathers, <hi type="italic">art</hi> not thou God in heaven? and rulest <hi type="italic">not</hi> thou over all the kingdoms of the heathen? and in thine hand <hi type="italic">is there not</hi> power and might, so that none is able to withstand thee?

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:7
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Art</hi> not thou our God, <hi type="italic">who</hi> didst drive out the inhabitants of this land before thy people Israel, and gavest it to the seed of Abraham thy friend for ever?

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:8
verses.text: And they dwelt therein, and have built thee a sanctuary therein for thy name, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:9
verses.text: If, <hi type="italic">when</hi> evil cometh upon us, <hi type="italic">as</hi> the sword, judgment, or pestilence, or famine, we stand before this house, and in thy presence, (for thy name <hi type="italic">is</hi> in this house,) and cry unto thee in our affliction, then thou wilt hear and help.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:10
verses.text: And now, behold, the children of Ammon and Moab and mount Seir, whom thou wouldest not let Israel invade, when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned from them, and destroyed them not;

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:11
verses.text: Behold, <hi type="italic">I say</hi>, <hi type="italic">how</hi> they reward us, to come to cast us out of thy possession, which thou hast given us to inherit.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:12
verses.text: O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes <hi type="italic">are</hi> upon thee.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:13
verses.text: And all Judah stood before the Lord, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:14
verses.text: ¶ Then upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, came the Spirit of the Lord in the midst of the congregation;

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:15
verses.text: And he said, Hearken ye, all Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and thou king Jehoshaphat, Thus saith the Lord unto you, Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle <hi type="italic">is</hi> not yours, but God’s.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:16
verses.text: To morrow go ye down against them: behold, they come up by the cliff of Ziz; and ye shall find them at the end of the brook, before the wilderness of Jeruel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:17
verses.text: Ye shall not <hi type="italic">need</hi> to fight in this <hi type="italic">battle:</hi> set yourselves, stand ye <hi type="italic">still</hi>, and see the salvation of the Lord with you, O Judah and Jerusalem: fear not, nor be dismayed; to morrow go out against them: for the Lord <hi type="italic">will be</hi> with you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:18
verses.text: And Jehoshaphat bowed his head with <hi type="italic">his</hi> face to the ground: and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell before the Lord, worshipping the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:19
verses.text: And the Levites, of the children of the Kohathites, and of the children of the Korhites, stood up to praise the Lord God of Israel with a loud voice on high.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:20
verses.text: ¶ And they rose early in the morning, and went forth into the wilderness of Tekoa: and as they went forth, Jehoshaphat stood and said, Hear me, O Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem; Believe in the Lord your God, so shall ye be established; believe his prophets, so shall ye prosper.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:21
verses.text: And when he had consulted with the people, he appointed singers unto the Lord, and that should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army, and to say, Praise the Lord; for his mercy <hi type="italic">endureth</hi> for ever.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:22
verses.text: ¶ And when they began to sing and to praise, the Lord set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Judah; and they were smitten.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:23
verses.text: For the children of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants of mount Seir, utterly to slay and destroy <hi type="italic">them:</hi> and when they had made an end of the inhabitants of Seir, every one helped to destroy another.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:24
verses.text: And when Judah came toward the watch tower in the wilderness, they looked unto the multitude, and, behold, they <hi type="italic">were</hi> dead bodies fallen to the earth, and none escaped.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:25
verses.text: And when Jehoshaphat and his people came to take away the spoil of them, they found among them in abundance both riches with the dead bodies, and precious jewels, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could carry away: and they were three days in gathering of the spoil, it was so much.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:26
verses.text: ¶ And on the fourth day they assembled themselves in the valley of Berachah; for there they blessed the Lord: therefore the name of the same place was called, The valley of Berachah, unto this day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:27
verses.text: Then they returned, every man of Judah and Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat in the forefront of them, to go again to Jerusalem with joy; for the Lord had made them to rejoice over their enemies.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:28
verses.text: And they came to Jerusalem with psalteries and harps and trumpets unto the house of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:29
verses.text: And the fear of God was on all the kingdoms of <hi type="italic">those</hi> countries, when they had heard that the Lord fought against the enemies of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:30
verses.text: So the realm of Jehoshaphat was quiet: for his God gave him rest round about.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:31
verses.text: ¶ And Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah: <hi type="italic">he was</hi> thirty and five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty and five years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:32
verses.text: And he walked in the way of Asa his father, and departed not from it, doing <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> right in the sight of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:33
verses.text: Howbeit the high places were not taken away: for as yet the people had not prepared their hearts unto the God of their fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:34
verses.text: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, first and last, behold, they <hi type="italic">are</hi> written in the book of Jehu the son of Hanani, who <hi type="italic">is</hi> mentioned in the book of the kings of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:35
verses.text: ¶ And after this did Jehoshaphat king of Judah join himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, who did very wickedly:

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:36
verses.text: And he joined himself with him to make ships to go to Tarshish: and they made the ships in Ezion-geber.

verses.name: II Chronicles 20:37
verses.text: Then Eliezer the son of Dodavah of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, Because thou hast joined thyself with Ahaziah, the Lord hath broken thy works. And the ships were broken, that they were not able to go to Tarshish.  <chapter eID="2Chr.20"/><div eID="gen402" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:1
verses.text: NOW Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And Jehoram his son reigned in his stead.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:2
verses.text: And he had brethren the sons of Jehoshaphat, Azariah, and Jehiel, and Zechariah, and Azariah, and Michael, and Shephatiah: all these <hi type="italic">were</hi> the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:3
verses.text: And their father gave them great gifts of silver, and of gold, and of precious things, with fenced cities in Judah: but the kingdom gave he to Jehoram; because he <hi type="italic">was</hi> the firstborn.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:4
verses.text: Now when Jehoram was risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself, and slew all his brethren with the sword, and <hi type="italic">divers</hi> also of the princes of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:5
verses.text: ¶ Jehoram <hi type="italic">was</hi> thirty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:6
verses.text: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, like as did the house of Ahab: for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife: and he wrought <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> evil in the eyes of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:7
verses.text: Howbeit the Lord would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he promised to give a light to him and to his sons for ever.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:8
verses.text: ¶ In his days the Edomites revolted from under the dominion of Judah, and made themselves a king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:9
verses.text: Then Jehoram went forth with his princes, and all his chariots with him: and he rose up by night, and smote the Edomites which compassed him in, and the captains of the chariots.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:10
verses.text: So the Edomites revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day. The same time <hi type="italic">also</hi> did Libnah revolt from under his hand; because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:11
verses.text: Moreover he made high places in the mountains of Judah, and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication, and compelled Judah <hi type="italic">thereto</hi>.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:12
verses.text: ¶ And there came a writing to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, Thus saith the Lord God of David thy father, Because thou hast not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat thy father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:13
verses.text: But hast walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and hast made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to go a whoring, like to the whoredoms of the house of Ahab, and also hast slain thy brethren of thy father’s house, <hi type="italic">which were</hi> better than thyself:

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:14
verses.text: Behold, with a great plague will the Lord smite thy people, and thy children, and thy wives, and all thy goods:

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:15
verses.text: And thou <hi type="italic">shalt have</hi> great sickness by disease of thy bowels, until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:16
verses.text: ¶ Moreover the Lord stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians, that <hi type="italic">were</hi> near the Ethiopians:

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:17
verses.text: And they came up into Judah, and brake into it, and carried away all the substance that was found in the king’s house, and his sons also, and his wives; so that there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:18
verses.text: ¶ And after all this the Lord smote him in his bowels with an incurable disease.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:19
verses.text: And it came to pass, that in process of time, after the end of two years, his bowels fell out by reason of his sickness: so he died of sore diseases. And his people made no burning for him, like the burning of his fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 21:20
