verses.text: Thirty and two years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem eight years, and departed without being desired. Howbeit they buried him in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings.  <chapter eID="2Chr.21"/><div eID="gen403" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:1
verses.text: AND the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his stead: for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:2
verses.text: Forty and two years old <hi type="italic">was</hi> Ahaziah when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also <hi type="italic">was</hi> Athaliah the daughter of Omri.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:3
verses.text: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counseller to do wickedly.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:4
verses.text: Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the Lord like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellers after the death of his father to his destruction.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:5
verses.text: ¶ He walked also after their counsel, and went with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead: and the Syrians smote Joram.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:6
verses.text: And he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds which were given him at Ramah, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. And Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab at Jezreel, because he was sick.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:7
verses.text: And the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram: for when he was come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:8
verses.text: And it came to pass, that, when Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, and found the princes of Judah, and the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah, that ministered to Ahaziah, he slew them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:9
verses.text: And he sought Ahaziah: and they caught him, (for he was hid in Samaria,) and brought him to Jehu: and when they had slain him, they buried him: Because, said they, he <hi type="italic">is</hi> the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart. So the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep still the kingdom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:10
verses.text: ¶ But when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:11
verses.text: But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, (for she was the sister of Ahaziah,) hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not.

verses.name: II Chronicles 22:12
verses.text: And he was with them hid in the house of God six years: and Athaliah reigned over the land.  <chapter eID="2Chr.22"/><div eID="gen404" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:1
verses.text: AND in the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself, and took the captains of hundreds, Azariah the son of Jeroham, and Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, and Azariah the son of Obed, and Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, into covenant with him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:2
verses.text: And they went about in Judah, and gathered the Levites out of all the cities of Judah, and the chief of the fathers of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:3
verses.text: And all the congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And he said unto them, Behold, the king’s son shall reign, as the Lord hath said of the sons of David.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:4
verses.text: This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the thing that ye shall do; A third part of you entering on the sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> porters of the doors;

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:5
verses.text: And a third part <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> at the king’s house; and a third part at the gate of the foundation: and all the people <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> in the courts of the house of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:6
verses.text: But let none come into the house of the Lord, save the priests, and they that minister of the Levites; they shall go in, for they <hi type="italic">are</hi> holy: but all the people shall keep the watch of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:7
verses.text: And the Levites shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand; and whosoever <hi type="italic">else</hi> cometh into the house, he shall be put to death: but be ye with the king when he cometh in, and when he goeth out.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:8
verses.text: So the Levites and all Judah did according to all things that Jehoiada the priest had commanded, and took every man his men that were to come in on the sabbath, with them that were to go <hi type="italic">out</hi> on the sabbath: for Jehoiada the priest dismissed not the courses.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:9
verses.text: Moreover Jehoiada the priest delivered to the captains of hundreds spears, and bucklers, and shields, that <hi type="italic">had been</hi> king David’s, which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in the house of God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:10
verses.text: And he set all the people, every man having his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the temple to the left side of the temple, along by the altar and the temple, by the king round about.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:11
verses.text: Then they brought out the king’s son, and put upon him the crown, and <hi type="italic">gave him</hi> the testimony, and made him king. And Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and said, God save the king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:12
verses.text: ¶ Now when Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people into the house of the Lord:

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:13
verses.text: And she looked, and, behold, the king stood at his pillar at the entering in, and the princes and the trumpets by the king: and all the people of the land rejoiced, and sounded with trumpets, also the singers with instruments of musick, and such as taught to sing praise. Then Athaliah rent her clothes, and said, Treason, Treason.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:14
verses.text: Then Jehoiada the priest brought out the captains of hundreds that were set over the host, and said unto them, Have her forth of the ranges: and whoso followeth her, let him be slain with the sword. For the priest said, Slay her not in the house of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:15
verses.text: So they laid hands on her; and when she was come to the entering of the horse gate by the king’s house, they slew her there.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:16
verses.text: ¶ And Jehoiada made a covenant between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the Lord’s people.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:17
verses.text: Then all the people went to the house of Baal, and brake it down, and brake his altars and his images in pieces, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:18
verses.text: Also Jehoiada appointed the offices of the house of the Lord by the hand of the priests the Levites, whom David had distributed in the house of the Lord, to offer the burnt offerings of the Lord, as <hi type="italic">it is</hi> written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and with singing, <hi type="italic">as it was ordained</hi> by David.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:19
verses.text: And he set the porters at the gates of the house of the Lord, that none <hi type="italic">which was</hi> unclean in any thing should enter in.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:20
verses.text: And he took the captains of hundreds, and the nobles, and the governors of the people, and all the people of the land, and brought down the king from the house of the Lord: and they came through the high gate into the king’s house, and set the king upon the throne of the kingdom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 23:21
verses.text: And all the people of the land rejoiced: and the city was quiet, after that they had slain Athaliah with the sword.  <chapter eID="2Chr.23"/><div eID="gen405" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:1
verses.text: JOASH <hi type="italic">was</hi> seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also <hi type="italic">was</hi> Zibiah of Beer-sheba.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:2
verses.text: And Joash did <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> right in the sight of the Lord all the days of Jehoiada the priest.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:3
verses.text: And Jehoiada took for him two wives; and he begat sons and daughters.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:4
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass after this, <hi type="italic">that</hi> Joash was minded to repair the house of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:5
verses.text: And he gathered together the priests and the Levites, and said to them, Go out unto the cities of Judah, and gather of all Israel money to repair the house of your God from year to year, and see that ye hasten the matter. Howbeit the Levites hastened <hi type="italic">it</hi> not.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:6
verses.text: And the king called for Jehoiada the chief, and said unto him, Why hast thou not required of the Levites to bring in out of Judah and out of Jerusalem the collection, <hi type="italic">according to the commandment</hi> of Moses the servant of the Lord, and of the congregation of Israel, for the tabernacle of witness?

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:7
verses.text: For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of God; and also all the dedicated things of the house of the Lord did they bestow upon Baalim.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:8
verses.text: And at the king’s commandment they made a chest, and set it without at the gate of the house of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:9
verses.text: And they made a proclamation through Judah and Jerusalem, to bring in to the Lord the collection <hi type="italic">that</hi> Moses the servant of God <hi type="italic">laid</hi> upon Israel in the wilderness.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:10
verses.text: And all the princes and all the people rejoiced, and brought in, and cast into the chest, until they had made an end.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:11
verses.text: Now it came to pass, that at what time the chest was brought unto the king’s office by the hand of the Levites, and when they saw that <hi type="italic">there was</hi> much money, the king’s scribe and the high priest’s officer came and emptied the chest, and took it, and carried it to his place again. Thus they did day by day, and gathered money in abundance.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:12
verses.text: And the king and Jehoiada gave it to such as did the work of the service of the house of the Lord, and hired masons and carpenters to repair the house of the Lord, and also such as wrought iron and brass to mend the house of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:13
verses.text: So the workmen wrought, and the work was perfected by them, and they set the house of God in his state, and strengthened it.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:14
verses.text: And when they had finished <hi type="italic">it</hi>, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Jehoiada, whereof were made vessels for the house of the Lord, <hi type="italic">even</hi> vessels to minister, and to offer <hi type="italic">withal</hi>, and spoons, and vessels of gold and silver. And they offered burnt offerings in the house of the Lord continually all the days of Jehoiada.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:15
verses.text: ¶ But Jehoiada waxed old, and was full of days when he died; an hundred and thirty years old <hi type="italic">was he</hi> when he died.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:16
verses.text: And they buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel, both toward God, and toward his house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:17
verses.text: Now after the death of Jehoiada came the princes of Judah, and made obeisance to the king. Then the king hearkened unto them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:18
verses.text: And they left the house of the Lord God of their fathers, and served groves and idols: and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this their trespass.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:19
verses.text: Yet he sent prophets to them, to bring them again unto the Lord; and they testified against them: but they would not give ear.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:20
verses.text: And the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, which stood above the people, and said unto them, Thus saith God, Why transgress ye the commandments of the Lord, that ye cannot prosper? because ye have forsaken the Lord, he hath also forsaken you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:21
verses.text: And they conspired against him, and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of the house of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:22
verses.text: Thus Joash the king remembered not the kindness which Jehoiada his father had done to him, but slew his son. And when he died, he said, The Lord look upon <hi type="italic">it</hi>, and require <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:23
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass at the end of the year, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the host of Syria came up against him: and they came to Judah and Jerusalem, and destroyed all the princes of the people from among the people, and sent all the spoil of them unto the king of Damascus.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:24
verses.text: For the army of the Syrians came with a small company of men, and the Lord delivered a very great host into their hand, because they had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers. So they executed judgment against Joash.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:25
verses.text: And when they were departed from him, (for they left him in great diseases,) his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and slew him on his bed, and he died: and they buried him in the city of David, but they buried him not in the sepulchres of the kings.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:26
verses.text: And these are they that conspired against him; Zabad the son of Shimeath an Ammonitess, and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith a Moabitess.

verses.name: II Chronicles 24:27
verses.text: ¶ Now <hi type="italic">concerning</hi> his sons, and the greatness of the burdens <hi type="italic">laid</hi> upon him, and the repairing of the house of God, behold, they <hi type="italic">are</hi> written in the story of the book of the kings. And Amaziah his son reigned in his stead.  <chapter eID="2Chr.24"/><div eID="gen406" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:1
verses.text: AMAZIAH <hi type="italic">was</hi> twenty and five years old <hi type="italic">when</hi> he began to reign, and he reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:2
verses.text: And he did <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> right in the sight of the Lord, but not with a perfect heart.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:3
verses.text: ¶ Now it came to pass, when the kingdom was established to him, that he slew his servants that had killed the king his father.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:4
verses.text: But he slew not their children, but <hi type="italic">did</hi> as <hi type="italic">it is</hi> written in the law in the book of Moses, where the Lord commanded, saying, The fathers shall not die for the children, neither shall the children die for the fathers, but every man shall die for his own sin.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:5
verses.text: ¶ Moreover Amaziah gathered Judah together, and made them captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, according to the houses of <hi type="italic">their</hi> fathers, throughout all Judah and Benjamin: and he numbered them from twenty years old and above, and found them three hundred thousand choice <hi type="italic">men</hi>, <hi type="italic">able</hi> to go forth to war, that could handle spear and shield.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:6
verses.text: He hired also an hundred thousand mighty men of valour out of Israel for an hundred talents of silver.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:7
verses.text: But there came a man of God to him, saying, O king, let not the army of Israel go with thee; for the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> not with Israel, <hi type="italic">to wit</hi>, <hi type="italic">with</hi> all the children of Ephraim.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:8
verses.text: But if thou wilt go, do <hi type="italic">it</hi>, be strong for the battle: God shall make thee fall before the enemy: for God hath power to help, and to cast down.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:9
verses.text: And Amaziah said to the man of God, But what shall we do for the hundred talents which I have given to the army of Israel? And the man of God answered, The Lord is able to give thee much more than this.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:10
verses.text: Then Amaziah separated them, <hi type="italic">to wit</hi>, the army that was come to him out of Ephraim, to go home again: wherefore their anger was greatly kindled against Judah, and they returned home in great anger.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:11
verses.text: ¶ And Amaziah strengthened himself, and led forth his people, and went to the valley of salt, and smote of the children of Seir ten thousand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:12
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">other</hi> ten thousand <hi type="italic">left</hi> alive did the children of Judah carry away captive, and brought them unto the top of the rock, and cast them down from the top of the rock, that they all were broken in pieces.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:13
verses.text: ¶ But the soldiers of the army which Amaziah sent back, that they should not go with him to battle, fell upon the cities of Judah, from Samaria even unto Beth-horon, and smote three thousand of them, and took much spoil.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:14
verses.text: ¶ Now it came to pass, after that Amaziah was come from the slaughter of the Edomites, that he brought the gods of the children of Seir, and set them up <hi type="italic">to be</hi> his gods, and bowed down himself before them, and burned incense unto them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:15
verses.text: Wherefore the anger of the Lord was kindled against Amaziah, and he sent unto him a prophet, which said unto him, Why hast thou sought after the gods of the people, which could not deliver their own people out of thine hand?

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:16
verses.text: And it came to pass, as he talked with him, that <hi type="italic">the king</hi> said unto him, Art thou made of the king’s counsel? forbear; why shouldest thou be smitten? Then the prophet forbare, and said, I know that God hath determined to destroy thee, because thou hast done this, and hast not hearkened unto my counsel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:17
verses.text: ¶ Then Amaziah king of Judah took advice, and sent to Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, Come, let us see one another in the face.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:18
verses.text: And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, The thistle that <hi type="italic">was</hi> in Lebanon sent to the cedar that <hi type="italic">was</hi> in Lebanon, saying, Give thy daughter to my son to wife: and there passed by a wild beast that <hi type="italic">was</hi> in Lebanon, and trode down the thistle.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:19
verses.text: Thou sayest, Lo, thou hast smitten the Edomites; and thine heart lifteth thee up to boast: abide now at home; why shouldest thou meddle to <hi type="italic">thine</hi> hurt, that thou shouldest fall, <hi type="italic">even</hi> thou, and Judah with thee?

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:20
verses.text: But Amaziah would not hear; for it <hi type="italic">came</hi> of God, that he might deliver them into the hand <hi type="italic">of their enemies</hi>, because they sought after the gods of Edom.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:21
verses.text: So Joash the king of Israel went up; and they saw one another in the face, <hi type="italic">both</hi> he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, which <hi type="italic">belongeth</hi> to Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:22
verses.text: And Judah was put to the worse before Israel, and they fled every man to his tent.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:23
verses.text: And Joash the king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh, and brought him to Jerusalem, and brake down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:24
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">he took</hi> all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of God with Obed-edom, and the treasures of the king’s house, the hostages also, and returned to Samaria.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:25
verses.text: ¶ And Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lived after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:26
verses.text: Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, first and last, behold, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel?

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:27
verses.text: ¶ Now after the time that Amaziah did turn away from following the Lord they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem; and he fled to Lachish: but they sent to Lachish after him, and slew him there.

verses.name: II Chronicles 25:28
verses.text: And they brought him upon horses, and buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah.  <chapter eID="2Chr.25"/><div eID="gen407" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:1
verses.text: THEN all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who <hi type="italic">was</hi> sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amaziah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:2
verses.text: He built Eloth, and restored it to Judah, after that the king slept with his fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:3
verses.text: Sixteen years old <hi type="italic">was</hi> Uzziah when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty and two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also <hi type="italic">was</hi> Jecoliah of Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:4
verses.text: And he did <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Amaziah did.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:5
verses.text: And he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God: and as long as he sought the Lord, God made him to prosper.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:6
verses.text: And he went forth and warred against the Philistines, and brake down the wall of Gath, and the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod, and built cities about Ashdod, and among the Philistines.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:7
verses.text: And God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians that dwelt in Gur-baal, and the Mehunims.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:8
verses.text: And the Ammonites gave gifts to Uzziah: and his name spread abroad <hi type="italic">even</hi> to the entering in of Egypt; for he strengthened <hi type="italic">himself</hi> exceedingly.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:9
verses.text: Moreover Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate, and at the valley gate, and at the turning <hi type="italic">of the wall</hi>, and fortified them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:10
verses.text: Also he built towers in the desert, and digged many wells: for he had much cattle, both in the low country, and in the plains: husbandmen <hi type="italic">also</hi>, and vine dressers in the mountains, and in Carmel: for he loved husbandry.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:11
verses.text: Moreover Uzziah had an host of fighting men, that went out to war by bands, according to the number of their account by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the ruler, under the hand of Hananiah, <hi type="italic">one</hi> of the king’s captains.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:12
verses.text: The whole number of the chief of the fathers of the mighty men of valour <hi type="italic">were</hi> two thousand and six hundred.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:13
verses.text: And under their hand <hi type="italic">was</hi> an army, three hundred thousand and seven thousand and five hundred, that made war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:14
verses.text: And Uzziah prepared for them throughout all the host shields, and spears, and helmets, and habergeons, and bows, and slings <hi type="italic">to cast</hi> stones.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:15
verses.text: And he made in Jerusalem engines, invented by cunning men, to be on the towers and upon the bulwarks, to shoot arrows and great stones withal. And his name spread far abroad; for he was marvellously helped, till he was strong.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:16
verses.text: ¶ But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to <hi type="italic">his</hi> destruction: for he transgressed against the Lord his God, and went into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:17
verses.text: And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him fourscore priests of the Lord, <hi type="italic">that were</hi> valiant men:

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:18
verses.text: And they withstood Uzziah the king, and said unto him, <hi type="italic">It appertaineth</hi> not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the Lord, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed; neither <hi type="italic">shall it be</hi> for thine honour from the Lord God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:19
verses.text: Then Uzziah was wroth, and <hi type="italic">had</hi> a censer in his hand to burn incense: and while he was wroth with the priests, the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests in the house of the Lord, from beside the incense altar.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:20
verses.text: And Azariah the chief priest, and all the priests, looked upon him, and, behold, he <hi type="italic">was</hi> leprous in his forehead, and they thrust him out from thence; yea, himself hasted also to go out, because the Lord had smitten him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:21
verses.text: And Uzziah the king was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a several house, <hi type="italic">being</hi> a leper; for he was cut off from the house of the Lord: and Jotham his son <hi type="italic">was</hi> over the king’s house, judging the people of the land.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:22
verses.text: ¶ Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, first and last, did Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, write.

verses.name: II Chronicles 26:23
verses.text: So Uzziah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the burial which <hi type="italic">belonged</hi> to the kings; for they said, He <hi type="italic">is</hi> a leper: and Jotham his son reigned in his stead.  <chapter eID="2Chr.26"/><div eID="gen408" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:1
verses.text: JOTHAM <hi type="italic">was</hi> twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also <hi type="italic">was</hi> Jerushah, the daughter of Zadok.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:2
verses.text: And he did <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Uzziah did: howbeit he entered not into the temple of the Lord. And the people did yet corruptly.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:3
verses.text: He built the high gate of the house of the Lord, and on the wall of Ophel he built much.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:4
verses.text: Moreover he built cities in the mountains of Judah, and in the forests he built castles and towers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:5
verses.text: ¶ He fought also with the king of the Ammonites, and prevailed against them. And the children of Ammon gave him the same year an hundred talents of silver, and ten thousand measures of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. So much did the children of Ammon pay unto him, both the second year, and the third.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:6
verses.text: So Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the Lord his God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:7
verses.text: ¶ Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars, and his ways, lo, they <hi type="italic">are</hi> written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:8
verses.text: He was five and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 27:9
verses.text: ¶ And Jotham slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David: and Ahaz his son reigned in his stead.  <chapter eID="2Chr.27"/><div eID="gen409" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:1
verses.text: AHAZ <hi type="italic">was</hi> twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem: but he did not <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> right in the sight of the Lord, like David his father:

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:2
verses.text: For he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and made also molten images for Baalim.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:3
verses.text: Moreover he burnt incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burnt his children in the fire, after the abominations of the heathen whom the Lord had cast out before the children of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:4
verses.text: He sacrificed also and burnt incense in the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:5
verses.text: Wherefore the Lord his God delivered him into the hand of the king of Syria; and they smote him, and carried away a great multitude of them captives, and brought <hi type="italic">them</hi> to Damascus. And he was also delivered into the hand of the king of Israel, who smote him with a great slaughter.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:6
verses.text: ¶ For Pekah the son of Remaliah slew in Judah an hundred and twenty thousand in one day, <hi type="italic">which were</hi> all valiant men; because they had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:7
verses.text: And Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, slew Maaseiah the king’s son, and Azrikam the governor of the house, and Elkanah <hi type="italic">that was</hi> next to the king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:8
verses.text: And the children of Israel carried away captive of their brethren two hundred thousand, women, sons, and daughters, and took also away much spoil from them, and brought the spoil to Samaria.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:9
verses.text: But a prophet of the Lord was there, whose name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Oded: and he went out before the host that came to Samaria, and said unto them, Behold, because the Lord God of your fathers was wroth with Judah, he hath delivered them into your hand, and ye have slain them in a rage <hi type="italic">that</hi> reacheth up unto heaven.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:10
verses.text: And now ye purpose to keep under the children of Judah and Jerusalem for bondmen and bondwomen unto you: <hi type="italic">but are there</hi> not with you, even with you, sins against the Lord your God?

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:11
verses.text: Now hear me therefore, and deliver the captives again, which ye have taken captive of your brethren: for the fierce wrath of the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> upon you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:12
verses.text: Then certain of the heads of the children of Ephraim, Azariah the son of Johanan, Berechiah the son of Meshillemoth, and Jehizkiah the son of Shallum, and Amasa the son of Hadlai, stood up against them that came from the war,

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:13
verses.text: And said unto them, Ye shall not bring in the captives hither: for whereas we have offended against the Lord <hi type="italic">already</hi>, ye intend to add <hi type="italic">more</hi> to our sins and to our trespass: for our trespass is great, and <hi type="italic">there is</hi> fierce wrath against Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:14
verses.text: So the armed men left the captives and the spoil before the princes and all the congregation.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:15
verses.text: And the men which were expressed by name rose up, and took the captives, and with the spoil clothed all that were naked among them, and arrayed them, and shod them, and gave them to eat and to drink, and anointed them, and carried all the feeble of them upon asses, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brethren: then they returned to Samaria.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:16
verses.text: ¶ At that time did king Ahaz send unto the kings of Assyria to help him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:17
verses.text: For again the Edomites had come and smitten Judah, and carried away captives.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:18
verses.text: The Philistines also had invaded the cities of the low country, and of the south of Judah, and had taken Beth-shemesh, and Ajalon, and Gederoth, and Shocho with the villages thereof, and Timnah with the villages thereof, Gimzo also and the villages thereof: and they dwelt there.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:19
verses.text: For the Lord brought Judah low because of Ahaz king of Israel; for he made Judah naked, and transgressed sore against the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:20
verses.text: And Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came unto him, and distressed him, but strengthened him not.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:21
verses.text: For Ahaz took away a portion <hi type="italic">out</hi> of the house of the Lord, and <hi type="italic">out</hi> of the house of the king, and of the princes, and gave <hi type="italic">it</hi> unto the king of Assyria: but he helped him not.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:22
verses.text: ¶ And in the time of his distress did he trespass yet more against the Lord: this <hi type="italic">is that</hi> king Ahaz.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:23
verses.text: For he sacrificed unto the gods of Damascus, which smote him: and he said, Because the gods of the kings of Syria help them, <hi type="italic">therefore</hi> will I sacrifice to them, that they may help me. But they were the ruin of him, and of all Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:24
verses.text: And Ahaz gathered together the vessels of the house of God, and cut in pieces the vessels of the house of God, and shut up the doors of the house of the Lord, and he made him altars in every corner of Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:25
verses.text: And in every several city of Judah he made high places to burn incense unto other gods, and provoked to anger the Lord God of his fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:26
verses.text: ¶ Now the rest of his acts and of all his ways, first and last, behold, they <hi type="italic">are</hi> written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 28:27
verses.text: And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, <hi type="italic">even</hi> in Jerusalem: but they brought him not into the sepulchres of the kings of Israel: and Hezekiah his son reigned in his stead.  <chapter eID="2Chr.28"/><div eID="gen410" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:1
verses.text: HEZEKIAH began to reign <hi type="italic">when he was</hi> five and twenty years old, and he reigned nine and twenty years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:2
verses.text: And he did <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:3
verses.text: ¶ He in the first year of his reign, in the first month, opened the doors of the house of the Lord, and repaired them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:4
verses.text: And he brought in the priests and the Levites, and gathered them together into the east street,

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:5
verses.text: And said unto them, Hear me, ye Levites, sanctify now yourselves, and sanctify the house of the Lord God of your fathers, and carry forth the filthiness out of the holy <hi type="italic">place</hi>.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:6
verses.text: For our fathers have trespassed, and done <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> evil in the eyes of the Lord our God, and have forsaken him, and have turned away their faces from the habitation of the Lord, and turned <hi type="italic">their</hi> backs.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:7
verses.text: Also they have shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps, and have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the holy <hi type="italic">place</hi> unto the God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:8
verses.text: Wherefore the wrath of the Lord was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he hath delivered them to trouble, to astonishment, and to hissing, as ye see with your eyes.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:9
verses.text: For, lo, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives <hi type="italic">are</hi> in captivity for this.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:10
verses.text: Now <hi type="italic">it is</hi> in mine heart to make a covenant with the Lord God of Israel, that his fierce wrath may turn away from us.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:11
verses.text: My sons, be not now negligent: for the Lord hath chosen you to stand before him, to serve him, and that ye should minister unto him, and burn incense.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:12
verses.text: ¶ Then the Levites arose, Mahath the son of Amasai, and Joel the son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites: and of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi, and Azariah the son of Jehalelel: and of the Gershonites; Joah the son of Zimmah, and Eden the son of Joah:

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:13
verses.text: And of the sons of Elizaphan; Shimri, and Jeiel: and of the sons of Asaph; Zechariah, and Mattaniah:

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:14
verses.text: And of the sons of Heman; Jehiel, and Shimei: and of the sons of Jeduthun; Shemaiah, and Uzziel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:15
verses.text: And they gathered their brethren, and sanctified themselves, and came, according to the commandment of the king, by the words of the Lord, to cleanse the house of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:16
verses.text: And the priests went into the inner part of the house of the Lord, to cleanse <hi type="italic">it</hi>, and brought out all the uncleanness that they found in the temple of the Lord into the court of the house of the Lord. And the Levites took <hi type="italic">it</hi>, to carry <hi type="italic">it</hi> out abroad into the brook Kidron.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:17
verses.text: Now they began on the first <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the first month to sanctify, and on the eighth day of the month came they to the porch of the Lord: so they sanctified the house of the Lord in eight days; and in the sixteenth day of the first month they made an end.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:18
verses.text: Then they went in to Hezekiah the king, and said, We have cleansed all the house of the Lord, and the altar of burnt offering, with all the vessels thereof, and the shewbread table, with all the vessels thereof.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:19
verses.text: Moreover all the vessels, which king Ahaz in his reign did cast away in his transgression, have we prepared and sanctified, and, behold, they <hi type="italic">are</hi> before the altar of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:20
verses.text: ¶ Then Hezekiah the king rose early, and gathered the rulers of the city, and went up to the house of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:21
verses.text: And they brought seven bullocks, and seven rams, and seven lambs, and seven he goats, for a sin offering for the kingdom, and for the sanctuary, and for Judah. And he commanded the priests the sons of Aaron to offer <hi type="italic">them</hi> on the altar of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:22
verses.text: So they killed the bullocks, and the priests received the blood, and sprinkled <hi type="italic">it</hi> on the altar: likewise, when they had killed the rams, they sprinkled the blood upon the altar: they killed also the lambs, and they sprinkled the blood upon the altar.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:23
verses.text: And they brought forth the he goats <hi type="italic">for</hi> the sin offering before the king and the congregation; and they laid their hands upon them:

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:24
verses.text: And the priests killed them, and they made reconciliation with their blood upon the altar, to make an atonement for all Israel: for the king commanded <hi type="italic">that</hi> the burnt offering and the sin offering <hi type="italic">should be made</hi> for all Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:25
verses.text: And he set the Levites in the house of the Lord with cymbals, with psalteries, and with harps, according to the commandment of David, and of Gad the king’s seer, and Nathan the prophet: for <hi type="italic">so was</hi> the commandment of the Lord by his prophets.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:26
verses.text: And the Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:27
verses.text: And Hezekiah commanded to offer the burnt offering upon the altar. And when the burnt offering began, the song of the Lord began <hi type="italic">also</hi> with the trumpets, and with the instruments <hi type="italic">ordained</hi> by David king of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:28
verses.text: And all the congregation worshipped, and the singers sang, and the trumpeters sounded: <hi type="italic">and</hi> all <hi type="italic">this continued</hi> until the burnt offering was finished.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:29
verses.text: And when they had made an end of offering, the king and all that were present with him bowed themselves, and worshipped.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:30
verses.text: Moreover Hezekiah the king and the princes commanded the Levites to sing praise unto the Lord with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer. And they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshipped.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:31
verses.text: Then Hezekiah answered and said, Now ye have consecrated yourselves unto the Lord, come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings into the house of the Lord. And the congregation brought in sacrifices and thank offerings; and as many as were of a free heart burnt offerings.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:32
verses.text: And the number of the burnt offerings, which the congregation brought, was threescore and ten bullocks, an hundred rams, <hi type="italic">and</hi> two hundred lambs: all these <hi type="italic">were</hi> for a burnt offering to the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:33
verses.text: And the consecrated things <hi type="italic">were</hi> six hundred oxen and three thousand sheep.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:34
verses.text: But the priests were too few, so that they could not flay all the burnt offerings: wherefore their brethren the Levites did help them, till the work was ended, and until the <hi type="italic">other</hi> priests had sanctified themselves: for the Levites <hi type="italic">were</hi> more upright in heart to sanctify themselves than the priests.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:35
verses.text: And also the burnt offerings <hi type="italic">were</hi> in abundance, with the fat of the peace offerings, and the drink offerings for <hi type="italic">every</hi> burnt offering. So the service of the house of the Lord was set in order.

verses.name: II Chronicles 29:36
verses.text: And Hezekiah rejoiced, and all the people, that God had prepared the people: for the thing was <hi type="italic">done</hi> suddenly.  <chapter eID="2Chr.29"/><div eID="gen411" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:1
verses.text: AND Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, to keep the passover unto the Lord God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:2
verses.text: For the king had taken counsel, and his princes, and all the congregation in Jerusalem, to keep the passover in the second month.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:3
verses.text: For they could not keep it at that time, because the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently, neither had the people gathered themselves together to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:4
verses.text: And the thing pleased the king and all the congregation.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:5
verses.text: So they established a decree to make proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beer-sheba even to Dan, that they should come to keep the passover unto the Lord God of Israel at Jerusalem: for they had not done <hi type="italic">it</hi> of a long <hi type="italic">time in such sort</hi> as it was written.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:6
verses.text: So the posts went with the letters from the king and his princes throughout all Israel and Judah, and according to the commandment of the king, saying, Ye children of Israel, turn again unto the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:7
verses.text: And be not ye like your fathers, and like your brethren, which trespassed against the Lord God of their fathers, <hi type="italic">who</hi> therefore gave them up to desolation, as ye see.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:8
verses.text: Now be ye not stiffnecked, as your fathers <hi type="italic">were</hi>, <hi type="italic">but</hi> yield yourselves unto the Lord, and enter into his sanctuary, which he hath sanctified for ever: and serve the Lord your God, that the fierceness of his wrath may turn away from you.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:9
verses.text: For if ye turn again unto the Lord, your brethren and your children <hi type="italic">shall find</hi> compassion before them that lead them captive, so that they shall come again into this land: for the Lord your God <hi type="italic">is</hi> gracious and merciful, and will not turn away <hi type="italic">his</hi> face from you, if ye return unto him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:10
verses.text: So the posts passed from city to city through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh even unto Zebulun: but they laughed them to scorn, and mocked them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:11
verses.text: Nevertheless divers of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and came to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:12
verses.text: Also in Judah the hand of God was to give them one heart to do the commandment of the king and of the princes, by the word of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:13
verses.text: ¶ And there assembled at Jerusalem much people to keep the feast of unleavened bread in the second month, a very great congregation.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:14
verses.text: And they arose and took away the altars that <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Jerusalem, and all the altars for incense took they away, and cast <hi type="italic">them</hi> into the brook Kidron.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:15
verses.text: Then they killed the passover on the fourteenth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the second month: and the priests and the Levites were ashamed, and sanctified themselves, and brought in the burnt offerings into the house of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:16
verses.text: And they stood in their place after their manner, according to the law of Moses the man of God: the priests sprinkled the blood, <hi type="italic">which they received</hi> of the hand of the Levites.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:17
verses.text: For <hi type="italic">there were</hi> many in the congregation that were not sanctified: therefore the Levites had the charge of the killing of the passovers for every one <hi type="italic">that was</hi> not clean, to sanctify <hi type="italic">them</hi> unto the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:18
verses.text: For a multitude of the people, <hi type="italic">even</hi> many of Ephraim, and Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves, yet did they eat the passover otherwise than it was written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, The good Lord pardon every one

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:19
verses.text: <hi type="italic">That</hi> prepareth his heart to seek God, the Lord God of his fathers, though <hi type="italic">he be</hi> not <hi type="italic">cleansed</hi> according to the purification of the sanctuary.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:20
verses.text: And the Lord hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:21
verses.text: And the children of Israel that were present at Jerusalem kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness: and the Levites and the priests praised the Lord day by day, <hi type="italic">singing</hi> with loud instruments unto the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:22
verses.text: And Hezekiah spake comfortably unto all the Levites that taught the good knowledge of the Lord: and they did eat throughout the feast seven days, offering peace offerings, and making confession to the Lord God of their fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:23
verses.text: And the whole assembly took counsel to keep other seven days: and they kept <hi type="italic">other</hi> seven days with gladness.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:24
verses.text: For Hezekiah king of Judah did give to the congregation a thousand bullocks and seven thousand sheep; and the princes gave to the congregation a thousand bullocks and ten thousand sheep: and a great number of priests sanctified themselves.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:25
verses.text: And all the congregation of Judah, with the priests and the Levites, and all the congregation that came out of Israel, and the strangers that came out of the land of Israel, and that dwelt in Judah, rejoiced.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:26
verses.text: So there was great joy in Jerusalem: for since the time of Solomon the son of David king of Israel <hi type="italic">there was</hi> not the like in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 30:27
verses.text: ¶ Then the priests the Levites arose and blessed the people: and their voice was heard, and their prayer came <hi type="italic">up</hi> to his holy dwelling place, <hi type="italic">even</hi> unto heaven.  <chapter eID="2Chr.30"/><div eID="gen412" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:1
verses.text: NOW when all this was finished, all Israel that were present went out to the cities of Judah, and brake the images in pieces, and cut down the groves, and threw down the high places and the altars out of all Judah and Benjamin, in Ephraim also and Manasseh, until they had utterly destroyed them all. Then all the children of Israel returned, every man to his possession, into their own cities.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:2
verses.text: ¶ And Hezekiah appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites after their courses, every man according to his service, the priests and Levites for burnt offerings and for peace offerings, to minister, and to give thanks, and to praise in the gates of the tents of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:3
verses.text: <hi type="italic">He appointed</hi> also the king’s portion of his substance for the burnt offerings, <hi type="italic">to wit</hi>, for the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the sabbaths, and for the new moons, and for the set feasts, as <hi type="italic">it is</hi> written in the law of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:4
verses.text: Moreover he commanded the people that dwelt in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that they might be encouraged in the law of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:5
verses.text: ¶ And as soon as the commandment came abroad, the children of Israel brought in abundance the firstfruits of corn, wine, and oil, and honey, and of all the increase of the field; and the tithe of all <hi type="italic">things</hi> brought they in abundantly.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:6
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">concerning</hi> the children of Israel and Judah, that dwelt in the cities of Judah, they also brought in the tithe of oxen and sheep, and the tithe of holy things which were consecrated unto the Lord their God, and laid <hi type="italic">them</hi> by heaps.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:7
verses.text: In the third month they began to lay the foundation of the heaps, and finished <hi type="italic">them</hi> in the seventh month.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:8
verses.text: And when Hezekiah and the princes came and saw the heaps, they blessed the Lord, and his people Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:9
verses.text: Then Hezekiah questioned with the priests and the Levites concerning the heaps.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:10
verses.text: And Azariah the chief priest of the house of Zadok answered him, and said, Since <hi type="italic">the people</hi> began to bring the offerings into the house of the Lord, we have had enough to eat, and have left plenty: for the Lord hath blessed his people; and that which is left <hi type="italic">is</hi> this great store.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:11
verses.text: ¶ Then Hezekiah commanded to prepare chambers in the house of the Lord; and they prepared <hi type="italic">them</hi>,

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:12
verses.text: And brought in the offerings and the tithes and the dedicated <hi type="italic">things</hi> faithfully: over which Cononiah the Levite <hi type="italic">was</hi> ruler, and Shimei his brother <hi type="italic">was</hi> the next.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:13
verses.text: And Jehiel, and Azaziah, and Nahath, and Asahel, and Jerimoth, and Jozabad, and Eliel, and Ismachiah, and Mahath, and Benaiah, <hi type="italic">were</hi> overseers under the hand of Cononiah and Shimei his brother, at the commandment of Hezekiah the king, and Azariah the ruler of the house of God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:14
verses.text: And Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, the porter toward the east, <hi type="italic">was</hi> over the freewill offerings of God, to distribute the oblations of the Lord, and the most holy things.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:15
verses.text: And next him <hi type="italic">were</hi> Eden, and Miniamin, and Jeshua, and Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, in <hi type="italic">their</hi> set office, to give to their brethren by courses, as well to the great as to the small:

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:16
verses.text: Beside their genealogy of males, from three years old and upward, <hi type="italic">even</hi> unto every one that entereth into the house of the Lord, his daily portion for their service in their charges according to their courses;

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:17
verses.text: Both to the genealogy of the priests by the house of their fathers, and the Levites from twenty years old and upward, in their charges by their courses;

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:18
verses.text: And to the genealogy of all their little ones, their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, through all the congregation: for in their set office they sanctified themselves in holiness:

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:19
verses.text: Also of the sons of Aaron the priests, <hi type="italic">which were</hi> in the fields of the suburbs of their cities, in every several city, the men that were expressed by name, to give portions to all the males among the priests, and to all that were reckoned by genealogies among the Levites.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:20
verses.text: ¶ And thus did Hezekiah throughout all Judah, and wrought <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> good and right and truth before the Lord his God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 31:21
verses.text: And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did <hi type="italic">it</hi> with all his heart, and prospered.  <chapter eID="2Chr.31"/><div eID="gen413" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:1
verses.text: AFTER these things, and the establishment thereof, Sennacherib king of Assyria came, and entered into Judah, and encamped against the fenced cities, and thought to win them for himself.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:2
verses.text: And when Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib was come, and that he was purposed to fight against Jerusalem,

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:3
verses.text: He took counsel with his princes and his mighty men to stop the waters of the fountains which <hi type="italic">were</hi> without the city: and they did help him.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:4
verses.text: So there was gathered much people together, who stopped all the fountains, and the brook that ran through the midst of the land, saying, Why should the kings of Assyria come, and find much water?

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:5
verses.text: Also he strengthened himself, and built up all the wall that was broken, and raised <hi type="italic">it</hi> up to the towers, and another wall without, and repaired Millo <hi type="italic">in</hi> the city of David, and made darts and shields in abundance.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:6
verses.text: And he set captains of war over the people, and gathered them together to him in the street of the gate of the city, and spake comfortably to them, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:7
verses.text: Be strong and courageous, be not afraid nor dismayed for the king of Assyria, nor for all the multitude that <hi type="italic">is</hi> with him: for <hi type="italic">there be</hi> more with us than with him:

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:8
verses.text: With him <hi type="italic">is</hi> an arm of flesh; but with us <hi type="italic">is</hi> the Lord our God to help us, and to fight our battles. And the people rested themselves upon the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:9
verses.text: ¶ After this did Sennacherib king of Assyria send his servants to Jerusalem, (but he <hi type="italic">himself laid siege</hi> against Lachish, and all his power with him,) unto Hezekiah king of Judah, and unto all Judah that <hi type="italic">were</hi> at Jerusalem, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:10
verses.text: Thus saith Sennacherib king of Assyria, Whereon do ye trust, that ye abide in the siege in Jerusalem?

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:11
verses.text: Doth not Hezekiah persuade you to give over yourselves to die by famine and by thirst, saying, The Lord our God shall deliver us out of the hand of the king of Assyria?

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:12
verses.text: Hath not the same Hezekiah taken away his high places and his altars, and commanded Judah and Jerusalem, saying, Ye shall worship before one altar, and burn incense upon it?

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:13
verses.text: Know ye not what I and my fathers have done unto all the people of <hi type="italic">other</hi> lands? were the gods of the nations of those lands any ways able to deliver their lands out of mine hand?

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:14
verses.text: Who <hi type="italic">was there</hi> among all the gods of those nations that my fathers utterly destroyed, that could deliver his people out of mine hand, that your God should be able to deliver you out of mine hand?

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:15
verses.text: Now therefore let not Hezekiah deceive you, nor persuade you on this manner, neither yet believe him: for no god of any nation or kingdom was able to deliver his people out of mine hand, and out of the hand of my fathers: how much less shall your God deliver you out of mine hand?

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:16
verses.text: And his servants spake yet <hi type="italic">more</hi> against the Lord God, and against his servant Hezekiah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:17
verses.text: He wrote also letters to rail on the Lord God of Israel, and to speak against him, saying, As the gods of the nations of <hi type="italic">other</hi> lands have not delivered their people out of mine hand, so shall not the God of Hezekiah deliver his people out of mine hand.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:18
verses.text: Then they cried with a loud voice in the Jews’ speech unto the people of Jerusalem that <hi type="italic">were</hi> on the wall, to affright them, and to trouble them; that they might take the city.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:19
verses.text: And they spake against the God of Jerusalem, as against the gods of the people of the earth, <hi type="italic">which were</hi> the work of the hands of man.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:20
verses.text: And for this <hi type="italic">cause</hi> Hezekiah the king, and the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz, prayed and cried to heaven.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:21
verses.text: ¶ And the Lord sent an angel, which cut off all the mighty men of valour, and the leaders and captains in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned with shame of face to his own land. And when he was come into the house of his god, they that came forth of his own bowels slew him there with the sword.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:22
verses.text: Thus the Lord saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib the king of Assyria, and from the hand of all <hi type="italic">other</hi>, and guided them on every side.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:23
verses.text: And many brought gifts unto the Lord to Jerusalem, and presents to Hezekiah king of Judah: so that he was magnified in the sight of all nations from thenceforth.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:24
verses.text: ¶ In those days Hezekiah was sick to the death, and prayed unto the Lord: and he spake unto him, and he gave him a sign.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:25
verses.text: But Hezekiah rendered not again according to the benefit <hi type="italic">done</hi> unto him; for his heart was lifted up: therefore there was wrath upon him, and upon Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:26
verses.text: Notwithstanding Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, <hi type="italic">both</hi> he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the Lord came not upon them in the days of Hezekiah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:27
verses.text: ¶ And Hezekiah had exceeding much riches and honour: and he made himself treasuries for silver, and for gold, and for precious stones, and for spices, and for shields, and for all manner of pleasant jewels;

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:28
verses.text: Storehouses also for the increase of corn, and wine, and oil; and stalls for all manner of beasts, and cotes for flocks.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:29
verses.text: Moreover he provided him cities, and possessions of flocks and herds in abundance: for God had given him substance very much.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:30
verses.text: This same Hezekiah also stopped the upper watercourse of Gihon, and brought it straight down to the west side of the city of David. And Hezekiah prospered in all his works.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:31
verses.text: ¶ Howbeit in <hi type="italic">the business of</hi> the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon, who sent unto him to inquire of the wonder that was <hi type="italic">done</hi> in the land, God left him, to try him, that he might know all <hi type="italic">that was</hi> in his heart.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:32
verses.text: ¶ Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and his goodness, behold, they <hi type="italic">are</hi> written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, <hi type="italic">and</hi> in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 32:33
verses.text: And Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the chiefest of the sepulchres of the sons of David: and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did him honour at his death. And Manasseh his son reigned in his stead.  <chapter eID="2Chr.32"/><div eID="gen414" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:1
verses.text: MANASSEH <hi type="italic">was</hi> twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty and five years in Jerusalem:

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:2
verses.text: But did <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> evil in the sight of the Lord, like unto the abominations of the heathen, whom the Lord had cast out before the children of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:3
verses.text: ¶ For he built again the high places which Hezekiah his father had broken down, and he reared up altars for Baalim, and made groves, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:4
verses.text: Also he built altars in the house of the Lord, whereof the Lord had said, In Jerusalem shall my name be for ever.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:5
verses.text: And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:6
verses.text: And he caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom: also he observed times, and used enchantments, and used witchcraft, and dealt with a familiar spirit, and with wizards: he wrought much evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:7
verses.text: And he set a carved image, the idol which he had made, in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen before all the tribes of Israel, will I put my name for ever:

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:8
verses.text: Neither will I any more remove the foot of Israel from out of the land which I have appointed for your fathers; so that they will take heed to do all that I have commanded them, according to the whole law and the statutes and the ordinances by the hand of Moses.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:9
verses.text: So Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, <hi type="italic">and</hi> to do worse than the heathen, whom the Lord had destroyed before the children of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:10
verses.text: And the Lord spake to Manasseh, and to his people: but they would not hearken.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:11
verses.text: ¶ Wherefore the Lord brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, which took Manasseh among the thorns, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:12
verses.text: And when he was in affliction, he besought the Lord his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers,

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:13
verses.text: And prayed unto him: and he was intreated of him, and heard his supplication, and brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the Lord he <hi type="italic">was</hi> God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:14
verses.text: Now after this he built a wall without the city of David, on the west side of Gihon, in the valley, even to the entering in at the fish gate, and compassed about Ophel, and raised it up a very great height, and put captains of war in all the fenced cities of Judah.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:15
verses.text: And he took away the strange gods, and the idol out of the house of the Lord, and all the altars that he had built in the mount of the house of the Lord, and in Jerusalem, and cast <hi type="italic">them</hi> out of the city.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:16
verses.text: And he repaired the altar of the Lord, and sacrificed thereon peace offerings and thank offerings, and commanded Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:17
verses.text: Nevertheless the people did sacrifice still in the high places, <hi type="italic">yet</hi> unto the Lord their God only.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:18
verses.text: ¶ Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God, and the words of the seers that spake to him in the name of the Lord God of Israel, behold, they <hi type="italic">are written</hi> in the book of the kings of Israel.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:19
verses.text: His prayer also, and <hi type="italic">how God</hi> was intreated of him, and all his sin, and his trespass, and the places wherein he built high places, and set up groves and graven images, before he was humbled: behold, they <hi type="italic">are</hi> written among the sayings of the seers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:20
verses.text: ¶ So Manasseh slept with his fathers, and they buried him in his own house: and Amon his son reigned in his stead.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:21
verses.text: ¶ Amon <hi type="italic">was</hi> two and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned two years in Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:22
verses.text: But he did <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> evil in the sight of the Lord, as did Manasseh his father: for Amon sacrificed unto all the carved images which Manasseh his father had made, and served them;

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:23
verses.text: And humbled not himself before the Lord, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; but Amon trespassed more and more.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:24
verses.text: And his servants conspired against him, and slew him in his own house.

verses.name: II Chronicles 33:25
verses.text: ¶ But the people of the land slew all them that had conspired against king Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his stead.  <chapter eID="2Chr.33"/><div eID="gen415" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:1
verses.text: JOSIAH <hi type="italic">was</hi> eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem one and thirty years.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:2
verses.text: And he did <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the ways of David his father, and declined <hi type="italic">neither</hi> to the right hand, nor to the left.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:3
verses.text: ¶ For in the eighth year of his reign, while he was yet young, he began to seek after the God of David his father: and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, and the groves, and the carved images, and the molten images.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:4
verses.text: And they brake down the altars of Baalim in his presence; and the images, that <hi type="italic">were</hi> on high above them, he cut down; and the groves, and the carved images, and the molten images, he brake in pieces, and made dust <hi type="italic">of them</hi>, and strowed <hi type="italic">it</hi> upon the graves of them that had sacrificed unto them.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:5
verses.text: And he burnt the bones of the priests upon their altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:6
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">so did he</hi> in the cities of Manasseh, and Ephraim, and Simeon, even unto Naphtali, with their mattocks round about.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:7
verses.text: And when he had broken down the altars and the groves, and had beaten the graven images into powder, and cut down all the idols throughout all the land of Israel, he returned to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:8
verses.text: ¶ Now in the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had purged the land, and the house, he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, and Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the son of Joahaz the recorder, to repair the house of the Lord his God.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:9
verses.text: And when they came to Hilkiah the high priest, they delivered the money that was brought into the house of God, which the Levites that kept the doors had gathered of the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim, and of all the remnant of Israel, and of all Judah and Benjamin; and they returned to Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:10
verses.text: And they put <hi type="italic">it</hi> in the hand of the workmen that had the oversight of the house of the Lord, and they gave it to the workmen that wrought in the house of the Lord, to repair and amend the house:

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:11
verses.text: Even to the artificers and builders gave they <hi type="italic">it</hi>, to buy hewn stone, and timber for couplings, and to floor the houses which the kings of Judah had destroyed.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:12
verses.text: And the men did the work faithfully: and the overseers of them <hi type="italic">were</hi> Jahath and Obadiah, the Levites, of the sons of Merari; and Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Kohathites, to set <hi type="italic">it</hi> forward; and <hi type="italic">other of</hi> the Levites, all that could skill of instruments of musick.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:13
verses.text: Also <hi type="italic">they were</hi> over the bearers of burdens, and <hi type="italic">were</hi> overseers of all that wrought the work in any manner of service: and of the Levites <hi type="italic">there were</hi> scribes, and officers, and porters.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:14
verses.text: ¶ And when they brought out the money that was brought into the house of the Lord, Hilkiah the priest found a book of the law of the Lord <hi type="italic">given</hi> by Moses.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:15
verses.text: And Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe, I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Hilkiah delivered the book to Shaphan.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:16
verses.text: And Shaphan carried the book to the king, and brought the king word back again, saying, All that was committed to thy servants, they do <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:17
verses.text: And they have gathered together the money that was found in the house of the Lord, and have delivered it into the hand of the overseers, and to the hand of the workmen.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:18
verses.text: Then Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, Hilkiah the priest hath given me a book. And Shaphan read it before the king.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:19
verses.text: And it came to pass, when the king had heard the words of the law, that he rent his clothes.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:20
verses.text: And the king commanded Hilkiah, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Abdon the son of Micah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah a servant of the king’s, saying,

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:21
verses.text: Go, inquire of the Lord for me, and for them that are left in Israel and in Judah, concerning the words of the book that is found: for great <hi type="italic">is</hi> the wrath of the Lord that is poured out upon us, because our fathers have not kept the word of the Lord, to do after all that is written in this book.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:22
verses.text: And Hilkiah, and <hi type="italic">they</hi> that the king <hi type="italic">had appointed</hi>, went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe; (now she dwelt in Jerusalem in the college:) and they spake to her to that <hi type="italic">effect</hi>.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:23
verses.text: ¶ And she answered them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Tell ye the man that sent you to me,

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:24
verses.text: Thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will bring evil upon this place, and upon the inhabitants thereof, <hi type="italic">even</hi> all the curses that are written in the book which they have read before the king of Judah:

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:25
verses.text: Because they have forsaken me, and have burned incense unto other gods, that they might provoke me to anger with all the works of their hands; therefore my wrath shall be poured out upon this place, and shall not be quenched.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:26
verses.text: And as for the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the Lord, so shall ye say unto him, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel <hi type="italic">concerning</hi> the words which thou hast heard;

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:27
verses.text: Because thine heart was tender, and thou didst humble thyself before God, when thou heardest his words against this place, and against the inhabitants thereof, and humbledst thyself before me, and didst rend thy clothes, and weep before me; I have even heard <hi type="italic">thee</hi> also, saith the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:28
verses.text: Behold, I will gather thee to thy fathers, and thou shalt be gathered to thy grave in peace, neither shall thine eyes see all the evil that I will bring upon this place, and upon the inhabitants of the same. So they brought the king word again.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:29
verses.text: ¶ Then the king sent and gathered together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:30
verses.text: And the king went up into the house of the Lord, and all the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the priests, and the Levites, and all the people, great and small: and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that was found in the house of the Lord.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:31
verses.text: And the king stood in his place, and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord, and to keep his commandments, and his testimonies, and his statutes, with all his heart, and with all his soul, to perform the words of the covenant which are written in this book.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:32
verses.text: And he caused all that were present in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand <hi type="italic">to it</hi>. And the inhabitants of Jerusalem did according to the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.

verses.name: II Chronicles 34:33
verses.text: And Josiah took away all the abominations out of all the countries that <hi type="italic">pertained</hi> to the children of Israel, and made all that were present in Israel to serve, <hi type="italic">even</hi> to serve the Lord their God. <hi type="italic">And</hi> all his days they departed not from following the Lord, the God of their fathers.  <chapter eID="2Chr.34"/><div eID="gen416" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:1
verses.text: MOREOVER Josiah kept a passover unto the Lord in Jerusalem: and they killed the passover on the fourteenth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the first month.

verses.name: II Chronicles 35:2
