verses.name: Esther 2:22
verses.text: And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told <hi type="italic">it</hi> unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king <hi type="italic">thereof</hi> in Mordecai’s name.

verses.name: Esther 2:23
verses.text: And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.  <chapter eID="Esth.2"/><div eID="gen446" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 3:1
verses.text: AFTER these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him.

verses.name: Esther 3:2
verses.text: And all the king’s servants, that <hi type="italic">were</hi> in the king’s gate, bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did <hi type="italic">him</hi> reverence.

verses.name: Esther 3:3
verses.text: Then the king’s servants, which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in the king’s gate, said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the king’s commandment?

verses.name: Esther 3:4
verses.text: Now it came to pass, when they spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not unto them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai’s matters would stand: for he had told them that he <hi type="italic">was</hi> a Jew.

verses.name: Esther 3:5
verses.text: And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.

verses.name: Esther 3:6
verses.text: And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that <hi type="italic">were</hi> throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the people of Mordecai.

verses.name: Esther 3:7
verses.text: ¶ In the first month, that <hi type="italic">is</hi>, the month Nisan, in the twelfth year of king Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that <hi type="italic">is</hi>, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, <hi type="italic">to</hi> the twelfth <hi type="italic">month</hi>, that <hi type="italic">is</hi>, the month Adar.

verses.name: Esther 3:8
verses.text: ¶ And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their laws <hi type="italic">are</hi> diverse from all people; neither keep they the king’s laws: therefore it <hi type="italic">is</hi> not for the king’s profit to suffer them.

verses.name: Esther 3:9
verses.text: If it please the king, let it be written that they may be destroyed: and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver to the hands of those that have the charge of the business, to bring <hi type="italic">it</hi> into the king’s treasuries.

verses.name: Esther 3:10
verses.text: And the king took his ring from his hand, and gave it unto Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews’ enemy.

verses.name: Esther 3:11
verses.text: And the king said unto Haman, The silver <hi type="italic">is</hi> given to thee, the people also, to do with them as it seemeth good to thee.

verses.name: Esther 3:12
verses.text: Then were the king’s scribes called on the thirteenth day of the first month, and there was written according to all that Haman had commanded unto the king’s lieutenants, and to the governors that <hi type="italic">were</hi> over every province, and to the rulers of every people of every province according to the writing thereof, and <hi type="italic">to</hi> every people after their language; in the name of king Ahasuerus was it written, and sealed with the king’s ring.

verses.name: Esther 3:13
verses.text: And the letters were sent by posts into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day, <hi type="italic">even</hi> upon the thirteenth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the twelfth month, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> the month Adar, and <hi type="italic">to take</hi> the spoil of them for a prey.

verses.name: Esther 3:14
verses.text: The copy of the writing for a commandment to be given in every province was published unto all people, that they should be ready against that day.

verses.name: Esther 3:15
verses.text: The posts went out, being hastened by the king’s commandment, and the decree was given in Shushan the palace. And the king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city Shushan was perplexed.  <chapter eID="Esth.3"/><div eID="gen447" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 4:1
verses.text: WHEN Mordecai perceived all that was done, Mordecai rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the midst of the city, and cried with a loud and a bitter cry;

verses.name: Esther 4:2
verses.text: And came even before the king’s gate: for none <hi type="italic">might</hi> enter into the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth.

verses.name: Esther 4:3
verses.text: And in every province, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, <hi type="italic">there was</hi> great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

verses.name: Esther 4:4
verses.text: ¶ So Esther’s maids and her chamberlains came and told <hi type="italic">it</hi> her. Then was the queen exceedingly grieved; and she sent raiment to clothe Mordecai, and to take away his sackcloth from him: but he received <hi type="italic">it</hi> not.

verses.name: Esther 4:5
verses.text: Then called Esther for Hatach, <hi type="italic">one</hi> of the king’s chamberlains, whom he had appointed to attend upon her, and gave him a commandment to Mordecai, to know what it <hi type="italic">was</hi>, and why it <hi type="italic">was</hi>.

verses.name: Esther 4:6
verses.text: So Hatach went forth to Mordecai unto the street of the city, which <hi type="italic">was</hi> before the king’s gate.

verses.name: Esther 4:7
verses.text: And Mordecai told him of all that had happened unto him, and of the sum of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the king’s treasuries for the Jews, to destroy them.

verses.name: Esther 4:8
verses.text: Also he gave him the copy of the writing of the decree that was given at Shushan to destroy them, to shew <hi type="italic">it</hi> unto Esther, and to declare <hi type="italic">it</hi> unto her, and to charge her that she should go in unto the king, to make supplication unto him, and to make request before him for her people.

verses.name: Esther 4:9
verses.text: And Hatach came and told Esther the words of Mordecai.

verses.name: Esther 4:10
verses.text: ¶ Again Esther spake unto Hatach, and gave him commandment unto Mordecai;

verses.name: Esther 4:11
verses.text: All the king’s servants, and the people of the king’s provinces, do know, that whosoever, whether man or woman, shall come unto the king into the inner court, who is not called, <hi type="italic">there is</hi> one law of his to put <hi type="italic">him</hi> to death, except such to whom the king shall hold out the golden sceptre, that he may live: but I have not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days.

verses.name: Esther 4:12
verses.text: And they told to Mordecai Esther’s words.

verses.name: Esther 4:13
verses.text: Then Mordecai commanded to answer Esther, Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king’s house, more than all the Jews.

verses.name: Esther 4:14
verses.text: For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, <hi type="italic">then</hi> shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father’s house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for <hi type="italic">such</hi> a time as this?

verses.name: Esther 4:15
verses.text: ¶ Then Esther bade <hi type="italic">them</hi> return Mordecai <hi type="italic">this answer</hi>,

verses.name: Esther 4:16
verses.text: Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.

verses.name: Esther 4:17
verses.text: So Mordecai went his way, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.  <chapter eID="Esth.4"/><div eID="gen448" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 5:1
verses.text: NOW it came to pass on the third day, that Esther put on <hi type="italic">her</hi> royal <hi type="italic">apparel</hi>, and stood in the inner court of the king’s house, over against the king’s house: and the king sat upon his royal throne in the royal house, over against the gate of the house.

verses.name: Esther 5:2
verses.text: And it was so, when the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, <hi type="italic">that</hi> she obtained favour in his sight: and the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that <hi type="italic">was</hi> in his hand. So Esther drew near, and touched the top of the sceptre.

verses.name: Esther 5:3
verses.text: Then said the king unto her, What wilt thou, queen Esther? and what <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy request? it shall be even given thee to the half of the kingdom.

verses.name: Esther 5:4
verses.text: And Esther answered, If <hi type="italic">it seem</hi> good unto the king, let the king and Haman come this day unto the banquet that I have prepared for him.

verses.name: Esther 5:5
verses.text: Then the king said, Cause Haman to make haste, that he may do as Esther hath said. So the king and Haman came to the banquet that Esther had prepared.

verses.name: Esther 5:6
verses.text: ¶ And the king said unto Esther at the banquet of wine, What <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: and what <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy request? even to the half of the kingdom it shall be performed.

verses.name: Esther 5:7
verses.text: Then answered Esther, and said, My petition and my request <hi type="italic">is;</hi>

verses.name: Esther 5:8
verses.text: If I have found favour in the sight of the king, and if it please the king to grant my petition, and to perform my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet that I shall prepare for them, and I will do to morrow as the king hath said.

verses.name: Esther 5:9
verses.text: ¶ Then went Haman forth that day joyful and with a glad heart: but when Haman saw Mordecai in the king’s gate, that he stood not up, nor moved for him, he was full of indignation against Mordecai.

verses.name: Esther 5:10
verses.text: Nevertheless Haman refrained himself: and when he came home, he sent and called for his friends, and Zeresh his wife.

verses.name: Esther 5:11
verses.text: And Haman told them of the glory of his riches, and the multitude of his children, and all <hi type="italic">the things</hi> wherein the king had promoted him, and how he had advanced him above the princes and servants of the king.

verses.name: Esther 5:12
verses.text: Haman said moreover, Yea, Esther the queen did let no man come in with the king unto the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and to morrow am I invited unto her also with the king.

verses.name: Esther 5:13
verses.text: Yet all this availeth me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.

verses.name: Esther 5:14
verses.text: ¶ Then said Zeresh his wife and all his friends unto him, Let a gallows be made of fifty cubits high, and to morrow speak thou unto the king that Mordecai may be hanged thereon: then go thou in merrily with the king unto the banquet. And the thing pleased Haman; and he caused the gallows to be made.  <chapter eID="Esth.5"/><div eID="gen449" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 6:1
verses.text: ON that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.

verses.name: Esther 6:2
verses.text: And it was found written, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s chamberlains, the keepers of the door, who sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.

verses.name: Esther 6:3
verses.text: And the king said, What honour and dignity hath been done to Mordecai for this? Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, There is nothing done for him.

verses.name: Esther 6:4
verses.text: ¶ And the king said, Who <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the court? Now Haman was come into the outward court of the king’s house, to speak unto the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.

verses.name: Esther 6:5
verses.text: And the king’s servants said unto him, Behold, Haman standeth in the court. And the king said, Let him come in.

verses.name: Esther 6:6
verses.text: So Haman came in. And the king said unto him, What shall be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour? Now Haman thought in his heart, To whom would the king delight to do honour more than to myself?

verses.name: Esther 6:7
verses.text: And Haman answered the king, For the man whom the king delighteth to honour,

verses.name: Esther 6:8
verses.text: Let the royal apparel be brought which the king <hi type="italic">useth</hi> to wear, and the horse that the king rideth upon, and the crown royal which is set upon his head:

verses.name: Esther 6:9
verses.text: And let this apparel and horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king’s most noble princes, that they may array the man <hi type="italic">withal</hi> whom the king delighteth to honour, and bring him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaim before him, Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delighteth to honour.

verses.name: Esther 6:10
verses.text: Then the king said to Haman, Make haste, <hi type="italic">and</hi> take the apparel and the horse, as thou hast said, and do even so to Mordecai the Jew, that sitteth at the king’s gate: let nothing fail of all that thou hast spoken.

verses.name: Esther 6:11
verses.text: Then took Haman the apparel and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and brought him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaimed before him, Thus shall it be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour.

verses.name: Esther 6:12
verses.text: ¶ And Mordecai came again to the king’s gate. But Haman hasted to his house mourning, and having his head covered.

verses.name: Esther 6:13
verses.text: And Haman told Zeresh his wife and all his friends every <hi type="italic">thing</hi> that had befallen him. Then said his wise men and Zeresh his wife unto him, If Mordecai <hi type="italic">be</hi> of the seed of the Jews, before whom thou hast begun to fall, thou shalt not prevail against him, but shalt surely fall before him.

verses.name: Esther 6:14
verses.text: And while they <hi type="italic">were</hi> yet talking with him, came the king’s chamberlains, and hasted to bring Haman unto the banquet that Esther had prepared.  <chapter eID="Esth.6"/><div eID="gen450" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 7:1
verses.text: SO the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.

verses.name: Esther 7:2
verses.text: And the king said again unto Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine, What <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy petition, queen Esther? and it shall be granted thee: and what <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy request? and it shall be performed, <hi type="italic">even</hi> to the half of the kingdom.

verses.name: Esther 7:3
verses.text: Then Esther the queen answered and said, If I have found favour in thy sight, O king, and if it please the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request:

verses.name: Esther 7:4
verses.text: For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen, I had held my tongue, although the enemy could not countervail the king’s damage.

verses.name: Esther 7:5
verses.text: ¶ Then the king Ahasuerus answered and said unto Esther the queen, Who is he, and where is he, that durst presume in his heart to do so?

verses.name: Esther 7:6
verses.text: And Esther said, The adversary and enemy <hi type="italic">is</hi> this wicked Haman. Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.

verses.name: Esther 7:7
verses.text: ¶ And the king arising from the banquet of wine in his wrath <hi type="italic">went</hi> into the palace garden: and Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen; for he saw that there was evil determined against him by the king.

verses.name: Esther 7:8
verses.text: Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman was fallen upon the bed whereon Esther <hi type="italic">was</hi>. Then said the king, Will he force the queen also before me in the house? As the word went out of the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.

verses.name: Esther 7:9
verses.text: And Harbonah, one of the chamberlains, said before the king, Behold also, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman had made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standeth in the house of Haman. Then the king said, Hang him thereon.

verses.name: Esther 7:10
verses.text: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king’s wrath pacified.  <chapter eID="Esth.7"/><div eID="gen451" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 8:1
verses.text: ON that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jews’ enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he <hi type="italic">was</hi> unto her.

verses.name: Esther 8:2
verses.text: And the king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.

verses.name: Esther 8:3
verses.text: ¶ And Esther spake yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and besought him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his device that he had devised against the Jews.

verses.name: Esther 8:4
verses.text: Then the king held out the golden sceptre toward Esther. So Esther arose, and stood before the king,

verses.name: Esther 8:5
verses.text: And said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and the thing <hi type="italic">seem</hi> right before the king, and I <hi type="italic">be</hi> pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews which <hi type="italic">are</hi> in all the king’s provinces:

verses.name: Esther 8:6
verses.text: For how can I endure to see the evil that shall come unto my people? or how can I endure to see the destruction of my kindred?

verses.name: Esther 8:7
verses.text: ¶ Then the king Ahasuerus said unto Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him they have hanged upon the gallows, because he laid his hand upon the Jews.

verses.name: Esther 8:8
verses.text: Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king’s name, and seal <hi type="italic">it</hi> with the king’s ring: for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may no man reverse.

verses.name: Esther 8:9
verses.text: Then were the king’s scribes called at that time in the third month, that <hi type="italic">is</hi>, the month Sivan, on the three and twentieth <hi type="italic">day</hi> thereof; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded unto the Jews, and to the lieutenants, and the deputies and rulers of the provinces which <hi type="italic">are</hi> from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.

verses.name: Esther 8:10
verses.text: And he wrote in the king Ahasuerus’ name, and sealed <hi type="italic">it</hi> with the king’s ring, and sent letters by posts on horseback, <hi type="italic">and</hi> riders on mules, camels, <hi type="italic">and</hi> young dromedaries:

verses.name: Esther 8:11
verses.text: Wherein the king granted the Jews which <hi type="italic">were</hi> in every city to gather themselves together, and to stand for their life, to destroy, to slay, and to cause to perish, all the power of the people and province that would assault them, <hi type="italic">both</hi> little ones and women, and <hi type="italic">to take</hi> the spoil of them for a prey,

verses.name: Esther 8:12
verses.text: Upon one day in all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, <hi type="italic">namely</hi>, upon the thirteenth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the twelfth month, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> the month Adar.

verses.name: Esther 8:13
verses.text: The copy of the writing for a commandment to be given in every province <hi type="italic">was</hi> published unto all people, and that the Jews should be ready against that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.

verses.name: Esther 8:14
verses.text: <hi type="italic">So</hi> the posts that rode upon mules <hi type="italic">and</hi> camels went out, being hastened and pressed on by the king’s commandment. And the decree was given at Shushan the palace.

verses.name: Esther 8:15
verses.text: ¶ And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.

verses.name: Esther 8:16
verses.text: The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour.

verses.name: Esther 8:17
verses.text: And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.  <chapter eID="Esth.8"/><div eID="gen452" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 9:1
verses.text: NOW in the twelfth month, that <hi type="italic">is</hi>, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king’s commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over them that hated them;)

verses.name: Esther 9:2
verses.text: The Jews gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, to lay hand on such as sought their hurt: and no man could withstand them; for the fear of them fell upon all people.

verses.name: Esther 9:3
verses.text: And all the rulers of the provinces, and the lieutenants, and the deputies, and officers of the king, helped the Jews; because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them.

verses.name: Esther 9:4
verses.text: For Mordecai <hi type="italic">was</hi> great in the king’s house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces: for this man Mordecai waxed greater and greater.

verses.name: Esther 9:5
verses.text: Thus the Jews smote all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and slaughter, and destruction, and did what they would unto those that hated them.

verses.name: Esther 9:6
verses.text: And in Shushan the palace the Jews slew and destroyed five hundred men.

verses.name: Esther 9:7
verses.text: And Parshandatha, and Dalphon, and Aspatha,

verses.name: Esther 9:8
verses.text: And Poratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha,

verses.name: Esther 9:9
verses.text: And Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Vajezatha,

verses.name: Esther 9:10
verses.text: The ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews, slew they; but on the spoil laid they not their hand.

verses.name: Esther 9:11
verses.text: On that day the number of those that were slain in Shushan the palace was brought before the king.

verses.name: Esther 9:12
verses.text: ¶ And the king said unto Esther the queen, The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman; what have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces? now what <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: or what <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy request further? and it shall be done.

verses.name: Esther 9:13
verses.text: Then said Esther, If it please the king, let it be granted to the Jews which <hi type="italic">are</hi> in Shushan to do to morrow also according unto this day’s decree, and let Haman’s ten sons be hanged upon the gallows.

verses.name: Esther 9:14
verses.text: And the king commanded it so to be done: and the decree was given at Shushan; and they hanged Haman’s ten sons.

verses.name: Esther 9:15
verses.text: For the Jews that <hi type="italic">were</hi> in Shushan gathered themselves together on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and slew three hundred men at Shushan; but on the prey they laid not their hand.

verses.name: Esther 9:16
verses.text: But the other Jews that <hi type="italic">were</hi> in the king’s provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey,

verses.name: Esther 9:17
verses.text: On the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of the same rested they, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

verses.name: Esther 9:18
verses.text: But the Jews that <hi type="italic">were</hi> at Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth <hi type="italic">day</hi> thereof, and on the fourteenth thereof; and on the fifteenth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the same they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

verses.name: Esther 9:19
verses.text: Therefore the Jews of the villages, that dwelt in the unwalled towns, made the fourteenth day of the month Adar <hi type="italic">a day of</hi> gladness and feasting, and a good day, and of sending portions one to another.

verses.name: Esther 9:20
verses.text: ¶ And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters unto all the Jews that <hi type="italic">were</hi> in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, <hi type="italic">both</hi> nigh and far,

verses.name: Esther 9:21
verses.text: To stablish <hi type="italic">this</hi> among them, that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly,

verses.name: Esther 9:22
verses.text: As the days wherein the Jews rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.

verses.name: Esther 9:23
verses.text: And the Jews undertook to do as they had begun, and as Mordecai had written unto them;

verses.name: Esther 9:24
verses.text: Because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had devised against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that <hi type="italic">is</hi>, the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them;

verses.name: Esther 9:25
verses.text: But when <hi type="italic">Esther</hi> came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

verses.name: Esther 9:26
verses.text: Wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore for all the words of this letter, and <hi type="italic">of that</hi> which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them,

verses.name: Esther 9:27
verses.text: The Jews ordained, and took upon them, and upon their seed, and upon all such as joined themselves unto them, so as it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to their writing, and according to their <hi type="italic">appointed</hi> time every year;

verses.name: Esther 9:28
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">that</hi> these days <hi type="italic">should be</hi> remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and <hi type="italic">that</hi> these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.

verses.name: Esther 9:29
verses.text: Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all authority, to confirm this second letter of Purim.

verses.name: Esther 9:30
verses.text: And he sent the letters unto all the Jews, to the hundred twenty and seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, <hi type="italic">with</hi> words of peace and truth,

verses.name: Esther 9:31
verses.text: To confirm these days of Purim in their times <hi type="italic">appointed</hi>, according as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had enjoined them, and as they had decreed for themselves and for their seed, the matters of the fastings and their cry.

verses.name: Esther 9:32
verses.text: And the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.  <chapter eID="Esth.9"/><div eID="gen453" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Esther 10:1
verses.text: AND the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and <hi type="italic">upon</hi> the isles of the sea.

verses.name: Esther 10:2
verses.text: And all the acts of his power and of his might, and the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai, whereunto the king advanced him, <hi type="italic">are</hi> they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?

verses.name: Esther 10:3
verses.text: For Mordecai the Jew <hi type="italic">was</hi> next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.  <chapter eID="Esth.10"/><div eID="gen454" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen444" osisID="Esth" type="book"/>

verses.name: Job 1:1
verses.text: THERE was a man in the land of Uz, whose name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.

verses.name: Job 1:2
verses.text: And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters.

verses.name: Job 1:3
verses.text: His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east.

verses.name: Job 1:4
verses.text: And his sons went and feasted <hi type="italic">in their</hi> houses, every one his day; and sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

verses.name: Job 1:5
verses.text: And it was so, when the days of <hi type="italic">their</hi> feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings <hi type="italic">according</hi> to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.

verses.name: Job 1:6
verses.text: ¶ Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.

verses.name: Job 1:7
verses.text: And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

verses.name: Job 1:8
verses.text: And the Lord said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that <hi type="italic">there is</hi> none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?

verses.name: Job 1:9
verses.text: Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, Doth Job fear God for nought?

verses.name: Job 1:10
verses.text: Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side? thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.

verses.name: Job 1:11
verses.text: But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.

verses.name: Job 1:12
verses.text: And the Lord said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath <hi type="italic">is</hi> in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord.

verses.name: Job 1:13
verses.text: ¶ And there was a day when his sons and his daughters <hi type="italic">were</hi> eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house:

verses.name: Job 1:14
verses.text: And there came a messenger unto Job, and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them:

verses.name: Job 1:15
verses.text: And the Sabeans fell <hi type="italic">upon them</hi>, and took them away; yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

verses.name: Job 1:16
verses.text: While he <hi type="italic">was</hi> yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

verses.name: Job 1:17
verses.text: While he <hi type="italic">was</hi> yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have carried them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

verses.name: Job 1:18
verses.text: While he <hi type="italic">was</hi> yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters <hi type="italic">were</hi> eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house:

verses.name: Job 1:19
verses.text: And, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

verses.name: Job 1:20
verses.text: Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped,

verses.name: Job 1:21
verses.text: And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.

verses.name: Job 1:22
verses.text: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.  <chapter eID="Job.1"/><div eID="gen456" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 2:1
verses.text: AGAIN there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them to present himself before the Lord.

verses.name: Job 2:2
verses.text: And the Lord said unto Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

verses.name: Job 2:3
verses.text: And the Lord said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that <hi type="italic">there is</hi> none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.

verses.name: Job 2:4
verses.text: And Satan answered the Lord, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.

verses.name: Job 2:5
verses.text: But put forth thine hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse thee to thy face.

verses.name: Job 2:6
verses.text: And the Lord said unto Satan, Behold, he <hi type="italic">is</hi> in thine hand; but save his life.

verses.name: Job 2:7
verses.text: ¶ So went Satan forth from the presence of the Lord, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.

verses.name: Job 2:8
verses.text: And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes.

verses.name: Job 2:9
verses.text: ¶ Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.

verses.name: Job 2:10
verses.text: But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.

verses.name: Job 2:11
verses.text: ¶ Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.

verses.name: Job 2:12
verses.text: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.

verses.name: Job 2:13
verses.text: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that <hi type="italic">his</hi> grief was very great.  <chapter eID="Job.2"/><div eID="gen457" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 3:1
verses.text: AFTER this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.

verses.name: Job 3:2
verses.text: And Job spake, and said,

verses.name: Job 3:3
verses.text: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night <hi type="italic">in which</hi> it was said, There is a man child conceived.

verses.name: Job 3:4
verses.text: Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it.

verses.name: Job 3:5
verses.text: Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.

verses.name: Job 3:6
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As for</hi> that night, let darkness seize upon it; let it not be joined unto the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months.

verses.name: Job 3:7
verses.text: Lo, let that night be solitary, let no joyful voice come therein.

verses.name: Job 3:8
verses.text: Let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to raise up their mourning.

verses.name: Job 3:9
verses.text: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; let it look for light, but <hi type="italic">have</hi> none; neither let it see the dawning of the day:

verses.name: Job 3:10
verses.text: Because it shut not up the doors of my <hi type="italic">mother</hi>’<hi type="italic">s</hi> womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.

verses.name: Job 3:11
verses.text: Why died I not from the womb? <hi type="italic">why</hi> did I <hi type="italic">not</hi> give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?

verses.name: Job 3:12
verses.text: Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck?

verses.name: Job 3:13
verses.text: For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest,

verses.name: Job 3:14
verses.text: With kings and counsellers of the earth, which built desolate places for themselves;

verses.name: Job 3:15
verses.text: Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver:

verses.name: Job 3:16
verses.text: Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants <hi type="italic">which</hi> never saw light.

verses.name: Job 3:17
verses.text: There the wicked cease <hi type="italic">from</hi> troubling; and there the weary be at rest.

verses.name: Job 3:18
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There</hi> the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.

verses.name: Job 3:19
verses.text: The small and great are there; and the servant <hi type="italic">is</hi> free from his master.

verses.name: Job 3:20
verses.text: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life unto the bitter <hi type="italic">in</hi> soul;

verses.name: Job 3:21
verses.text: Which long for death, but it <hi type="italic">cometh</hi> not; and dig for it more than for hid treasures;

verses.name: Job 3:22
verses.text: Which rejoice exceedingly, <hi type="italic">and</hi> are glad, when they can find the grave?

verses.name: Job 3:23
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Why is light given</hi> to a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in?

verses.name: Job 3:24
verses.text: For my sighing cometh before I eat, and my roarings are poured out like the waters.

verses.name: Job 3:25
verses.text: For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me, and that which I was afraid of is come unto me.

verses.name: Job 3:26
verses.text: I was not in safety, neither had I rest, neither was I quiet; yet trouble came.  <chapter eID="Job.3"/><div eID="gen458" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 4:1
verses.text: THEN Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,

verses.name: Job 4:2
verses.text: <hi type="italic">If</hi> we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speaking?

verses.name: Job 4:3
verses.text: Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.

verses.name: Job 4:4
verses.text: Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees.

verses.name: Job 4:5
verses.text: But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.

verses.name: Job 4:6
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is</hi> not <hi type="italic">this</hi> thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways?

verses.name: Job 4:7
verses.text: Remember, I pray thee, who <hi type="italic">ever</hi> perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?

verses.name: Job 4:8
verses.text: Even as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, and sow wickedness, reap the same.

verses.name: Job 4:9
verses.text: By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of his nostrils are they consumed.

verses.name: Job 4:10
verses.text: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

verses.name: Job 4:11
verses.text: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion’s whelps are scattered abroad.

verses.name: Job 4:12
verses.text: Now a thing was secretly brought to me, and mine ear received a little thereof.

verses.name: Job 4:13
verses.text: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men,

verses.name: Job 4:14
verses.text: Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones to shake.

verses.name: Job 4:15
verses.text: Then a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up:

verses.name: Job 4:16
verses.text: It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image <hi type="italic">was</hi> before mine eyes, <hi type="italic">there was</hi> silence, and I heard a voice, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>,

verses.name: Job 4:17
verses.text: Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?

verses.name: Job 4:18
verses.text: Behold, he put no trust in his servants; and his angels he charged with folly:

verses.name: Job 4:19
verses.text: How much less <hi type="italic">in</hi> them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the dust, <hi type="italic">which</hi> are crushed before the moth?

verses.name: Job 4:20
verses.text: They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Job 4:21
verses.text: Doth not their excellency <hi type="italic">which is</hi> in them go away? they die, even without wisdom.  <chapter eID="Job.4"/><div eID="gen459" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 5:1
verses.text: CALL now, if there be any that will answer thee; and to which of the saints wilt thou turn?

verses.name: Job 5:2
verses.text: For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one.

verses.name: Job 5:3
verses.text: I have seen the foolish taking root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation.

verses.name: Job 5:4
verses.text: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither <hi type="italic">is there</hi> any to deliver <hi type="italic">them</hi>.

verses.name: Job 5:5
verses.text: Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, and taketh it even out of the thorns, and the robber swalloweth up their substance.

verses.name: Job 5:6
verses.text: Although affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;

verses.name: Job 5:7
verses.text: Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

verses.name: Job 5:8
verses.text: I would seek unto God, and unto God would I commit my cause:

verses.name: Job 5:9
verses.text: Which doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without number:

verses.name: Job 5:10
verses.text: Who giveth rain upon the earth, and sendeth waters upon the fields:

verses.name: Job 5:11
verses.text: To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety.

verses.name: Job 5:12
verses.text: He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform <hi type="italic">their</hi> enterprise.

verses.name: Job 5:13
verses.text: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.

verses.name: Job 5:14
verses.text: They meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night.

verses.name: Job 5:15
verses.text: But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.

verses.name: Job 5:16
verses.text: So the poor hath hope, and iniquity stoppeth her mouth.

verses.name: Job 5:17
verses.text: Behold, happy <hi type="italic">is</hi> the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty:

verses.name: Job 5:18
verses.text: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.

verses.name: Job 5:19
verses.text: He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.

verses.name: Job 5:20
verses.text: In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.

verses.name: Job 5:21
verses.text: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh.

verses.name: Job 5:22
verses.text: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh: neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.

verses.name: Job 5:23
verses.text: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field: and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.

verses.name: Job 5:24
verses.text: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.

verses.name: Job 5:25
verses.text: Thou shalt know also that thy seed <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.

verses.name: Job 5:26
verses.text: Thou shalt come to <hi type="italic">thy</hi> grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.

verses.name: Job 5:27
verses.text: Lo this, we have searched it, so it <hi type="italic">is;</hi> hear it, and know thou <hi type="italic">it</hi> for thy good.  <chapter eID="Job.5"/><div eID="gen460" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 6:1
verses.text: BUT Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 6:2
verses.text: Oh that my grief were throughly weighed, and my calamity laid in the balances together!

verses.name: Job 6:3
verses.text: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea: therefore my words are swallowed up.

verses.name: Job 6:4
verses.text: For the arrows of the Almighty <hi type="italic">are</hi> within me, the poison whereof drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.

verses.name: Job 6:5
verses.text: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or loweth the ox over his fodder?

verses.name: Job 6:6
verses.text: Can that which is unsavoury be eaten without salt? or is there <hi type="italic">any</hi> taste in the white of an egg?

verses.name: Job 6:7
verses.text: The things <hi type="italic">that</hi> my soul refused to touch <hi type="italic">are</hi> as my sorrowful meat.

verses.name: Job 6:8
verses.text: Oh that I might have my request; and that God would grant <hi type="italic">me</hi> the thing that I long for!

verses.name: Job 6:9
verses.text: Even that it would please God to destroy me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

verses.name: Job 6:10
verses.text: Then should I yet have comfort; yea, I would harden myself in sorrow: let him not spare; for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.

verses.name: Job 6:11
verses.text: What <hi type="italic">is</hi> my strength, that I should hope? and what <hi type="italic">is</hi> mine end, that I should prolong my life?

verses.name: Job 6:12
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is</hi> my strength the strength of stones? or <hi type="italic">is</hi> my flesh of brass?

verses.name: Job 6:13
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is</hi> not my help in me? and is wisdom driven quite from me?

verses.name: Job 6:14
verses.text: To him that is afflicted pity <hi type="italic">should be shewed</hi> from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.

verses.name: Job 6:15
verses.text: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, <hi type="italic">and</hi> as the stream of brooks they pass away;

verses.name: Job 6:16
verses.text: Which are blackish by reason of the ice, <hi type="italic">and</hi> wherein the snow is hid:

verses.name: Job 6:17
verses.text: What time they wax warm, they vanish: when it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

verses.name: Job 6:18
verses.text: The paths of their way are turned aside; they go to nothing, and perish.

verses.name: Job 6:19
verses.text: The troops of Tema looked, the companies of Sheba waited for them.

verses.name: Job 6:20
verses.text: They were confounded because they had hoped; they came thither, and were ashamed.

verses.name: Job 6:21
verses.text: For now ye are nothing; ye see <hi type="italic">my</hi> casting down, and are afraid.

verses.name: Job 6:22
verses.text: Did I say, Bring unto me? or, Give a reward for me of your substance?

verses.name: Job 6:23
verses.text: Or, Deliver me from the enemy’s hand? or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?

verses.name: Job 6:24
verses.text: Teach me, and I will hold my tongue: and cause me to understand wherein I have erred.

verses.name: Job 6:25
verses.text: How forcible are right words! but what doth your arguing reprove?

verses.name: Job 6:26
verses.text: Do ye imagine to reprove words, and the speeches of one that is desperate, <hi type="italic">which are</hi> as wind?

verses.name: Job 6:27
verses.text: Yea, ye overwhelm the fatherless, and ye dig <hi type="italic">a pit</hi> for your friend.

verses.name: Job 6:28
verses.text: Now therefore be content, look upon me; for <hi type="italic">it is</hi> evident unto you if I lie.

verses.name: Job 6:29
verses.text: Return, I pray you, let it not be iniquity; yea, return again, my righteousness <hi type="italic">is</hi> in it.

verses.name: Job 6:30
verses.text: Is there iniquity in my tongue? cannot my taste discern perverse things?  <chapter eID="Job.6"/><div eID="gen461" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 7:2
verses.text: As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for <hi type="italic">the reward of</hi> his work:

verses.name: Job 7:3
verses.text: So am I made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to me.

verses.name: Job 7:4
verses.text: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.

verses.name: Job 7:5
verses.text: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken, and become loathsome.

verses.name: Job 7:6
verses.text: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.

verses.name: Job 7:7
verses.text: O remember that my life <hi type="italic">is</hi> wind: mine eye shall no more see good.

verses.name: Job 7:8
verses.text: The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no <hi type="italic">more:</hi> thine eyes <hi type="italic">are</hi> upon me, and I <hi type="italic">am</hi> not.

verses.name: Job 7:9
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no <hi type="italic">more</hi>.

verses.name: Job 7:10
verses.text: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.

verses.name: Job 7:11
verses.text: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

verses.name: Job 7:12
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Am</hi> I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch over me?

verses.name: Job 7:13
verses.text: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;

verses.name: Job 7:14
verses.text: Then thou scarest me with dreams, and terrifiest me through visions:

verses.name: Job 7:15
verses.text: So that my soul chooseth strangling, <hi type="italic">and</hi> death rather than my life.

verses.name: Job 7:16
verses.text: I loathe <hi type="italic">it;</hi> I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days <hi type="italic">are</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Job 7:17
verses.text: What <hi type="italic">is</hi> man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him?

verses.name: Job 7:18
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou shouldest visit him every morning, <hi type="italic">and</hi> try him every moment?

verses.name: Job 7:19
verses.text: How long wilt thou not depart from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?

verses.name: Job 7:20
verses.text: I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself?

verses.name: Job 7:21
verses.text: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I <hi type="italic">shall</hi> not <hi type="italic">be</hi>.  <chapter eID="Job.7"/><div eID="gen462" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 8:1
verses.text: THEN answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,

verses.name: Job 8:2
verses.text: How long wilt thou speak these <hi type="italic">things?</hi> and <hi type="italic">how long shall</hi> the words of thy mouth <hi type="italic">be like</hi> a strong wind?

verses.name: Job 8:3
verses.text: Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?

verses.name: Job 8:4
verses.text: If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression;

verses.name: Job 8:5
verses.text: If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;

verses.name: Job 8:6
verses.text: If thou <hi type="italic">wert</hi> pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.

verses.name: Job 8:7
verses.text: Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.

verses.name: Job 8:8
verses.text: For inquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:

verses.name: Job 8:9
verses.text: (For we <hi type="italic">are but of</hi> yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth <hi type="italic">are</hi> a shadow:)

verses.name: Job 8:10
verses.text: Shall not they teach thee, <hi type="italic">and</hi> tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?

verses.name: Job 8:11
verses.text: Can the rush grow up without mire? can the flag grow without water?

verses.name: Job 8:12
verses.text: Whilst it <hi type="italic">is</hi> yet in his greenness, <hi type="italic">and</hi> not cut down, it withereth before any <hi type="italic">other</hi> herb.

verses.name: Job 8:13
verses.text: So <hi type="italic">are</hi> the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite’s hope shall perish:

verses.name: Job 8:14
verses.text: Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> a spider’s web.

verses.name: Job 8:15
verses.text: He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.

verses.name: Job 8:16
verses.text: He <hi type="italic">is</hi> green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.

verses.name: Job 8:17
verses.text: His roots are wrapped about the heap, <hi type="italic">and</hi> seeth the place of stones.

verses.name: Job 8:18
verses.text: If he destroy him from his place, then <hi type="italic">it</hi> shall deny him, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, I have not seen thee.

verses.name: Job 8:19
verses.text: Behold, this <hi type="italic">is</hi> the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow.

verses.name: Job 8:20
verses.text: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect <hi type="italic">man</hi>, neither will he help the evil doers:

verses.name: Job 8:21
verses.text: Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing.

verses.name: Job 8:22
verses.text: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought.  <chapter eID="Job.8"/><div eID="gen463" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 9:1
verses.text: THEN Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 9:2
verses.text: I know <hi type="italic">it is</hi> so of a truth: but how should man be just with God?

verses.name: Job 9:3
verses.text: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand.

verses.name: Job 9:4
verses.text: <hi type="italic">He is</hi> wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened <hi type="italic">himself</hi> against him, and hath prospered?

verses.name: Job 9:5
verses.text: Which removeth the mountains, and they know not: which overturneth them in his anger.

verses.name: Job 9:6
verses.text: Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.

verses.name: Job 9:7
verses.text: Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars.

verses.name: Job 9:8
verses.text: Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea.

verses.name: Job 9:9
verses.text: Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.

verses.name: Job 9:10
verses.text: Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.

verses.name: Job 9:11
verses.text: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see <hi type="italic">him</hi> not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.

verses.name: Job 9:12
verses.text: Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou?

verses.name: Job 9:13
verses.text: <hi type="italic">If</hi> God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him.

verses.name: Job 9:14
verses.text: How much less shall I answer him, <hi type="italic">and</hi> choose out my words <hi type="italic">to reason</hi> with him?

verses.name: Job 9:15
verses.text: Whom, though I were righteous, <hi type="italic">yet</hi> would I not answer, <hi type="italic">but</hi> I would make supplication to my judge.

verses.name: Job 9:16
verses.text: If I had called, and he had answered me; <hi type="italic">yet</hi> would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.

verses.name: Job 9:17
verses.text: For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause.

verses.name: Job 9:18
verses.text: He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness.

verses.name: Job 9:19
verses.text: If <hi type="italic">I speak</hi> of strength, lo, <hi type="italic">he is</hi> strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time <hi type="italic">to plead?</hi>

verses.name: Job 9:20
verses.text: If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: <hi type="italic">if I say</hi>, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.

verses.name: Job 9:21
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Though</hi> I <hi type="italic">were</hi> perfect, <hi type="italic">yet</hi> would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.

verses.name: Job 9:22
verses.text: This <hi type="italic">is</hi> one <hi type="italic">thing</hi>, therefore I said <hi type="italic">it</hi>, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.

verses.name: Job 9:23
verses.text: If the scourge slay suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent.

verses.name: Job 9:24
verses.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, <hi type="italic">and</hi> who <hi type="italic">is</hi> he?

verses.name: Job 9:25
verses.text: Now my days are swifter than a post: they flee away, they see no good.

verses.name: Job 9:26
verses.text: They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle <hi type="italic">that</hi> hasteth to the prey.

verses.name: Job 9:27
verses.text: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort <hi type="italic">myself:</hi>

verses.name: Job 9:28
verses.text: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.

verses.name: Job 9:29
verses.text: <hi type="italic">If</hi> I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?

verses.name: Job 9:30
verses.text: If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean;

verses.name: Job 9:31
verses.text: Yet shalt thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes shall abhor me.

verses.name: Job 9:32
verses.text: For <hi type="italic">he is</hi> not a man, as I <hi type="italic">am</hi>, <hi type="italic">that</hi> I should answer him, <hi type="italic">and</hi> we should come together in judgment.

verses.name: Job 9:33
verses.text: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, <hi type="italic">that</hi> might lay his hand upon us both.

verses.name: Job 9:34
verses.text: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me:

verses.name: Job 9:35
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Then</hi> would I speak, and not fear him; but <hi type="italic">it is</hi> not so with me.  <chapter eID="Job.9"/><div eID="gen464" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 10:1
verses.text: MY soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint upon myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

verses.name: Job 10:2
verses.text: I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; shew me wherefore thou contendest with me.

verses.name: Job 10:3
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is it</hi> good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thine hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?

verses.name: Job 10:4
verses.text: Hast thou eyes of flesh? or seest thou as man seeth?

verses.name: Job 10:5
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Are</hi> thy days as the days of man? <hi type="italic">are</hi> thy years as man’s days,

verses.name: Job 10:6
verses.text: That thou inquirest after mine iniquity, and searchest after my sin?

verses.name: Job 10:7
verses.text: Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and <hi type="italic">there is</hi> none that can deliver out of thine hand.

verses.name: Job 10:8
verses.text: Thine hands have made me and fashioned me together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.

verses.name: Job 10:9
verses.text: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay; and wilt thou bring me into dust again?

verses.name: Job 10:10
verses.text: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese?

verses.name: Job 10:11
verses.text: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews.

verses.name: Job 10:12
verses.text: Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.

verses.name: Job 10:13
verses.text: And these <hi type="italic">things</hi> hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this <hi type="italic">is</hi> with thee.

verses.name: Job 10:14
verses.text: If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.

verses.name: Job 10:15
verses.text: If I be wicked, woe unto me; and <hi type="italic">if</hi> I be righteous, <hi type="italic">yet</hi> will I not lift up my head. <hi type="italic">I am</hi> full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction;

verses.name: Job 10:16
verses.text: For it increaseth. Thou huntest me as a fierce lion: and again thou shewest thyself marvellous upon me.

verses.name: Job 10:17
verses.text: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war <hi type="italic">are</hi> against me.

verses.name: Job 10:18
verses.text: Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me!

verses.name: Job 10:19
verses.text: I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.

verses.name: Job 10:20
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Are</hi> not my days few? cease <hi type="italic">then</hi>, <hi type="italic">and</hi> let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,

verses.name: Job 10:21
verses.text: Before I go <hi type="italic">whence</hi> I shall not return, <hi type="italic">even</hi> to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;

verses.name: Job 10:22
verses.text: A land of darkness, as darkness <hi type="italic">itself; and</hi> of the shadow of death, without any order, and <hi type="italic">where</hi> the light <hi type="italic">is</hi> as darkness.  <chapter eID="Job.10"/><div eID="gen465" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 11:1
verses.text: THEN answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,

verses.name: Job 11:2
verses.text: Should not the multitude of words be answered? and should a man full of talk be justified?

verses.name: Job 11:3
verses.text: Should thy lies make men hold their peace? and when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?

verses.name: Job 11:4
verses.text: For thou hast said, My doctrine <hi type="italic">is</hi> pure, and I am clean in thine eyes.

verses.name: Job 11:5
verses.text: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against thee;

verses.name: Job 11:6
verses.text: And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that <hi type="italic">they are</hi> double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee <hi type="italic">less</hi> than thine iniquity <hi type="italic">deserveth</hi>.

verses.name: Job 11:7
verses.text: Canst thou by searching find out God? canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?

verses.name: Job 11:8
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know?

verses.name: Job 11:9
verses.text: The measure thereof <hi type="italic">is</hi> longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

verses.name: Job 11:10
verses.text: If he cut off, and shut up, or gather together, then who can hinder him?

verses.name: Job 11:11
verses.text: For he knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also; will he not then consider <hi type="italic">it?</hi>

verses.name: Job 11:12
verses.text: For vain man would be wise, though man be born <hi type="italic">like</hi> a wild ass’s colt.

verses.name: Job 11:13
verses.text: If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him;

verses.name: Job 11:14
verses.text: If iniquity <hi type="italic">be</hi> in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.

verses.name: Job 11:15
verses.text: For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:

verses.name: Job 11:16
verses.text: Because thou shalt forget <hi type="italic">thy</hi> misery, <hi type="italic">and</hi> remember <hi type="italic">it</hi> as waters <hi type="italic">that</hi> pass away:

verses.name: Job 11:17
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">thine</hi> age shall be clearer than the noonday; thou shalt shine forth, thou shalt be as the morning.

verses.name: Job 11:18
verses.text: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig <hi type="italic">about thee</hi>, <hi type="italic">and</hi> thou shalt take thy rest in safety.

verses.name: Job 11:19
verses.text: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make <hi type="italic">thee</hi> afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thee.

verses.name: Job 11:20
verses.text: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall not escape, and their hope <hi type="italic">shall be as</hi> the giving up of the ghost.  <chapter eID="Job.11"/><div eID="gen466" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 12:1
verses.text: AND Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 12:2
verses.text: No doubt but ye <hi type="italic">are</hi> the people, and wisdom shall die with you.

verses.name: Job 12:3
verses.text: But I have understanding as well as you; I <hi type="italic">am</hi> not inferior to you: yea, who knoweth not such things as these?

verses.name: Job 12:4
verses.text: I am <hi type="italic">as</hi> one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright <hi type="italic">man is</hi> laughed to scorn.

verses.name: Job 12:5
verses.text: He that is ready to slip with <hi type="italic">his</hi> feet <hi type="italic">is as</hi> a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease.

verses.name: Job 12:6
verses.text: The tabernacles of robbers prosper, and they that provoke God are secure; into whose hand God bringeth <hi type="italic">abundantly</hi>.

verses.name: Job 12:7
verses.text: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowls of the air, and they shall tell thee:

verses.name: Job 12:8
verses.text: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee: and the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee.

verses.name: Job 12:9
verses.text: Who knoweth not in all these that the hand of the Lord hath wrought this?

verses.name: Job 12:10
verses.text: In whose hand <hi type="italic">is</hi> the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind.

verses.name: Job 12:11
verses.text: Doth not the ear try words? and the mouth taste his meat?

verses.name: Job 12:12
verses.text: With the ancient <hi type="italic">is</hi> wisdom; and in length of days understanding.

verses.name: Job 12:13
verses.text: With him <hi type="italic">is</hi> wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding.

verses.name: Job 12:14
verses.text: Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again: he shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening.

verses.name: Job 12:15
verses.text: Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up: also he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth.

verses.name: Job 12:16
verses.text: With him <hi type="italic">is</hi> strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver <hi type="italic">are</hi> his.

verses.name: Job 12:17
verses.text: He leadeth counsellers away spoiled, and maketh the judges fools.

verses.name: Job 12:18
verses.text: He looseth the bond of kings, and girdeth their loins with a girdle.

verses.name: Job 12:19
verses.text: He leadeth princes away spoiled, and overthroweth the mighty.

verses.name: Job 12:20
verses.text: He removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged.

verses.name: Job 12:21
verses.text: He poureth contempt upon princes, and weakeneth the strength of the mighty.

verses.name: Job 12:22
verses.text: He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth out to light the shadow of death.

verses.name: Job 12:23
verses.text: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them <hi type="italic">again</hi>.

verses.name: Job 12:24
verses.text: He taketh away the heart of the chief of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a wilderness <hi type="italic">where there is</hi> no way.

verses.name: Job 12:25
verses.text: They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like <hi type="italic">a</hi> drunken <hi type="italic">man</hi>.  <chapter eID="Job.12"/><div eID="gen467" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 13:1
verses.text: LO, mine eye hath seen all <hi type="italic">this</hi>, mine ear hath heard and understood it.

verses.name: Job 13:2
verses.text: What ye know, <hi type="italic">the same</hi> do I know also: I <hi type="italic">am</hi> not inferior unto you.

verses.name: Job 13:3
verses.text: Surely I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God.

verses.name: Job 13:4
verses.text: But ye <hi type="italic">are</hi> forgers of lies, ye <hi type="italic">are</hi> all physicians of no value.

verses.name: Job 13:5
verses.text: O that ye would altogether hold your peace! and it should be your wisdom.

verses.name: Job 13:6
verses.text: Hear now my reasoning, and hearken to the pleadings of my lips.

verses.name: Job 13:7
verses.text: Will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him?

verses.name: Job 13:8
verses.text: Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God?

verses.name: Job 13:9
verses.text: Is it good that he should search you out? or as one man mocketh another, do ye <hi type="italic">so</hi> mock him?

verses.name: Job 13:10
verses.text: He will surely reprove you, if ye do secretly accept persons.

verses.name: Job 13:11
verses.text: Shall not his excellency make you afraid? and his dread fall upon you?

verses.name: Job 13:12
verses.text: Your remembrances <hi type="italic">are</hi> like unto ashes, your bodies to bodies of clay.

verses.name: Job 13:13
verses.text: Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak, and let come on me what <hi type="italic">will</hi>.

verses.name: Job 13:14
verses.text: Wherefore do I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in mine hand?

verses.name: Job 13:15
verses.text: Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him.

verses.name: Job 13:16
verses.text: He also <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> my salvation: for an hypocrite shall not come before him.

verses.name: Job 13:17
verses.text: Hear diligently my speech, and my declaration with your ears.

verses.name: Job 13:18
verses.text: Behold now, I have ordered <hi type="italic">my</hi> cause; I know that I shall be justified.

verses.name: Job 13:19
verses.text: Who <hi type="italic">is</hi> he <hi type="italic">that</hi> will plead with me? for now, if I hold my tongue, I shall give up the ghost.

verses.name: Job 13:20
verses.text: Only do not two <hi type="italic">things</hi> unto me: then will I not hide myself from thee.

verses.name: Job 13:21
verses.text: Withdraw thine hand far from me: and let not thy dread make me afraid.

verses.name: Job 13:22
verses.text: Then call thou, and I will answer: or let me speak, and answer thou me.

verses.name: Job 13:23
verses.text: How many <hi type="italic">are</hi> mine iniquities and sins? make me to know my transgression and my sin.

verses.name: Job 13:24
verses.text: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and holdest me for thine enemy?

verses.name: Job 13:25
verses.text: Wilt thou break a leaf driven to and fro? and wilt thou pursue the dry stubble?

verses.name: Job 13:26
verses.text: For thou writest bitter things against me, and makest me to possess the iniquities of my youth.

verses.name: Job 13:27
verses.text: Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, and lookest narrowly unto all my paths; thou settest a print upon the heels of my feet.

verses.name: Job 13:28
verses.text: And he, as a rotten thing, consumeth, as a garment that is moth eaten.  <chapter eID="Job.13"/><div eID="gen468" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 14:1
verses.text: MAN <hi type="italic">that is</hi> born of a woman <hi type="italic">is</hi> of few days, and full of trouble.

verses.name: Job 14:2
verses.text: He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.

verses.name: Job 14:3
verses.text: And dost thou open thine eyes upon such an one, and bringest me into judgment with thee?

verses.name: Job 14:4
verses.text: Who can bring a clean <hi type="italic">thing</hi> out of an unclean? not one.

verses.name: Job 14:5
verses.text: Seeing his days <hi type="italic">are</hi> determined, the number of his months <hi type="italic">are</hi> with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;

verses.name: Job 14:6
verses.text: Turn from him, that he may rest, till he shall accomplish, as an hireling, his day.

verses.name: Job 14:7
verses.text: For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again, and that the tender branch thereof will not cease.

verses.name: Job 14:8
verses.text: Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, and the stock thereof die in the ground;

verses.name: Job 14:9
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Yet</hi> through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant.

verses.name: Job 14:10
verses.text: But man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where <hi type="italic">is</hi> he?

verses.name: Job 14:11
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> the waters fail from the sea, and the flood decayeth and drieth up:

verses.name: Job 14:12
verses.text: So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens <hi type="italic">be</hi> no more, they shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep.

verses.name: Job 14:13
verses.text: O that thou wouldest hide me in the grave, that thou wouldest keep me secret, until thy wrath be past, that thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me!

verses.name: Job 14:14
verses.text: If a man die, shall he live <hi type="italic">again?</hi> all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.

verses.name: Job 14:15
verses.text: Thou shalt call, and I will answer thee: thou wilt have a desire to the work of thine hands.

verses.name: Job 14:16
verses.text: For now thou numberest my steps: dost thou not watch over my sin?

verses.name: Job 14:17
verses.text: My transgression <hi type="italic">is</hi> sealed up in a bag, and thou sewest up mine iniquity.

verses.name: Job 14:18
verses.text: And surely the mountain falling cometh to nought, and the rock is removed out of his place.

verses.name: Job 14:19
verses.text: The waters wear the stones: thou washest away the things which grow <hi type="italic">out</hi> of the dust of the earth; and thou destroyest the hope of man.

verses.name: Job 14:20
verses.text: Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth: thou changest his countenance, and sendest him away.

verses.name: Job 14:21
verses.text: His sons come to honour, and he knoweth <hi type="italic">it</hi> not; and they are brought low, but he perceiveth <hi type="italic">it</hi> not of them.

verses.name: Job 14:22
verses.text: But his flesh upon him shall have pain, and his soul within him shall mourn.  <chapter eID="Job.14"/><div eID="gen469" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 15:1
verses.text: THEN answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,

verses.name: Job 15:2
verses.text: Should a wise man utter vain knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind?

verses.name: Job 15:3
verses.text: Should he reason with unprofitable talk? or with speeches wherewith he can do no good?

verses.name: Job 15:4
verses.text: Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God.

verses.name: Job 15:5
verses.text: For thy mouth uttereth thine iniquity, and thou choosest the tongue of the crafty.

verses.name: Job 15:6
verses.text: Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I: yea, thine own lips testify against thee.

verses.name: Job 15:7
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Art</hi> thou the first man <hi type="italic">that</hi> was born? or wast thou made before the hills?

verses.name: Job 15:8
verses.text: Hast thou heard the secret of God? and dost thou restrain wisdom to thyself?

verses.name: Job 15:9
verses.text: What knowest thou, that we know not? <hi type="italic">what</hi> understandest thou, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> not in us?

verses.name: Job 15:10
verses.text: With us <hi type="italic">are</hi> both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father.

verses.name: Job 15:11
