verses.text: <hi type="italic">Are</hi> the consolations of God small with thee? is there any secret thing with thee?

verses.name: Job 15:12
verses.text: Why doth thine heart carry thee away? and what do thy eyes wink at,

verses.name: Job 15:13
verses.text: That thou turnest thy spirit against God, and lettest <hi type="italic">such</hi> words go out of thy mouth?

verses.name: Job 15:14
verses.text: What <hi type="italic">is</hi> man, that he should be clean? and <hi type="italic">he which is</hi> born of a woman, that he should be righteous?

verses.name: Job 15:15
verses.text: Behold, he putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight.

verses.name: Job 15:16
verses.text: How much more abominable and filthy <hi type="italic">is</hi> man, which drinketh iniquity like water?

verses.name: Job 15:17
verses.text: I will shew thee, hear me; and that <hi type="italic">which</hi> I have seen I will declare;

verses.name: Job 15:18
verses.text: Which wise men have told from their fathers, and have not hid <hi type="italic">it:</hi>

verses.name: Job 15:19
verses.text: Unto whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed among them.

verses.name: Job 15:20
verses.text: The wicked man travaileth with pain all <hi type="italic">his</hi> days, and the number of years is hidden to the oppressor.

verses.name: Job 15:21
verses.text: A dreadful sound <hi type="italic">is</hi> in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.

verses.name: Job 15:22
verses.text: He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.

verses.name: Job 15:23
verses.text: He wandereth abroad for bread, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, Where <hi type="italic">is it?</hi> he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.

verses.name: Job 15:24
verses.text: Trouble and anguish shall make him afraid; they shall prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.

verses.name: Job 15:25
verses.text: For he stretcheth out his hand against God, and strengtheneth himself against the Almighty.

verses.name: Job 15:26
verses.text: He runneth upon him, <hi type="italic">even</hi> on <hi type="italic">his</hi> neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers:

verses.name: Job 15:27
verses.text: Because he covereth his face with his fatness, and maketh collops of fat on <hi type="italic">his</hi> flanks.

verses.name: Job 15:28
verses.text: And he dwelleth in desolate cities, <hi type="italic">and</hi> in houses which no man inhabiteth, which are ready to become heaps.

verses.name: Job 15:29
verses.text: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he prolong the perfection thereof upon the earth.

verses.name: Job 15:30
verses.text: He shall not depart out of darkness; the flame shall dry up his branches, and by the breath of his mouth shall he go away.

verses.name: Job 15:31
verses.text: Let not him that is deceived trust in vanity: for vanity shall be his recompence.

verses.name: Job 15:32
verses.text: It shall be accomplished before his time, and his branch shall not be green.

verses.name: Job 15:33
verses.text: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive.

verses.name: Job 15:34
verses.text: For the congregation of hypocrites <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery.

verses.name: Job 15:35
verses.text: They conceive mischief, and bring forth vanity, and their belly prepareth deceit.  <chapter eID="Job.15"/><div eID="gen470" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 16:1
verses.text: THEN Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 16:2
verses.text: I have heard many such things: miserable comforters <hi type="italic">are</hi> ye all.

verses.name: Job 16:3
verses.text: Shall vain words have an end? or what emboldeneth thee that thou answerest?

verses.name: Job 16:4
verses.text: I also could speak as ye <hi type="italic">do:</hi> if your soul were in my soul’s stead, I could heap up words against you, and shake mine head at you.

verses.name: Job 16:5
verses.text: <hi type="italic">But</hi> I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the moving of my lips should asswage <hi type="italic">your grief</hi>.

verses.name: Job 16:6
verses.text: Though I speak, my grief is not asswaged: and <hi type="italic">though</hi> I forbear, what am I eased?

verses.name: Job 16:7
verses.text: But now he hath made me weary: thou hast made desolate all my company.

verses.name: Job 16:8
verses.text: And thou hast filled me with wrinkles, <hi type="italic">which</hi> is a witness <hi type="italic">against me:</hi> and my leanness rising up in me beareth witness to my face.

verses.name: Job 16:9
verses.text: He teareth <hi type="italic">me</hi> in his wrath, who hateth me: he gnasheth upon me with his teeth; mine enemy sharpeneth his eyes upon me.

verses.name: Job 16:10
verses.text: They have gaped upon me with their mouth; they have smitten me upon the cheek reproachfully; they have gathered themselves together against me.

verses.name: Job 16:11
verses.text: God hath delivered me to the ungodly, and turned me over into the hands of the wicked.

verses.name: Job 16:12
verses.text: I was at ease, but he hath broken me asunder: he hath also taken <hi type="italic">me</hi> by my neck, and shaken me to pieces, and set me up for his mark.

verses.name: Job 16:13
verses.text: His archers compass me round about, he cleaveth my reins asunder, and doth not spare; he poureth out my gall upon the ground.

verses.name: Job 16:14
verses.text: He breaketh me with breach upon breach, he runneth upon me like a giant.

verses.name: Job 16:15
verses.text: I have sewed sackcloth upon my skin, and defiled my horn in the dust.

verses.name: Job 16:16
verses.text: My face is foul with weeping, and on my eyelids <hi type="italic">is</hi> the shadow of death;

verses.name: Job 16:17
verses.text: Not for <hi type="italic">any</hi> injustice in mine hands: also my prayer <hi type="italic">is</hi> pure.

verses.name: Job 16:18
verses.text: O earth, cover not thou my blood, and let my cry have no place.

verses.name: Job 16:19
verses.text: Also now, behold, my witness <hi type="italic">is</hi> in heaven, and my record <hi type="italic">is</hi> on high.

verses.name: Job 16:20
verses.text: My friends scorn me: <hi type="italic">but</hi> mine eye poureth out <hi type="italic">tears</hi> unto God.

verses.name: Job 16:21
verses.text: O that one might plead for a man with God, as a man <hi type="italic">pleadeth</hi> for his neighbour!

verses.name: Job 16:22
verses.text: When a few years are come, then I shall go the way <hi type="italic">whence</hi> I shall not return.  <chapter eID="Job.16"/><div eID="gen471" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 17:1
verses.text: MY breath is corrupt, my days are extinct, the graves <hi type="italic">are ready</hi> for me.

verses.name: Job 17:2
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Are there</hi> not mockers with me? and doth not mine eye continue in their provocation?

verses.name: Job 17:3
verses.text: Lay down now, put me in a surety with thee; who <hi type="italic">is</hi> he <hi type="italic">that</hi> will strike hands with me?

verses.name: Job 17:4
verses.text: For thou hast hid their heart from understanding: therefore shalt thou not exalt <hi type="italic">them</hi>.

verses.name: Job 17:5
verses.text: He that speaketh flattery to <hi type="italic">his</hi> friends, even the eyes of his children shall fail.

verses.name: Job 17:6
verses.text: He hath made me also a byword of the people; and aforetime I was as a tabret.

verses.name: Job 17:7
verses.text: Mine eye also is dim by reason of sorrow, and all my members <hi type="italic">are</hi> as a shadow.

verses.name: Job 17:8
verses.text: Upright <hi type="italic">men</hi> shall be astonied at this, and the innocent shall stir up himself against the hypocrite.

verses.name: Job 17:9
verses.text: The righteous also shall hold on his way, and he that hath clean hands shall be stronger and stronger.

verses.name: Job 17:10
verses.text: But as for you all, do ye return, and come now: for I cannot find <hi type="italic">one</hi> wise <hi type="italic">man</hi> among you.

verses.name: Job 17:11
verses.text: My days are past, my purposes are broken off, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the thoughts of my heart.

verses.name: Job 17:12
verses.text: They change the night into day: the light <hi type="italic">is</hi> short because of darkness.

verses.name: Job 17:13
verses.text: If I wait, the grave <hi type="italic">is</hi> mine house: I have made my bed in the darkness.

verses.name: Job 17:14
verses.text: I have said to corruption, Thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> my father: to the worm, <hi type="italic">Thou art</hi> my mother, and my sister.

verses.name: Job 17:15
verses.text: And where <hi type="italic">is</hi> now my hope? as for my hope, who shall see it?

verses.name: Job 17:16
verses.text: They shall go down to the bars of the pit, when <hi type="italic">our</hi> rest together <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the dust.  <chapter eID="Job.17"/><div eID="gen472" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 18:1
verses.text: THEN answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,

verses.name: Job 18:2
verses.text: How long <hi type="italic">will it be ere</hi> ye make an end of words? mark, and afterwards we will speak.

verses.name: Job 18:3
verses.text: Wherefore are we counted as beasts, <hi type="italic">and</hi> reputed vile in your sight?

verses.name: Job 18:4
verses.text: He teareth himself in his anger: shall the earth be forsaken for thee? and shall the rock be removed out of his place?

verses.name: Job 18:5
verses.text: Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out, and the spark of his fire shall not shine.

verses.name: Job 18:6
verses.text: The light shall be dark in his tabernacle, and his candle shall be put out with him.

verses.name: Job 18:7
verses.text: The steps of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down.

verses.name: Job 18:8
verses.text: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he walketh upon a snare.

verses.name: Job 18:9
verses.text: The gin shall take <hi type="italic">him</hi> by the heel, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the robber shall prevail against him.

verses.name: Job 18:10
verses.text: The snare <hi type="italic">is</hi> laid for him in the ground, and a trap for him in the way.

verses.name: Job 18:11
verses.text: Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall drive him to his feet.

verses.name: Job 18:12
verses.text: His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> ready at his side.

verses.name: Job 18:13
verses.text: It shall devour the strength of his skin: <hi type="italic">even</hi> the firstborn of death shall devour his strength.

verses.name: Job 18:14
verses.text: His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors.

verses.name: Job 18:15
verses.text: It shall dwell in his tabernacle, because <hi type="italic">it is</hi> none of his: brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation.

verses.name: Job 18:16
verses.text: His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off.

verses.name: Job 18:17
verses.text: His remembrance shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name in the street.

verses.name: Job 18:18
verses.text: He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.

verses.name: Job 18:19
verses.text: He shall neither have son nor nephew among his people, nor any remaining in his dwellings.

verses.name: Job 18:20
verses.text: They that come after <hi type="italic">him</hi> shall be astonied at his day, as they that went before were affrighted.

verses.name: Job 18:21
verses.text: Surely such <hi type="italic">are</hi> the dwellings of the wicked, and this <hi type="italic">is</hi> the place <hi type="italic">of him that</hi> knoweth not God.  <chapter eID="Job.18"/><div eID="gen473" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 19:1
verses.text: THEN Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 19:2
verses.text: How long will ye vex my soul, and break me in pieces with words?

verses.name: Job 19:3
verses.text: These ten times have ye reproached me: ye are not ashamed <hi type="italic">that</hi> ye make yourselves strange to me.

verses.name: Job 19:4
verses.text: And be it indeed <hi type="italic">that</hi> I have erred, mine error remaineth with myself.

verses.name: Job 19:5
verses.text: If indeed ye will magnify <hi type="italic">yourselves</hi> against me, and plead against me my reproach:

verses.name: Job 19:6
verses.text: Know now that God hath overthrown me, and hath compassed me with his net.

verses.name: Job 19:7
verses.text: Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard: I cry aloud, but <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no judgment.

verses.name: Job 19:8
verses.text: He hath fenced up my way that I cannot pass, and he hath set darkness in my paths.

verses.name: Job 19:9
verses.text: He hath stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown <hi type="italic">from</hi> my head.

verses.name: Job 19:10
verses.text: He hath destroyed me on every side, and I am gone: and mine hope hath he removed like a tree.

verses.name: Job 19:11
verses.text: He hath also kindled his wrath against me, and he counteth me unto him as <hi type="italic">one of</hi> his enemies.

verses.name: Job 19:12
verses.text: His troops come together, and raise up their way against me, and encamp round about my tabernacle.

verses.name: Job 19:13
verses.text: He hath put my brethren far from me, and mine acquaintance are verily estranged from me.

verses.name: Job 19:14
verses.text: My kinsfolk have failed, and my familiar friends have forgotten me.

verses.name: Job 19:15
verses.text: They that dwell in mine house, and my maids, count me for a stranger: I am an alien in their sight.

verses.name: Job 19:16
verses.text: I called my servant, and he gave <hi type="italic">me</hi> no answer; I intreated him with my mouth.

verses.name: Job 19:17
verses.text: My breath is strange to my wife, though I intreated for the children’s <hi type="italic">sake</hi> of mine own body.

verses.name: Job 19:18
verses.text: Yea, young children despised me; I arose, and they spake against me.

verses.name: Job 19:19
verses.text: All my inward friends abhorred me: and they whom I loved are turned against me.

verses.name: Job 19:20
verses.text: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth.

verses.name: Job 19:21
verses.text: Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O ye my friends; for the hand of God hath touched me.

verses.name: Job 19:22
verses.text: Why do ye persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?

verses.name: Job 19:23
verses.text: Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book!

verses.name: Job 19:24
verses.text: That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever!

verses.name: Job 19:25
verses.text: For I know <hi type="italic">that</hi> my redeemer liveth, and <hi type="italic">that</hi> he shall stand at the latter <hi type="italic">day</hi> upon the earth:

verses.name: Job 19:26
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">though</hi> after my skin <hi type="italic">worms</hi> destroy this <hi type="italic">body</hi>, yet in my flesh shall I see God:

verses.name: Job 19:27
verses.text: Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another; <hi type="italic">though</hi> my reins be consumed within me.

verses.name: Job 19:28
verses.text: But ye should say, Why persecute we him, seeing the root of the matter is found in me?

verses.name: Job 19:29
verses.text: Be ye afraid of the sword: for wrath <hi type="italic">bringeth</hi> the punishments of the sword, that ye may know <hi type="italic">there is</hi> a judgment.  <chapter eID="Job.19"/><div eID="gen474" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 20:1
verses.text: THEN answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,

verses.name: Job 20:2
verses.text: Therefore do my thoughts cause me to answer, and for <hi type="italic">this</hi> I make haste.

verses.name: Job 20:3
verses.text: I have heard the check of my reproach, and the spirit of my understanding causeth me to answer.

verses.name: Job 20:4
verses.text: Knowest thou <hi type="italic">not</hi> this of old, since man was placed upon earth,

verses.name: Job 20:5
verses.text: That the triumphing of the wicked <hi type="italic">is</hi> short, and the joy of the hypocrite <hi type="italic">but</hi> for a moment?

verses.name: Job 20:6
verses.text: Though his excellency mount up to the heavens, and his head reach unto the clouds;

verses.name: Job 20:7
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Yet</hi> he shall perish for ever like his own dung: they which have seen him shall say, Where <hi type="italic">is</hi> he?

verses.name: Job 20:8
verses.text: He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found: yea, he shall be chased away as a vision of the night.

verses.name: Job 20:9
verses.text: The eye also <hi type="italic">which</hi> saw him shall <hi type="italic">see him</hi> no more; neither shall his place any more behold him.

verses.name: Job 20:10
verses.text: His children shall seek to please the poor, and his hands shall restore their goods.

verses.name: Job 20:11
verses.text: His bones are full <hi type="italic">of the sin</hi> of his youth, which shall lie down with him in the dust.

verses.name: Job 20:12
verses.text: Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, <hi type="italic">though</hi> he hide it under his tongue;

verses.name: Job 20:13
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Though</hi> he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth:

verses.name: Job 20:14
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Yet</hi> his meat in his bowels is turned, <hi type="italic">it is</hi> the gall of asps within him.

verses.name: Job 20:15
verses.text: He hath swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again: God shall cast them out of his belly.

verses.name: Job 20:16
verses.text: He shall suck the poison of asps: the viper’s tongue shall slay him.

verses.name: Job 20:17
verses.text: He shall not see the rivers, the floods, the brooks of honey and butter.

verses.name: Job 20:18
verses.text: That which he laboured for shall he restore, and shall not swallow <hi type="italic">it</hi> down: according to <hi type="italic">his</hi> substance <hi type="italic">shall</hi> the restitution <hi type="italic">be</hi>, and he shall not rejoice <hi type="italic">therein</hi>.

verses.name: Job 20:19
verses.text: Because he hath oppressed <hi type="italic">and</hi> hath forsaken the poor; <hi type="italic">because</hi> he hath violently taken away an house which he builded not;

verses.name: Job 20:20
verses.text: Surely he shall not feel quietness in his belly, he shall not save of that which he desired.

verses.name: Job 20:21
verses.text: There shall none of his meat be left; therefore shall no man look for his goods.

verses.name: Job 20:22
verses.text: In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.

verses.name: Job 20:23
verses.text: <hi type="italic">When</hi> he is about to fill his belly, <hi type="italic">God</hi> shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain <hi type="italic">it</hi> upon him while he is eating.

verses.name: Job 20:24
verses.text: He shall flee from the iron weapon, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the bow of steel shall strike him through.

verses.name: Job 20:25
verses.text: It is drawn, and cometh out of the body; yea, the glittering sword cometh out of his gall: terrors <hi type="italic">are</hi> upon him.

verses.name: Job 20:26
verses.text: All darkness <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> hid in his secret places: a fire not blown shall consume him; it shall go ill with him that is left in his tabernacle.

verses.name: Job 20:27
verses.text: The heaven shall reveal his iniquity; and the earth shall rise up against him.

verses.name: Job 20:28
verses.text: The increase of his house shall depart, <hi type="italic">and his goods</hi> shall flow away in the day of his wrath.

verses.name: Job 20:29
verses.text: This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed unto him by God.  <chapter eID="Job.20"/><div eID="gen475" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 21:1
verses.text: BUT Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 21:2
verses.text: Hear diligently my speech, and let this be your consolations.

verses.name: Job 21:3
verses.text: Suffer me that I may speak; and after that I have spoken, mock on.

verses.name: Job 21:4
verses.text: As for me, <hi type="italic">is</hi> my complaint to man? and if <hi type="italic">it were so</hi>, why should not my spirit be troubled?

verses.name: Job 21:5
verses.text: Mark me, and be astonished, and lay <hi type="italic">your</hi> hand upon <hi type="italic">your</hi> mouth.

verses.name: Job 21:6
verses.text: Even when I remember I am afraid, and trembling taketh hold on my flesh.

verses.name: Job 21:7
verses.text: Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power?

verses.name: Job 21:8
verses.text: Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes.

verses.name: Job 21:9
verses.text: Their houses <hi type="italic">are</hi> safe from fear, neither <hi type="italic">is</hi> the rod of God upon them.

verses.name: Job 21:10
verses.text: Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.

verses.name: Job 21:11
verses.text: They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance.

verses.name: Job 21:12
verses.text: They take the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.

verses.name: Job 21:13
verses.text: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave.

verses.name: Job 21:14
verses.text: Therefore they say unto God, Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.

verses.name: Job 21:15
verses.text: What <hi type="italic">is</hi> the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?

verses.name: Job 21:16
verses.text: Lo, their good <hi type="italic">is</hi> not in their hand: the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

verses.name: Job 21:17
verses.text: How oft is the candle of the wicked put out! and <hi type="italic">how oft</hi> cometh their destruction upon them! <hi type="italic">God</hi> distributeth sorrows in his anger.

verses.name: Job 21:18
verses.text: They are as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the storm carrieth away.

verses.name: Job 21:19
verses.text: God layeth up his iniquity for his children: he rewardeth him, and he shall know <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Job 21:20
verses.text: His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.

verses.name: Job 21:21
verses.text: For what pleasure <hi type="italic">hath</hi> he in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off in the midst?

verses.name: Job 21:22
verses.text: Shall <hi type="italic">any</hi> teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high.

verses.name: Job 21:23
verses.text: One dieth in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.

verses.name: Job 21:24
verses.text: His breasts are full of milk, and his bones are moistened with marrow.

verses.name: Job 21:25
verses.text: And another dieth in the bitterness of his soul, and never eateth with pleasure.

verses.name: Job 21:26
verses.text: They shall lie down alike in the dust, and the worms shall cover them.

verses.name: Job 21:27
verses.text: Behold, I know your thoughts, and the devices <hi type="italic">which</hi> ye wrongfully imagine against me.

verses.name: Job 21:28
verses.text: For ye say, Where <hi type="italic">is</hi> the house of the prince? and where <hi type="italic">are</hi> the dwelling places of the wicked?

verses.name: Job 21:29
verses.text: Have ye not asked them that go by the way? and do ye not know their tokens,

verses.name: Job 21:30
verses.text: That the wicked is reserved to the day of destruction? they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.

verses.name: Job 21:31
verses.text: Who shall declare his way to his face? and who shall repay him <hi type="italic">what</hi> he hath done?

verses.name: Job 21:32
verses.text: Yet shall he be brought to the grave, and shall remain in the tomb.

verses.name: Job 21:33
verses.text: The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, and every man shall draw after him, as <hi type="italic">there are</hi> innumerable before him.

verses.name: Job 21:34
verses.text: How then comfort ye me in vain, seeing in your answers there remaineth falsehood?  <chapter eID="Job.21"/><div eID="gen476" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 22:1
verses.text: THEN Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,

verses.name: Job 22:2
verses.text: Can a man be profitable unto God, as he that is wise may be profitable unto himself?

verses.name: Job 22:3
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is it</hi> any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? or <hi type="italic">is it</hi> gain <hi type="italic">to him</hi>, that thou makest thy ways perfect?

verses.name: Job 22:4
verses.text: Will he reprove thee for fear of thee? will he enter with thee into judgment?

verses.name: Job 22:5
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is</hi> not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?

verses.name: Job 22:6
verses.text: For thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother for nought, and stripped the naked of their clothing.

verses.name: Job 22:7
verses.text: Thou hast not given water to the weary to drink, and thou hast withholden bread from the hungry.

verses.name: Job 22:8
verses.text: But <hi type="italic">as for</hi> the mighty man, he had the earth; and the honourable man dwelt in it.

verses.name: Job 22:9
verses.text: Thou hast sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.

verses.name: Job 22:10
verses.text: Therefore snares <hi type="italic">are</hi> round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee;

verses.name: Job 22:11
verses.text: Or darkness, <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou canst not see; and abundance of waters cover thee.

verses.name: Job 22:12
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is</hi> not God in the height of heaven? and behold the height of the stars, how high they are!

verses.name: Job 22:13
verses.text: And thou sayest, How doth God know? can he judge through the dark cloud?

verses.name: Job 22:14
verses.text: Thick clouds <hi type="italic">are</hi> a covering to him, that he seeth not; and he walketh in the circuit of heaven.

verses.name: Job 22:15
verses.text: Hast thou marked the old way which wicked men have trodden?

verses.name: Job 22:16
verses.text: Which were cut down out of time, whose foundation was overflown with a flood:

verses.name: Job 22:17
verses.text: Which said unto God, Depart from us: and what can the Almighty do for them?

verses.name: Job 22:18
verses.text: Yet he filled their houses with good <hi type="italic">things:</hi> but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

verses.name: Job 22:19
verses.text: The righteous see <hi type="italic">it</hi>, and are glad: and the innocent laugh them to scorn.

verses.name: Job 22:20
verses.text: Whereas our substance is not cut down, but the remnant of them the fire consumeth.

verses.name: Job 22:21
verses.text: Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come unto thee.

verses.name: Job 22:22
verses.text: Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, and lay up his words in thine heart.

verses.name: Job 22:23
verses.text: If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, thou shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacles.

verses.name: Job 22:24
verses.text: Then shalt thou lay up gold as dust, and the <hi type="italic">gold</hi> of Ophir as the stones of the brooks.

verses.name: Job 22:25
verses.text: Yea, the Almighty shall be thy defence, and thou shalt have plenty of silver.

verses.name: Job 22:26
verses.text: For then shalt thou have thy delight in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face unto God.

verses.name: Job 22:27
verses.text: Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he shall hear thee, and thou shalt pay thy vows.

verses.name: Job 22:28
verses.text: Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee: and the light shall shine upon thy ways.

verses.name: Job 22:29
verses.text: When <hi type="italic">men</hi> are cast down, then thou shalt say, <hi type="italic">There is</hi> lifting up; and he shall save the humble person.

verses.name: Job 22:30
verses.text: He shall deliver the island of the innocent: and it is delivered by the pureness of thine hands.  <chapter eID="Job.22"/><div eID="gen477" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 23:1
verses.text: THEN Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 23:2
verses.text: Even to day <hi type="italic">is</hi> my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning.

verses.name: Job 23:3
verses.text: Oh that I knew where I might find him! <hi type="italic">that</hi> I might come <hi type="italic">even</hi> to his seat!

verses.name: Job 23:4
verses.text: I would order <hi type="italic">my</hi> cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.

verses.name: Job 23:5
verses.text: I would know the words <hi type="italic">which</hi> he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me.

verses.name: Job 23:6
verses.text: Will he plead against me with <hi type="italic">his</hi> great power? No; but he would put <hi type="italic">strength</hi> in me.

verses.name: Job 23:7
verses.text: There the righteous might dispute with him; so should I be delivered for ever from my judge.

verses.name: Job 23:8
verses.text: Behold, I go forward, but he <hi type="italic">is</hi> not <hi type="italic">there;</hi> and backward, but I cannot perceive him:

verses.name: Job 23:9
verses.text: On the left hand, where he doth work, but I cannot behold <hi type="italic">him:</hi> he hideth himself on the right hand, that I cannot see <hi type="italic">him:</hi>

verses.name: Job 23:10
verses.text: But he knoweth the way that I take: <hi type="italic">when</hi> he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.

verses.name: Job 23:11
verses.text: My foot hath held his steps, his way have I kept, and not declined.

verses.name: Job 23:12
verses.text: Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary <hi type="italic">food</hi>.

verses.name: Job 23:13
verses.text: But he <hi type="italic">is</hi> in one <hi type="italic">mind</hi>, and who can turn him? and <hi type="italic">what</hi> his soul desireth, even <hi type="italic">that</hi> he doeth.

verses.name: Job 23:14
verses.text: For he performeth <hi type="italic">the thing that is</hi> appointed for me: and many such <hi type="italic">things are</hi> with him.

verses.name: Job 23:15
verses.text: Therefore am I troubled at his presence: when I consider, I am afraid of him.

verses.name: Job 23:16
verses.text: For God maketh my heart soft, and the Almighty troubleth me:

verses.name: Job 23:17
verses.text: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, <hi type="italic">neither</hi> hath he covered the darkness from my face.  <chapter eID="Job.23"/><div eID="gen478" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 24:1
verses.text: WHY, seeing times are not hidden from the Almighty, do they that know him not see his days?

verses.name: Job 24:2
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Some</hi> remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and feed <hi type="italic">thereof</hi>.

verses.name: Job 24:3
verses.text: They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.

verses.name: Job 24:4
verses.text: They turn the needy out of the way: the poor of the earth hide themselves together.

verses.name: Job 24:5
verses.text: Behold, <hi type="italic">as</hi> wild asses in the desert, go they forth to their work; rising betimes for a prey: the wilderness <hi type="italic">yieldeth</hi> food for them <hi type="italic">and</hi> for <hi type="italic">their</hi> children.

verses.name: Job 24:6
verses.text: They reap <hi type="italic">every one</hi> his corn in the field: and they gather the vintage of the wicked.

verses.name: Job 24:7
verses.text: They cause the naked to lodge without clothing, that <hi type="italic">they have</hi> no covering in the cold.

verses.name: Job 24:8
verses.text: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for want of a shelter.

verses.name: Job 24:9
verses.text: They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor.

verses.name: Job 24:10
verses.text: They cause <hi type="italic">him</hi> to go naked without clothing, and they take away the sheaf <hi type="italic">from</hi> the hungry;

verses.name: Job 24:11
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Which</hi> make oil within their walls, <hi type="italic">and</hi> tread <hi type="italic">their</hi> winepresses, and suffer thirst.

verses.name: Job 24:12
verses.text: Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out: yet God layeth not folly <hi type="italic">to them</hi>.

verses.name: Job 24:13
verses.text: They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof, nor abide in the paths thereof.

verses.name: Job 24:14
verses.text: The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief.

verses.name: Job 24:15
verses.text: The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth <hi type="italic">his</hi> face.

verses.name: Job 24:16
verses.text: In the dark they dig through houses, <hi type="italic">which</hi> they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light.

verses.name: Job 24:17
verses.text: For the morning <hi type="italic">is</hi> to them even as the shadow of death: if <hi type="italic">one</hi> know <hi type="italic">them</hi>, <hi type="italic">they are in</hi> the terrors of the shadow of death.

verses.name: Job 24:18
verses.text: He <hi type="italic">is</hi> swift as the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth: he beholdeth not the way of the vineyards.

verses.name: Job 24:19
verses.text: Drought and heat consume the snow waters: <hi type="italic">so doth</hi> the grave <hi type="italic">those which</hi> have sinned.

verses.name: Job 24:20
verses.text: The womb shall forget him; the worm shall feed sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered; and wickedness shall be broken as a tree.

verses.name: Job 24:21
verses.text: He evil entreateth the barren <hi type="italic">that</hi> beareth not: and doeth not good to the widow.

verses.name: Job 24:22
verses.text: He draweth also the mighty with his power: he riseth up, and no <hi type="italic">man</hi> is sure of life.

verses.name: Job 24:23
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Though</hi> it be given him <hi type="italic">to be</hi> in safety, whereon he resteth; yet his eyes <hi type="italic">are</hi> upon their ways.

verses.name: Job 24:24
verses.text: They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all <hi type="italic">other</hi>, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn.

verses.name: Job 24:25
verses.text: And if <hi type="italic">it be</hi> not <hi type="italic">so</hi> now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?  <chapter eID="Job.24"/><div eID="gen479" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 25:1
verses.text: THEN answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,

verses.name: Job 25:2
verses.text: Dominion and fear <hi type="italic">are</hi> with him, he maketh peace in his high places.

verses.name: Job 25:3
verses.text: Is there any number of his armies? and upon whom doth not his light arise?

verses.name: Job 25:4
verses.text: How then can man be justified with God? or how can he be clean <hi type="italic">that is</hi> born of a woman?

verses.name: Job 25:5
verses.text: Behold even to the moon, and it shineth not; yea, the stars are not pure in his sight.

verses.name: Job 25:6
verses.text: How much less man, <hi type="italic">that is</hi> a worm? and the son of man, <hi type="italic">which is</hi> a worm?  <chapter eID="Job.25"/><div eID="gen480" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 26:1
verses.text: BUT Job answered and said,

verses.name: Job 26:2
verses.text: How hast thou helped <hi type="italic">him that is</hi> without power? <hi type="italic">how</hi> savest thou the arm <hi type="italic">that hath</hi> no strength?

verses.name: Job 26:3
verses.text: How hast thou counselled <hi type="italic">him that hath</hi> no wisdom? and <hi type="italic">how</hi> hast thou plentifully declared the thing as it is?

verses.name: Job 26:4
verses.text: To whom hast thou uttered words? and whose spirit came from thee?

verses.name: Job 26:5
verses.text: Dead <hi type="italic">things</hi> are formed from under the waters, and the inhabitants thereof.

verses.name: Job 26:6
verses.text: Hell <hi type="italic">is</hi> naked before him, and destruction hath no covering.

verses.name: Job 26:7
verses.text: He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, <hi type="italic">and</hi> hangeth the earth upon nothing.

verses.name: Job 26:8
verses.text: He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; and the cloud is not rent under them.

verses.name: Job 26:9
verses.text: He holdeth back the face of his throne, <hi type="italic">and</hi> spreadeth his cloud upon it.

verses.name: Job 26:10
verses.text: He hath compassed the waters with bounds, until the day and night come to an end.

verses.name: Job 26:11
verses.text: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his reproof.

verses.name: Job 26:12
verses.text: He divideth the sea with his power, and by his understanding he smiteth through the proud.

verses.name: Job 26:13
verses.text: By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.

verses.name: Job 26:14
verses.text: Lo, these <hi type="italic">are</hi> parts of his ways: but how little a portion is heard of him? but the thunder of his power who can understand?  <chapter eID="Job.26"/><div eID="gen481" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 27:1
verses.text: MOREOVER Job continued his parable, and said,

verses.name: Job 27:2
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> God liveth, <hi type="italic">who</hi> hath taken away my judgment; and the Almighty, <hi type="italic">who</hi> hath vexed my soul;

verses.name: Job 27:3
verses.text: All the while my breath <hi type="italic">is</hi> in me, and the spirit of God <hi type="italic">is</hi> in my nostrils;

verses.name: Job 27:4
verses.text: My lips shall not speak wickedness, nor my tongue utter deceit.

verses.name: Job 27:5
verses.text: God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.

verses.name: Job 27:6
verses.text: My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach <hi type="italic">me</hi> so long as I live.

verses.name: Job 27:7
verses.text: Let mine enemy be as the wicked, and he that riseth up against me as the unrighteous.

verses.name: Job 27:8
verses.text: For what <hi type="italic">is</hi> the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when God taketh away his soul?

verses.name: Job 27:9
verses.text: Will God hear his cry when trouble cometh upon him?

verses.name: Job 27:10
verses.text: Will he delight himself in the Almighty? will he always call upon God?

verses.name: Job 27:11
verses.text: I will teach you by the hand of God: <hi type="italic">that</hi> which <hi type="italic">is</hi> with the Almighty will I not conceal.

verses.name: Job 27:12
verses.text: Behold, all ye yourselves have seen <hi type="italic">it;</hi> why then are ye thus altogether vain?

verses.name: Job 27:13
verses.text: This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of oppressors, <hi type="italic">which</hi> they shall receive of the Almighty.

verses.name: Job 27:14
verses.text: If his children be multiplied, <hi type="italic">it is</hi> for the sword: and his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.

verses.name: Job 27:15
verses.text: Those that remain of him shall be buried in death: and his widows shall not weep.

verses.name: Job 27:16
verses.text: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare raiment as the clay;

verses.name: Job 27:17
verses.text: He may prepare <hi type="italic">it</hi>, but the just shall put <hi type="italic">it</hi> on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.

verses.name: Job 27:18
verses.text: He buildeth his house as a moth, and as a booth <hi type="italic">that</hi> the keeper maketh.

verses.name: Job 27:19
verses.text: The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he openeth his eyes, and he <hi type="italic">is</hi> not.

verses.name: Job 27:20
verses.text: Terrors take hold on him as waters, a tempest stealeth him away in the night.

verses.name: Job 27:21
verses.text: The east wind carrieth him away, and he departeth: and as a storm hurleth him out of his place.

verses.name: Job 27:22
verses.text: For <hi type="italic">God</hi> shall cast upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand.

verses.name: Job 27:23
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Men</hi> shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.  <chapter eID="Job.27"/><div eID="gen482" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 28:1
verses.text: SURELY there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold <hi type="italic">where</hi> they fine <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Job 28:2
verses.text: Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass <hi type="italic">is</hi> molten <hi type="italic">out of</hi> the stone.

verses.name: Job 28:3
verses.text: He setteth an end to darkness, and searcheth out all perfection: the stones of darkness, and the shadow of death.

verses.name: Job 28:4
verses.text: The flood breaketh out from the inhabitant; <hi type="italic">even the waters</hi> forgotten of the foot: they are dried up, they are gone away from men.

verses.name: Job 28:5
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As for</hi> the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire.

verses.name: Job 28:6
verses.text: The stones of it <hi type="italic">are</hi> the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold.

verses.name: Job 28:7
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture’s eye hath not seen:

verses.name: Job 28:8
verses.text: The lion’s whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.

verses.name: Job 28:9
verses.text: He putteth forth his hand upon the rock; he overturneth the mountains by the roots.

verses.name: Job 28:10
verses.text: He cutteth out rivers among the rocks; and his eye seeth every precious thing.

verses.name: Job 28:11
verses.text: He bindeth the floods from overflowing; and <hi type="italic">the thing that is</hi> hid bringeth he forth to light.

verses.name: Job 28:12
verses.text: But where shall wisdom be found? and where <hi type="italic">is</hi> the place of understanding?

verses.name: Job 28:13
verses.text: Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living.

verses.name: Job 28:14
verses.text: The depth saith, It <hi type="italic">is</hi> not in me: and the sea saith, <hi type="italic">It is</hi> not with me.

verses.name: Job 28:15
verses.text: It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed <hi type="italic">for</hi> the price thereof.

verses.name: Job 28:16
verses.text: It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.

verses.name: Job 28:17
verses.text: The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it <hi type="italic">shall not be for</hi> jewels of fine gold.

verses.name: Job 28:18
verses.text: No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> above rubies.

verses.name: Job 28:19
verses.text: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold.

verses.name: Job 28:20
verses.text: Whence then cometh wisdom? and where <hi type="italic">is</hi> the place of understanding?

verses.name: Job 28:21
verses.text: Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air.

verses.name: Job 28:22
verses.text: Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears.

verses.name: Job 28:23
verses.text: God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof.

verses.name: Job 28:24
verses.text: For he looketh to the ends of the earth, <hi type="italic">and</hi> seeth under the whole heaven;

verses.name: Job 28:25
verses.text: To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure.

verses.name: Job 28:26
verses.text: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder:

verses.name: Job 28:27
verses.text: Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out.

verses.name: Job 28:28
verses.text: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that <hi type="italic">is</hi> wisdom; and to depart from evil <hi type="italic">is</hi> understanding.  <chapter eID="Job.28"/><div eID="gen483" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 29:1
verses.text: MOREOVER Job continued his parable, and said,

verses.name: Job 29:2
verses.text: Oh that I were as <hi type="italic">in</hi> months past, as <hi type="italic">in</hi> the days <hi type="italic">when</hi> God preserved me;

verses.name: Job 29:3
verses.text: When his candle shined upon my head, <hi type="italic">and when</hi> by his light I walked <hi type="italic">through</hi> darkness;

verses.name: Job 29:4
verses.text: As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God <hi type="italic">was</hi> upon my tabernacle;

verses.name: Job 29:5
verses.text: When the Almighty <hi type="italic">was</hi> yet with me, <hi type="italic">when</hi> my children <hi type="italic">were</hi> about me;

verses.name: Job 29:6
verses.text: When I washed my steps with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil;

verses.name: Job 29:7
verses.text: When I went out to the gate through the city, <hi type="italic">when</hi> I prepared my seat in the street!

verses.name: Job 29:8
verses.text: The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, <hi type="italic">and</hi> stood up.

verses.name: Job 29:9
verses.text: The princes refrained talking, and laid <hi type="italic">their</hi> hand on their mouth.

verses.name: Job 29:10
verses.text: The nobles held their peace, and their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth.

verses.name: Job 29:11
verses.text: When the ear heard <hi type="italic">me</hi>, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw <hi type="italic">me</hi>, it gave witness to me:

verses.name: Job 29:12
verses.text: Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and <hi type="italic">him that had</hi> none to help him.

verses.name: Job 29:13
verses.text: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.

verses.name: Job 29:14
verses.text: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment <hi type="italic">was</hi> as a robe and a diadem.

verses.name: Job 29:15
verses.text: I was eyes to the blind, and feet <hi type="italic">was</hi> I to the lame.

verses.name: Job 29:16
verses.text: I <hi type="italic">was</hi> a father to the poor: and the cause <hi type="italic">which</hi> I knew not I searched out.

verses.name: Job 29:17
verses.text: And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth.

verses.name: Job 29:18
verses.text: Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply <hi type="italic">my</hi> days as the sand.

verses.name: Job 29:19
verses.text: My root <hi type="italic">was</hi> spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch.

verses.name: Job 29:20
verses.text: My glory <hi type="italic">was</hi> fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand.

verses.name: Job 29:21
verses.text: Unto me <hi type="italic">men</hi> gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.

verses.name: Job 29:22
verses.text: After my words they spake not again; and my speech dropped upon them.

verses.name: Job 29:23
verses.text: And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide <hi type="italic">as</hi> for the latter rain.

verses.name: Job 29:24
verses.text: <hi type="italic">If</hi> I laughed on them, they believed <hi type="italic">it</hi> not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down.

verses.name: Job 29:25
verses.text: I chose out their way, and sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one <hi type="italic">that</hi> comforteth the mourners.  <chapter eID="Job.29"/><div eID="gen484" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 30:1
verses.text: BUT now <hi type="italic">they that are</hi> younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.

verses.name: Job 30:2
verses.text: Yea, whereto <hi type="italic">might</hi> the strength of their hands <hi type="italic">profit</hi> me, in whom old age was perished?

verses.name: Job 30:3
verses.text: For want and famine <hi type="italic">they were</hi> solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.

verses.name: Job 30:4
verses.text: Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots <hi type="italic">for</hi> their meat.

verses.name: Job 30:5
verses.text: They were driven forth from among <hi type="italic">men</hi>, (they cried after them as <hi type="italic">after</hi> a thief;)

verses.name: Job 30:6
verses.text: To dwell in the clifts of the valleys, <hi type="italic">in</hi> caves of the earth, and <hi type="italic">in</hi> the rocks.

verses.name: Job 30:7
verses.text: Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together.

verses.name: Job 30:8
verses.text: <hi type="italic">They were</hi> children of fools, yea, children of base men: they were viler than the earth.

verses.name: Job 30:9
verses.text: And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.

verses.name: Job 30:10
verses.text: They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.

verses.name: Job 30:11
verses.text: Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me.

verses.name: Job 30:12
verses.text: Upon <hi type="italic">my</hi> right <hi type="italic">hand</hi> rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.

verses.name: Job 30:13
verses.text: They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, they have no helper.

verses.name: Job 30:14
verses.text: They came <hi type="italic">upon me</hi> as a wide breaking in <hi type="italic">of waters:</hi> in the desolation they rolled themselves <hi type="italic">upon me</hi>.

verses.name: Job 30:15
verses.text: Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud.

verses.name: Job 30:16
verses.text: And now my soul is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have taken hold upon me.

verses.name: Job 30:17
verses.text: My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.

verses.name: Job 30:18
verses.text: By the great force <hi type="italic">of my disease</hi> is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.

verses.name: Job 30:19
verses.text: He hath cast me into the mire, and I am become like dust and ashes.

verses.name: Job 30:20
verses.text: I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me <hi type="italic">not</hi>.

verses.name: Job 30:21
verses.text: Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me.

verses.name: Job 30:22
verses.text: Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to ride <hi type="italic">upon it</hi>, and dissolvest my substance.

verses.name: Job 30:23
verses.text: For I know <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou wilt bring me <hi type="italic">to</hi> death, and <hi type="italic">to</hi> the house appointed for all living.

verses.name: Job 30:24
verses.text: Howbeit he will not stretch out <hi type="italic">his</hi> hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction.

verses.name: Job 30:25
verses.text: Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was <hi type="italic">not</hi> my soul grieved for the poor?

verses.name: Job 30:26
verses.text: When I looked for good, then evil came <hi type="italic">unto me:</hi> and when I waited for light, there came darkness.

verses.name: Job 30:27
verses.text: My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.

verses.name: Job 30:28
verses.text: I went mourning without the sun: I stood up, <hi type="italic">and</hi> I cried in the congregation.

verses.name: Job 30:29
verses.text: I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.

verses.name: Job 30:30
verses.text: My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.

verses.name: Job 30:31
verses.text: My harp also is <hi type="italic">turned</hi> to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.  <chapter eID="Job.30"/><div eID="gen485" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 31:1
verses.text: I MADE a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?

verses.name: Job 31:2
verses.text: For what portion of God <hi type="italic">is there</hi> from above? and <hi type="italic">what</hi> inheritance of the Almighty from on high?

verses.name: Job 31:3
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is</hi> not destruction to the wicked? and a strange <hi type="italic">punishment</hi> to the workers of iniquity?

verses.name: Job 31:4
verses.text: Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?

verses.name: Job 31:5
verses.text: If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit;

verses.name: Job 31:6
verses.text: Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know mine integrity.

verses.name: Job 31:7
verses.text: If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands;

verses.name: Job 31:8
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Then</hi> let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.

verses.name: Job 31:9
verses.text: If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or <hi type="italic">if</hi> I have laid wait at my neighbour’s door;

verses.name: Job 31:10
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Then</hi> let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.

verses.name: Job 31:11
verses.text: For this <hi type="italic">is</hi> an heinous crime; yea, it <hi type="italic">is</hi> an iniquity <hi type="italic">to be punished by</hi> the judges.

verses.name: Job 31:12
verses.text: For it <hi type="italic">is</hi> a fire <hi type="italic">that</hi> consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.

verses.name: Job 31:13
verses.text: If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me;

verses.name: Job 31:14
verses.text: What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?

verses.name: Job 31:15
verses.text: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?

verses.name: Job 31:16
verses.text: If I have withheld the poor from <hi type="italic">their</hi> desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;

verses.name: Job 31:17
verses.text: Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof;

verses.name: Job 31:18
verses.text: (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as <hi type="italic">with</hi> a father, and I have guided her from my mother’s womb;)

verses.name: Job 31:19
verses.text: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering;

verses.name: Job 31:20
verses.text: If his loins have not blessed me, and <hi type="italic">if</hi> he were <hi type="italic">not</hi> warmed with the fleece of my sheep;

verses.name: Job 31:21
verses.text: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate:

verses.name: Job 31:22
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Then</hi> let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.

verses.name: Job 31:23
verses.text: For destruction <hi type="italic">from</hi> God <hi type="italic">was</hi> a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.

verses.name: Job 31:24
verses.text: If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, <hi type="italic">Thou art</hi> my confidence;

verses.name: Job 31:25
verses.text: If I rejoiced because my wealth <hi type="italic">was</hi> great, and because mine hand had gotten much;

verses.name: Job 31:26
verses.text: If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking <hi type="italic">in</hi> brightness;

verses.name: Job 31:27
verses.text: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand:

verses.name: Job 31:28
verses.text: This also <hi type="italic">were</hi> an iniquity <hi type="italic">to be punished by</hi> the judge: for I should have denied the God <hi type="italic">that is</hi> above.

verses.name: Job 31:29
verses.text: If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him:

verses.name: Job 31:30
verses.text: Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul.

verses.name: Job 31:31
verses.text: If the men of my tabernacle said not, Oh that we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied.

verses.name: Job 31:32
verses.text: The stranger did not lodge in the street: <hi type="italic">but</hi> I opened my doors to the traveller.

verses.name: Job 31:33
verses.text: If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom:

verses.name: Job 31:34
verses.text: Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, <hi type="italic">and</hi> went not out of the door?

verses.name: Job 31:35
verses.text: Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire <hi type="italic">is</hi>, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the Almighty would answer me, and <hi type="italic">that</hi> mine adversary had written a book.

verses.name: Job 31:36
verses.text: Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, <hi type="italic">and</hi> bind it <hi type="italic">as</hi> a crown to me.

verses.name: Job 31:37
verses.text: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near unto him.

verses.name: Job 31:38
verses.text: If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain;

verses.name: Job 31:39
verses.text: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life:

verses.name: Job 31:40
verses.text: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.  <chapter eID="Job.31"/><div eID="gen486" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 32:1
verses.text: SO these three men ceased to answer Job, because he <hi type="italic">was</hi> righteous in his own eyes.

verses.name: Job 32:2
verses.text: Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God.

verses.name: Job 32:3
verses.text: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and <hi type="italic">yet</hi> had condemned Job.

verses.name: Job 32:4
verses.text: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they <hi type="italic">were</hi> elder than he.

verses.name: Job 32:5
verses.text: When Elihu saw that <hi type="italic">there was</hi> no answer in the mouth of <hi type="italic">these</hi> three men, then his wrath was kindled.

verses.name: Job 32:6
verses.text: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> young, and ye <hi type="italic">are</hi> very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion.

verses.name: Job 32:7
verses.text: I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.

verses.name: Job 32:8
verses.text: But <hi type="italic">there is</hi> a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.

verses.name: Job 32:9
verses.text: Great men are not <hi type="italic">always</hi> wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.

verses.name: Job 32:10
verses.text: Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will shew mine opinion.

verses.name: Job 32:11
verses.text: Behold, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say.

verses.name: Job 32:12
verses.text: Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold, <hi type="italic">there was</hi> none of you that convinced Job, <hi type="italic">or</hi> that answered his words:

verses.name: Job 32:13
verses.text: Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man.

verses.name: Job 32:14
verses.text: Now he hath not directed <hi type="italic">his</hi> words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches.

verses.name: Job 32:15
verses.text: They were amazed, they answered no more: they left off speaking.

verses.name: Job 32:16
verses.text: When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still, <hi type="italic">and</hi> answered no more;)

verses.name: Job 32:17
verses.text: <hi type="italic">I said</hi>, I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion.

verses.name: Job 32:18
verses.text: For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me.

verses.name: Job 32:19
verses.text: Behold, my belly <hi type="italic">is</hi> as wine <hi type="italic">which</hi> hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles.

verses.name: Job 32:20
verses.text: I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer.

verses.name: Job 32:21
verses.text: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man’s person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.

verses.name: Job 32:22
verses.text: For I know not to give flattering titles; <hi type="italic">in so doing</hi> my maker would soon take me away.  <chapter eID="Job.32"/><div eID="gen487" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 33:1
verses.text: WHEREFORE, Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words.

verses.name: Job 33:2
verses.text: Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth.

verses.name: Job 33:3
verses.text: My words <hi type="italic">shall be of</hi> the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.

verses.name: Job 33:4
verses.text: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.

verses.name: Job 33:5
verses.text: If thou canst answer me, set <hi type="italic">thy words</hi> in order before me, stand up.

verses.name: Job 33:6
verses.text: Behold, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> according to thy wish in God’s stead: I also am formed out of the clay.

verses.name: Job 33:7
verses.text: Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee.

verses.name: Job 33:8
verses.text: Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of <hi type="italic">thy</hi> words, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>,

verses.name: Job 33:9
verses.text: I am clean without transgression, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> innocent; neither <hi type="italic">is there</hi> iniquity in me.

verses.name: Job 33:10
verses.text: Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy,

verses.name: Job 33:11
verses.text: He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.

verses.name: Job 33:12
verses.text: Behold, <hi type="italic">in</hi> this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.

verses.name: Job 33:13
verses.text: Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters.

verses.name: Job 33:14
verses.text: For God speaketh once, yea twice, <hi type="italic">yet man</hi> perceiveth it not.

verses.name: Job 33:15
verses.text: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed;

verses.name: Job 33:16
verses.text: Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction,

verses.name: Job 33:17
verses.text: That he may withdraw man <hi type="italic">from his</hi> purpose, and hide pride from man.

verses.name: Job 33:18
verses.text: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.

verses.name: Job 33:19
verses.text: He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong <hi type="italic">pain:</hi>

verses.name: Job 33:20
verses.text: So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat.

verses.name: Job 33:21
verses.text: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones <hi type="italic">that</hi> were not seen stick out.

verses.name: Job 33:22
verses.text: Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers.

verses.name: Job 33:23
verses.text: If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness:

verses.name: Job 33:24
verses.text: Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.

verses.name: Job 33:25
verses.text: His flesh shall be fresher than a child’s: he shall return to the days of his youth:

verses.name: Job 33:26
verses.text: He shall pray unto God, and he will be favourable unto him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness.

verses.name: Job 33:27
verses.text: He looketh upon men, and <hi type="italic">if any</hi> say, I have sinned, and perverted <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> right, and it profited me not;

verses.name: Job 33:28
verses.text: He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.

verses.name: Job 33:29
verses.text: Lo, all these <hi type="italic">things</hi> worketh God oftentimes with man,

verses.name: Job 33:30
verses.text: To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.

verses.name: Job 33:31
verses.text: Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I will speak.

verses.name: Job 33:32
verses.text: If thou hast any thing to say, answer me: speak, for I desire to justify thee.

verses.name: Job 33:33
verses.text: If not, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom.  <chapter eID="Job.33"/><div eID="gen488" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 34:1
verses.text: FURTHERMORE Elihu answered and said,

verses.name: Job 34:2
verses.text: Hear my words, O ye wise <hi type="italic">men;</hi> and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.

verses.name: Job 34:3
verses.text: For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat.

verses.name: Job 34:4
verses.text: Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what <hi type="italic">is</hi> good.

verses.name: Job 34:5
verses.text: For Job hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my judgment.

verses.name: Job 34:6
verses.text: Should I lie against my right? my wound <hi type="italic">is</hi> incurable without transgression.

verses.name: Job 34:7
verses.text: What man <hi type="italic">is</hi> like Job, <hi type="italic">who</hi> drinketh up scorning like water?

verses.name: Job 34:8
verses.text: Which goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men.

verses.name: Job 34:9
verses.text: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.

verses.name: Job 34:10
verses.text: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God, <hi type="italic">that he should do</hi> wickedness; and <hi type="italic">from</hi> the Almighty, <hi type="italic">that he should commit</hi> iniquity.

verses.name: Job 34:11
verses.text: For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to <hi type="italic">his</hi> ways.

verses.name: Job 34:12
verses.text: Yea, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.

verses.name: Job 34:13
verses.text: Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world?

verses.name: Job 34:14
verses.text: If he set his heart upon man, <hi type="italic">if</hi> he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;

verses.name: Job 34:15
verses.text: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust.

verses.name: Job 34:16
verses.text: If now <hi type="italic">thou hast</hi> understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.

verses.name: Job 34:17
verses.text: Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just?

verses.name: Job 34:18
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is it fit</hi> to say to a king, <hi type="italic">Thou art</hi> wicked? <hi type="italic">and</hi> to princes, <hi type="italic">Ye are</hi> ungodly?

verses.name: Job 34:19
verses.text: <hi type="italic">How much less to him</hi> that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all <hi type="italic">are</hi> the work of his hands.

verses.name: Job 34:20
verses.text: In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand.

verses.name: Job 34:21
verses.text: For his eyes <hi type="italic">are</hi> upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.

verses.name: Job 34:22
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

verses.name: Job 34:23
verses.text: For he will not lay upon man more <hi type="italic">than right;</hi> that he should enter into judgment with God.

verses.name: Job 34:24
verses.text: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.

verses.name: Job 34:25
verses.text: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth <hi type="italic">them</hi> in the night, so that they are destroyed.

verses.name: Job 34:26
verses.text: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others;

verses.name: Job 34:27
verses.text: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways:

verses.name: Job 34:28
verses.text: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.

verses.name: Job 34:29
verses.text: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth <hi type="italic">his</hi> face, who then can behold him? whether <hi type="italic">it be done</hi> against a nation, or against a man only:

verses.name: Job 34:30
verses.text: That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared.

verses.name: Job 34:31
verses.text: Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne <hi type="italic">chastisement</hi>, I will not offend <hi type="italic">any more:</hi>

verses.name: Job 34:32
verses.text: <hi type="italic">That which</hi> I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.

verses.name: Job 34:33
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Should it be</hi> according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.

verses.name: Job 34:34
verses.text: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me.

verses.name: Job 34:35
verses.text: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words <hi type="italic">were</hi> without wisdom.

verses.name: Job 34:36
verses.text: My desire <hi type="italic">is that</hi> Job may be tried unto the end because of <hi type="italic">his</hi> answers for wicked men.

verses.name: Job 34:37
verses.text: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth <hi type="italic">his hands</hi> among us, and multiplieth his words against God.  <chapter eID="Job.34"/><div eID="gen489" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 35:1
verses.text: ELIHU spake moreover, and said,

verses.name: Job 35:2
verses.text: Thinkest thou this to be right, <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou saidst, My righteousness <hi type="italic">is</hi> more than God’s?

verses.name: Job 35:3
verses.text: For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee? <hi type="italic">and</hi>, What profit shall I have, <hi type="italic">if I be cleansed</hi> from my sin?

verses.name: Job 35:4
verses.text: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee.

verses.name: Job 35:5
verses.text: Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds <hi type="italic">which</hi> are higher than thou.

verses.name: Job 35:6
verses.text: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or <hi type="italic">if</hi> thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?

verses.name: Job 35:7
verses.text: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? or what receiveth he of thine hand?

verses.name: Job 35:8
verses.text: Thy wickedness <hi type="italic">may hurt</hi> a man as thou <hi type="italic">art;</hi> and thy righteousness <hi type="italic">may profit</hi> the son of man.

verses.name: Job 35:9
verses.text: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make <hi type="italic">the oppressed</hi> to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.

verses.name: Job 35:10
verses.text: But none saith, Where <hi type="italic">is</hi> God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;

verses.name: Job 35:11
verses.text: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven?

verses.name: Job 35:12
verses.text: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men.

verses.name: Job 35:13
verses.text: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.

verses.name: Job 35:14
verses.text: Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, <hi type="italic">yet</hi> judgment <hi type="italic">is</hi> before him; therefore trust thou in him.

verses.name: Job 35:15
verses.text: But now, because <hi type="italic">it is</hi> not <hi type="italic">so</hi>, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth <hi type="italic">it</hi> not in great extremity:

verses.name: Job 35:16
verses.text: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge.  <chapter eID="Job.35"/><div eID="gen490" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 36:1
verses.text: ELIHU also proceeded, and said,

verses.name: Job 36:2
verses.text: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that <hi type="italic">I have</hi> yet to speak on God’s behalf.

verses.name: Job 36:3
verses.text: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.

verses.name: Job 36:4
verses.text: For truly my words <hi type="italic">shall</hi> not <hi type="italic">be</hi> false: he that is perfect in knowledge <hi type="italic">is</hi> with thee.

verses.name: Job 36:5
verses.text: Behold, God <hi type="italic">is</hi> mighty, and despiseth not <hi type="italic">any: he is</hi> mighty in strength <hi type="italic">and</hi> wisdom.

verses.name: Job 36:6
verses.text: He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor.

verses.name: Job 36:7
verses.text: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings <hi type="italic">are they</hi> on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.

verses.name: Job 36:8
verses.text: And if <hi type="italic">they be</hi> bound in fetters, <hi type="italic">and</hi> be holden in cords of affliction;

verses.name: Job 36:9
verses.text: Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.

verses.name: Job 36:10
verses.text: He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.

verses.name: Job 36:11
verses.text: If they obey and serve <hi type="italic">him</hi>, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.

verses.name: Job 36:12
verses.text: But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge.

verses.name: Job 36:13
verses.text: But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them.

verses.name: Job 36:14
verses.text: They die in youth, and their life <hi type="italic">is</hi> among the unclean.

verses.name: Job 36:15
verses.text: He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.

verses.name: Job 36:16
verses.text: Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait <hi type="italic">into</hi> a broad place, where <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table <hi type="italic">should be</hi> full of fatness.

verses.name: Job 36:17
verses.text: But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold <hi type="italic">on thee</hi>.

verses.name: Job 36:18
verses.text: Because <hi type="italic">there is</hi> wrath, <hi type="italic">beware</hi> lest he take thee away with <hi type="italic">his</hi> stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee.

verses.name: Job 36:19
verses.text: Will he esteem thy riches? <hi type="italic">no</hi>, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.

verses.name: Job 36:20
verses.text: Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.

verses.name: Job 36:21
verses.text: Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.

verses.name: Job 36:22
verses.text: Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?

verses.name: Job 36:23
verses.text: Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity?

verses.name: Job 36:24
verses.text: Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.

verses.name: Job 36:25
verses.text: Every man may see it; man may behold <hi type="italic">it</hi> afar off.

verses.name: Job 36:26
verses.text: Behold, God <hi type="italic">is</hi> great, and we know <hi type="italic">him</hi> not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.

verses.name: Job 36:27
verses.text: For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapour thereof:

verses.name: Job 36:28
verses.text: Which the clouds do drop <hi type="italic">and</hi> distil upon man abundantly.

verses.name: Job 36:29
verses.text: Also can <hi type="italic">any</hi> understand the spreadings of the clouds, <hi type="italic">or</hi> the noise of his tabernacle?

verses.name: Job 36:30
verses.text: Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea.

verses.name: Job 36:31
verses.text: For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance.

verses.name: Job 36:32
verses.text: With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it <hi type="italic">not to shine</hi> by <hi type="italic">the cloud</hi> that cometh betwixt.

verses.name: Job 36:33
verses.text: The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapour.  <chapter eID="Job.36"/><div eID="gen491" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Job 37:1
verses.text: AT this also my heart trembleth, and is moved out of his place.

verses.name: Job 37:2
verses.text: Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound <hi type="italic">that</hi> goeth out of his mouth.

verses.name: Job 37:3
verses.text: He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his lightning unto the ends of the earth.

verses.name: Job 37:4
verses.text: After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his excellency; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.

verses.name: Job 37:5
verses.text: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.

verses.name: Job 37:6
verses.text: For he saith to the snow, Be thou <hi type="italic">on</hi> the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.

verses.name: Job 37:7
