verses.text: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully <hi type="italic">and</hi> wonderfully made: marvellous <hi type="italic">are</hi> thy works; and <hi type="italic">that</hi> my soul knoweth right well.

verses.name: Psalms 139:15
verses.text: My substance was not hid from thee, when I was made in secret, <hi type="italic">and</hi> curiously wrought in the lowest parts of the earth.

verses.name: Psalms 139:16
verses.text: Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all <hi type="italic">my members</hi> were written, <hi type="italic">which</hi> in continuance were fashioned, when <hi type="italic">as yet there was</hi> none of them.

verses.name: Psalms 139:17
verses.text: How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! how great is the sum of them!

verses.name: Psalms 139:18
verses.text: <hi type="italic">If</hi> I should count them, they are more in number than the sand: when I awake, I am still with thee.

verses.name: Psalms 139:19
verses.text: Surely thou wilt slay the wicked, O God: depart from me therefore, ye bloody men.

verses.name: Psalms 139:20
verses.text: For they speak against thee wickedly, <hi type="italic">and</hi> thine enemies take <hi type="italic">thy name</hi> in vain.

verses.name: Psalms 139:21
verses.text: Do not I hate them, O Lord, that hate thee? and am not I grieved with those that rise up against thee?

verses.name: Psalms 139:22
verses.text: I hate them with perfect hatred: I count them mine enemies.

verses.name: Psalms 139:23
verses.text: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts:

verses.name: Psalms 139:24
verses.text: And see if <hi type="italic">there be any</hi> wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.  <chapter eID="Ps.139"/>

verses.name: Psalms 140:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv132"/><title canonical="true" type="psalm">To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.</title> <div sID="gen681" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv132"/>DELIVER me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man;

verses.name: Psalms 140:2
verses.text: Which imagine mischiefs in <hi type="italic">their</hi> heart; continually are they gathered together <hi type="italic">for</hi> war.

verses.name: Psalms 140:3
verses.text: They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison <hi type="italic">is</hi> under their lips. Selah.

verses.name: Psalms 140:4
verses.text: Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.

verses.name: Psalms 140:5
verses.text: The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me. Selah.

verses.name: Psalms 140:6
verses.text: I said unto the Lord, Thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> my God: hear the voice of my supplications, O Lord.

verses.name: Psalms 140:7
verses.text: O God the Lord, the strength of my salvation, thou hast covered my head in the day of battle.

verses.name: Psalms 140:8
verses.text: Grant not, O Lord, the desires of the wicked: further not his wicked device; <hi type="italic">lest</hi> they exalt themselves. Selah.

verses.name: Psalms 140:9
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As for</hi> the head of those that compass me about, let the mischief of their own lips cover them.

verses.name: Psalms 140:10
verses.text: Let burning coals fall upon them: let them be cast into the fire; into deep pits, that they rise not up again.

verses.name: Psalms 140:11
verses.text: Let not an evil speaker be established in the earth: evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow <hi type="italic">him</hi>.

verses.name: Psalms 140:12
verses.text: I know that the Lord will maintain the cause of the afflicted, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the right of the poor.

verses.name: Psalms 140:13
verses.text: Surely the righteous shall give thanks unto thy name: the upright shall dwell in thy presence.  <chapter eID="Ps.140"/>

verses.name: Psalms 141:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv133"/><title canonical="true" type="psalm">A Psalm of David.</title> <div sID="gen682" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv133"/>LORD, I cry unto thee: make haste unto me; give ear unto my voice, when I cry unto thee.

verses.name: Psalms 141:2
verses.text: Let my prayer be set forth before thee <hi type="italic">as</hi> incense; <hi type="italic">and</hi> the lifting up of my hands <hi type="italic">as</hi> the evening sacrifice.

verses.name: Psalms 141:3
verses.text: Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips.

verses.name: Psalms 141:4
verses.text: Incline not my heart to <hi type="italic">any</hi> evil thing, to practise wicked works with men that work iniquity: and let me not eat of their dainties.

verses.name: Psalms 141:5
verses.text: Let the righteous smite me; <hi type="italic">it shall be</hi> a kindness: and let him reprove me; <hi type="italic">it shall be</hi> an excellent oil, <hi type="italic">which</hi> shall not break my head: for yet my prayer also <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> in their calamities.

verses.name: Psalms 141:6
verses.text: When their judges are overthrown in stony places, they shall hear my words; for they are sweet.

verses.name: Psalms 141:7
verses.text: Our bones are scattered at the grave’s mouth, as when one cutteth and cleaveth <hi type="italic">wood</hi> upon the earth.

verses.name: Psalms 141:8
verses.text: But mine eyes <hi type="italic">are</hi> unto thee, O God the Lord: in thee is my trust; leave not my soul destitute.

verses.name: Psalms 141:9
verses.text: Keep me from the snares <hi type="italic">which</hi> they have laid for me, and the gins of the workers of iniquity.

verses.name: Psalms 141:10
verses.text: Let the wicked fall into their own nets, whilst that I withal escape.  <chapter eID="Ps.141"/>

verses.name: Psalms 142:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv134"/><title canonical="true" type="psalm">Maschil of David; A Prayer when he was in the cave.</title> <div sID="gen683" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv134"/>I CRIED unto the Lord with my voice; with my voice unto the Lord did I make my supplication.

verses.name: Psalms 142:2
verses.text: I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.

verses.name: Psalms 142:3
verses.text: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, then thou knewest my path. In the way wherein I walked have they privily laid a snare for me.

verses.name: Psalms 142:4
verses.text: I looked on <hi type="italic">my</hi> right hand, and beheld, but <hi type="italic">there was</hi> no man that would know me: refuge failed me; no man cared for my soul.

verses.name: Psalms 142:5
verses.text: I cried unto thee, O Lord: I said, Thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> my refuge <hi type="italic">and</hi> my portion in the land of the living.

verses.name: Psalms 142:6
verses.text: Attend unto my cry; for I am brought very low: deliver me from my persecutors; for they are stronger than I.

verses.name: Psalms 142:7
verses.text: Bring my soul out of prison, that I may praise thy name: the righteous shall compass me about; for thou shalt deal bountifully with me.  <chapter eID="Ps.142"/>

verses.name: Psalms 143:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv135"/><title canonical="true" type="psalm">A Psalm of David.</title> <div sID="gen684" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv135"/>HEAR my prayer, O Lord, give ear to my supplications: in thy faithfulness answer me, <hi type="italic">and</hi> in thy righteousness.

verses.name: Psalms 143:2
verses.text: And enter not into judgment with thy servant: for in thy sight shall no man living be justified.

verses.name: Psalms 143:3
verses.text: For the enemy hath persecuted my soul; he hath smitten my life down to the ground; he hath made me to dwell in darkness, as those that have been long dead.

verses.name: Psalms 143:4
verses.text: Therefore is my spirit overwhelmed within me; my heart within me is desolate.

verses.name: Psalms 143:5
verses.text: I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.

verses.name: Psalms 143:6
verses.text: I stretch forth my hands unto thee: my soul <hi type="italic">thirsteth</hi> after thee, as a thirsty land. Selah.

verses.name: Psalms 143:7
verses.text: Hear me speedily, O Lord: my spirit faileth: hide not thy face from me, lest I be like unto them that go down into the pit.

verses.name: Psalms 143:8
verses.text: Cause me to hear thy lovingkindness in the morning; for in thee do I trust: cause me to know the way wherein I should walk; for I lift up my soul unto thee.

verses.name: Psalms 143:9
verses.text: Deliver me, O Lord, from mine enemies: I flee unto thee to hide me.

verses.name: Psalms 143:10
verses.text: Teach me to do thy will; for thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> my God: thy spirit <hi type="italic">is</hi> good; lead me into the land of uprightness.

verses.name: Psalms 143:11
verses.text: Quicken me, O Lord, for thy name’s sake: for thy righteousness’ sake bring my soul out of trouble.

verses.name: Psalms 143:12
verses.text: And of thy mercy cut off mine enemies, and destroy all them that afflict my soul: for I <hi type="italic">am</hi> thy servant.  <chapter eID="Ps.143"/>

verses.name: Psalms 144:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv136"/><title canonical="true" type="psalm"><hi type="italic">A Psalm</hi> of David.</title> <div sID="gen685" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv136"/>BLESSED <hi type="italic">be</hi> the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, <hi type="italic">and</hi> my fingers to fight:

verses.name: Psalms 144:2
verses.text: My goodness, and my fortress; my high tower, and my deliverer; my shield, and <hi type="italic">he</hi> in whom I trust; who subdueth my people under me.

verses.name: Psalms 144:3
verses.text: Lord, what <hi type="italic">is</hi> man, that thou takest knowledge of him! <hi type="italic">or</hi> the son of man, that thou makest account of him!

verses.name: Psalms 144:4
verses.text: Man is like to vanity: his days <hi type="italic">are</hi> as a shadow that passeth away.

verses.name: Psalms 144:5
verses.text: Bow thy heavens, O Lord, and come down: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke.

verses.name: Psalms 144:6
verses.text: Cast forth lightning, and scatter them: shoot out thine arrows, and destroy them.

verses.name: Psalms 144:7
verses.text: Send thine hand from above; rid me, and deliver me out of great waters, from the hand of strange children;

verses.name: Psalms 144:8
verses.text: Whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand <hi type="italic">is</hi> a right hand of falsehood.

verses.name: Psalms 144:9
verses.text: I will sing a new song unto thee, O God: upon a psaltery <hi type="italic">and</hi> an instrument of ten strings will I sing praises unto thee.

verses.name: Psalms 144:10
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is he</hi> that giveth salvation unto kings: who delivereth David his servant from the hurtful sword.

verses.name: Psalms 144:11
verses.text: Rid me, and deliver me from the hand of strange children, whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand <hi type="italic">is</hi> a right hand of falsehood:

verses.name: Psalms 144:12
verses.text: That our sons <hi type="italic">may be</hi> as plants grown up in their youth; <hi type="italic">that</hi> our daughters <hi type="italic">may be</hi> as corner stones, polished <hi type="italic">after</hi> the similitude of a palace:

verses.name: Psalms 144:13
verses.text: <hi type="italic">That</hi> our garners <hi type="italic">may be</hi> full, affording all manner of store: <hi type="italic">that</hi> our sheep may bring forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets:

verses.name: Psalms 144:14
verses.text: <hi type="italic">That</hi> our oxen <hi type="italic">may be</hi> strong to labour; <hi type="italic">that there be</hi> no breaking in, nor going out; that <hi type="italic">there be</hi> no complaining in our streets.

verses.name: Psalms 144:15
verses.text: Happy <hi type="italic">is that</hi> people, that is in such a case: <hi type="italic">yea</hi>, happy <hi type="italic">is that</hi> people, whose God <hi type="italic">is</hi> the Lord.  <chapter eID="Ps.144"/>

verses.name: Psalms 145:1
verses.text: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv137"/><title canonical="true" type="psalm">David’s <hi type="italic">Psalm</hi> of praise.</title> <div sID="gen686" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv137"/>I WILL extol thee, my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever.

verses.name: Psalms 145:2
verses.text: Every day will I bless thee; and I will praise thy name for ever and ever.

verses.name: Psalms 145:3
verses.text: Great <hi type="italic">is</hi> the Lord, and greatly to be praised; and his greatness <hi type="italic">is</hi> unsearchable.

verses.name: Psalms 145:4
verses.text: One generation shall praise thy works to another, and shall declare thy mighty acts.

verses.name: Psalms 145:5
verses.text: I will speak of the glorious honour of thy majesty, and of thy wondrous works.

verses.name: Psalms 145:6
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">men</hi> shall speak of the might of thy terrible acts: and I will declare thy greatness.

verses.name: Psalms 145:7
verses.text: They shall abundantly utter the memory of thy great goodness, and shall sing of thy righteousness.

verses.name: Psalms 145:8
verses.text: The Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> gracious, and full of compassion; slow to anger, and of great mercy.

verses.name: Psalms 145:9
verses.text: The Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> good to all: and his tender mercies <hi type="italic">are</hi> over all his works.

verses.name: Psalms 145:10
verses.text: All thy works shall praise thee, O Lord; and thy saints shall bless thee.

verses.name: Psalms 145:11
verses.text: They shall speak of the glory of thy kingdom, and talk of thy power;

verses.name: Psalms 145:12
verses.text: To make known to the sons of men his mighty acts, and the glorious majesty of his kingdom.

verses.name: Psalms 145:13
verses.text: Thy kingdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> an everlasting kingdom, and thy dominion <hi type="italic">endureth</hi> throughout all generations.

verses.name: Psalms 145:14
verses.text: The Lord upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all <hi type="italic">those that be</hi> bowed down.

verses.name: Psalms 145:15
verses.text: The eyes of all wait upon thee; and thou givest them their meat in due season.

verses.name: Psalms 145:16
verses.text: Thou openest thine hand, and satisfiest the desire of every living thing.

verses.name: Psalms 145:17
verses.text: The Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works.

verses.name: Psalms 145:18
verses.text: The Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.

verses.name: Psalms 145:19
verses.text: He will fulfil the desire of them that fear him: he also will hear their cry, and will save them.

verses.name: Psalms 145:20
verses.text: The Lord preserveth all them that love him: but all the wicked will he destroy.

verses.name: Psalms 145:21
verses.text: My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord: and let all flesh bless his holy name for ever and ever.  <chapter eID="Ps.145"/><div eID="gen686" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Psalms 146:1
verses.text: PRAISE ye the Lord. Praise the Lord, O my soul.

verses.name: Psalms 146:2
verses.text: While I live will I praise the Lord: I will sing praises unto my God while I have any being.

verses.name: Psalms 146:3
verses.text: Put not your trust in princes, <hi type="italic">nor</hi> in the son of man, in whom <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no help.

verses.name: Psalms 146:4
verses.text: His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish.

verses.name: Psalms 146:5
verses.text: Happy <hi type="italic">is he</hi> that <hi type="italic">hath</hi> the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the Lord his God:

verses.name: Psalms 146:6
verses.text: Which made heaven, and earth, the sea, and all that therein <hi type="italic">is:</hi> which keepeth truth for ever:

verses.name: Psalms 146:7
verses.text: Which executeth judgment for the oppressed: which giveth food to the hungry. The Lord looseth the prisoners:

verses.name: Psalms 146:8
verses.text: The Lord openeth <hi type="italic">the eyes of</hi> the blind: the Lord raiseth them that are bowed down: the Lord loveth the righteous:

verses.name: Psalms 146:9
verses.text: The Lord preserveth the strangers; he relieveth the fatherless and widow: but the way of the wicked he turneth upside down.

verses.name: Psalms 146:10
verses.text: The Lord shall reign for ever, <hi type="italic">even</hi> thy God, O Zion, unto all generations. Praise ye the Lord.  <chapter eID="Ps.146"/><div eID="gen687" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Psalms 147:1
verses.text: PRAISE ye the Lord: for <hi type="italic">it is</hi> good to sing praises unto our God; for <hi type="italic">it is</hi> pleasant; <hi type="italic">and</hi> praise is comely.

verses.name: Psalms 147:2
verses.text: The Lord doth build up Jerusalem: he gathereth together the outcasts of Israel.

verses.name: Psalms 147:3
verses.text: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.

verses.name: Psalms 147:4
verses.text: He telleth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by <hi type="italic">their</hi> names.

verses.name: Psalms 147:5
verses.text: Great <hi type="italic">is</hi> our Lord, and of great power: his understanding <hi type="italic">is</hi> infinite.

verses.name: Psalms 147:6
verses.text: The Lord lifteth up the meek: he casteth the wicked down to the ground.

verses.name: Psalms 147:7
verses.text: Sing unto the Lord with thanksgiving; sing praise upon the harp unto our God:

verses.name: Psalms 147:8
verses.text: Who covereth the heaven with clouds, who prepareth rain for the earth, who maketh grass to grow upon the mountains.

verses.name: Psalms 147:9
verses.text: He giveth to the beast his food, <hi type="italic">and</hi> to the young ravens which cry.

verses.name: Psalms 147:10
verses.text: He delighteth not in the strength of the horse: he taketh not pleasure in the legs of a man.

verses.name: Psalms 147:11
verses.text: The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.

verses.name: Psalms 147:12
verses.text: Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem; praise thy God, O Zion.

verses.name: Psalms 147:13
verses.text: For he hath strengthened the bars of thy gates; he hath blessed thy children within thee.

verses.name: Psalms 147:14
verses.text: He maketh peace <hi type="italic">in</hi> thy borders, <hi type="italic">and</hi> filleth thee with the finest of the wheat.

verses.name: Psalms 147:15
verses.text: He sendeth forth his commandment <hi type="italic">upon</hi> earth: his word runneth very swiftly.

verses.name: Psalms 147:16
verses.text: He giveth snow like wool: he scattereth the hoarfrost like ashes.

verses.name: Psalms 147:17
verses.text: He casteth forth his ice like morsels: who can stand before his cold?

verses.name: Psalms 147:18
verses.text: He sendeth out his word, and melteth them: he causeth his wind to blow, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the waters flow.

verses.name: Psalms 147:19
verses.text: He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.

verses.name: Psalms 147:20
verses.text: He hath not dealt so with any nation: and <hi type="italic">as for his</hi> judgments, they have not known them. Praise ye the Lord.  <chapter eID="Ps.147"/><div eID="gen688" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Psalms 148:1
verses.text: PRAISE ye the Lord. Praise ye the Lord from the heavens: praise him in the heights.

verses.name: Psalms 148:2
verses.text: Praise ye him, all his angels: praise ye him, all his hosts.

verses.name: Psalms 148:3
verses.text: Praise ye him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars of light.

verses.name: Psalms 148:4
verses.text: Praise him, ye heavens of heavens, and ye waters that <hi type="italic">be</hi> above the heavens.

verses.name: Psalms 148:5
verses.text: Let them praise the name of the Lord: for he commanded, and they were created.

verses.name: Psalms 148:6
verses.text: He hath also stablished them for ever and ever: he hath made a decree which shall not pass.

verses.name: Psalms 148:7
verses.text: Praise the Lord from the earth, ye dragons, and all deeps:

verses.name: Psalms 148:8
verses.text: Fire, and hail; snow, and vapour; stormy wind fulfilling his word:

verses.name: Psalms 148:9
verses.text: Mountains, and all hills; fruitful trees, and all cedars:

verses.name: Psalms 148:10
verses.text: Beasts, and all cattle; creeping things, and flying fowl:

verses.name: Psalms 148:11
verses.text: Kings of the earth, and all people; princes, and all judges of the earth:

verses.name: Psalms 148:12
verses.text: Both young men, and maidens; old men, and children:

verses.name: Psalms 148:13
verses.text: Let them praise the name of the Lord: for his name alone is excellent; his glory <hi type="italic">is</hi> above the earth and heaven.

verses.name: Psalms 148:14
verses.text: He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; <hi type="italic">even</hi> of the children of Israel, a people near unto him. Praise ye the Lord.  <chapter eID="Ps.148"/><div eID="gen689" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Psalms 149:1
verses.text: PRAISE ye the Lord. Sing unto the Lord a new song, <hi type="italic">and</hi> his praise in the congregation of saints.

verses.name: Psalms 149:2
verses.text: Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: let the children of Zion be joyful in their King.

verses.name: Psalms 149:3
verses.text: Let them praise his name in the dance: let them sing praises unto him with the timbrel and harp.

verses.name: Psalms 149:4
verses.text: For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people: he will beautify the meek with salvation.

verses.name: Psalms 149:5
verses.text: Let the saints be joyful in glory: let them sing aloud upon their beds.

verses.name: Psalms 149:6
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Let</hi> the high <hi type="italic">praises</hi> of God <hi type="italic">be</hi> in their mouth, and a twoedged sword in their hand;

verses.name: Psalms 149:7
verses.text: To execute vengeance upon the heathen, <hi type="italic">and</hi> punishments upon the people;

verses.name: Psalms 149:8
verses.text: To bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron;

verses.name: Psalms 149:9
verses.text: To execute upon them the judgment written: this honour have all his saints. Praise ye the Lord.  <chapter eID="Ps.149"/><div eID="gen690" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Psalms 150:1
verses.text: PRAISE ye the Lord. Praise God in his sanctuary: praise him in the firmament of his power.

verses.name: Psalms 150:2
verses.text: Praise him for his mighty acts: praise him according to his excellent greatness.

verses.name: Psalms 150:3
verses.text: Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with the psaltery and harp.

verses.name: Psalms 150:4
verses.text: Praise him with the timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and organs.

verses.name: Psalms 150:5
verses.text: Praise him upon the loud cymbals: praise him upon the high sounding cymbals.

verses.name: Psalms 150:6
verses.text: Let every thing that hath breath praise the Lord. Praise ye the Lord. <chapter eID="Ps.150"/><div eID="gen691" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen498" osisID="Ps" type="book"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 1:1
verses.text: THE proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel;

verses.name: Proverbs 1:2
verses.text: To know wisdom and instruction; to perceive the words of understanding;

verses.name: Proverbs 1:3
verses.text: To receive the instruction of wisdom, justice, and judgment, and equity;

verses.name: Proverbs 1:4
verses.text: To give subtilty to the simple, to the young man knowledge and discretion.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:5
verses.text: A wise <hi type="italic">man</hi> will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels:

verses.name: Proverbs 1:6
verses.text: To understand a proverb, and the interpretation; the words of the wise, and their dark sayings.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:7
verses.text: ¶ The fear of the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> the beginning of knowledge: <hi type="italic">but</hi> fools despise wisdom and instruction.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:8
verses.text: My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother:

verses.name: Proverbs 1:9
verses.text: For they <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> an ornament of grace unto thy head, and chains about thy neck.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:10
verses.text: ¶ My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:11
verses.text: If they say, Come with us, let us lay wait for blood, let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause:

verses.name: Proverbs 1:12
verses.text: Let us swallow them up alive as the grave; and whole, as those that go down into the pit:

verses.name: Proverbs 1:13
verses.text: We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoil:

verses.name: Proverbs 1:14
verses.text: Cast in thy lot among us; let us all have one purse:

verses.name: Proverbs 1:15
verses.text: My son, walk not thou in the way with them; refrain thy foot from their path:

verses.name: Proverbs 1:16
verses.text: For their feet run to evil, and make haste to shed blood.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:17
verses.text: Surely in vain the net is spread in the sight of any bird.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:18
verses.text: And they lay wait for their <hi type="italic">own</hi> blood; they lurk privily for their <hi type="italic">own</hi> lives.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:19
verses.text: So <hi type="italic">are</hi> the ways of every one that is greedy of gain; <hi type="italic">which</hi> taketh away the life of the owners thereof.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:20
verses.text: ¶ Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets:

verses.name: Proverbs 1:21
verses.text: She crieth in the chief place of concourse, in the openings of the gates: in the city she uttereth her words, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>,

verses.name: Proverbs 1:22
verses.text: How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge?

verses.name: Proverbs 1:23
verses.text: Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:24
verses.text: ¶ Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded;

verses.name: Proverbs 1:25
verses.text: But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof:

verses.name: Proverbs 1:26
verses.text: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh;

verses.name: Proverbs 1:27
verses.text: When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:28
verses.text: Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:

verses.name: Proverbs 1:29
verses.text: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord:

verses.name: Proverbs 1:30
verses.text: They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:31
verses.text: Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:32
verses.text: For the turning away of the simple shall slay them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them.

verses.name: Proverbs 1:33
verses.text: But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell safely, and shall be quiet from fear of evil.  <chapter eID="Prov.1"/><div eID="gen693" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 2:1
verses.text: MY son, if thou wilt receive my words, and hide my commandments with thee;

verses.name: Proverbs 2:2
verses.text: So that thou incline thine ear unto wisdom, <hi type="italic">and</hi> apply thine heart to understanding;

verses.name: Proverbs 2:3
verses.text: Yea, if thou criest after knowledge, <hi type="italic">and</hi> liftest up thy voice for understanding;

verses.name: Proverbs 2:4
verses.text: If thou seekest her as silver, and searchest for her as <hi type="italic">for</hi> hid treasures;

verses.name: Proverbs 2:5
verses.text: Then shalt thou understand the fear of the Lord, and find the knowledge of God.

verses.name: Proverbs 2:6
verses.text: For the Lord giveth wisdom: out of his mouth <hi type="italic">cometh</hi> knowledge and understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 2:7
verses.text: He layeth up sound wisdom for the righteous: <hi type="italic">he is</hi> a buckler to them that walk uprightly.

verses.name: Proverbs 2:8
verses.text: He keepeth the paths of judgment, and preserveth the way of his saints.

verses.name: Proverbs 2:9
verses.text: Then shalt thou understand righteousness, and judgment, and equity; <hi type="italic">yea</hi>, every good path.

verses.name: Proverbs 2:10
verses.text: ¶ When wisdom entereth into thine heart, and knowledge is pleasant unto thy soul;

verses.name: Proverbs 2:11
verses.text: Discretion shall preserve thee, understanding shall keep thee:

verses.name: Proverbs 2:12
verses.text: To deliver thee from the way of the evil <hi type="italic">man</hi>, from the man that speaketh froward things;

verses.name: Proverbs 2:13
verses.text: Who leave the paths of uprightness, to walk in the ways of darkness;

verses.name: Proverbs 2:14
verses.text: Who rejoice to do evil, <hi type="italic">and</hi> delight in the frowardness of the wicked;

verses.name: Proverbs 2:15
verses.text: Whose ways <hi type="italic">are</hi> crooked, and <hi type="italic">they</hi> froward in their paths:

verses.name: Proverbs 2:16
verses.text: To deliver thee from the strange woman, <hi type="italic">even</hi> from the stranger <hi type="italic">which</hi> flattereth with her words;

verses.name: Proverbs 2:17
verses.text: Which forsaketh the guide of her youth, and forgetteth the covenant of her God.

verses.name: Proverbs 2:18
verses.text: For her house inclineth unto death, and her paths unto the dead.

verses.name: Proverbs 2:19
verses.text: None that go unto her return again, neither take they hold of the paths of life.

verses.name: Proverbs 2:20
verses.text: That thou mayest walk in the way of good <hi type="italic">men</hi>, and keep the paths of the righteous.

verses.name: Proverbs 2:21
verses.text: For the upright shall dwell in the land, and the perfect shall remain in it.

verses.name: Proverbs 2:22
verses.text: But the wicked shall be cut off from the earth, and the transgressors shall be rooted out of it.  <chapter eID="Prov.2"/><div eID="gen694" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 3:1
verses.text: MY son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments:

verses.name: Proverbs 3:2
verses.text: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:3
verses.text: Let not mercy and truth forsake thee: bind them about thy neck; write them upon the table of thine heart:

verses.name: Proverbs 3:4
verses.text: So shalt thou find favour and good understanding in the sight of God and man.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:5
verses.text: ¶ Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:6
verses.text: In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:7
verses.text: ¶ Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the Lord, and depart from evil.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:8
verses.text: It shall be health to thy navel, and marrow to thy bones.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:9
verses.text: Honour the Lord with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase:

verses.name: Proverbs 3:10
verses.text: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:11
verses.text: ¶ My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; neither be weary of his correction:

verses.name: Proverbs 3:12
verses.text: For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son <hi type="italic">in whom</hi> he delighteth.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:13
verses.text: ¶ Happy <hi type="italic">is</hi> the man <hi type="italic">that</hi> findeth wisdom, and the man <hi type="italic">that</hi> getteth understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:14
verses.text: For the merchandise of it <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than the merchandise of silver, and the gain thereof than fine gold.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:15
verses.text: She <hi type="italic">is</hi> more precious than rubies: and all the things thou canst desire are not to be compared unto her.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:16
verses.text: Length of days <hi type="italic">is</hi> in her right hand; <hi type="italic">and</hi> in her left hand riches and honour.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:17
verses.text: Her ways <hi type="italic">are</hi> ways of pleasantness, and all her paths <hi type="italic">are</hi> peace.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:18
verses.text: She <hi type="italic">is</hi> a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: and happy <hi type="italic">is every one</hi> that retaineth her.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:19
verses.text: The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth; by understanding hath he established the heavens.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:20
verses.text: By his knowledge the depths are broken up, and the clouds drop down the dew.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:21
verses.text: ¶ My son, let not them depart from thine eyes: keep sound wisdom and discretion:

verses.name: Proverbs 3:22
verses.text: So shall they be life unto thy soul, and grace to thy neck.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:23
verses.text: Then shalt thou walk in thy way safely, and thy foot shall not stumble.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:24
verses.text: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:25
verses.text: Be not afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it cometh.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:26
verses.text: For the Lord shall be thy confidence, and shall keep thy foot from being taken.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:27
verses.text: ¶ Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thine hand to do <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:28
verses.text: Say not unto thy neighbour, Go, and come again, and to morrow I will give; when thou hast it by thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:29
verses.text: Devise not evil against thy neighbour, seeing he dwelleth securely by thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:30
verses.text: ¶ Strive not with a man without cause, if he have done thee no harm.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:31
verses.text: ¶ Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:32
verses.text: For the froward <hi type="italic">is</hi> abomination to the Lord: but his secret <hi type="italic">is</hi> with the righteous.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:33
verses.text: ¶ The curse of the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the house of the wicked: but he blesseth the habitation of the just.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:34
verses.text: Surely he scorneth the scorners: but he giveth grace unto the lowly.

verses.name: Proverbs 3:35
verses.text: The wise shall inherit glory: but shame shall be the promotion of fools.  <chapter eID="Prov.3"/><div eID="gen695" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 4:1
verses.text: HEAR, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:2
verses.text: For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:3
verses.text: For I was my father’s son, tender and only <hi type="italic">beloved</hi> in the sight of my mother.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:4
verses.text: He taught me also, and said unto me, Let thine heart retain my words: keep my commandments, and live.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:5
verses.text: Get wisdom, get understanding: forget <hi type="italic">it</hi> not; neither decline from the words of my mouth.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:6
verses.text: Forsake her not, and she shall preserve thee: love her, and she shall keep thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:7
verses.text: Wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> the principal thing; <hi type="italic">therefore</hi> get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:8
verses.text: Exalt her, and she shall promote thee: she shall bring thee to honour, when thou dost embrace her.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:9
verses.text: She shall give to thine head an ornament of grace: a crown of glory shall she deliver to thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:10
verses.text: Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings; and the years of thy life shall be many.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:11
verses.text: I have taught thee in the way of wisdom; I have led thee in right paths.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:12
verses.text: When thou goest, thy steps shall not be straitened; and when thou runnest, thou shalt not stumble.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:13
verses.text: Take fast hold of instruction; let <hi type="italic">her</hi> not go: keep her; for she <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy life.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:14
verses.text: ¶ Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil <hi type="italic">men</hi>.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:15
verses.text: Avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, and pass away.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:16
verses.text: For they sleep not, except they have done mischief; and their sleep is taken away, unless they cause <hi type="italic">some</hi> to fall.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:17
verses.text: For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of violence.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:18
verses.text: But the path of the just <hi type="italic">is</hi> as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:19
verses.text: The way of the wicked <hi type="italic">is</hi> as darkness: they know not at what they stumble.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:20
verses.text: ¶ My son, attend to my words; incline thine ear unto my sayings.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:21
verses.text: Let them not depart from thine eyes; keep them in the midst of thine heart.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:22
verses.text: For they <hi type="italic">are</hi> life unto those that find them, and health to all their flesh.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:23
verses.text: ¶ Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it <hi type="italic">are</hi> the issues of life.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:24
verses.text: Put away from thee a froward mouth, and perverse lips put far from thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:25
verses.text: Let thine eyes look right on, and let thine eyelids look straight before thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:26
verses.text: Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.

verses.name: Proverbs 4:27
verses.text: Turn not to the right hand nor to the left: remove thy foot from evil.  <chapter eID="Prov.4"/><div eID="gen696" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 5:1
verses.text: MY son, attend unto my wisdom, <hi type="italic">and</hi> bow thine ear to my understanding:

verses.name: Proverbs 5:2
verses.text: That thou mayest regard discretion, and <hi type="italic">that</hi> thy lips may keep knowledge.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:3
verses.text: ¶ For the lips of a strange woman drop <hi type="italic">as</hi> an honeycomb, and her mouth <hi type="italic">is</hi> smoother than oil:

verses.name: Proverbs 5:4
verses.text: But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a twoedged sword.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:5
verses.text: Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on hell.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:6
verses.text: Lest thou shouldest ponder the path of life, her ways are moveable, <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou canst not know <hi type="italic">them</hi>.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:7
verses.text: Hear me now therefore, O ye children, and depart not from the words of my mouth.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:8
verses.text: Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the door of her house:

verses.name: Proverbs 5:9
verses.text: Lest thou give thine honour unto others, and thy years unto the cruel:

verses.name: Proverbs 5:10
verses.text: Lest strangers be filled with thy wealth; and thy labours <hi type="italic">be</hi> in the house of a stranger;

verses.name: Proverbs 5:11
verses.text: And thou mourn at the last, when thy flesh and thy body are consumed,

verses.name: Proverbs 5:12
verses.text: And say, How have I hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof;

verses.name: Proverbs 5:13
verses.text: And have not obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor inclined mine ear to them that instructed me!

verses.name: Proverbs 5:14
verses.text: I was almost in all evil in the midst of the congregation and assembly.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:15
verses.text: ¶ Drink waters out of thine own cistern, and running waters out of thine own well.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:16
verses.text: Let thy fountains be dispersed abroad, <hi type="italic">and</hi> rivers of waters in the streets.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:17
verses.text: Let them be only thine own, and not strangers’ with thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:18
verses.text: Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:19
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Let her be as</hi> the loving hind and pleasant roe; let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:20
verses.text: And why wilt thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?

verses.name: Proverbs 5:21
verses.text: For the ways of man <hi type="italic">are</hi> before the eyes of the Lord, and he pondereth all his goings.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:22
verses.text: ¶ His own iniquities shall take the wicked himself, and he shall be holden with the cords of his sins.

verses.name: Proverbs 5:23
verses.text: He shall die without instruction; and in the greatness of his folly he shall go astray.  <chapter eID="Prov.5"/><div eID="gen697" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 6:1
verses.text: MY son, if thou be surety for thy friend, <hi type="italic">if</hi> thou hast stricken thy hand with a stranger,

verses.name: Proverbs 6:2
verses.text: Thou art snared with the words of thy mouth, thou art taken with the words of thy mouth.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:3
verses.text: Do this now, my son, and deliver thyself, when thou art come into the hand of thy friend; go, humble thyself, and make sure thy friend.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:4
verses.text: Give not sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber to thine eyelids.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:5
verses.text: Deliver thyself as a roe from the hand <hi type="italic">of the hunter</hi>, and as a bird from the hand of the fowler.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:6
verses.text: ¶ Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:

verses.name: Proverbs 6:7
verses.text: Which having no guide, overseer, or ruler,

verses.name: Proverbs 6:8
verses.text: Provideth her meat in the summer, <hi type="italic">and</hi> gathereth her food in the harvest.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:9
verses.text: How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? when wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?

verses.name: Proverbs 6:10
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Yet</hi> a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:

verses.name: Proverbs 6:11
verses.text: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth, and thy want as an armed man.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:12
verses.text: ¶ A naughty person, a wicked man, walketh with a froward mouth.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:13
verses.text: He winketh with his eyes, he speaketh with his feet, he teacheth with his fingers;

verses.name: Proverbs 6:14
verses.text: Frowardness <hi type="italic">is</hi> in his heart, he deviseth mischief continually; he soweth discord.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:15
verses.text: Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly; suddenly shall he be broken without remedy.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:16
verses.text: ¶ These six <hi type="italic">things</hi> doth the Lord hate: yea, seven <hi type="italic">are</hi> an abomination unto him:

verses.name: Proverbs 6:17
verses.text: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood,

verses.name: Proverbs 6:18
verses.text: An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief,

verses.name: Proverbs 6:19
verses.text: A false witness <hi type="italic">that</hi> speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:20
verses.text: ¶ My son, keep thy father’s commandment, and forsake not the law of thy mother:

verses.name: Proverbs 6:21
verses.text: Bind them continually upon thine heart, <hi type="italic">and</hi> tie them about thy neck.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:22
verses.text: When thou goest, it shall lead thee; when thou sleepest, it shall keep thee; and <hi type="italic">when</hi> thou awakest, it shall talk with thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:23
verses.text: For the commandment <hi type="italic">is</hi> a lamp; and the law <hi type="italic">is</hi> light; and reproofs of instruction <hi type="italic">are</hi> the way of life:

verses.name: Proverbs 6:24
verses.text: To keep thee from the evil woman, from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:25
verses.text: Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:26
verses.text: For by means of a whorish woman <hi type="italic">a man is brought</hi> to a piece of bread: and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:27
verses.text: Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?

verses.name: Proverbs 6:28
verses.text: Can one go upon hot coals, and his feet not be burned?

verses.name: Proverbs 6:29
verses.text: So he that goeth in to his neighbour’s wife; whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:30
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Men</hi> do not despise a thief, if he steal to satisfy his soul when he is hungry;

verses.name: Proverbs 6:31
verses.text: But <hi type="italic">if</hi> he be found, he shall restore sevenfold; he shall give all the substance of his house.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:32
verses.text: <hi type="italic">But</hi> whoso committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding: he <hi type="italic">that</hi> doeth it destroyeth his own soul.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:33
verses.text: A wound and dishonour shall he get; and his reproach shall not be wiped away.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:34
verses.text: For jealousy <hi type="italic">is</hi> the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance.

verses.name: Proverbs 6:35
verses.text: He will not regard any ransom; neither will he rest content, though thou givest many gifts.  <chapter eID="Prov.6"/><div eID="gen698" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 7:1
verses.text: MY son, keep my words, and lay up my commandments with thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:2
verses.text: Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:3
verses.text: Bind them upon thy fingers, write them upon the table of thine heart.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:4
verses.text: Say unto wisdom, Thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> my sister; and call understanding <hi type="italic">thy</hi> kinswoman:

verses.name: Proverbs 7:5
verses.text: That they may keep thee from the strange woman, from the stranger <hi type="italic">which</hi> flattereth with her words.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:6
verses.text: ¶ For at the window of my house I looked through my casement,

verses.name: Proverbs 7:7
verses.text: And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding,

verses.name: Proverbs 7:8
verses.text: Passing through the street near her corner; and he went the way to her house,

verses.name: Proverbs 7:9
verses.text: In the twilight, in the evening, in the black and dark night:

verses.name: Proverbs 7:10
verses.text: And, behold, there met him a woman <hi type="italic">with</hi> the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:11
verses.text: (She <hi type="italic">is</hi> loud and stubborn; her feet abide not in her house:

verses.name: Proverbs 7:12
verses.text: Now <hi type="italic">is she</hi> without, now in the streets, and lieth in wait at every corner.)

verses.name: Proverbs 7:13
verses.text: So she caught him, and kissed him, <hi type="italic">and</hi> with an impudent face said unto him,

verses.name: Proverbs 7:14
verses.text: <hi type="italic">I have</hi> peace offerings with me; this day have I payed my vows.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:15
verses.text: Therefore came I forth to meet thee, diligently to seek thy face, and I have found thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:16
verses.text: I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved <hi type="italic">works</hi>, with fine linen of Egypt.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:17
verses.text: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:18
verses.text: Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:19
verses.text: For the goodman <hi type="italic">is</hi> not at home, he is gone a long journey:

verses.name: Proverbs 7:20
verses.text: He hath taken a bag of money with him, <hi type="italic">and</hi> will come home at the day appointed.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:21
verses.text: With her much fair speech she caused him to yield, with the flattering of her lips she forced him.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:22
verses.text: He goeth after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks;

verses.name: Proverbs 7:23
verses.text: Till a dart strike through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it <hi type="italic">is</hi> for his life.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:24
verses.text: ¶ Hearken unto me now therefore, O ye children, and attend to the words of my mouth.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:25
verses.text: Let not thine heart decline to her ways, go not astray in her paths.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:26
verses.text: For she hath cast down many wounded: yea, many strong <hi type="italic">men</hi> have been slain by her.

verses.name: Proverbs 7:27
verses.text: Her house <hi type="italic">is</hi> the way to hell, going down to the chambers of death.  <chapter eID="Prov.7"/><div eID="gen699" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 8:1
verses.text: DOTH not wisdom cry? and understanding put forth her voice?

verses.name: Proverbs 8:2
verses.text: She standeth in the top of high places, by the way in the places of the paths.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:3
verses.text: She crieth at the gates, at the entry of the city, at the coming in at the doors.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:4
verses.text: Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice <hi type="italic">is</hi> to the sons of man.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:5
verses.text: O ye simple, understand wisdom: and, ye fools, be ye of an understanding heart.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:6
verses.text: Hear; for I will speak of excellent things; and the opening of my lips <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> right things.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:7
verses.text: For my mouth shall speak truth; and wickedness <hi type="italic">is</hi> an abomination to my lips.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:8
verses.text: All the words of my mouth <hi type="italic">are</hi> in righteousness; <hi type="italic">there is</hi> nothing froward or perverse in them.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:9
verses.text: They <hi type="italic">are</hi> all plain to him that understandeth, and right to them that find knowledge.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:10
verses.text: Receive my instruction, and not silver; and knowledge rather than choice gold.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:11
verses.text: For wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than rubies; and all the things that may be desired are not to be compared to it.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:12
verses.text: I wisdom dwell with prudence, and find out knowledge of witty inventions.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:13
verses.text: The fear of the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:14
verses.text: Counsel <hi type="italic">is</hi> mine, and sound wisdom: I <hi type="italic">am</hi> understanding; I have strength.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:15
verses.text: By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:16
verses.text: By me princes rule, and nobles, <hi type="italic">even</hi> all the judges of the earth.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:17
verses.text: I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:18
verses.text: Riches and honour <hi type="italic">are</hi> with me; <hi type="italic">yea</hi>, durable riches and righteousness.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:19
verses.text: My fruit <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:20
verses.text: I lead in the way of righteousness, in the midst of the paths of judgment:

verses.name: Proverbs 8:21
verses.text: That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance; and I will fill their treasures.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:22
verses.text: The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:23
verses.text: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:24
verses.text: When <hi type="italic">there were</hi> no depths, I was brought forth; when <hi type="italic">there were</hi> no fountains abounding with water.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:25
verses.text: Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth:

verses.name: Proverbs 8:26
verses.text: While as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the highest part of the dust of the world.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:27
verses.text: When he prepared the heavens, I <hi type="italic">was</hi> there: when he set a compass upon the face of the depth:

verses.name: Proverbs 8:28
verses.text: When he established the clouds above: when he strengthened the fountains of the deep:

verses.name: Proverbs 8:29
verses.text: When he gave to the sea his decree, that the waters should not pass his commandment: when he appointed the foundations of the earth:

verses.name: Proverbs 8:30
verses.text: Then I was by him, <hi type="italic">as</hi> one brought up <hi type="italic">with him:</hi> and I was daily <hi type="italic">his</hi> delight, rejoicing always before him;

verses.name: Proverbs 8:31
verses.text: Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights <hi type="italic">were</hi> with the sons of men.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:32
verses.text: Now therefore hearken unto me, O ye children: for blessed <hi type="italic">are they that</hi> keep my ways.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:33
verses.text: Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:34
verses.text: Blessed <hi type="italic">is</hi> the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:35
verses.text: For whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour of the Lord.

verses.name: Proverbs 8:36
verses.text: But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: all they that hate me love death.  <chapter eID="Prov.8"/><div eID="gen700" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 9:1
verses.text: WISDOM hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars:

verses.name: Proverbs 9:2
verses.text: She hath killed her beasts; she hath mingled her wine; she hath also furnished her table.

verses.name: Proverbs 9:3
verses.text: She hath sent forth her maidens: she crieth upon the highest places of the city,

verses.name: Proverbs 9:4
verses.text: Whoso <hi type="italic">is</hi> simple, let him turn in hither: <hi type="italic">as for</hi> him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,

verses.name: Proverbs 9:5
verses.text: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine <hi type="italic">which</hi> I have mingled.

verses.name: Proverbs 9:6
verses.text: Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 9:7
verses.text: He that reproveth a scorner getteth to himself shame: and he that rebuketh a wicked <hi type="italic">man getteth</hi> himself a blot.

verses.name: Proverbs 9:8
verses.text: Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee: rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 9:9
verses.text: Give <hi type="italic">instruction</hi> to a wise <hi type="italic">man</hi>, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just <hi type="italic">man</hi>, and he will increase in learning.

verses.name: Proverbs 9:10
verses.text: The fear of the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy <hi type="italic">is</hi> understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 9:11
verses.text: For by me thy days shall be multiplied, and the years of thy life shall be increased.

verses.name: Proverbs 9:12
verses.text: If thou be wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself: but <hi type="italic">if</hi> thou scornest, thou alone shalt bear <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Proverbs 9:13
verses.text: ¶ A foolish woman <hi type="italic">is</hi> clamorous: <hi type="italic">she is</hi> simple, and knoweth nothing.

verses.name: Proverbs 9:14
verses.text: For she sitteth at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,

verses.name: Proverbs 9:15
verses.text: To call passengers who go right on their ways:

verses.name: Proverbs 9:16
verses.text: Whoso <hi type="italic">is</hi> simple, let him turn in hither: and <hi type="italic">as for</hi> him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,

verses.name: Proverbs 9:17
verses.text: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread <hi type="italic">eaten</hi> in secret is pleasant.

verses.name: Proverbs 9:18
verses.text: But he knoweth not that the dead <hi type="italic">are</hi> there; <hi type="italic">and that</hi> her guests <hi type="italic">are</hi> in the depths of hell.  <chapter eID="Prov.9"/><div eID="gen701" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 10:1
verses.text: THE proverbs of Solomon. A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish son <hi type="italic">is</hi> the heaviness of his mother.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:2
verses.text: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing: but righteousness delivereth from death.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:3
verses.text: The Lord will not suffer the soul of the righteous to famish: but he casteth away the substance of the wicked.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:4
verses.text: He becometh poor that dealeth <hi type="italic">with</hi> a slack hand: but the hand of the diligent maketh rich.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:5
verses.text: He that gathereth in summer <hi type="italic">is</hi> a wise son: <hi type="italic">but</hi> he that sleepeth in harvest <hi type="italic">is</hi> a son that causeth shame.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:6
verses.text: Blessings <hi type="italic">are</hi> upon the head of the just: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:7
verses.text: The memory of the just <hi type="italic">is</hi> blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:8
verses.text: The wise in heart will receive commandments: but a prating fool shall fall.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:9
verses.text: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:10
verses.text: He that winketh with the eye causeth sorrow: but a prating fool shall fall.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:11
verses.text: The mouth of a righteous <hi type="italic">man is</hi> a well of life: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:12
verses.text: Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:13
verses.text: In the lips of him that hath understanding wisdom is found: but a rod <hi type="italic">is</hi> for the back of him that is void of understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:14
verses.text: Wise <hi type="italic">men</hi> lay up knowledge: but the mouth of the foolish <hi type="italic">is</hi> near destruction.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:15
verses.text: The rich man’s wealth <hi type="italic">is</hi> his strong city: the destruction of the poor <hi type="italic">is</hi> their poverty.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:16
verses.text: The labour of the righteous <hi type="italic">tendeth</hi> to life: the fruit of the wicked to sin.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:17
verses.text: He <hi type="italic">is in</hi> the way of life that keepeth instruction: but he that refuseth reproof erreth.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:18
verses.text: He that hideth hatred <hi type="italic">with</hi> lying lips, and he that uttereth a slander, <hi type="italic">is</hi> a fool.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:19
verses.text: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips <hi type="italic">is</hi> wise.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:20
verses.text: The tongue of the just <hi type="italic">is as</hi> choice silver: the heart of the wicked <hi type="italic">is</hi> little worth.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:21
verses.text: The lips of the righteous feed many: but fools die for want of wisdom.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:22
verses.text: The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:23
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> as sport to a fool to do mischief: but a man of understanding hath wisdom.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:24
verses.text: The fear of the wicked, it shall come upon him: but the desire of the righteous shall be granted.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:25
verses.text: As the whirlwind passeth, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> the wicked no <hi type="italic">more:</hi> but the righteous <hi type="italic">is</hi> an everlasting foundation.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:26
verses.text: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> the sluggard to them that send him.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:27
verses.text: The fear of the Lord prolongeth days: but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:28
verses.text: The hope of the righteous <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> gladness: but the expectation of the wicked shall perish.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:29
verses.text: The way of the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> strength to the upright: but destruction <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> to the workers of iniquity.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:30
verses.text: The righteous shall never be removed: but the wicked shall not inhabit the earth.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:31
verses.text: The mouth of the just bringeth forth wisdom: but the froward tongue shall be cut out.

verses.name: Proverbs 10:32
verses.text: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable: but the mouth of the wicked <hi type="italic">speaketh</hi> frowardness.  <chapter eID="Prov.10"/><div eID="gen702" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 11:1
verses.text: A FALSE balance <hi type="italic">is</hi> abomination to the Lord: but a just weight <hi type="italic">is</hi> his delight.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:2
verses.text: <hi type="italic">When</hi> pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly <hi type="italic">is</hi> wisdom.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:3
verses.text: The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:4
verses.text: Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:5
verses.text: The righteousness of the perfect shall direct his way: but the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:6
verses.text: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them: but transgressors shall be taken in <hi type="italic">their own</hi> naughtiness.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:7
verses.text: When a wicked man dieth, <hi type="italic">his</hi> expectation shall perish: and the hope of unjust <hi type="italic">men</hi> perisheth.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:8
verses.text: The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:9
verses.text: An hypocrite with <hi type="italic">his</hi> mouth destroyeth his neighbour: but through knowledge shall the just be delivered.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:10
verses.text: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth: and when the wicked perish, <hi type="italic">there is</hi> shouting.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:11
verses.text: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted: but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:12
verses.text: He that is void of wisdom despiseth his neighbour: but a man of understanding holdeth his peace.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:13
verses.text: A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:14
verses.text: Where no counsel <hi type="italic">is</hi>, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellers <hi type="italic">there is</hi> safety.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:15
verses.text: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart <hi type="italic">for it:</hi> and he that hateth suretiship is sure.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:16
verses.text: A gracious woman retaineth honour: and strong <hi type="italic">men</hi> retain riches.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:17
verses.text: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul: but <hi type="italic">he that is</hi> cruel troubleth his own flesh.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:18
verses.text: The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> a sure reward.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:19
verses.text: As righteousness <hi type="italic">tendeth</hi> to life: so he that pursueth evil <hi type="italic">pursueth it</hi> to his own death.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:20
verses.text: They that are of a froward heart <hi type="italic">are</hi> abomination to the Lord: but <hi type="italic">such as are</hi> upright in <hi type="italic">their</hi> way <hi type="italic">are</hi> his delight.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:21
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Though</hi> hand <hi type="italic">join</hi> in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:22
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> a jewel of gold in a swine’s snout, <hi type="italic">so is</hi> a fair woman which is without discretion.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:23
verses.text: The desire of the righteous <hi type="italic">is</hi> only good: <hi type="italic">but</hi> the expectation of the wicked <hi type="italic">is</hi> wrath.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:24
verses.text: There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and <hi type="italic">there is</hi> that withholdeth more than is meet, but <hi type="italic">it tendeth</hi> to poverty.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:25
verses.text: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:26
verses.text: He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him: but blessing <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> upon the head of him that selleth <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:27
verses.text: He that diligently seeketh good procureth favour: but he that seeketh mischief, it shall come unto him.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:28
verses.text: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall: but the righteous shall flourish as a branch.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:29
verses.text: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind: and the fool <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> servant to the wise of heart.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:30
verses.text: The fruit of the righteous <hi type="italic">is</hi> a tree of life; and he that winneth souls <hi type="italic">is</hi> wise.

verses.name: Proverbs 11:31
verses.text: Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner.  <chapter eID="Prov.11"/><div eID="gen703" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 12:1
verses.text: WHOSO loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof <hi type="italic">is</hi> brutish.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:2
verses.text: A good <hi type="italic">man</hi> obtaineth favour of the Lord: but a man of wicked devices will he condemn.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:3
verses.text: A man shall not be established by wickedness: but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:4
verses.text: A virtuous woman <hi type="italic">is</hi> a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed <hi type="italic">is</hi> as rottenness in his bones.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:5
verses.text: The thoughts of the righteous <hi type="italic">are</hi> right: <hi type="italic">but</hi> the counsels of the wicked <hi type="italic">are</hi> deceit.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:6
verses.text: The words of the wicked <hi type="italic">are</hi> to lie in wait for blood: but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:7
verses.text: The wicked are overthrown, and <hi type="italic">are</hi> not: but the house of the righteous shall stand.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:8
verses.text: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom: but he that is of a perverse heart shall be despised.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:9
verses.text: <hi type="italic">He that is</hi> despised, and hath a servant, <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than he that honoureth himself, and lacketh bread.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:10
verses.text: A righteous <hi type="italic">man</hi> regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked <hi type="italic">are</hi> cruel.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:11
verses.text: He that tilleth his land shall be satisfied with bread: but he that followeth vain <hi type="italic">persons is</hi> void of understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:12
verses.text: The wicked desireth the net of evil <hi type="italic">men:</hi> but the root of the righteous yieldeth <hi type="italic">fruit</hi>.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:13
verses.text: The wicked is snared by the transgression of <hi type="italic">his</hi> lips: but the just shall come out of trouble.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:14
verses.text: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of <hi type="italic">his</hi> mouth: and the recompence of a man’s hands shall be rendered unto him.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:15
verses.text: The way of a fool <hi type="italic">is</hi> right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel <hi type="italic">is</hi> wise.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:16
verses.text: A fool’s wrath is presently known: but a prudent <hi type="italic">man</hi> covereth shame.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:17
verses.text: <hi type="italic">He that</hi> speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:18
verses.text: There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise <hi type="italic">is</hi> health.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:19
verses.text: The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue <hi type="italic">is</hi> but for a moment.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:20
verses.text: Deceit <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the heart of them that imagine evil: but to the counsellers of peace <hi type="italic">is</hi> joy.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:21
verses.text: There shall no evil happen to the just: but the wicked shall be filled with mischief.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:22
verses.text: Lying lips <hi type="italic">are</hi> abomination to the Lord: but they that deal truly <hi type="italic">are</hi> his delight.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:23
verses.text: A prudent man concealeth knowledge: but the heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:24
verses.text: The hand of the diligent shall bear rule: but the slothful shall be under tribute.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:25
verses.text: Heaviness in the heart of man maketh it stoop: but a good word maketh it glad.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:26
verses.text: The righteous <hi type="italic">is</hi> more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:27
verses.text: The slothful <hi type="italic">man</hi> roasteth not that which he took in hunting: but the substance of a diligent man <hi type="italic">is</hi> precious.

verses.name: Proverbs 12:28
verses.text: In the way of righteousness <hi type="italic">is</hi> life; and <hi type="italic">in</hi> the pathway <hi type="italic">thereof there is</hi> no death.  <chapter eID="Prov.12"/><div eID="gen704" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 13:1
verses.text: A WISE son <hi type="italic">heareth</hi> his father’s instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:2
verses.text: A man shall eat good by the fruit of <hi type="italic">his</hi> mouth: but the soul of the transgressors <hi type="italic">shall eat</hi> violence.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:3
verses.text: He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: <hi type="italic">but</hi> he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:4
verses.text: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and <hi type="italic">hath</hi> nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:5
verses.text: A righteous <hi type="italic">man</hi> hateth lying: but a wicked <hi type="italic">man</hi> is loathsome, and cometh to shame.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:6
verses.text: Righteousness keepeth <hi type="italic">him that is</hi> upright in the way: but wickedness overthroweth the sinner.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:7
verses.text: There is that maketh himself rich, yet <hi type="italic">hath</hi> nothing: <hi type="italic">there is</hi> that maketh himself poor, yet <hi type="italic">hath</hi> great riches.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:8
verses.text: The ransom of a man’s life <hi type="italic">are</hi> his riches: but the poor heareth not rebuke.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:9
verses.text: The light of the righteous rejoiceth: but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:10
verses.text: Only by pride cometh contention: but with the well advised <hi type="italic">is</hi> wisdom.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:11
verses.text: Wealth <hi type="italic">gotten</hi> by vanity shall be diminished: but he that gathereth by labour shall increase.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:12
verses.text: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but <hi type="italic">when</hi> the desire cometh, <hi type="italic">it is</hi> a tree of life.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:13
verses.text: Whoso despiseth the word shall be destroyed: but he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:14
verses.text: The law of the wise <hi type="italic">is</hi> a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:15
verses.text: Good understanding giveth favour: but the way of transgressors <hi type="italic">is</hi> hard.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:16
verses.text: Every prudent <hi type="italic">man</hi> dealeth with knowledge: but a fool layeth open <hi type="italic">his</hi> folly.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:17
verses.text: A wicked messenger falleth into mischief: but a faithful ambassador <hi type="italic">is</hi> health.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:18
verses.text: Poverty and shame <hi type="italic">shall be to</hi> him that refuseth instruction: but he that regardeth reproof shall be honoured.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:19
verses.text: The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul: but <hi type="italic">it is</hi> abomination to fools to depart from evil.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:20
verses.text: He that walketh with wise <hi type="italic">men</hi> shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:21
verses.text: Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:22
verses.text: A good <hi type="italic">man</hi> leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children: and the wealth of the sinner <hi type="italic">is</hi> laid up for the just.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:23
verses.text: Much food <hi type="italic">is in</hi> the tillage of the poor: but there is <hi type="italic">that is</hi> destroyed for want of judgment.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:24
verses.text: He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.

verses.name: Proverbs 13:25
verses.text: The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul: but the belly of the wicked shall want.  <chapter eID="Prov.13"/><div eID="gen705" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 14:1
verses.text: EVERY wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:2
verses.text: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth the Lord: but <hi type="italic">he that is</hi> perverse in his ways despiseth him.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:3
verses.text: In the mouth of the foolish <hi type="italic">is</hi> a rod of pride: but the lips of the wise shall preserve them.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:4
verses.text: Where no oxen <hi type="italic">are</hi>, the crib <hi type="italic">is</hi> clean: but much increase <hi type="italic">is</hi> by the strength of the ox.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:5
verses.text: A faithful witness will not lie: but a false witness will utter lies.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:6
verses.text: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and <hi type="italic">findeth it</hi> not: but knowledge <hi type="italic">is</hi> easy unto him that understandeth.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:7
verses.text: Go from the presence of a foolish man, when thou perceivest not <hi type="italic">in him</hi> the lips of knowledge.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:8
verses.text: The wisdom of the prudent <hi type="italic">is</hi> to understand his way: but the folly of fools <hi type="italic">is</hi> deceit.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:9
verses.text: Fools make a mock at sin: but among the righteous <hi type="italic">there is</hi> favour.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:10
verses.text: The heart knoweth his own bitterness; and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:11
verses.text: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown: but the tabernacle of the upright shall flourish.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:12
verses.text: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof <hi type="italic">are</hi> the ways of death.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:13
verses.text: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; and the end of that mirth <hi type="italic">is</hi> heaviness.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:14
verses.text: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways: and a good man <hi type="italic">shall be satisfied</hi> from himself.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:15
verses.text: The simple believeth every word: but the prudent <hi type="italic">man</hi> looketh well to his going.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:16
verses.text: A wise <hi type="italic">man</hi> feareth, and departeth from evil: but the fool rageth, and is confident.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:17
verses.text: <hi type="italic">He that is</hi> soon angry dealeth foolishly: and a man of wicked devices is hated.
