verses.name: Proverbs 14:18
verses.text: The simple inherit folly: but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:19
verses.text: The evil bow before the good; and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:20
verses.text: The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the rich <hi type="italic">hath</hi> many friends.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:21
verses.text: He that despiseth his neighbour sinneth: but he that hath mercy on the poor, happy <hi type="italic">is</hi> he.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:22
verses.text: Do they not err that devise evil? but mercy and truth <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> to them that devise good.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:23
verses.text: In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips <hi type="italic">tendeth</hi> only to penury.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:24
verses.text: The crown of the wise <hi type="italic">is</hi> their riches: <hi type="italic">but</hi> the foolishness of fools <hi type="italic">is</hi> folly.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:25
verses.text: A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful <hi type="italic">witness</hi> speaketh lies.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:26
verses.text: In the fear of the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:27
verses.text: The fear of the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:28
verses.text: In the multitude of people <hi type="italic">is</hi> the king’s honour: but in the want of people <hi type="italic">is</hi> the destruction of the prince.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:29
verses.text: <hi type="italic">He that is</hi> slow to wrath <hi type="italic">is</hi> of great understanding: but <hi type="italic">he that is</hi> hasty of spirit exalteth folly.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:30
verses.text: A sound heart <hi type="italic">is</hi> the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:31
verses.text: He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:32
verses.text: The wicked is driven away in his wickedness: but the righteous hath hope in his death.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:33
verses.text: Wisdom resteth in the heart of him that hath understanding: but <hi type="italic">that which is</hi> in the midst of fools is made known.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:34
verses.text: Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin <hi type="italic">is</hi> a reproach to any people.

verses.name: Proverbs 14:35
verses.text: The king’s favour <hi type="italic">is</hi> toward a wise servant: but his wrath is <hi type="italic">against</hi> him that causeth shame.  <chapter eID="Prov.14"/><div eID="gen706" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:1
verses.text: A SOFT answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:2
verses.text: The tongue of the wise useth knowledge aright: but the mouth of fools poureth out foolishness.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:3
verses.text: The eyes of the Lord <hi type="italic">are</hi> in every place, beholding the evil and the good.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:4
verses.text: A wholesome tongue <hi type="italic">is</hi> a tree of life: but perverseness therein <hi type="italic">is</hi> a breach in the spirit.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:5
verses.text: A fool despiseth his father’s instruction: but he that regardeth reproof is prudent.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:6
verses.text: In the house of the righteous <hi type="italic">is</hi> much treasure: but in the revenues of the wicked is trouble.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:7
verses.text: The lips of the wise disperse knowledge: but the heart of the foolish <hi type="italic">doeth</hi> not so.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:8
verses.text: The sacrifice of the wicked <hi type="italic">is</hi> an abomination to the Lord: but the prayer of the upright <hi type="italic">is</hi> his delight.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:9
verses.text: The way of the wicked <hi type="italic">is</hi> an abomination unto the Lord: but he loveth him that followeth after righteousness.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:10
verses.text: Correction <hi type="italic">is</hi> grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: <hi type="italic">and</hi> he that hateth reproof shall die.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:11
verses.text: Hell and destruction <hi type="italic">are</hi> before the Lord: how much more then the hearts of the children of men?

verses.name: Proverbs 15:12
verses.text: A scorner loveth not one that reproveth him: neither will he go unto the wise.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:13
verses.text: A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:14
verses.text: The heart of him that hath understanding seeketh knowledge: but the mouth of fools feedeth on foolishness.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:15
verses.text: All the days of the afflicted <hi type="italic">are</hi> evil: but he that is of a merry heart <hi type="italic">hath</hi> a continual feast.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:16
verses.text: Better <hi type="italic">is</hi> little with the fear of the Lord than great treasure and trouble therewith.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:17
verses.text: Better <hi type="italic">is</hi> a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:18
verses.text: A wrathful man stirreth up strife: but <hi type="italic">he that is</hi> slow to anger appeaseth strife.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:19
verses.text: The way of the slothful <hi type="italic">man is</hi> as an hedge of thorns: but the way of the righteous <hi type="italic">is</hi> made plain.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:20
verses.text: A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish man despiseth his mother.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:21
verses.text: Folly <hi type="italic">is</hi> joy to <hi type="italic">him that is</hi> destitute of wisdom: but a man of understanding walketh uprightly.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:22
verses.text: Without counsel purposes are disappointed: but in the multitude of counsellers they are established.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:23
verses.text: A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word <hi type="italic">spoken</hi> in due season, how good <hi type="italic">is it!</hi>

verses.name: Proverbs 15:24
verses.text: The way of life <hi type="italic">is</hi> above to the wise, that he may depart from hell beneath.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:25
verses.text: The Lord will destroy the house of the proud: but he will establish the border of the widow.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:26
verses.text: The thoughts of the wicked <hi type="italic">are</hi> an abomination to the Lord: but <hi type="italic">the words</hi> of the pure <hi type="italic">are</hi> pleasant words.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:27
verses.text: He that is greedy of gain troubleth his own house; but he that hateth gifts shall live.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:28
verses.text: The heart of the righteous studieth to answer: but the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:29
verses.text: The Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:30
verses.text: The light of the eyes rejoiceth the heart: <hi type="italic">and</hi> a good report maketh the bones fat.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:31
verses.text: The ear that heareth the reproof of life abideth among the wise.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:32
verses.text: He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul: but he that heareth reproof getteth understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 15:33
verses.text: The fear of the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> the instruction of wisdom; and before honour <hi type="italic">is</hi> humility.  <chapter eID="Prov.15"/><div eID="gen707" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 16:1
verses.text: THE preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, <hi type="italic">is</hi> from the Lord.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:2
verses.text: All the ways of a man <hi type="italic">are</hi> clean in his own eyes; but the Lord weigheth the spirits.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:3
verses.text: Commit thy works unto the Lord, and thy thoughts shall be established.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:4
verses.text: The Lord hath made all <hi type="italic">things</hi> for himself: yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:5
verses.text: Every one <hi type="italic">that is</hi> proud in heart <hi type="italic">is</hi> an abomination to the Lord: <hi type="italic">though</hi> hand <hi type="italic">join</hi> in hand, he shall not be unpunished.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:6
verses.text: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged: and by the fear of the Lord <hi type="italic">men</hi> depart from evil.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:7
verses.text: When a man’s ways please the Lord, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:8
verses.text: Better <hi type="italic">is</hi> a little with righteousness than great revenues without right.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:9
verses.text: A man’s heart deviseth his way: but the Lord directeth his steps.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:10
verses.text: A divine sentence <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the lips of the king: his mouth transgresseth not in judgment.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:11
verses.text: A just weight and balance <hi type="italic">are</hi> the Lord’s: all the weights of the bag <hi type="italic">are</hi> his work.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:12
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> an abomination to kings to commit wickedness: for the throne is established by righteousness.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:13
verses.text: Righteous lips <hi type="italic">are</hi> the delight of kings; and they love him that speaketh right.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:14
verses.text: The wrath of a king <hi type="italic">is as</hi> messengers of death: but a wise man will pacify it.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:15
verses.text: In the light of the king’s countenance <hi type="italic">is</hi> life; and his favour <hi type="italic">is</hi> as a cloud of the latter rain.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:16
verses.text: How much better <hi type="italic">is it</hi> to get wisdom than gold! and to get understanding rather to be chosen than silver!

verses.name: Proverbs 16:17
verses.text: The highway of the upright <hi type="italic">is</hi> to depart from evil: he that keepeth his way preserveth his soul.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:18
verses.text: Pride <hi type="italic">goeth</hi> before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:19
verses.text: Better <hi type="italic">it is to be</hi> of an humble spirit with the lowly, than to divide the spoil with the proud.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:20
verses.text: He that handleth a matter wisely shall find good: and whoso trusteth in the Lord, happy <hi type="italic">is</hi> he.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:21
verses.text: The wise in heart shall be called prudent: and the sweetness of the lips increaseth learning.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:22
verses.text: Understanding <hi type="italic">is</hi> a wellspring of life unto him that hath it: but the instruction of fools <hi type="italic">is</hi> folly.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:23
verses.text: The heart of the wise teacheth his mouth, and addeth learning to his lips.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:24
verses.text: Pleasant words <hi type="italic">are as</hi> an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:25
verses.text: There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof <hi type="italic">are</hi> the ways of death.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:26
verses.text: He that laboureth laboureth for himself; for his mouth craveth it of him.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:27
verses.text: An ungodly man diggeth up evil: and in his lips <hi type="italic">there is</hi> as a burning fire.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:28
verses.text: A froward man soweth strife: and a whisperer separateth chief friends.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:29
verses.text: A violent man enticeth his neighbour, and leadeth him into the way <hi type="italic">that is</hi> not good.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:30
verses.text: He shutteth his eyes to devise froward things: moving his lips he bringeth evil to pass.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:31
verses.text: The hoary head <hi type="italic">is</hi> a crown of glory, <hi type="italic">if</hi> it be found in the way of righteousness.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:32
verses.text: <hi type="italic">He that is</hi> slow to anger <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.

verses.name: Proverbs 16:33
verses.text: The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof <hi type="italic">is</hi> of the Lord.  <chapter eID="Prov.16"/><div eID="gen708" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:1
verses.text: BETTER <hi type="italic">is</hi> a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices <hi type="italic">with</hi> strife.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:2
verses.text: A wise servant shall have rule over a son that causeth shame, and shall have part of the inheritance among the brethren.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:3
verses.text: The fining pot <hi type="italic">is</hi> for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the Lord trieth the hearts.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:4
verses.text: A wicked doer giveth heed to false lips; <hi type="italic">and</hi> a liar giveth ear to a naughty tongue.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:5
verses.text: Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker: <hi type="italic">and</hi> he that is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:6
verses.text: Children’s children <hi type="italic">are</hi> the crown of old men; and the glory of children <hi type="italic">are</hi> their fathers.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:7
verses.text: Excellent speech becometh not a fool: much less do lying lips a prince.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:8
verses.text: A gift <hi type="italic">is as</hi> a precious stone in the eyes of him that hath it: whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:9
verses.text: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth <hi type="italic">very</hi> friends.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:10
verses.text: A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:11
verses.text: An evil <hi type="italic">man</hi> seeketh only rebellion: therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:12
verses.text: Let a bear robbed of her whelps meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:13
verses.text: Whoso rewardeth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:14
verses.text: The beginning of strife <hi type="italic">is as</hi> when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:15
verses.text: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both <hi type="italic">are</hi> abomination to the Lord.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:16
verses.text: Wherefore <hi type="italic">is there</hi> a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, seeing <hi type="italic">he hath</hi> no heart <hi type="italic">to it?</hi>

verses.name: Proverbs 17:17
verses.text: A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:18
verses.text: A man void of understanding striketh hands, <hi type="italic">and</hi> becometh surety in the presence of his friend.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:19
verses.text: He loveth transgression that loveth strife: <hi type="italic">and</hi> he that exalteth his gate seeketh destruction.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:20
verses.text: He that hath a froward heart findeth no good: and he that hath a perverse tongue falleth into mischief.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:21
verses.text: He that begetteth a fool <hi type="italic">doeth it</hi> to his sorrow: and the father of a fool hath no joy.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:22
verses.text: A merry heart doeth good <hi type="italic">like</hi> a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:23
verses.text: A wicked <hi type="italic">man</hi> taketh a gift out of the bosom to pervert the ways of judgment.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:24
verses.text: Wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool <hi type="italic">are</hi> in the ends of the earth.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:25
verses.text: A foolish son <hi type="italic">is</hi> a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:26
verses.text: Also to punish the just <hi type="italic">is</hi> not good, <hi type="italic">nor</hi> to strike princes for equity.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:27
verses.text: He that hath knowledge spareth his words: <hi type="italic">and</hi> a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit.

verses.name: Proverbs 17:28
verses.text: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: <hi type="italic">and</hi> he that shutteth his lips <hi type="italic">is esteemed</hi> a man of understanding.  <chapter eID="Prov.17"/><div eID="gen709" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 18:1
verses.text: THROUGH desire a man, having separated himself, seeketh <hi type="italic">and</hi> intermeddleth with all wisdom.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:2
verses.text: A fool hath no delight in understanding, but that his heart may discover itself.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:3
verses.text: When the wicked cometh, <hi type="italic">then</hi> cometh also contempt, and with ignominy reproach.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:4
verses.text: The words of a man’s mouth <hi type="italic">are as</hi> deep waters, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the wellspring of wisdom <hi type="italic">as</hi> a flowing brook.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:5
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> not good to accept the person of the wicked, to overthrow the righteous in judgment.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:6
verses.text: A fool’s lips enter into contention, and his mouth calleth for strokes.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:7
verses.text: A fool’s mouth <hi type="italic">is</hi> his destruction, and his lips <hi type="italic">are</hi> the snare of his soul.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:8
verses.text: The words of a talebearer <hi type="italic">are</hi> as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:9
verses.text: He also that is slothful in his work is brother to him that is a great waster.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:10
verses.text: The name of the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:11
verses.text: The rich man’s wealth <hi type="italic">is</hi> his strong city, and as an high wall in his own conceit.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:12
verses.text: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour <hi type="italic">is</hi> humility.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:13
verses.text: He that answereth a matter before he heareth <hi type="italic">it</hi>, it <hi type="italic">is</hi> folly and shame unto him.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:14
verses.text: The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; but a wounded spirit who can bear?

verses.name: Proverbs 18:15
verses.text: The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; and the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:16
verses.text: A man’s gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:17
verses.text: <hi type="italic">He that is</hi> first in his own cause <hi type="italic">seemeth</hi> just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:18
verses.text: The lot causeth contentions to cease, and parteth between the mighty.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:19
verses.text: A brother offended <hi type="italic">is harder to be won</hi> than a strong city: and <hi type="italic">their</hi> contentions <hi type="italic">are</hi> like the bars of a castle.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:20
verses.text: A man’s belly shall be satisfied with the fruit of his mouth; <hi type="italic">and</hi> with the increase of his lips shall he be filled.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:21
verses.text: Death and life <hi type="italic">are</hi> in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:22
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Whoso</hi> findeth a wife findeth a good <hi type="italic">thing</hi>, and obtaineth favour of the Lord.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:23
verses.text: The poor useth intreaties; but the rich answereth roughly.

verses.name: Proverbs 18:24
verses.text: A man <hi type="italic">that hath</hi> friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend <hi type="italic">that</hi> sticketh closer than a brother.  <chapter eID="Prov.18"/><div eID="gen710" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 19:1
verses.text: BETTER <hi type="italic">is</hi> the poor that walketh in his integrity, than <hi type="italic">he that is</hi> perverse in his lips, and is a fool.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:2
verses.text: Also, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the soul <hi type="italic">be</hi> without knowledge, <hi type="italic">it is</hi> not good; and he that hasteth with <hi type="italic">his</hi> feet sinneth.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:3
verses.text: The foolishness of man perverteth his way: and his heart fretteth against the Lord.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:4
verses.text: Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:5
verses.text: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and <hi type="italic">he that</hi> speaketh lies shall not escape.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:6
verses.text: Many will intreat the favour of the prince: and every man <hi type="italic">is</hi> a friend to him that giveth gifts.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:7
verses.text: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth <hi type="italic">them with</hi> words, <hi type="italic">yet</hi> they <hi type="italic">are</hi> wanting <hi type="italic">to him</hi>.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:8
verses.text: He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: he that keepeth understanding shall find good.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:9
verses.text: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and <hi type="italic">he that</hi> speaketh lies shall perish.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:10
verses.text: Delight is not seemly for a fool; much less for a servant to have rule over princes.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:11
verses.text: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and <hi type="italic">it is</hi> his glory to pass over a transgression.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:12
verses.text: The king’s wrath <hi type="italic">is</hi> as the roaring of a lion; but his favour <hi type="italic">is</hi> as dew upon the grass.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:13
verses.text: A foolish son <hi type="italic">is</hi> the calamity of his father: and the contentions of a wife <hi type="italic">are</hi> a continual dropping.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:14
verses.text: House and riches <hi type="italic">are</hi> the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife <hi type="italic">is</hi> from the Lord.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:15
verses.text: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; and an idle soul shall suffer hunger.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:16
verses.text: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; <hi type="italic">but</hi> he that despiseth his ways shall die.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:17
verses.text: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:18
verses.text: Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:19
verses.text: A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment: for if thou deliver <hi type="italic">him</hi>, yet thou must do it again.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:20
verses.text: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:21
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There are</hi> many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of the Lord, that shall stand.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:22
verses.text: The desire of a man <hi type="italic">is</hi> his kindness: and a poor man <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than a liar.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:23
verses.text: The fear of the Lord <hi type="italic">tendeth</hi> to life: and <hi type="italic">he that hath it</hi> shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:24
verses.text: A slothful <hi type="italic">man</hi> hideth his hand in <hi type="italic">his</hi> bosom, and will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:25
verses.text: Smite a scorner, and the simple will beware: and reprove one that hath understanding, <hi type="italic">and</hi> he will understand knowledge.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:26
verses.text: He that wasteth <hi type="italic">his</hi> father, <hi type="italic">and</hi> chaseth away <hi type="italic">his</hi> mother, <hi type="italic">is</hi> a son that causeth shame, and bringeth reproach.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:27
verses.text: Cease, my son, to hear the instruction <hi type="italic">that causeth</hi> to err from the words of knowledge.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:28
verses.text: An ungodly witness scorneth judgment: and the mouth of the wicked devoureth iniquity.

verses.name: Proverbs 19:29
verses.text: Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of fools.  <chapter eID="Prov.19"/><div eID="gen711" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 20:1
verses.text: WINE <hi type="italic">is</hi> a mocker, strong drink <hi type="italic">is</hi> raging: and whosoever is deceived thereby is not wise.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:2
verses.text: The fear of a king <hi type="italic">is</hi> as the roaring of a lion: <hi type="italic">whoso</hi> provoketh him to anger sinneth <hi type="italic">against</hi> his own soul.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:3
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:4
verses.text: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the cold; <hi type="italic">therefore</hi> shall he beg in harvest, and <hi type="italic">have</hi> nothing.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:5
verses.text: Counsel in the heart of man <hi type="italic">is like</hi> deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:6
verses.text: Most men will proclaim every one his own goodness: but a faithful man who can find?

verses.name: Proverbs 20:7
verses.text: The just <hi type="italic">man</hi> walketh in his integrity: his children <hi type="italic">are</hi> blessed after him.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:8
verses.text: A king that sitteth in the throne of judgment scattereth away all evil with his eyes.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:9
verses.text: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?

verses.name: Proverbs 20:10
verses.text: Divers weights, <hi type="italic">and</hi> divers measures, both of them <hi type="italic">are</hi> alike abomination to the Lord.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:11
verses.text: Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work <hi type="italic">be</hi> pure, and whether <hi type="italic">it be</hi> right.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:12
verses.text: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the Lord hath made even both of them.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:13
verses.text: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thine eyes, <hi type="italic">and</hi> thou shalt be satisfied with bread.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:14
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> naught, <hi type="italic">it is</hi> naught, saith the buyer: but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:15
verses.text: There is gold, and a multitude of rubies: but the lips of knowledge <hi type="italic">are</hi> a precious jewel.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:16
verses.text: Take his garment that is surety <hi type="italic">for</hi> a stranger: and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:17
verses.text: Bread of deceit <hi type="italic">is</hi> sweet to a man; but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:18
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Every</hi> purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:19
verses.text: He that goeth about <hi type="italic">as</hi> a talebearer revealeth secrets: therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:20
verses.text: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in obscure darkness.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:21
verses.text: An inheritance <hi type="italic">may be</hi> gotten hastily at the beginning; but the end thereof shall not be blessed.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:22
verses.text: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; <hi type="italic">but</hi> wait on the Lord, and he shall save thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:23
verses.text: Divers weights <hi type="italic">are</hi> an abomination unto the Lord; and a false balance <hi type="italic">is</hi> not good.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:24
verses.text: Man’s goings <hi type="italic">are</hi> of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?

verses.name: Proverbs 20:25
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> a snare to the man <hi type="italic">who</hi> devoureth <hi type="italic">that which is</hi> holy, and after vows to make inquiry.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:26
verses.text: A wise king scattereth the wicked, and bringeth the wheel over them.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:27
verses.text: The spirit of man <hi type="italic">is</hi> the candle of the Lord, searching all the inward parts of the belly.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:28
verses.text: Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:29
verses.text: The glory of young men <hi type="italic">is</hi> their strength: and the beauty of old men <hi type="italic">is</hi> the gray head.

verses.name: Proverbs 20:30
verses.text: The blueness of a wound cleanseth away evil: so <hi type="italic">do</hi> stripes the inward parts of the belly.  <chapter eID="Prov.20"/><div eID="gen712" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 21:1
verses.text: THE king’s heart <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the hand of the Lord, <hi type="italic">as</hi> the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:2
verses.text: Every way of a man <hi type="italic">is</hi> right in his own eyes: but the Lord pondereth the hearts.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:3
verses.text: To do justice and judgment <hi type="italic">is</hi> more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:4
verses.text: An high look, and a proud heart, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the plowing of the wicked, <hi type="italic">is</hi> sin.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:5
verses.text: The thoughts of the diligent <hi type="italic">tend</hi> only to plenteousness; but of every one <hi type="italic">that is</hi> hasty only to want.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:6
verses.text: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue <hi type="italic">is</hi> a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:7
verses.text: The robbery of the wicked shall destroy them; because they refuse to do judgment.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:8
verses.text: The way of man <hi type="italic">is</hi> froward and strange: but <hi type="italic">as for</hi> the pure, his work <hi type="italic">is</hi> right.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:9
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:10
verses.text: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: his neighbour findeth no favour in his eyes.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:11
verses.text: When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise: and when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:12
verses.text: The righteous <hi type="italic">man</hi> wisely considereth the house of the wicked: <hi type="italic">but God</hi> overthroweth the wicked for <hi type="italic">their</hi> wickedness.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:13
verses.text: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:14
verses.text: A gift in secret pacifieth anger: and a reward in the bosom strong wrath.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:15
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> joy to the just to do judgment: but destruction <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> to the workers of iniquity.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:16
verses.text: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:17
verses.text: He that loveth pleasure <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> a poor man: he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:18
verses.text: The wicked <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:19
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:20
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:21
verses.text: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:22
verses.text: A wise <hi type="italic">man</hi> scaleth the city of the mighty, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:23
verses.text: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:24
verses.text: Proud <hi type="italic">and</hi> haughty scorner <hi type="italic">is</hi> his name, who dealeth in proud wrath.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:25
verses.text: The desire of the slothful killeth him; for his hands refuse to labour.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:26
verses.text: He coveteth greedily all the day long: but the righteous giveth and spareth not.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:27
verses.text: The sacrifice of the wicked <hi type="italic">is</hi> abomination: how much more, <hi type="italic">when</hi> he bringeth it with a wicked mind?

verses.name: Proverbs 21:28
verses.text: A false witness shall perish: but the man that heareth speaketh constantly.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:29
verses.text: A wicked man hardeneth his face: but <hi type="italic">as for</hi> the upright, he directeth his way.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:30
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the Lord.

verses.name: Proverbs 21:31
verses.text: The horse <hi type="italic">is</hi> prepared against the day of battle: but safety <hi type="italic">is</hi> of the Lord.  <chapter eID="Prov.21"/><div eID="gen713" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 22:1
verses.text: A <hi type="italic">GOOD</hi> name <hi type="italic">is</hi> rather to be chosen than great riches, <hi type="italic">and</hi> loving favour rather than silver and gold.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:2
verses.text: The rich and poor meet together: the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> the maker of them all.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:3
verses.text: A prudent <hi type="italic">man</hi> foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:4
verses.text: By humility <hi type="italic">and</hi> the fear of the Lord <hi type="italic">are</hi> riches, and honour, and life.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:5
verses.text: Thorns <hi type="italic">and</hi> snares <hi type="italic">are</hi> in the way of the froward: he that doth keep his soul shall be far from them.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:6
verses.text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:7
verses.text: The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower <hi type="italic">is</hi> servant to the lender.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:8
verses.text: He that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity: and the rod of his anger shall fail.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:9
verses.text: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:10
verses.text: Cast out the scorner, and contention shall go out; yea, strife and reproach shall cease.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:11
verses.text: He that loveth pureness of heart, <hi type="italic">for</hi> the grace of his lips the king <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> his friend.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:12
verses.text: The eyes of the Lord preserve knowledge, and he overthroweth the words of the transgressor.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:13
verses.text: The slothful <hi type="italic">man</hi> saith, <hi type="italic">There is</hi> a lion without, I shall be slain in the streets.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:14
verses.text: The mouth of strange women <hi type="italic">is</hi> a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the Lord shall fall therein.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:15
verses.text: Foolishness <hi type="italic">is</hi> bound in the heart of a child; <hi type="italic">but</hi> the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:16
verses.text: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his <hi type="italic">riches</hi>, <hi type="italic">and</hi> he that giveth to the rich, <hi type="italic">shall</hi> surely <hi type="italic">come</hi> to want.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:17
verses.text: Bow down thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply thine heart unto my knowledge.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:18
verses.text: For <hi type="italic">it is</hi> a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee; they shall withal be fitted in thy lips.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:19
verses.text: That thy trust may be in the Lord, I have made known to thee this day, even to thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:20
verses.text: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge,

verses.name: Proverbs 22:21
verses.text: That I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth; that thou mightest answer the words of truth to them that send unto thee?

verses.name: Proverbs 22:22
verses.text: Rob not the poor, because he <hi type="italic">is</hi> poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:

verses.name: Proverbs 22:23
verses.text: For the Lord will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:24
verses.text: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go:

verses.name: Proverbs 22:25
verses.text: Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:26
verses.text: Be not thou <hi type="italic">one</hi> of them that strike hands, <hi type="italic">or</hi> of them that are sureties for debts.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:27
verses.text: If thou hast nothing to pay, why should he take away thy bed from under thee?

verses.name: Proverbs 22:28
verses.text: Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set.

verses.name: Proverbs 22:29
verses.text: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean <hi type="italic">men</hi>.  <chapter eID="Prov.22"/><div eID="gen714" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 23:1
verses.text: WHEN thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what <hi type="italic">is</hi> before thee:

verses.name: Proverbs 23:2
verses.text: And put a knife to thy throat, if thou <hi type="italic">be</hi> a man given to appetite.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:3
verses.text: Be not desirous of his dainties: for they <hi type="italic">are</hi> deceitful meat.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:4
verses.text: Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:5
verses.text: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? for <hi type="italic">riches</hi> certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:6
verses.text: Eat thou not the bread of <hi type="italic">him that hath</hi> an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:

verses.name: Proverbs 23:7
verses.text: For as he thinketh in his heart, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; but his heart <hi type="italic">is</hi> not with thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:8
verses.text: The morsel <hi type="italic">which</hi> thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, and lose thy sweet words.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:9
verses.text: Speak not in the ears of a fool: for he will despise the wisdom of thy words.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:10
verses.text: Remove not the old landmark; and enter not into the fields of the fatherless:

verses.name: Proverbs 23:11
verses.text: For their redeemer <hi type="italic">is</hi> mighty; he shall plead their cause with thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:12
verses.text: Apply thine heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:13
verses.text: Withhold not correction from the child: for <hi type="italic">if</hi> thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:14
verses.text: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:15
verses.text: My son, if thine heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:16
verses.text: Yea, my reins shall rejoice, when thy lips speak right things.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:17
verses.text: Let not thine heart envy sinners: but <hi type="italic">be thou</hi> in the fear of the Lord all the day long.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:18
verses.text: For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:19
verses.text: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:20
verses.text: Be not among winebibbers; among riotous eaters of flesh:

verses.name: Proverbs 23:21
verses.text: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe <hi type="italic">a man</hi> with rags.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:22
verses.text: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:23
verses.text: Buy the truth, and sell <hi type="italic">it</hi> not; <hi type="italic">also</hi> wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:24
verses.text: The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice: and he that begetteth a wise <hi type="italic">child</hi> shall have joy of him.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:25
verses.text: Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:26
verses.text: My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:27
verses.text: For a whore <hi type="italic">is</hi> a deep ditch; and a strange woman <hi type="italic">is</hi> a narrow pit.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:28
verses.text: She also lieth in wait as <hi type="italic">for</hi> a prey, and increaseth the transgressors among men.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:29
verses.text: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? who hath babbling? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?

verses.name: Proverbs 23:30
verses.text: They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to seek mixed wine.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:31
verses.text: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, <hi type="italic">when</hi> it moveth itself aright.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:32
verses.text: At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:33
verses.text: Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:34
verses.text: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.

verses.name: Proverbs 23:35
verses.text: They have stricken me, <hi type="italic">shalt thou say</hi>, <hi type="italic">and</hi> I was not sick; they have beaten me, <hi type="italic">and</hi> I felt <hi type="italic">it</hi> not: when shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.  <chapter eID="Prov.23"/><div eID="gen715" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 24:1
verses.text: BE not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:2
verses.text: For their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:3
verses.text: Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established:

verses.name: Proverbs 24:4
verses.text: And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:5
verses.text: A wise man <hi type="italic">is</hi> strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:6
verses.text: For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellers <hi type="italic">there is</hi> safety.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:7
verses.text: Wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:8
verses.text: He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a mischievous person.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:9
verses.text: The thought of foolishness <hi type="italic">is</hi> sin: and the scorner <hi type="italic">is</hi> an abomination to men.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:10
verses.text: <hi type="italic">If</hi> thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength <hi type="italic">is</hi> small.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:11
verses.text: If thou forbear to deliver <hi type="italic">them that are</hi> drawn unto death, and <hi type="italic">those that are</hi> ready to be slain;

verses.name: Proverbs 24:12
verses.text: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider <hi type="italic">it?</hi> and he that keepeth thy soul, doth <hi type="italic">not</hi> he know <hi type="italic">it?</hi> and shall <hi type="italic">not</hi> he render to <hi type="italic">every</hi> man according to his works?

verses.name: Proverbs 24:13
verses.text: My son, eat thou honey, because <hi type="italic">it is</hi> good; and the honeycomb, <hi type="italic">which is</hi> sweet to thy taste:

verses.name: Proverbs 24:14
verses.text: So <hi type="italic">shall</hi> the knowledge of wisdom <hi type="italic">be</hi> unto thy soul: when thou hast found <hi type="italic">it</hi>, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:15
verses.text: Lay not wait, O wicked <hi type="italic">man</hi>, against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place:

verses.name: Proverbs 24:16
verses.text: For a just <hi type="italic">man</hi> falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:17
verses.text: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:

verses.name: Proverbs 24:18
verses.text: Lest the Lord see <hi type="italic">it</hi>, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:19
verses.text: Fret not thyself because of evil <hi type="italic">men</hi>, neither be thou envious at the wicked;

verses.name: Proverbs 24:20
verses.text: For there shall be no reward to the evil <hi type="italic">man;</hi> the candle of the wicked shall be put out.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:21
verses.text: My son, fear thou the Lord and the king: <hi type="italic">and</hi> meddle not with them that are given to change:

verses.name: Proverbs 24:22
verses.text: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?

verses.name: Proverbs 24:23
verses.text: These <hi type="italic">things</hi> also <hi type="italic">belong</hi> to the wise. <hi type="italic">It is</hi> not good to have respect of persons in judgment.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:24
verses.text: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him:

verses.name: Proverbs 24:25
verses.text: But to them that rebuke <hi type="italic">him</hi> shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:26
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Every man</hi> shall kiss <hi type="italic">his</hi> lips that giveth a right answer.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:27
verses.text: Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:28
verses.text: Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive <hi type="italic">not</hi> with thy lips.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:29
verses.text: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me: I will render to the man according to his work.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:30
verses.text: I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;

verses.name: Proverbs 24:31
verses.text: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, <hi type="italic">and</hi> nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:32
verses.text: Then I saw, <hi type="italic">and</hi> considered <hi type="italic">it</hi> well: I looked upon <hi type="italic">it</hi>, <hi type="italic">and</hi> received instruction.

verses.name: Proverbs 24:33
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Yet</hi> a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:

verses.name: Proverbs 24:34
verses.text: So shall thy poverty come <hi type="italic">as</hi> one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.  <chapter eID="Prov.24"/><div eID="gen716" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:1
verses.text: THESE <hi type="italic">are</hi> also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:2
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings <hi type="italic">is</hi> to search out a matter.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:3
verses.text: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings <hi type="italic">is</hi> unsearchable.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:4
verses.text: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:5
verses.text: Take away the wicked <hi type="italic">from</hi> before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:6
verses.text: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great <hi type="italic">men:</hi>

verses.name: Proverbs 25:7
verses.text: For better <hi type="italic">it is</hi> that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:8
verses.text: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest <hi type="italic">thou know not</hi> what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:9
verses.text: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour <hi type="italic">himself;</hi> and discover not a secret to another:

verses.name: Proverbs 25:10
verses.text: Lest he that heareth <hi type="italic">it</hi> put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:11
verses.text: A word fitly spoken <hi type="italic">is like</hi> apples of gold in pictures of silver.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:12
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, <hi type="italic">so is</hi> a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:13
verses.text: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, <hi type="italic">so is</hi> a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:14
verses.text: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift <hi type="italic">is like</hi> clouds and wind without rain.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:15
verses.text: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:16
verses.text: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:17
verses.text: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour’s house; lest he be weary of thee, and <hi type="italic">so</hi> hate thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:18
verses.text: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour <hi type="italic">is</hi> a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:19
verses.text: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble <hi type="italic">is like</hi> a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:20
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, <hi type="italic">and as</hi> vinegar upon nitre, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:21
verses.text: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

verses.name: Proverbs 25:22
verses.text: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:23
verses.text: The north wind driveth away rain: so <hi type="italic">doth</hi> an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:24
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:25
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> cold waters to a thirsty soul, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> good news from a far country.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:26
verses.text: A righteous man falling down before the wicked <hi type="italic">is as</hi> a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:27
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> not good to eat much honey: so <hi type="italic">for men</hi> to search their own glory <hi type="italic">is not</hi> glory.

verses.name: Proverbs 25:28
verses.text: He that <hi type="italic">hath</hi> no rule over his own spirit <hi type="italic">is like</hi> a city <hi type="italic">that is</hi> broken down, <hi type="italic">and</hi> without walls.  <chapter eID="Prov.25"/><div eID="gen717" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 26:1
verses.text: AS snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:2
verses.text: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:3
verses.text: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool’s back.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:4
verses.text: Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:5
verses.text: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:6
verses.text: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet, <hi type="italic">and</hi> drinketh damage.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:7
verses.text: The legs of the lame are not equal: so <hi type="italic">is</hi> a parable in the mouth of fools.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:8
verses.text: As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> he that giveth honour to a fool.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:9
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> a parable in the mouth of fools.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:10
verses.text: The great <hi type="italic">God</hi> that formed all <hi type="italic">things</hi> both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:11
verses.text: As a dog returneth to his vomit, <hi type="italic">so</hi> a fool returneth to his folly.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:12
verses.text: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? <hi type="italic">there is</hi> more hope of a fool than of him.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:13
verses.text: The slothful <hi type="italic">man</hi> saith, <hi type="italic">There is</hi> a lion in the way; a lion <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the streets.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:14
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> the door turneth upon his hinges, so <hi type="italic">doth</hi> the slothful upon his bed.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:15
verses.text: The slothful hideth his hand in <hi type="italic">his</hi> bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:16
verses.text: The sluggard <hi type="italic">is</hi> wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:17
verses.text: He that passeth by, <hi type="italic">and</hi> meddleth with strife <hi type="italic">belonging</hi> not to him, <hi type="italic">is like</hi> one that taketh a dog by the ears.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:18
verses.text: As a mad <hi type="italic">man</hi> who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death,

verses.name: Proverbs 26:19
verses.text: So <hi type="italic">is</hi> the man <hi type="italic">that</hi> deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport?

verses.name: Proverbs 26:20
verses.text: Where no wood is, <hi type="italic">there</hi> the fire goeth out: so where <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:21
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> coals <hi type="italic">are</hi> to burning coals, and wood to fire; so <hi type="italic">is</hi> a contentious man to kindle strife.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:22
verses.text: The words of a talebearer <hi type="italic">are</hi> as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:23
verses.text: Burning lips and a wicked heart <hi type="italic">are like</hi> a potsherd covered with silver dross.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:24
verses.text: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;

verses.name: Proverbs 26:25
verses.text: When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for <hi type="italic">there are</hi> seven abominations in his heart.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:26
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Whose</hi> hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the <hi type="italic">whole</hi> congregation.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:27
verses.text: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.

verses.name: Proverbs 26:28
verses.text: A lying tongue hateth <hi type="italic">those that are</hi> afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.  <chapter eID="Prov.26"/><div eID="gen718" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 27:1
verses.text: BOAST not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:2
verses.text: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:3
verses.text: A stone <hi type="italic">is</hi> heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool’s wrath <hi type="italic">is</hi> heavier than them both.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:4
verses.text: Wrath <hi type="italic">is</hi> cruel, and anger <hi type="italic">is</hi> outrageous; but who <hi type="italic">is</hi> able to stand before envy?

verses.name: Proverbs 27:5
verses.text: Open rebuke <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than secret love.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:6
verses.text: Faithful <hi type="italic">are</hi> the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy <hi type="italic">are</hi> deceitful.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:7
verses.text: The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:8
verses.text: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> a man that wandereth from his place.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:9
verses.text: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so <hi type="italic">doth</hi> the sweetness of a man’s friend by hearty counsel.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:10
verses.text: Thine own friend, and thy father’s friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother’s house in the day of thy calamity: <hi type="italic">for</hi> better <hi type="italic">is</hi> a neighbour <hi type="italic">that is</hi> near than a brother far off.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:11
verses.text: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:12
verses.text: A prudent <hi type="italic">man</hi> foreseeth the evil, <hi type="italic">and</hi> hideth himself; <hi type="italic">but</hi> the simple pass on, <hi type="italic">and</hi> are punished.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:13
verses.text: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:14
verses.text: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:15
verses.text: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:16
verses.text: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, <hi type="italic">which</hi> bewrayeth <hi type="italic">itself</hi>.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:17
verses.text: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:18
verses.text: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:19
verses.text: As in water face <hi type="italic">answereth</hi> to face, so the heart of man to man.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:20
verses.text: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:21
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so <hi type="italic">is</hi> a man to his praise.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:22
verses.text: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, <hi type="italic">yet</hi> will not his foolishness depart from him.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:23
verses.text: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, <hi type="italic">and</hi> look well to thy herds.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:24
verses.text: For riches <hi type="italic">are</hi> not for ever: and doth the crown <hi type="italic">endure</hi> to every generation?

verses.name: Proverbs 27:25
verses.text: The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:26
verses.text: The lambs <hi type="italic">are</hi> for thy clothing, and the goats <hi type="italic">are</hi> the price of the field.

verses.name: Proverbs 27:27
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">thou shalt have</hi> goats’ milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and <hi type="italic">for</hi> the maintenance for thy maidens.  <chapter eID="Prov.27"/><div eID="gen719" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 28:1
verses.text: THE wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:2
verses.text: For the transgression of a land many <hi type="italic">are</hi> the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding <hi type="italic">and</hi> knowledge the state <hi type="italic">thereof</hi> shall be prolonged.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:3
verses.text: A poor man that oppresseth the poor <hi type="italic">is like</hi> a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:4
verses.text: They that forsake the law praise the wicked: but such as keep the law contend with them.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:5
verses.text: Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the Lord understand all <hi type="italic">things</hi>.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:6
verses.text: Better <hi type="italic">is</hi> the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than <hi type="italic">he that is</hi> perverse <hi type="italic">in his</hi> ways, though he <hi type="italic">be</hi> rich.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:7
verses.text: Whoso keepeth the law <hi type="italic">is</hi> a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous <hi type="italic">men</hi> shameth his father.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:8
verses.text: He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:9
verses.text: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> abomination.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:10
verses.text: Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good <hi type="italic">things</hi> in possession.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:11
verses.text: The rich man <hi type="italic">is</hi> wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:12
verses.text: When righteous <hi type="italic">men</hi> do rejoice, <hi type="italic">there is</hi> great glory: but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:13
verses.text: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh <hi type="italic">them</hi> shall have mercy.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:14
verses.text: Happy <hi type="italic">is</hi> the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:15
verses.text: <hi type="italic">As</hi> a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; <hi type="italic">so is</hi> a wicked ruler over the poor people.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:16
verses.text: The prince that wanteth understanding <hi type="italic">is</hi> also a great oppressor: <hi type="italic">but</hi> he that hateth covetousness shall prolong <hi type="italic">his</hi> days.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:17
verses.text: A man that doeth violence to the blood of <hi type="italic">any</hi> person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:18
verses.text: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but <hi type="italic">he that is</hi> perverse <hi type="italic">in his</hi> ways shall fall at once.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:19
verses.text: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain <hi type="italic">persons</hi> shall have poverty enough.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:20
verses.text: A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:21
verses.text: To have respect of persons <hi type="italic">is</hi> not good: for for a piece of bread <hi type="italic">that</hi> man will transgress.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:22
verses.text: He that hasteth to be rich <hi type="italic">hath</hi> an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:23
verses.text: He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour than he that flattereth with the tongue.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:24
verses.text: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, <hi type="italic">It is</hi> no transgression; the same <hi type="italic">is</hi> the companion of a destroyer.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:25
verses.text: He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the Lord shall be made fat.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:26
verses.text: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:27
verses.text: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.

verses.name: Proverbs 28:28
verses.text: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase.  <chapter eID="Prov.28"/><div eID="gen720" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 29:1
verses.text: HE, that being often reproved hardeneth <hi type="italic">his</hi> neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:2
verses.text: When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:3
verses.text: Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father: but he that keepeth company with harlots spendeth <hi type="italic">his</hi> substance.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:4
verses.text: The king by judgment establisheth the land: but he that receiveth gifts overthroweth it.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:5
verses.text: A man that flattereth his neighbour spreadeth a net for his feet.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:6
verses.text: In the transgression of an evil man <hi type="italic">there is</hi> a snare: but the righteous doth sing and rejoice.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:7
verses.text: The righteous considereth the cause of the poor: <hi type="italic">but</hi> the wicked regardeth not to know <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:8
verses.text: Scornful men bring a city into a snare: but wise <hi type="italic">men</hi> turn away wrath.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:9
verses.text: <hi type="italic">If</hi> a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no rest.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:10
verses.text: The bloodthirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:11
verses.text: A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise <hi type="italic">man</hi> keepeth it in till afterwards.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:12
verses.text: If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants <hi type="italic">are</hi> wicked.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:13
verses.text: The poor and the deceitful man meet together: the Lord lighteneth both their eyes.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:14
verses.text: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:15
verses.text: The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left <hi type="italic">to himself</hi> bringeth his mother to shame.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:16
verses.text: When the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth: but the righteous shall see their fall.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:17
verses.text: Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:18
verses.text: Where <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy <hi type="italic">is</hi> he.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:19
verses.text: A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understand he will not answer.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:20
verses.text: Seest thou a man <hi type="italic">that is</hi> hasty in his words? <hi type="italic">there is</hi> more hope of a fool than of him.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:21
verses.text: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become <hi type="italic">his</hi> son at the length.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:22
verses.text: An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:23
verses.text: A man’s pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:24
verses.text: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth <hi type="italic">it</hi> not.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:25
verses.text: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:26
verses.text: Many seek the ruler’s favour; but <hi type="italic">every</hi> man’s judgment <hi type="italic">cometh</hi> from the Lord.

verses.name: Proverbs 29:27
verses.text: An unjust man <hi type="italic">is</hi> an abomination to the just: and <hi type="italic">he that is</hi> upright in the way <hi type="italic">is</hi> abomination to the wicked.  <chapter eID="Prov.29"/><div eID="gen721" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 30:1
verses.text: THE words of Agur the son of Jakeh, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal,

verses.name: Proverbs 30:2
verses.text: Surely I <hi type="italic">am</hi> more brutish than <hi type="italic">any</hi> man, and have not the understanding of a man.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:3
verses.text: I neither learned wisdom, nor have the knowledge of the holy.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:4
verses.text: Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what <hi type="italic">is</hi> his name, and what <hi type="italic">is</hi> his son’s name, if thou canst tell?

verses.name: Proverbs 30:5
verses.text: Every word of God <hi type="italic">is</hi> pure: he <hi type="italic">is</hi> a shield unto them that put their trust in him.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:6
verses.text: Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:7
verses.text: Two <hi type="italic">things</hi> have I required of thee; deny me <hi type="italic">them</hi> not before I die:

verses.name: Proverbs 30:8
verses.text: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me:

verses.name: Proverbs 30:9
verses.text: Lest I be full, and deny <hi type="italic">thee</hi>, and say, Who <hi type="italic">is</hi> the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God <hi type="italic">in vain</hi>.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:10
verses.text: Accuse not a servant unto his master, lest he curse thee, and thou be found guilty.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:11
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> a generation <hi type="italic">that</hi> curseth their father, and doth not bless their mother.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:12
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> a generation <hi type="italic">that are</hi> pure in their own eyes, and <hi type="italic">yet</hi> is not washed from their filthiness.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:13
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> a generation, O how lofty are their eyes! and their eyelids are lifted up.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:14
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> a generation, whose teeth <hi type="italic">are as</hi> swords, and their jaw teeth <hi type="italic">as</hi> knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from <hi type="italic">among</hi> men.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:15
verses.text: The horseleach hath two daughters, <hi type="italic">crying</hi>, Give, give. There are three <hi type="italic">things that</hi> are never satisfied, <hi type="italic">yea</hi>, four <hi type="italic">things</hi> say not, <hi type="italic">It is</hi> enough:

verses.name: Proverbs 30:16
verses.text: The grave; and the barren womb; the earth <hi type="italic">that</hi> is not filled with water; and the fire <hi type="italic">that</hi> saith not, <hi type="italic">It is</hi> enough.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:17
verses.text: The eye <hi type="italic">that</hi> mocketh at <hi type="italic">his</hi> father, and despiseth to obey <hi type="italic">his</hi> mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:18
verses.text: There be three <hi type="italic">things which</hi> are too wonderful for me, yea, four which I know not:

verses.name: Proverbs 30:19
verses.text: The way of an eagle in the air; the way of a serpent upon a rock; the way of a ship in the midst of the sea; and the way of a man with a maid.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:20
verses.text: Such <hi type="italic">is</hi> the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:21
verses.text: For three <hi type="italic">things</hi> the earth is disquieted, and for four <hi type="italic">which</hi> it cannot bear:

verses.name: Proverbs 30:22
verses.text: For a servant when he reigneth; and a fool when he is filled with meat;

verses.name: Proverbs 30:23
verses.text: For an odious <hi type="italic">woman</hi> when she is married; and an handmaid that is heir to her mistress.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:24
verses.text: There be four <hi type="italic">things which are</hi> little upon the earth, but they <hi type="italic">are</hi> exceeding wise:

verses.name: Proverbs 30:25
verses.text: The ants <hi type="italic">are</hi> a people not strong, yet they prepare their meat in the summer;

verses.name: Proverbs 30:26
verses.text: The conies <hi type="italic">are but</hi> a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks;

verses.name: Proverbs 30:27
verses.text: The locusts have no king, yet go they forth all of them by bands;

verses.name: Proverbs 30:28
verses.text: The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings’ palaces.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:29
verses.text: There be three <hi type="italic">things</hi> which go well, yea, four are comely in going:

verses.name: Proverbs 30:30
verses.text: A lion <hi type="italic">which is</hi> strongest among beasts, and turneth not away for any;

verses.name: Proverbs 30:31
verses.text: A greyhound; an he goat also; and a king, against whom <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no rising up.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:32
verses.text: If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, or if thou hast thought evil, <hi type="italic">lay</hi> thine hand upon thy mouth.

verses.name: Proverbs 30:33
verses.text: Surely the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, and the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood: so the forcing of wrath bringeth forth strife.  <chapter eID="Prov.30"/><div eID="gen722" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Proverbs 31:1
verses.text: THE words of king Lemuel, the prophecy that his mother taught him.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:2
verses.text: What, my son? and what, the son of my womb? and what, the son of my vows?

verses.name: Proverbs 31:3
verses.text: Give not thy strength unto women, nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:4
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> not for kings, O Lemuel, <hi type="italic">it is</hi> not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink:

verses.name: Proverbs 31:5
verses.text: Lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:6
verses.text: Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, and wine unto those that be of heavy hearts.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:7
verses.text: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:8
verses.text: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:9
verses.text: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:10
verses.text: ¶ Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price <hi type="italic">is</hi> far above rubies.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:11
verses.text: The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:12
verses.text: She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:13
verses.text: She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:14
verses.text: She is like the merchants’ ships; she bringeth her food from afar.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:15
verses.text: She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:16
