verses.text: She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:17
verses.text: She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:18
verses.text: She perceiveth that her merchandise <hi type="italic">is</hi> good: her candle goeth not out by night.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:19
verses.text: She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:20
verses.text: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:21
verses.text: She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household <hi type="italic">are</hi> clothed with scarlet.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:22
verses.text: She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing <hi type="italic">is</hi> silk and purple.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:23
verses.text: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:24
verses.text: She maketh fine linen, and selleth <hi type="italic">it;</hi> and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:25
verses.text: Strength and honour <hi type="italic">are</hi> her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:26
verses.text: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue <hi type="italic">is</hi> the law of kindness.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:27
verses.text: She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:28
verses.text: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband <hi type="italic">also</hi>, and he praiseth her.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:29
verses.text: Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:30
verses.text: Favour <hi type="italic">is</hi> deceitful, and beauty <hi type="italic">is</hi> vain: <hi type="italic">but</hi> a woman <hi type="italic">that</hi> feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.

verses.name: Proverbs 31:31
verses.text: Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.  <chapter eID="Prov.31"/><div eID="gen723" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen692" osisID="Prov" type="book"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:1
verses.text: THE words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:2
verses.text: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:3
verses.text: What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:4
verses.text: <hi type="italic">One</hi> generation passeth away, and <hi type="italic">another</hi> generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:5
verses.text: The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:6
verses.text: The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the north; it whirleth about continually, and the wind returneth again according to his circuits.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:7
verses.text: All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea <hi type="italic">is</hi> not full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:8
verses.text: All things <hi type="italic">are</hi> full of labour; man cannot utter <hi type="italic">it:</hi> the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:9
verses.text: The thing that hath been, it <hi type="italic">is that</hi> which shall be; and that which is done <hi type="italic">is</hi> that which shall be done: and <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no new <hi type="italic">thing</hi> under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:10
verses.text: Is there <hi type="italic">any</hi> thing whereof it may be said, See, this <hi type="italic">is</hi> new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:11
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> no remembrance of former <hi type="italic">things;</hi> neither shall there be <hi type="italic">any</hi> remembrance of <hi type="italic">things</hi> that are to come with <hi type="italic">those</hi> that shall come after.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:12
verses.text: ¶ I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:13
verses.text: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all <hi type="italic">things</hi> that are done under heaven: this sore travail hath God given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:14
verses.text: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:15
verses.text: <hi type="italic">That which is</hi> crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:16
verses.text: I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I am come to great estate, and have gotten more wisdom than all <hi type="italic">they</hi> that have been before me in Jerusalem: yea, my heart had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:17
verses.text: And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 1:18
verses.text: For in much wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.  <chapter eID="Eccl.1"/><div eID="gen725" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:1
verses.text: I SAID in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:2
verses.text: I said of laughter, <hi type="italic">It is</hi> mad: and of mirth, What doeth it?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:3
verses.text: I sought in mine heart to give myself unto wine, yet acquainting mine heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what <hi type="italic">was</hi> that good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:4
verses.text: I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:5
verses.text: I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all <hi type="italic">kind of</hi> fruits:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:6
verses.text: I made me pools of water, to water therewith the wood that bringeth forth trees:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:7
verses.text: I got <hi type="italic">me</hi> servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that were in Jerusalem before me:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:8
verses.text: I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces: I gat me men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men, <hi type="italic">as</hi> musical instruments, and that of all sorts.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:9
verses.text: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:10
verses.text: And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them, I withheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labour: and this was my portion of all my labour.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:11
verses.text: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all <hi type="italic">was</hi> vanity and vexation of spirit, and <hi type="italic">there was</hi> no profit under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:12
verses.text: ¶ And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what <hi type="italic">can</hi> the man <hi type="italic">do</hi> that cometh after the king? <hi type="italic">even</hi> that which hath been already done.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:13
verses.text: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:14
verses.text: The wise man’s eyes <hi type="italic">are</hi> in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:15
verses.text: Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:16
verses.text: For <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise <hi type="italic">man?</hi> as the fool.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:17
verses.text: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun <hi type="italic">is</hi> grievous unto me: for all <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:18
verses.text: ¶ Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:19
verses.text: And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise <hi type="italic">man</hi> or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This <hi type="italic">is</hi> also vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:20
verses.text: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour which I took under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:21
verses.text: For there is a man whose labour <hi type="italic">is</hi> in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it <hi type="italic">for</hi> his portion. This also <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity and a great evil.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:22
verses.text: For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:23
verses.text: For all his days <hi type="italic">are</hi> sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:24
verses.text: ¶ <hi type="italic">There is</hi> nothing better for a man, <hi type="italic">than</hi> that he should eat and drink, and <hi type="italic">that</hi> he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it <hi type="italic">was</hi> from the hand of God.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:25
verses.text: For who can eat, or who else can hasten <hi type="italic">hereunto</hi>, more than I?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 2:26
verses.text: For <hi type="italic">God</hi> giveth to a man that <hi type="italic">is</hi> good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to <hi type="italic">him that is</hi> good before God. This also <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity and vexation of spirit.  <chapter eID="Eccl.2"/><div eID="gen726" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:1
verses.text: TO every <hi type="italic">thing there is</hi> a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:2
verses.text: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up <hi type="italic">that which is</hi> planted;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:3
verses.text: A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:4
verses.text: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:5
verses.text: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:6
verses.text: A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:7
verses.text: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:8
verses.text: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:9
verses.text: What profit hath he that worketh in that wherein he laboureth?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:10
verses.text: I have seen the travail, which God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:11
verses.text: He hath made every <hi type="italic">thing</hi> beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:12
verses.text: I know that <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no good in them, but for <hi type="italic">a man</hi> to rejoice, and to do good in his life.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:13
verses.text: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it <hi type="italic">is</hi> the gift of God.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:14
verses.text: I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth <hi type="italic">it</hi>, that <hi type="italic">men</hi> should fear before him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:15
verses.text: That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:16
verses.text: ¶ And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, <hi type="italic">that</hi> wickedness <hi type="italic">was</hi> there; and the place of righteousness, <hi type="italic">that</hi> iniquity <hi type="italic">was</hi> there.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:17
verses.text: I said in mine heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for <hi type="italic">there is</hi> a time there for every purpose and for every work.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:18
verses.text: I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:19
verses.text: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:20
verses.text: All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:21
verses.text: Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 3:22
verses.text: Wherefore I perceive that <hi type="italic">there is</hi> nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that <hi type="italic">is</hi> his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?  <chapter eID="Eccl.3"/><div eID="gen727" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:1
verses.text: SO I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of <hi type="italic">such as were</hi> oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors <hi type="italic">there was</hi> power; but they had no comforter.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:2
verses.text: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:3
verses.text: Yea, better <hi type="italic">is he</hi> than both they, which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:4
verses.text: ¶ Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This <hi type="italic">is</hi> also vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:5
verses.text: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:6
verses.text: Better <hi type="italic">is</hi> an handful <hi type="italic">with</hi> quietness, than both the hands full <hi type="italic">with</hi> travail and vexation of spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:7
verses.text: ¶ Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:8
verses.text: There is one <hi type="italic">alone</hi>, and <hi type="italic">there is</hi> not a second; yea, he hath neither child nor brother: yet <hi type="italic">is there</hi> no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither <hi type="italic">saith he</hi>, For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This <hi type="italic">is</hi> also vanity, yea, it <hi type="italic">is</hi> a sore travail.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:9
verses.text: ¶ Two <hi type="italic">are</hi> better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:10
verses.text: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him <hi type="italic">that is</hi> alone when he falleth; for <hi type="italic">he hath</hi> not another to help him up.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:11
verses.text: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm <hi type="italic">alone?</hi>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:12
verses.text: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:13
verses.text: ¶ Better <hi type="italic">is</hi> a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:14
verses.text: For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also <hi type="italic">he that is</hi> born in his kingdom becometh poor.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:15
verses.text: I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 4:16
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> no end of all the people, <hi type="italic">even</hi> of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity and vexation of spirit.  <chapter eID="Eccl.4"/><div eID="gen728" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:1
verses.text: KEEP thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:2
verses.text: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter <hi type="italic">any</hi> thing before God: for God <hi type="italic">is</hi> in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:3
verses.text: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool’s voice <hi type="italic">is known</hi> by multitude of words.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:4
verses.text: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for <hi type="italic">he hath</hi> no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:5
verses.text: Better <hi type="italic">is it</hi> that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:6
verses.text: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it <hi type="italic">was</hi> an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:7
verses.text: For in the multitude of dreams and many words <hi type="italic">there are</hi> also <hi type="italic">divers</hi> vanities: but fear thou God.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:8
verses.text: ¶ If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for <hi type="italic">he that is</hi> higher than the highest regardeth; and <hi type="italic">there be</hi> higher than they.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:9
verses.text: ¶ Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king <hi type="italic">himself</hi> is served by the field.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:10
verses.text: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this <hi type="italic">is</hi> also vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:11
verses.text: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good <hi type="italic">is there</hi> to the owners thereof, saving the beholding <hi type="italic">of them</hi> with their eyes?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:12
verses.text: The sleep of a labouring man <hi type="italic">is</hi> sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:13
verses.text: There is a sore evil <hi type="italic">which</hi> I have seen under the sun, <hi type="italic">namely</hi>, riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:14
verses.text: But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and <hi type="italic">there is</hi> nothing in his hand.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:15
verses.text: As he came forth of his mother’s womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:16
verses.text: And this also <hi type="italic">is</hi> a sore evil, <hi type="italic">that</hi> in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that hath laboured for the wind?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:17
verses.text: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and <hi type="italic">he hath</hi> much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:18
verses.text: ¶ Behold <hi type="italic">that</hi> which I have seen: <hi type="italic">it is</hi> good and comely <hi type="italic">for one</hi> to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, which God giveth him: for it <hi type="italic">is</hi> his portion.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:19
verses.text: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this <hi type="italic">is</hi> the gift of God.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 5:20
verses.text: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth <hi type="italic">him</hi> in the joy of his heart.  <chapter eID="Eccl.5"/><div eID="gen729" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:1
verses.text: THERE is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it <hi type="italic">is</hi> common among men:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:2
verses.text: A man to whom God hath given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity, and it <hi type="italic">is</hi> an evil disease.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:3
verses.text: ¶ If a man beget an hundred <hi type="italic">children</hi>, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also <hi type="italic">that</hi> he have no burial; I say, <hi type="italic">that</hi> an untimely birth <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than he.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:4
verses.text: For he cometh in with vanity, and departeth in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:5
verses.text: Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known <hi type="italic">any thing:</hi> this hath more rest than the other.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:6
verses.text: ¶ Yea, though he live a thousand years twice <hi type="italic">told</hi>, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:7
verses.text: All the labour of man <hi type="italic">is</hi> for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:8
verses.text: For what hath the wise more than the fool? what hath the poor, that knoweth to walk before the living?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:9
verses.text: ¶ Better <hi type="italic">is</hi> the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this <hi type="italic">is</hi> also vanity and vexation of spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:10
verses.text: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it <hi type="italic">is</hi> man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:11
verses.text: ¶ Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what <hi type="italic">is</hi> man the better?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 6:12
verses.text: For who knoweth what <hi type="italic">is</hi> good for man in <hi type="italic">this</hi> life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?  <chapter eID="Eccl.6"/><div eID="gen730" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:1
verses.text: A GOOD name <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:2
verses.text: ¶ <hi type="italic">It is</hi> better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that <hi type="italic">is</hi> the end of all men; and the living will lay <hi type="italic">it</hi> to his heart.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:3
verses.text: Sorrow <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:4
verses.text: The heart of the wise <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the house of mirth.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:5
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:6
verses.text: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> the laughter of the fool: this also <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:7
verses.text: ¶ Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:8
verses.text: Better <hi type="italic">is</hi> the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: <hi type="italic">and</hi> the patient in spirit <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than the proud in spirit.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:9
verses.text: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:10
verses.text: Say not thou, What is <hi type="italic">the cause</hi> that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not inquire wisely concerning this.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:11
verses.text: ¶ Wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> good with an inheritance: and <hi type="italic">by it there is</hi> profit to them that see the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:12
verses.text: For wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> a defence, <hi type="italic">and</hi> money <hi type="italic">is</hi> a defence: but the excellency of knowledge <hi type="italic">is</hi>, <hi type="italic">that</hi> wisdom giveth life to them that have it.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:13
verses.text: Consider the work of God: for who can make <hi type="italic">that</hi> straight, which he hath made crooked?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:14
verses.text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:15
verses.text: All <hi type="italic">things</hi> have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just <hi type="italic">man</hi> that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked <hi type="italic">man</hi> that prolongeth <hi type="italic">his life</hi> in his wickedness.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:16
verses.text: Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:17
verses.text: Be not over much wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:18
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:19
verses.text: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty <hi type="italic">men</hi> which are in the city.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:20
verses.text: For <hi type="italic">there is</hi> not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:21
verses.text: Also take no heed unto all words that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:22
verses.text: For oftentimes also thine own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:23
verses.text: ¶ All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it <hi type="italic">was</hi> far from me.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:24
verses.text: That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:25
verses.text: I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason <hi type="italic">of things</hi>, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness <hi type="italic">and</hi> madness:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:26
verses.text: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart <hi type="italic">is</hi> snares and nets, <hi type="italic">and</hi> her hands <hi type="italic">as</hi> bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:27
verses.text: Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, <hi type="italic">counting</hi> one by one, to find out the account:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:28
verses.text: Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 7:29
verses.text: Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.  <chapter eID="Eccl.7"/><div eID="gen731" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:1
verses.text: WHO <hi type="italic">is</hi> as the wise <hi type="italic">man?</hi> and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:2
verses.text: I <hi type="italic">counsel thee</hi> to keep the king’s commandment, and <hi type="italic">that</hi> in regard of the oath of God.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:3
verses.text: Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he doeth whatsoever pleaseth him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:4
verses.text: Where the word of a king <hi type="italic">is</hi>, <hi type="italic">there is</hi> power: and who may say unto him, What doest thou?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:5
verses.text: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man’s heart discerneth both time and judgment.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:6
verses.text: ¶ Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man <hi type="italic">is</hi> great upon him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:7
verses.text: For he knoweth not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:8
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There is</hi> no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither <hi type="italic">hath he</hi> power in the day of death: and <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no discharge in <hi type="italic">that</hi> war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:9
verses.text: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: <hi type="italic">there is</hi> a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:10
verses.text: And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this <hi type="italic">is</hi> also vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:11
verses.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:12
verses.text: ¶ Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his <hi type="italic">days</hi> be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:13
verses.text: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong <hi type="italic">his</hi> days, <hi type="italic">which are</hi> as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:14
verses.text: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be just <hi type="italic">men</hi>, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked <hi type="italic">men</hi>, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:15
verses.text: Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God giveth him under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:16
verses.text: ¶ When I applied mine heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also <hi type="italic">there is that</hi> neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes:)

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 8:17
verses.text: Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek <hi type="italic">it</hi> out, yet he shall not find <hi type="italic">it;</hi> yea further; though a wise <hi type="italic">man</hi> think to know <hi type="italic">it</hi>, yet shall he not be able to find <hi type="italic">it</hi>.  <chapter eID="Eccl.8"/><div eID="gen732" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:1
verses.text: FOR all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, <hi type="italic">are</hi> in the hand of God: no man knoweth either love or hatred <hi type="italic">by</hi> all <hi type="italic">that is</hi> before them.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:2
verses.text: All <hi type="italic">things come</hi> alike to all: <hi type="italic">there is</hi> one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as <hi type="italic">is</hi> the good, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> the sinner; <hi type="italic">and</hi> he that sweareth, as <hi type="italic">he</hi> that feareth an oath.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:3
verses.text: This <hi type="italic">is</hi> an evil among all <hi type="italic">things</hi> that are done under the sun, that <hi type="italic">there is</hi> one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness <hi type="italic">is</hi> in their heart while they live, and after that <hi type="italic">they go</hi> to the dead.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:4
verses.text: ¶ For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:5
verses.text: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:6
verses.text: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any <hi type="italic">thing</hi> that is done under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:7
verses.text: ¶ Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:8
verses.text: Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no ointment.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:9
verses.text: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy portion in <hi type="italic">this</hi> life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:10
verses.text: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do <hi type="italic">it</hi> with thy might; for <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:11
verses.text: ¶ I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race <hi type="italic">is</hi> not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:12
verses.text: For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so <hi type="italic">are</hi> the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:13
verses.text: ¶ This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it <hi type="italic">seemed</hi> great unto me:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:14
verses.text: <hi type="italic">There was</hi> a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:15
verses.text: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:16
verses.text: Then said I, Wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than strength: nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> despised, and his words are not heard.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:17
verses.text: The words of wise <hi type="italic">men are</hi> heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 9:18
verses.text: Wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.  <chapter eID="Eccl.9"/><div eID="gen733" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:1
verses.text: DEAD flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: <hi type="italic">so doth</hi> a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom <hi type="italic">and</hi> honour.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:2
verses.text: A wise man’s heart <hi type="italic">is</hi> at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:3
verses.text: Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth <hi type="italic">him</hi>, and he saith to every one <hi type="italic">that</hi> he <hi type="italic">is</hi> a fool.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:4
verses.text: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:5
verses.text: There is an evil <hi type="italic">which</hi> I have seen under the sun, as an error <hi type="italic">which</hi> proceedeth from the ruler:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:6
verses.text: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:7
verses.text: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:8
verses.text: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:9
verses.text: Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; <hi type="italic">and</hi> he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:10
verses.text: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> profitable to direct.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:11
verses.text: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:12
verses.text: The words of a wise man’s mouth <hi type="italic">are</hi> gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:13
verses.text: The beginning of the words of his mouth <hi type="italic">is</hi> foolishness: and the end of his talk <hi type="italic">is</hi> mischievous madness.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:14
verses.text: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:15
verses.text: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knoweth not how to go to the city.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:16
verses.text: ¶ Woe to thee, O land, when thy king <hi type="italic">is</hi> a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:17
verses.text: Blessed <hi type="italic">art</hi> thou, O land, when thy king <hi type="italic">is</hi> the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:18
verses.text: ¶ By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:19
verses.text: ¶ A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all <hi type="italic">things</hi>.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 10:20
verses.text: ¶ Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.  <chapter eID="Eccl.10"/><div eID="gen734" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:1
verses.text: CAST thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:2
verses.text: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:3
verses.text: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty <hi type="italic">themselves</hi> upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:4
verses.text: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:5
verses.text: As thou knowest not what <hi type="italic">is</hi> the way of the spirit, <hi type="italic">nor</hi> how the bones <hi type="italic">do grow</hi> in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:6
verses.text: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> alike good.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:7
verses.text: ¶ Truly the light <hi type="italic">is</hi> sweet, and a pleasant <hi type="italic">thing it is</hi> for the eyes to behold the sun:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:8
verses.text: But if a man live many years, <hi type="italic">and</hi> rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:9
verses.text: ¶ Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these <hi type="italic">things</hi> God will bring thee into judgment.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 11:10
verses.text: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth <hi type="italic">are</hi> vanity.  <chapter eID="Eccl.11"/><div eID="gen735" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:1
verses.text: REMEMBER now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:2
verses.text: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:3
verses.text: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened,

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:4
verses.text: And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low;

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:5
verses.text: Also <hi type="italic">when</hi> they shall be afraid of <hi type="italic">that which is</hi> high, and fears <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:6
verses.text: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:7
verses.text: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:8
verses.text: ¶ Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all <hi type="italic">is</hi> vanity.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:9
verses.text: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, <hi type="italic">and</hi> set in order many proverbs.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:10
verses.text: The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> written <hi type="italic">was</hi> upright, <hi type="italic">even</hi> words of truth.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:11
verses.text: The words of the wise <hi type="italic">are</hi> as goads, and as nails fastened <hi type="italic">by</hi> the masters of assemblies, <hi type="italic">which</hi> are given from one shepherd.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:12
verses.text: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no end; and much study <hi type="italic">is</hi> a weariness of the flesh.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:13
verses.text: ¶ Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this <hi type="italic">is</hi> the whole <hi type="italic">duty</hi> of man.

verses.name: Ecclesiastes 12:14
verses.text: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether <hi type="italic">it be</hi> good, or whether <hi type="italic">it be</hi> evil. THE  <chapter eID="Eccl.12"/><div eID="gen736" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen724" osisID="Eccl" type="book"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:1
verses.text: THE song of songs, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> Solomon’s.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:2
verses.text: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love <hi type="italic">is</hi> better than wine.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:3
verses.text: Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name <hi type="italic">is as</hi> ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:4
verses.text: Draw me, we will run after thee: the king hath brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will remember thy love more than wine: the upright love thee.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:5
verses.text: I <hi type="italic">am</hi> black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:6
verses.text: Look not upon me, because I <hi type="italic">am</hi> black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mother’s children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; <hi type="italic">but</hi> mine own vineyard have I not kept.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:7
verses.text: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest <hi type="italic">thy flock</hi> to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions?

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:8
verses.text: ¶ If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds’ tents.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:9
verses.text: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh’s chariots.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:10
verses.text: Thy cheeks are comely with rows <hi type="italic">of jewels</hi>, thy neck with chains <hi type="italic">of gold</hi>.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:11
verses.text: We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:12
verses.text: ¶ While the king <hi type="italic">sitteth</hi> at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:13
verses.text: A bundle of myrrh <hi type="italic">is</hi> my wellbeloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:14
verses.text: My beloved <hi type="italic">is</hi> unto me <hi type="italic">as</hi> a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of En-gedi.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:15
verses.text: Behold, thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> fair, my love; behold, thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> fair; thou <hi type="italic">hast</hi> doves’ eyes.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:16
verses.text: Behold, thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed <hi type="italic">is</hi> green.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 1:17
verses.text: The beams of our house <hi type="italic">are</hi> cedar, <hi type="italic">and</hi> our rafters of fir.  <chapter eID="Song.1"/><div eID="gen738" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:1
verses.text: I <hi type="italic">AM</hi> the rose of Sharon, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the lily of the valleys.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:2
verses.text: As the lily among thorns, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> my love among the daughters.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:3
verses.text: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so <hi type="italic">is</hi> my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit <hi type="italic">was</hi> sweet to my taste.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:4
verses.text: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me <hi type="italic">was</hi> love.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:5
verses.text: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I <hi type="italic">am</hi> sick of love.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:6
verses.text: His left hand <hi type="italic">is</hi> under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:7
verses.text: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake <hi type="italic">my</hi> love, till he please.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:8
verses.text: ¶ The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:9
verses.text: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he standeth behind our wall, he looketh forth at the windows, shewing himself through the lattice.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:10
verses.text: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:11
verses.text: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over <hi type="italic">and</hi> gone;

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:12
verses.text: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing <hi type="italic">of birds</hi> is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:13
verses.text: The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines <hi type="italic">with</hi> the tender grape give a <hi type="italic">good</hi> smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:14
verses.text: ¶ O my dove, <hi type="italic">that art</hi> in the clefts of the rock, in the secret <hi type="italic">places</hi> of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy voice, and thy countenance <hi type="italic">is</hi> comely.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:15
verses.text: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines <hi type="italic">have</hi> tender grapes.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:16
verses.text: ¶ My beloved <hi type="italic">is</hi> mine, and I <hi type="italic">am</hi> his: he feedeth among the lilies.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 2:17
verses.text: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.  <chapter eID="Song.2"/><div eID="gen739" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:1
verses.text: BY night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:2
verses.text: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:3
verses.text: The watchmen that go about the city found me: <hi type="italic">to whom I said</hi>, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:4
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It was</hi> but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:5
verses.text: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake <hi type="italic">my</hi> love, till he please.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:6
verses.text: ¶ Who <hi type="italic">is</hi> this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:7
verses.text: Behold his bed, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> Solomon’s; threescore valiant men <hi type="italic">are</hi> about it, of the valiant of Israel.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:8
verses.text: They all hold swords, <hi type="italic">being</hi> expert in war: every man <hi type="italic">hath</hi> his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:9
verses.text: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:10
verses.text: He made the pillars thereof <hi type="italic">of</hi> silver, the bottom thereof <hi type="italic">of</hi> gold, the covering of it <hi type="italic">of</hi> purple, the midst thereof being paved <hi type="italic">with</hi> love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 3:11
verses.text: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.  <chapter eID="Song.3"/><div eID="gen740" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:1
verses.text: BEHOLD, thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> fair, my love; behold, thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> fair; thou <hi type="italic">hast</hi> doves’ eyes within thy locks: thy hair <hi type="italic">is</hi> as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:2
verses.text: Thy teeth <hi type="italic">are</hi> like a flock <hi type="italic">of sheep that are even</hi> shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none <hi type="italic">is</hi> barren among them.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:3
verses.text: Thy lips <hi type="italic">are</hi> like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech <hi type="italic">is</hi> comely: thy temples <hi type="italic">are</hi> like a piece of a pomegranate within thy locks.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:4
verses.text: Thy neck <hi type="italic">is</hi> like the tower of David builded for an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:5
verses.text: Thy two breasts <hi type="italic">are</hi> like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:6
verses.text: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:7
verses.text: Thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> all fair, my love; <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no spot in thee.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:8
verses.text: ¶ Come with me from Lebanon, <hi type="italic">my</hi> spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:9
verses.text: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, <hi type="italic">my</hi> spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:10
verses.text: How fair is thy love, my sister, <hi type="italic">my</hi> spouse! how much better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thine ointments than all spices!

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:11
verses.text: Thy lips, O <hi type="italic">my</hi> spouse, drop <hi type="italic">as</hi> the honeycomb: honey and milk <hi type="italic">are</hi> under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments <hi type="italic">is</hi> like the smell of Lebanon.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:12
verses.text: A garden inclosed <hi type="italic">is</hi> my sister, <hi type="italic">my</hi> spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:13
verses.text: Thy plants <hi type="italic">are</hi> an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:14
verses.text: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:15
verses.text: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 4:16
verses.text: ¶ Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.  <chapter eID="Song.4"/><div eID="gen741" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:1
verses.text: I AM come into my garden, my sister, <hi type="italic">my</hi> spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:2
verses.text: ¶ I sleep, but my heart waketh: <hi type="italic">it is</hi> the voice of my beloved that knocketh, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, <hi type="italic">and</hi> my locks with the drops of the night.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:3
verses.text: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:4
verses.text: My beloved put in his hand by the hole <hi type="italic">of the door</hi>, and my bowels were moved for him.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:5
verses.text: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped <hi type="italic">with</hi> myrrh, and my fingers <hi type="italic">with</hi> sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:6
verses.text: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, <hi type="italic">and</hi> was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:7
verses.text: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:8
verses.text: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> sick of love.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:9
verses.text: ¶ What <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy beloved more than <hi type="italic">another</hi> beloved, O thou fairest among women? what <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy beloved more than <hi type="italic">another</hi> beloved, that thou dost so charge us?

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:10
verses.text: My beloved <hi type="italic">is</hi> white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:11
verses.text: His head <hi type="italic">is as</hi> the most fine gold, his locks <hi type="italic">are</hi> bushy, <hi type="italic">and</hi> black as a raven.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:12
verses.text: His eyes <hi type="italic">are</hi> as <hi type="italic">the eyes</hi> of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, <hi type="italic">and</hi> fitly set.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:13
verses.text: His cheeks <hi type="italic">are</hi> as a bed of spices, <hi type="italic">as</hi> sweet flowers: his lips <hi type="italic">like</hi> lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:14
verses.text: His hands <hi type="italic">are as</hi> gold rings set with the beryl: his belly <hi type="italic">is as</hi> bright ivory overlaid <hi type="italic">with</hi> sapphires.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:15
verses.text: His legs <hi type="italic">are as</hi> pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance <hi type="italic">is</hi> as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 5:16
verses.text: His mouth <hi type="italic">is</hi> most sweet: yea, he <hi type="italic">is</hi> altogether lovely. This <hi type="italic">is</hi> my beloved, and this <hi type="italic">is</hi> my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.  <chapter eID="Song.5"/><div eID="gen742" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:1
verses.text: WHITHER is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:2
verses.text: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:3
verses.text: I <hi type="italic">am</hi> my beloved’s, and my beloved <hi type="italic">is</hi> mine: he feedeth among the lilies.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:4
verses.text: ¶ Thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as <hi type="italic">an army</hi> with banners.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:5
verses.text: Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy hair <hi type="italic">is</hi> as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:6
verses.text: Thy teeth <hi type="italic">are</hi> as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one beareth twins, and <hi type="italic">there is</hi> not one barren among them.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:7
verses.text: As a piece of a pomegranate <hi type="italic">are</hi> thy temples within thy locks.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:8
verses.text: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:9
verses.text: My dove, my undefiled is <hi type="italic">but</hi> one; she <hi type="italic">is</hi> the <hi type="italic">only</hi> one of her mother, she <hi type="italic">is</hi> the choice <hi type="italic">one</hi> of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; <hi type="italic">yea</hi>, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:10
verses.text: ¶ Who <hi type="italic">is</hi> she <hi type="italic">that</hi> looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, <hi type="italic">and</hi> terrible as <hi type="italic">an army</hi> with banners?

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:11
verses.text: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, <hi type="italic">and</hi> to see whether the vine flourished, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the pomegranates budded.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:12
verses.text: Or ever I was aware, my soul made me <hi type="italic">like</hi> the chariots of Amminadib.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 6:13
verses.text: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.  <chapter eID="Song.6"/><div eID="gen743" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:1
verses.text: HOW beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince’s daughter! the joints of thy thighs <hi type="italic">are</hi> like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:2
verses.text: Thy navel <hi type="italic">is like</hi> a round goblet, <hi type="italic">which</hi> wanteth not liquor: thy belly <hi type="italic">is like</hi> an heap of wheat set about with lilies.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:3
verses.text: Thy two breasts <hi type="italic">are</hi> like two young roes <hi type="italic">that are</hi> twins.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:4
verses.text: Thy neck <hi type="italic">is</hi> as a tower of ivory; thine eyes <hi type="italic">like</hi> the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim: thy nose <hi type="italic">is</hi> as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:5
verses.text: Thine head upon thee <hi type="italic">is</hi> like Carmel, and the hair of thine head like purple; the king <hi type="italic">is</hi> held in the galleries.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:6
verses.text: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:7
verses.text: This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters <hi type="italic">of grapes</hi>.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:8
verses.text: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of thy nose like apples;

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:9
verses.text: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth <hi type="italic">down</hi> sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:10
verses.text: ¶ I <hi type="italic">am</hi> my beloved’s, and his desire <hi type="italic">is</hi> toward me.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:11
verses.text: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:12
verses.text: Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourish, <hi type="italic">whether</hi> the tender grape appear, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 7:13
verses.text: The mandrakes give a smell, and at our gates <hi type="italic">are</hi> all manner of pleasant <hi type="italic">fruits</hi>, new and old, <hi type="italic">which</hi> I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.  <chapter eID="Song.7"/><div eID="gen744" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:1
verses.text: O THAT thou <hi type="italic">wert</hi> as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother! <hi type="italic">when</hi> I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; yea, I should not be despised.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:2
verses.text: I would lead thee, <hi type="italic">and</hi> bring thee into my mother’s house, <hi type="italic">who</hi> would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:3
verses.text: His left hand <hi type="italic">should be</hi> under my head, and his right hand should embrace me.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:4
verses.text: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up, nor awake <hi type="italic">my</hi> love, until he please.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:5
verses.text: Who <hi type="italic">is</hi> this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth: there she brought thee forth <hi type="italic">that</hi> bare thee.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:6
verses.text: ¶ Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love <hi type="italic">is</hi> strong as death; jealousy <hi type="italic">is</hi> cruel as the grave: the coals thereof <hi type="italic">are</hi> coals of fire, <hi type="italic">which hath</hi> a most vehement flame.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:7
verses.text: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:8
verses.text: ¶ We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:9
verses.text: If she <hi type="italic">be</hi> a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: and if she <hi type="italic">be</hi> a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:10
verses.text: I <hi type="italic">am</hi> a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found favour.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:11
verses.text: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; he let out the vineyard unto keepers; every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand <hi type="italic">pieces</hi> of silver.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:12
verses.text: My vineyard, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> mine, <hi type="italic">is</hi> before me: thou, O Solomon, <hi type="italic">must have</hi> a thousand, and those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:13
verses.text: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken to thy voice: cause me to hear <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Song of Solomon 8:14
verses.text: ¶ Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like to a roe or to a young hart upon the mountains of spices.  <chapter eID="Song.8"/><div eID="gen745" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen737" osisID="Song" type="book"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 1:1
verses.text: THE vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, <hi type="italic">and</hi> Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:2
verses.text: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth: for the Lord hath spoken, I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:3
verses.text: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: <hi type="italic">but</hi> Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:4
verses.text: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:5
verses.text: ¶ Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:6
verses.text: From the sole of the foot even unto the head <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no soundness in it; <hi type="italic">but</hi> wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:7
verses.text: Your country <hi type="italic">is</hi> desolate, your cities <hi type="italic">are</hi> burned with fire: your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and <hi type="italic">it is</hi> desolate, as overthrown by strangers.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:8
verses.text: And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:9
verses.text: Except the Lord of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, <hi type="italic">and</hi> we should have been like unto Gomorrah.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:10
verses.text: ¶ Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom; give ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:11
verses.text: To what purpose <hi type="italic">is</hi> the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the Lord: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:12
verses.text: When ye come to appear before me, who hath required this at your hand, to tread my courts?

verses.name: Isaiah 1:13
verses.text: Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me; the new moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, I cannot away with; <hi type="italic">it is</hi> iniquity, even the solemn meeting.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:14
verses.text: Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth: they are a trouble unto me; I am weary to bear <hi type="italic">them</hi>.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:15
verses.text: And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you: yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:16
verses.text: ¶ Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil;

verses.name: Isaiah 1:17
verses.text: Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:18
verses.text: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the Lord: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:19
verses.text: If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land:

verses.name: Isaiah 1:20
verses.text: But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:21
verses.text: ¶ How is the faithful city become an harlot! it was full of judgment; righteousness lodged in it; but now murderers.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:22
verses.text: Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water:

verses.name: Isaiah 1:23
verses.text: Thy princes <hi type="italic">are</hi> rebellious, and companions of thieves: every one loveth gifts, and followeth after rewards: they judge not the fatherless, neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:24
verses.text: Therefore saith the Lord, the Lord of hosts, the mighty One of Israel, Ah, I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge me of mine enemies:

verses.name: Isaiah 1:25
verses.text: ¶ And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin:

verses.name: Isaiah 1:26
verses.text: And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellers as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:27
verses.text: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:28
verses.text: ¶ And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> together, and they that forsake the Lord shall be consumed.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:29
verses.text: For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired, and ye shall be confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:30
verses.text: For ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth, and as a garden that hath no water.

verses.name: Isaiah 1:31
verses.text: And the strong shall be as tow, and the maker of it as a spark, and they shall both burn together, and none shall quench <hi type="italic">them</hi>.  <chapter eID="Isa.1"/><div eID="gen747" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 2:1
verses.text: THE word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:2
verses.text: And it shall come to pass in the last days, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:3
verses.text: And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:4
verses.text: And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:5
verses.text: O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the Lord.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:6
verses.text: ¶ Therefore thou hast forsaken thy people the house of Jacob, because they be replenished from the east, and <hi type="italic">are</hi> soothsayers like the Philistines, and they please themselves in the children of strangers.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:7
verses.text: Their land also is full of silver and gold, neither <hi type="italic">is there any</hi> end of their treasures; their land is also full of horses, neither <hi type="italic">is there any</hi> end of their chariots:

verses.name: Isaiah 2:8
verses.text: Their land also is full of idols; they worship the work of their own hands, that which their own fingers have made:

verses.name: Isaiah 2:9
verses.text: And the mean man boweth down, and the great man humbleth himself: therefore forgive them not.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:10
verses.text: ¶ Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:11
verses.text: The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:12
verses.text: For the day of the Lord of hosts <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> upon every <hi type="italic">one that is</hi> proud and lofty, and upon every <hi type="italic">one that is</hi> lifted up; and he shall be brought low:

verses.name: Isaiah 2:13
verses.text: And upon all the cedars of Lebanon, <hi type="italic">that are</hi> high and lifted up, and upon all the oaks of Bashan,

verses.name: Isaiah 2:14
verses.text: And upon all the high mountains, and upon all the hills <hi type="italic">that are</hi> lifted up,

verses.name: Isaiah 2:15
verses.text: And upon every high tower, and upon every fenced wall,

verses.name: Isaiah 2:16
verses.text: And upon all the ships of Tarshish, and upon all pleasant pictures.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:17
