verses.text: And the loftiness of man shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be made low: and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:18
verses.text: And the idols he shall utterly abolish.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:19
verses.text: And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:20
verses.text: In that day a man shall cast his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which they made <hi type="italic">each one</hi> for himself to worship, to the moles and to the bats;

verses.name: Isaiah 2:21
verses.text: To go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the tops of the ragged rocks, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

verses.name: Isaiah 2:22
verses.text: Cease ye from man, whose breath <hi type="italic">is</hi> in his nostrils: for wherein is he to be accounted of?  <chapter eID="Isa.2"/><div eID="gen748" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 3:1
verses.text: FOR, behold, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, doth take away from Jerusalem and from Judah the stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water,

verses.name: Isaiah 3:2
verses.text: The mighty man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet, and the prudent, and the ancient,

verses.name: Isaiah 3:3
verses.text: The captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counseller, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:4
verses.text: And I will give children <hi type="italic">to be</hi> their princes, and babes shall rule over them.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:5
verses.text: And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour: the child shall behave himself proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:6
verses.text: When a man shall take hold of his brother of the house of his father, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and <hi type="italic">let</hi> this ruin <hi type="italic">be</hi> under thy hand:

verses.name: Isaiah 3:7
verses.text: In that day shall he swear, saying, I will not be an healer; for in my house <hi type="italic">is</hi> neither bread nor clothing: make me not a ruler of the people.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:8
verses.text: For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen: because their tongue and their doings <hi type="italic">are</hi> against the Lord, to provoke the eyes of his glory.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:9
verses.text: ¶ The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide <hi type="italic">it</hi> not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:10
verses.text: Say ye to the righteous, that <hi type="italic">it shall be</hi> well <hi type="italic">with him:</hi> for they shall eat the fruit of their doings.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:11
verses.text: Woe unto the wicked! <hi type="italic">it shall be</hi> ill <hi type="italic">with him:</hi> for the reward of his hands shall be given him.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:12
verses.text: ¶ <hi type="italic">As for</hi> my people, children <hi type="italic">are</hi> their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause <hi type="italic">thee</hi> to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:13
verses.text: The Lord standeth up to plead, and standeth to judge the people.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:14
verses.text: The Lord will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and the princes thereof: for ye have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor <hi type="italic">is</hi> in your houses.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:15
verses.text: What mean ye <hi type="italic">that</hi> ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? saith the Lord God of hosts.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:16
verses.text: ¶ Moreover the Lord saith, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing <hi type="italic">as</hi> they go, and making a tinkling with their feet:

verses.name: Isaiah 3:17
verses.text: Therefore the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord will discover their secret parts.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:18
verses.text: In that day the Lord will take away the bravery of <hi type="italic">their</hi> tinkling ornaments <hi type="italic">about their feet</hi>, and <hi type="italic">their</hi> cauls, and <hi type="italic">their</hi> round tires like the moon,

verses.name: Isaiah 3:19
verses.text: The chains, and the bracelets, and the mufflers,

verses.name: Isaiah 3:20
verses.text: The bonnets, and the ornaments of the legs, and the headbands, and the tablets, and the earrings,

verses.name: Isaiah 3:21
verses.text: The rings, and nose jewels,

verses.name: Isaiah 3:22
verses.text: The changeable suits of apparel, and the mantles, and the wimples, and the crisping pins,

verses.name: Isaiah 3:23
verses.text: The glasses, and the fine linen, and the hoods, and the vails.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:24
verses.text: And it shall come to pass, <hi type="italic">that</hi> instead of sweet smell there shall be stink; and instead of a girdle a rent; and instead of well set hair baldness; and instead of a stomacher a girding of sackcloth; <hi type="italic">and</hi> burning instead of beauty.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:25
verses.text: Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the war.

verses.name: Isaiah 3:26
verses.text: And her gates shall lament and mourn; and she <hi type="italic">being</hi> desolate shall sit upon the ground.  <chapter eID="Isa.3"/><div eID="gen749" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 4:1
verses.text: AND in that day seven women shall take hold of one man, saying, We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be called by thy name, to take away our reproach.

verses.name: Isaiah 4:2
verses.text: In that day shall the branch of the Lord be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel.

verses.name: Isaiah 4:3
verses.text: And it shall come to pass, <hi type="italic">that he that is</hi> left in Zion, and <hi type="italic">he that</hi> remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, <hi type="italic">even</hi> every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem:

verses.name: Isaiah 4:4
verses.text: When the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from the midst thereof by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning.

verses.name: Isaiah 4:5
verses.text: And the Lord will create upon every dwelling place of mount Zion, and upon her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night: for upon all the glory <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> a defence.

verses.name: Isaiah 4:6
verses.text: And there shall be a tabernacle for a shadow in the daytime from the heat, and for a place of refuge, and for a covert from storm and from rain.  <chapter eID="Isa.4"/><div eID="gen750" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 5:1
verses.text: NOW will I sing to my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard. My wellbeloved hath a vineyard in a very fruitful hill:

verses.name: Isaiah 5:2
verses.text: And he fenced it, and gathered out the stones thereof, and planted it with the choicest vine, and built a tower in the midst of it, and also made a winepress therein: and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:3
verses.text: And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem, and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:4
verses.text: What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes?

verses.name: Isaiah 5:5
verses.text: And now go to; I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; <hi type="italic">and</hi> break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down:

verses.name: Isaiah 5:6
verses.text: And I will lay it waste: it shall not be pruned, nor digged; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:7
verses.text: For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts <hi type="italic">is</hi> the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:8
verses.text: ¶ Woe unto them that join house to house, <hi type="italic">that</hi> lay field to field, till <hi type="italic">there be</hi> no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!

verses.name: Isaiah 5:9
verses.text: In mine ears <hi type="italic">said</hi> the Lord of hosts, Of a truth many houses shall be desolate, <hi type="italic">even</hi> great and fair, without inhabitant.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:10
verses.text: Yea, ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and the seed of an homer shall yield an ephah.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:11
verses.text: ¶ Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, <hi type="italic">that</hi> they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, <hi type="italic">till</hi> wine inflame them!

verses.name: Isaiah 5:12
verses.text: And the harp, and the viol, the tabret, and pipe, and wine, are in their feasts: but they regard not the work of the Lord, neither consider the operation of his hands.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:13
verses.text: ¶ Therefore my people are gone into captivity, because <hi type="italic">they have</hi> no knowledge: and their honourable men <hi type="italic">are</hi> famished, and their multitude dried up with thirst.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:14
verses.text: Therefore hell hath enlarged herself, and opened her mouth without measure: and their glory, and their multitude, and their pomp, and he that rejoiceth, shall descend into it.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:15
verses.text: And the mean man shall be brought down, and the mighty man shall be humbled, and the eyes of the lofty shall be humbled:

verses.name: Isaiah 5:16
verses.text: But the Lord of hosts shall be exalted in judgment, and God that is holy shall be sanctified in righteousness.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:17
verses.text: Then shall the lambs feed after their manner, and the waste places of the fat ones shall strangers eat.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:18
verses.text: Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as it were with a cart rope:

verses.name: Isaiah 5:19
verses.text: That say, Let him make speed, <hi type="italic">and</hi> hasten his work, that we may see <hi type="italic">it:</hi> and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw nigh and come, that we may know <hi type="italic">it!</hi>

verses.name: Isaiah 5:20
verses.text: ¶ Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!

verses.name: Isaiah 5:21
verses.text: Woe unto <hi type="italic">them that are</hi> wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!

verses.name: Isaiah 5:22
verses.text: Woe unto <hi type="italic">them that are</hi> mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink:

verses.name: Isaiah 5:23
verses.text: Which justify the wicked for reward, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him!

verses.name: Isaiah 5:24
verses.text: Therefore as the fire devoureth the stubble, and the flame consumeth the chaff, <hi type="italic">so</hi> their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust: because they have cast away the law of the Lord of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:25
verses.text: Therefore is the anger of the Lord kindled against his people, and he hath stretched forth his hand against them, and hath smitten them: and the hills did tremble, and their carcases <hi type="italic">were</hi> torn in the midst of the streets. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand <hi type="italic">is</hi> stretched out still.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:26
verses.text: ¶ And he will lift up an ensign to the nations from far, and will hiss unto them from the end of the earth: and, behold, they shall come with speed swiftly:

verses.name: Isaiah 5:27
verses.text: None shall be weary nor stumble among them; none shall slumber nor sleep; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken:

verses.name: Isaiah 5:28
verses.text: Whose arrows <hi type="italic">are</hi> sharp, and all their bows bent, their horses’ hoofs shall be counted like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind:

verses.name: Isaiah 5:29
verses.text: Their roaring <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> like a lion, they shall roar like young lions: yea, they shall roar, and lay hold of the prey, and shall carry <hi type="italic">it</hi> away safe, and none shall deliver <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Isaiah 5:30
verses.text: And in that day they shall roar against them like the roaring of the sea: and if <hi type="italic">one</hi> look unto the land, behold darkness <hi type="italic">and</hi> sorrow, and the light is darkened in the heavens thereof.  <chapter eID="Isa.5"/><div eID="gen751" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 6:1
verses.text: IN the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.

verses.name: Isaiah 6:2
verses.text: Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.

verses.name: Isaiah 6:3
verses.text: And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, <hi type="italic">is</hi> the Lord of hosts: the whole earth <hi type="italic">is</hi> full of his glory.

verses.name: Isaiah 6:4
verses.text: And the posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.

verses.name: Isaiah 6:5
verses.text: ¶ Then said I, Woe <hi type="italic">is</hi> me! for I am undone; because I <hi type="italic">am</hi> a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts.

verses.name: Isaiah 6:6
verses.text: Then flew one of the seraphims unto me, having a live coal in his hand, <hi type="italic">which</hi> he had taken with the tongs from off the altar:

verses.name: Isaiah 6:7
verses.text: And he laid <hi type="italic">it</hi> upon my mouth, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged.

verses.name: Isaiah 6:8
verses.text: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here <hi type="italic">am</hi> I; send me.

verses.name: Isaiah 6:9
verses.text: ¶ And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.

verses.name: Isaiah 6:10
verses.text: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.

verses.name: Isaiah 6:11
verses.text: Then said I, Lord, how long? And he answered, Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate,

verses.name: Isaiah 6:12
verses.text: And the Lord have removed men far away, and <hi type="italic">there be</hi> a great forsaking in the midst of the land.

verses.name: Isaiah 6:13
verses.text: ¶ But yet in it <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> a tenth, and <hi type="italic">it</hi> shall return, and shall be eaten: as a teil tree, and as an oak, whose substance <hi type="italic">is</hi> in them, when they cast <hi type="italic">their leaves: so</hi> the holy seed <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> the substance thereof.  <chapter eID="Isa.6"/><div eID="gen752" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 7:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, <hi type="italic">that</hi> Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:2
verses.text: And it was told the house of David, saying, Syria is confederate with Ephraim. And his heart was moved, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:3
verses.text: Then said the Lord unto Isaiah, Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shear-jashub thy son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field;

verses.name: Isaiah 7:4
verses.text: And say unto him, Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be fainthearted for the two tails of these smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin with Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:5
verses.text: Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have taken evil counsel against thee, saying,

verses.name: Isaiah 7:6
verses.text: Let us go up against Judah, and vex it, and let us make a breach therein for us, and set a king in the midst of it, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the son of Tabeal:

verses.name: Isaiah 7:7
verses.text: Thus saith the Lord God, It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:8
verses.text: For the head of Syria <hi type="italic">is</hi> Damascus, and the head of Damascus <hi type="italic">is</hi> Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:9
verses.text: And the head of Ephraim <hi type="italic">is</hi> Samaria, and the head of Samaria <hi type="italic">is</hi> Remaliah’s son. If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:10
verses.text: ¶ Moreover the Lord spake again unto Ahaz, saying,

verses.name: Isaiah 7:11
verses.text: Ask thee a sign of the Lord thy God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:12
verses.text: But Ahaz said, I will not ask, neither will I tempt the Lord.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:13
verses.text: And he said, Hear ye now, O house of David; <hi type="italic">Is it</hi> a small thing for you to weary men, but will ye weary my God also?

verses.name: Isaiah 7:14
verses.text: Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:15
verses.text: Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:16
verses.text: For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:17
verses.text: ¶ The Lord shall bring upon thee, and upon thy people, and upon thy father’s house, days that have not come, from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah; <hi type="italic">even</hi> the king of Assyria.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:18
verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the Lord shall hiss for the fly that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the land of Assyria.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:19
verses.text: And they shall come, and shall rest all of them in the desolate valleys, and in the holes of the rocks, and upon all thorns, and upon all bushes.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:20
verses.text: In the same day shall the Lord shave with a rasor that is hired, <hi type="italic">namely</hi>, by them beyond the river, by the king of Assyria, the head, and the hair of the feet: and it shall also consume the beard.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:21
verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, <hi type="italic">that</hi> a man shall nourish a young cow, and two sheep;

verses.name: Isaiah 7:22
verses.text: And it shall come to pass, for the abundance of milk <hi type="italic">that</hi> they shall give he shall eat butter: for butter and honey shall every one eat that is left in the land.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:23
verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, <hi type="italic">that</hi> every place shall be, where there were a thousand vines at a thousand silverlings, it shall <hi type="italic">even</hi> be for briers and thorns.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:24
verses.text: With arrows and with bows shall <hi type="italic">men</hi> come thither; because all the land shall become briers and thorns.

verses.name: Isaiah 7:25
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">on</hi> all hills that shall be digged with the mattock, there shall not come thither the fear of briers and thorns: but it shall be for the sending forth of oxen, and for the treading of lesser cattle.  <chapter eID="Isa.7"/><div eID="gen753" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 8:1
verses.text: MOREOVER the Lord said unto me, Take thee a great roll, and write in it with a man’s pen concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:2
verses.text: And I took unto me faithful witnesses to record, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:3
verses.text: And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. Then said the Lord to me, Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:4
verses.text: For before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother, the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:5
verses.text: ¶ The Lord spake also unto me again, saying,

verses.name: Isaiah 8:6
verses.text: Forasmuch as this people refuseth the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son;

verses.name: Isaiah 8:7
verses.text: Now therefore, behold, the Lord bringeth up upon them the waters of the river, strong and many, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the king of Assyria, and all his glory: and he shall come up over all his channels, and go over all his banks:

verses.name: Isaiah 8:8
verses.text: And he shall pass through Judah; he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach <hi type="italic">even</hi> to the neck; and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:9
verses.text: ¶ Associate yourselves, O ye people, and ye shall be broken in pieces; and give ear, all ye of far countries: gird yourselves, and ye shall be broken in pieces; gird yourselves, and ye shall be broken in pieces.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:10
verses.text: Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God <hi type="italic">is</hi> with us.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:11
verses.text: ¶ For the Lord spake thus to me with a strong hand, and instructed me that I should not walk in the way of this people, saying,

verses.name: Isaiah 8:12
verses.text: Say ye not, A confederacy, to all <hi type="italic">them to</hi> whom this people shall say, A confederacy; neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:13
verses.text: Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and <hi type="italic">let</hi> him <hi type="italic">be</hi> your fear, and <hi type="italic">let</hi> him <hi type="italic">be</hi> your dread.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:14
verses.text: And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:15
verses.text: And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:16
verses.text: Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:17
verses.text: And I will wait upon the Lord, that hideth his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:18
verses.text: Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me <hi type="italic">are</hi> for signs and for wonders in Israel from the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth in mount Zion.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:19
verses.text: ¶ And when they shall say unto you, Seek unto them that have familiar spirits, and unto wizards that peep, and that mutter: should not a people seek unto their God? for the living to the dead?

verses.name: Isaiah 8:20
verses.text: To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, <hi type="italic">it is</hi> because <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no light in them.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:21
verses.text: And they shall pass through it, hardly bestead and hungry: and it shall come to pass, that when they shall be hungry, they shall fret themselves, and curse their king and their God, and look upward.

verses.name: Isaiah 8:22
verses.text: And they shall look unto the earth; and behold trouble and darkness, dimness of anguish; and <hi type="italic">they shall be</hi> driven to darkness.  <chapter eID="Isa.8"/><div eID="gen754" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 9:1
verses.text: NEVERTHELESS the dimness <hi type="italic">shall</hi> not <hi type="italic">be</hi> such as <hi type="italic">was</hi> in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict <hi type="italic">her by</hi> the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:2
verses.text: The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:3
verses.text: Thou hast multiplied the nation, <hi type="italic">and</hi> not increased the joy: they joy before thee according to the joy in harvest, <hi type="italic">and</hi> as <hi type="italic">men</hi> rejoice when they divide the spoil.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:4
verses.text: For thou hast broken the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, as in the day of Midian.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:5
verses.text: For every battle of the warrior <hi type="italic">is</hi> with confused noise, and garments rolled in blood; but <hi type="italic">this</hi> shall be with burning <hi type="italic">and</hi> fuel of fire.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:6
verses.text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counseller, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:7
verses.text: Of the increase of <hi type="italic">his</hi> government and peace <hi type="italic">there shall be</hi> no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:8
verses.text: ¶ The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:9
verses.text: And all the people shall know, <hi type="italic">even</hi> Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria, that say in the pride and stoutness of heart,

verses.name: Isaiah 9:10
verses.text: The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with hewn stones: the sycomores are cut down, but we will change <hi type="italic">them into</hi> cedars.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:11
verses.text: Therefore the Lord shall set up the adversaries of Rezin against him, and join his enemies together;

verses.name: Isaiah 9:12
verses.text: The Syrians before, and the Philistines behind; and they shall devour Israel with open mouth. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand <hi type="italic">is</hi> stretched out still.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:13
verses.text: ¶ For the people turneth not unto him that smiteth them, neither do they seek the Lord of hosts.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:14
verses.text: Therefore the Lord will cut off from Israel head and tail, branch and rush, in one day.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:15
verses.text: The ancient and honourable, he <hi type="italic">is</hi> the head; and the prophet that teacheth lies, he <hi type="italic">is</hi> the tail.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:16
verses.text: For the leaders of this people cause <hi type="italic">them</hi> to err; and <hi type="italic">they that are</hi> led of them <hi type="italic">are</hi> destroyed.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:17
verses.text: Therefore the Lord shall have no joy in their young men, neither shall have mercy on their fatherless and widows: for every one <hi type="italic">is</hi> an hypocrite and an evildoer, and every mouth speaketh folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand <hi type="italic">is</hi> stretched out still.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:18
verses.text: ¶ For wickedness burneth as the fire: it shall devour the briers and thorns, and shall kindle in the thickets of the forest, and they shall mount up <hi type="italic">like</hi> the lifting up of smoke.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:19
verses.text: Through the wrath of the Lord of hosts is the land darkened, and the people shall be as the fuel of the fire: no man shall spare his brother.

verses.name: Isaiah 9:20
verses.text: And he shall snatch on the right hand, and be hungry; and he shall eat on the left hand, and they shall not be satisfied: they shall eat every man the flesh of his own arm:

verses.name: Isaiah 9:21
verses.text: Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh: <hi type="italic">and</hi> they together <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand <hi type="italic">is</hi> stretched out still.  <chapter eID="Isa.9"/><div eID="gen755" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 10:1
verses.text: WOE unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness <hi type="italic">which</hi> they have prescribed;

verses.name: Isaiah 10:2
verses.text: To turn aside the needy from judgment, and to take away the right from the poor of my people, that widows may be their prey, and <hi type="italic">that</hi> they may rob the fatherless!

verses.name: Isaiah 10:3
verses.text: And what will ye do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation <hi type="italic">which</hi> shall come from far? to whom will ye flee for help? and where will ye leave your glory?

verses.name: Isaiah 10:4
verses.text: Without me they shall bow down under the prisoners, and they shall fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand <hi type="italic">is</hi> stretched out still.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:5
verses.text: ¶ O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:6
verses.text: I will send him against an hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:7
verses.text: Howbeit he meaneth not so, neither doth his heart think so; but <hi type="italic">it is</hi> in his heart to destroy and cut off nations not a few.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:8
verses.text: For he saith, <hi type="italic">Are</hi> not my princes altogether kings?

verses.name: Isaiah 10:9
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is</hi> not Calno as Carchemish? <hi type="italic">is</hi> not Hamath as Arpad? <hi type="italic">is</hi> not Samaria as Damascus?

verses.name: Isaiah 10:10
verses.text: As my hand hath found the kingdoms of the idols, and whose graven images did excel them of Jerusalem and of Samaria;

verses.name: Isaiah 10:11
verses.text: Shall I not, as I have done unto Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?

verses.name: Isaiah 10:12
verses.text: Wherefore it shall come to pass, <hi type="italic">that</hi> when the Lord hath performed his whole work upon mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria, and the glory of his high looks.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:13
verses.text: For he saith, By the strength of my hand I have done <hi type="italic">it</hi>, and by my wisdom; for I am prudent: and I have removed the bounds of the people, and have robbed their treasures, and I have put down the inhabitants like a valiant <hi type="italic">man:</hi>

verses.name: Isaiah 10:14
verses.text: And my hand hath found as a nest the riches of the people: and as one gathereth eggs <hi type="italic">that are</hi> left, have I gathered all the earth; and there was none that moved the wing, or opened the mouth, or peeped.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:15
verses.text: Shall the axe boast itself against him that heweth therewith? <hi type="italic">or</hi> shall the saw magnify itself against him that shaketh it? as if the rod should shake <hi type="italic">itself</hi> against them that lift it up, <hi type="italic">or</hi> as if the staff should lift up <hi type="italic">itself</hi>, <hi type="italic">as if it were</hi> no wood.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:16
verses.text: Therefore shall the Lord, the Lord of hosts, send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory he shall kindle a burning like the burning of a fire.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:17
verses.text: And the light of Israel shall be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame: and it shall burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day;

verses.name: Isaiah 10:18
verses.text: And shall consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful field, both soul and body: and they shall be as when a standardbearer fainteth.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:19
verses.text: And the rest of the trees of his forest shall be few, that a child may write them.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:20
verses.text: ¶ And it shall come to pass in that day, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the remnant of Israel, and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob, shall no more again stay upon him that smote them; but shall stay upon the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:21
verses.text: The remnant shall return, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the remnant of Jacob, unto the mighty God.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:22
verses.text: For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, <hi type="italic">yet</hi> a remnant of them shall return: the consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:23
verses.text: For the Lord God of hosts shall make a consumption, even determined, in the midst of all the land.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:24
verses.text: ¶ Therefore thus saith the Lord God of hosts, O my people that dwellest in Zion, be not afraid of the Assyrian: he shall smite thee with a rod, and shall lift up his staff against thee, after the manner of Egypt.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:25
verses.text: For yet a very little while, and the indignation shall cease, and mine anger in their destruction.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:26
verses.text: And the Lord of hosts shall stir up a scourge for him according to the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb: and <hi type="italic">as</hi> his rod <hi type="italic">was</hi> upon the sea, so shall he lift it up after the manner of Egypt.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:27
verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, <hi type="italic">that</hi> his burden shall be taken away from off thy shoulder, and his yoke from off thy neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:28
verses.text: He is come to Aiath, he is passed to Migron; at Michmash he hath laid up his carriages:

verses.name: Isaiah 10:29
verses.text: They are gone over the passage: they have taken up their lodging at Geba; Ramah is afraid; Gibeah of Saul is fled.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:30
verses.text: Lift up thy voice, O daughter of Gallim: cause it to be heard unto Laish, O poor Anathoth.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:31
verses.text: Madmenah is removed; the inhabitants of Gebim gather themselves to flee.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:32
verses.text: As yet shall he remain at Nob that day: he shall shake his hand <hi type="italic">against</hi> the mount of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:33
verses.text: Behold, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, shall lop the bough with terror: and the high ones of stature <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> hewn down, and the haughty shall be humbled.

verses.name: Isaiah 10:34
verses.text: And he shall cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one.  <chapter eID="Isa.10"/><div eID="gen756" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 11:1
verses.text: AND there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots:

verses.name: Isaiah 11:2
verses.text: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord;

verses.name: Isaiah 11:3
verses.text: And shall make him of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord: and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears:

verses.name: Isaiah 11:4
verses.text: But with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.

verses.name: Isaiah 11:5
verses.text: And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and faithfulness the girdle of his reins.

verses.name: Isaiah 11:6
verses.text: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.

verses.name: Isaiah 11:7
verses.text: And the cow and the bear shall feed; their young ones shall lie down together: and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.

verses.name: Isaiah 11:8
verses.text: And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice’ den.

verses.name: Isaiah 11:9
verses.text: They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain: for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.

verses.name: Isaiah 11:10
verses.text: ¶ And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.

verses.name: Isaiah 11:11
verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.

verses.name: Isaiah 11:12
verses.text: And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

verses.name: Isaiah 11:13
verses.text: The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.

verses.name: Isaiah 11:14
verses.text: But they shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines toward the west; they shall spoil them of the east together: they shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moab; and the children of Ammon shall obey them.

verses.name: Isaiah 11:15
verses.text: And the Lord shall utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his mighty wind shall he shake his hand over the river, and shall smite it in the seven streams, and make <hi type="italic">men</hi> go over dryshod.

verses.name: Isaiah 11:16
verses.text: And there shall be an highway for the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria; like as it was to Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.  <chapter eID="Isa.11"/><div eID="gen757" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 12:1
verses.text: AND in that day thou shalt say, O Lord, I will praise thee: though thou wast angry with me, thine anger is turned away, and thou comfortedst me.

verses.name: Isaiah 12:2
verses.text: Behold, God <hi type="italic">is</hi> my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid: for the Lord JEHOVAH <hi type="italic">is</hi> my strength and <hi type="italic">my</hi> song; he also is become my salvation.

verses.name: Isaiah 12:3
verses.text: Therefore with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation.

verses.name: Isaiah 12:4
verses.text: And in that day shall ye say, Praise the Lord, call upon his name, declare his doings among the people, make mention that his name is exalted.

verses.name: Isaiah 12:5
verses.text: Sing unto the Lord; for he hath done excellent things: this <hi type="italic">is</hi> known in all the earth.

verses.name: Isaiah 12:6
verses.text: Cry out and shout, thou inhabitant of Zion: for great <hi type="italic">is</hi> the Holy One of Israel in the midst of thee.  <chapter eID="Isa.12"/><div eID="gen758" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 13:1
verses.text: THE burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:2
verses.text: Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain, exalt the voice unto them, shake the hand, that they may go into the gates of the nobles.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:3
verses.text: I have commanded my sanctified ones, I have also called my mighty ones for mine anger, <hi type="italic">even</hi> them that rejoice in my highness.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:4
verses.text: The noise of a multitude in the mountains, like as of a great people; a tumultuous noise of the kingdoms of nations gathered together: the Lord of hosts mustereth the host of the battle.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:5
verses.text: They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the Lord, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:6
verses.text: ¶ Howl ye; for the day of the Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> at hand; it shall come as a destruction from the Almighty.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:7
verses.text: Therefore shall all hands be faint, and every man’s heart shall melt:

verses.name: Isaiah 13:8
verses.text: And they shall be afraid: pangs and sorrows shall take hold of them; they shall be in pain as a woman that travaileth: they shall be amazed one at another; their faces <hi type="italic">shall be as</hi> flames.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:9
verses.text: Behold, the day of the Lord cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:10
verses.text: For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:11
verses.text: And I will punish the world for <hi type="italic">their</hi> evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; and I will cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease, and will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:12
verses.text: I will make a man more precious than fine gold; even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:13
verses.text: Therefore I will shake the heavens, and the earth shall remove out of her place, in the wrath of the Lord of hosts, and in the day of his fierce anger.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:14
verses.text: And it shall be as the chased roe, and as a sheep that no man taketh up: they shall every man turn to his own people, and flee every one into his own land.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:15
verses.text: Every one that is found shall be thrust through; and every one that is joined <hi type="italic">unto them</hi> shall fall by the sword.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:16
verses.text: Their children also shall be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses shall be spoiled, and their wives ravished.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:17
verses.text: Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, which shall not regard silver; and <hi type="italic">as for</hi> gold, they shall not delight in it.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:18
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Their</hi> bows also shall dash the young men to pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:19
verses.text: ¶ And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:20
verses.text: It shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation: neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there; neither shall the shepherds make their fold there.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:21
verses.text: But wild beasts of the desert shall lie there; and their houses shall be full of doleful creatures; and owls shall dwell there, and satyrs shall dance there.

verses.name: Isaiah 13:22
verses.text: And the wild beasts of the islands shall cry in their desolate houses, and dragons in <hi type="italic">their</hi> pleasant palaces: and her time <hi type="italic">is</hi> near to come, and her days shall not be prolonged.  <chapter eID="Isa.13"/><div eID="gen759" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 14:1
verses.text: FOR the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:2
verses.text: And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:3
verses.text: And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve,

verses.name: Isaiah 14:4
verses.text: ¶ That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!

verses.name: Isaiah 14:5
verses.text: The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the sceptre of the rulers.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:6
verses.text: He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke, he that ruled the nations in anger, is persecuted, <hi type="italic">and</hi> none hindereth.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:7
verses.text: The whole earth is at rest, <hi type="italic">and</hi> is quiet: they break forth into singing.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:8
verses.text: Yea, the fir trees rejoice at thee, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the cedars of Lebanon, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, Since thou art laid down, no feller is come up against us.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:9
verses.text: Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet <hi type="italic">thee</hi> at thy coming: it stirreth up the dead for thee, <hi type="italic">even</hi> all the chief ones of the earth; it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:10
verses.text: All they shall speak and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?

verses.name: Isaiah 14:11
verses.text: Thy pomp is brought down to the grave, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the noise of thy viols: the worm is spread under thee, and the worms cover thee.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:12
verses.text: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! <hi type="italic">how</hi> art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!

verses.name: Isaiah 14:13
verses.text: For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north:

verses.name: Isaiah 14:14
verses.text: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:15
verses.text: Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:16
verses.text: They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, <hi type="italic">and</hi> consider thee, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, <hi type="italic">Is</hi> this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms;

verses.name: Isaiah 14:17
verses.text: <hi type="italic">That</hi> made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof; <hi type="italic">that</hi> opened not the house of his prisoners?

verses.name: Isaiah 14:18
verses.text: All the kings of the nations, <hi type="italic">even</hi> all of them, lie in glory, every one in his own house.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:19
verses.text: But thou art cast out of thy grave like an abominable branch, <hi type="italic">and as</hi> the raiment of those that are slain, thrust through with a sword, that go down to the stones of the pit; as a carcase trodden under feet.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:20
verses.text: Thou shalt not be joined with them in burial, because thou hast destroyed thy land, <hi type="italic">and</hi> slain thy people: the seed of evildoers shall never be renowned.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:21
verses.text: Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:22
verses.text: For I will rise up against them, saith the Lord of hosts, and cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew, saith the Lord.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:23
verses.text: I will also make it a possession for the bittern, and pools of water: and I will sweep it with the besom of destruction, saith the Lord of hosts.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:24
verses.text: ¶ The Lord of hosts hath sworn, saying, Surely as I have thought, so shall it come to pass; and as I have purposed, <hi type="italic">so</hi> shall it stand:

verses.name: Isaiah 14:25
verses.text: That I will break the Assyrian in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot: then shall his yoke depart from off them, and his burden depart from off their shoulders.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:26
verses.text: This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the purpose that is purposed upon the whole earth: and this <hi type="italic">is</hi> the hand that is stretched out upon all the nations.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:27
verses.text: For the Lord of hosts hath purposed, and who shall disannul <hi type="italic">it?</hi> and his hand <hi type="italic">is</hi> stretched out, and who shall turn it back?

verses.name: Isaiah 14:28
verses.text: In the year that king Ahaz died was this burden.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:29
verses.text: ¶ Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina, because the rod of him that smote thee is broken: for out of the serpent’s root shall come forth a cockatrice, and his fruit <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> a fiery flying serpent.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:30
verses.text: And the firstborn of the poor shall feed, and the needy shall lie down in safety: and I will kill thy root with famine, and he shall slay thy remnant.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:31
verses.text: Howl, O gate; cry, O city; thou, whole Palestina, <hi type="italic">art</hi> dissolved: for there shall come from the north a smoke, and none <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> alone in his appointed times.

verses.name: Isaiah 14:32
verses.text: What shall <hi type="italic">one</hi> then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.  <chapter eID="Isa.14"/><div eID="gen760" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 15:1
verses.text: THE burden of Moab. Because in the night Ar of Moab is laid waste, <hi type="italic">and</hi> brought to silence; because in the night Kir of Moab is laid waste, <hi type="italic">and</hi> brought to silence;

verses.name: Isaiah 15:2
verses.text: He is gone up to Bajith, and to Dibon, the high places, to weep: Moab shall howl over Nebo, and over Medeba: on all their heads <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> baldness, <hi type="italic">and</hi> every beard cut off.

verses.name: Isaiah 15:3
verses.text: In their streets they shall gird themselves with sackcloth: on the tops of their houses, and in their streets, every one shall howl, weeping abundantly.

verses.name: Isaiah 15:4
verses.text: And Heshbon shall cry, and Elealeh: their voice shall be heard <hi type="italic">even</hi> unto Jahaz: therefore the armed soldiers of Moab shall cry out; his life shall be grievous unto him.

verses.name: Isaiah 15:5
verses.text: My heart shall cry out for Moab; his fugitives <hi type="italic">shall flee</hi> unto Zoar, an heifer of three years old: for by the mounting up of Luhith with weeping shall they go it up; for in the way of Horonaim they shall raise up a cry of destruction.

verses.name: Isaiah 15:6
verses.text: For the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate: for the hay is withered away, the grass faileth, there is no green thing.

verses.name: Isaiah 15:7
verses.text: Therefore the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have laid up, shall they carry away to the brook of the willows.

verses.name: Isaiah 15:8
verses.text: For the cry is gone round about the borders of Moab; the howling thereof unto Eglaim, and the howling thereof unto Beer-elim.

verses.name: Isaiah 15:9
verses.text: For the waters of Dimon shall be full of blood: for I will bring more upon Dimon, lions upon him that escapeth of Moab, and upon the remnant of the land.  <chapter eID="Isa.15"/><div eID="gen761" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 16:1
verses.text: SEND ye the lamb to the ruler of the land from Sela to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:2
verses.text: For it shall be, <hi type="italic">that</hi>, as a wandering bird cast out of the nest, <hi type="italic">so</hi> the daughters of Moab shall be at the fords of Arnon.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:3
verses.text: Take counsel, execute judgment; make thy shadow as the night in the midst of the noonday; hide the outcasts; bewray not him that wandereth.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:4
verses.text: Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab; be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler: for the extortioner is at an end, the spoiler ceaseth, the oppressors are consumed out of the land.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:5
verses.text: And in mercy shall the throne be established: and he shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging, and seeking judgment, and hasting righteousness.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:6
verses.text: ¶ We have heard of the pride of Moab; <hi type="italic">he is</hi> very proud: <hi type="italic">even</hi> of his haughtiness, and his pride, and his wrath: <hi type="italic">but</hi> his lies <hi type="italic">shall</hi> not <hi type="italic">be</hi> so.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:7
verses.text: Therefore shall Moab howl for Moab, every one shall howl: for the foundations of Kir-hareseth shall ye mourn; surely <hi type="italic">they are</hi> stricken.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:8
verses.text: For the fields of Heshbon languish, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the vine of Sibmah: the lords of the heathen have broken down the principal plants thereof, they are come <hi type="italic">even</hi> unto Jazer, they wandered <hi type="italic">through</hi> the wilderness: her branches are stretched out, they are gone over the sea.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:9
verses.text: ¶ Therefore I will bewail with the weeping of Jazer the vine of Sibmah: I will water thee with my tears, O Heshbon, and Elealeh: for the shouting for thy summer fruits and for thy harvest is fallen.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:10
verses.text: And gladness is taken away, and joy out of the plentiful field; and in the vineyards there shall be no singing, neither shall there be shouting: the treaders shall tread out no wine in <hi type="italic">their</hi> presses; I have made <hi type="italic">their vintage</hi> shouting to cease.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:11
verses.text: Wherefore my bowels shall sound like an harp for Moab, and mine inward parts for Kir-haresh.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:12
verses.text: ¶ And it shall come to pass, when it is seen that Moab is weary on the high place, that he shall come to his sanctuary to pray; but he shall not prevail.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:13
verses.text: This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the word that the Lord hath spoken concerning Moab since that time.

verses.name: Isaiah 16:14
verses.text: But now the Lord hath spoken, saying, Within three years, as the years of an hireling, and the glory of Moab shall be contemned, with all that great multitude; and the remnant <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> very small <hi type="italic">and</hi> feeble.  <chapter eID="Isa.16"/><div eID="gen762" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 17:1
verses.text: THE burden of Damascus. Behold, Damascus is taken away from <hi type="italic">being</hi> a city, and it shall be a ruinous heap.

verses.name: Isaiah 17:2
verses.text: The cities of Aroer <hi type="italic">are</hi> forsaken: they shall be for flocks, which shall lie down, and none shall make <hi type="italic">them</hi> afraid.

verses.name: Isaiah 17:3
verses.text: The fortress also shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria: they shall be as the glory of the children of Israel, saith the Lord of hosts.

verses.name: Isaiah 17:4
verses.text: And in that day it shall come to pass, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the glory of Jacob shall be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh shall wax lean.

verses.name: Isaiah 17:5
verses.text: And it shall be as when the harvestman gathereth the corn, and reapeth the ears with his arm; and it shall be as he that gathereth ears in the valley of Rephaim.

verses.name: Isaiah 17:6
verses.text: ¶ Yet gleaning grapes shall be left in it, as the shaking of an olive tree, two <hi type="italic">or</hi> three berries in the top of the uppermost bough, four <hi type="italic">or</hi> five in the outmost fruitful branches thereof, saith the Lord God of Israel.

verses.name: Isaiah 17:7
verses.text: At that day shall a man look to his Maker, and his eyes shall have respect to the Holy One of Israel.

verses.name: Isaiah 17:8
verses.text: And he shall not look to the altars, the work of his hands, neither shall respect <hi type="italic">that</hi> which his fingers have made, either the groves, or the images.

verses.name: Isaiah 17:9
verses.text: ¶ In that day shall his strong cities be as a forsaken bough, and an uppermost branch, which they left because of the children of Israel: and there shall be desolation.

verses.name: Isaiah 17:10
verses.text: Because thou hast forgotten the God of thy salvation, and hast not been mindful of the rock of thy strength, therefore shalt thou plant pleasant plants, and shalt set it with strange slips:

verses.name: Isaiah 17:11
verses.text: In the day shalt thou make thy plant to grow, and in the morning shalt thou make thy seed to flourish: <hi type="italic">but</hi> the harvest <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> a heap in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow.

verses.name: Isaiah 17:12
verses.text: ¶ Woe to the multitude of many people, <hi type="italic">which</hi> make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, <hi type="italic">that</hi> make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!

verses.name: Isaiah 17:13
verses.text: The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters: but <hi type="italic">God</hi> shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thing before the whirlwind.

verses.name: Isaiah 17:14
verses.text: And behold at eveningtide trouble; <hi type="italic">and</hi> before the morning he <hi type="italic">is</hi> not. This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the portion of them that spoil us, and the lot of them that rob us.  <chapter eID="Isa.17"/><div eID="gen763" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 18:1
verses.text: WOE to the land shadowing with wings, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> beyond the rivers of Ethiopia:

verses.name: Isaiah 18:2
verses.text: That sendeth ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of bulrushes upon the waters, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, Go, ye swift messengers, to a nation scattered and peeled, to a people terrible from their beginning hitherto; a nation meted out and trodden down, whose land the rivers have spoiled!

verses.name: Isaiah 18:3
verses.text: All ye inhabitants of the world, and dwellers on the earth, see ye, when he lifteth up an ensign on the mountains; and when he bloweth a trumpet, hear ye.

verses.name: Isaiah 18:4
verses.text: For so the Lord said unto me, I will take my rest, and I will consider in my dwelling place like a clear heat upon herbs, <hi type="italic">and</hi> like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.

verses.name: Isaiah 18:5
verses.text: For afore the harvest, when the bud is perfect, and the sour grape is ripening in the flower, he shall both cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and take away <hi type="italic">and</hi> cut down the branches.

verses.name: Isaiah 18:6
verses.text: They shall be left together unto the fowls of the mountains, and to the beasts of the earth: and the fowls shall summer upon them, and all the beasts of the earth shall winter upon them.

verses.name: Isaiah 18:7
verses.text: ¶ In that time shall the present be brought unto the Lord of hosts of a people scattered and peeled, and from a people terrible from their beginning hitherto; a nation meted out and trodden under foot, whose land the rivers have spoiled, to the place of the name of the Lord of hosts, the mount Zion.  <chapter eID="Isa.18"/><div eID="gen764" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 19:1
verses.text: THE burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst of it.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:2
verses.text: And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, <hi type="italic">and</hi> kingdom against kingdom.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:3
verses.text: And the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof; and I will destroy the counsel thereof: and they shall seek to the idols, and to the charmers, and to them that have familiar spirits, and to the wizards.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:4
verses.text: And the Egyptians will I give over into the hand of a cruel lord; and a fierce king shall rule over them, saith the Lord, the Lord of hosts.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:5
verses.text: And the waters shall fail from the sea, and the river shall be wasted and dried up.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:6
verses.text: And they shall turn the rivers far away; <hi type="italic">and</hi> the brooks of defence shall be emptied and dried up: the reeds and flags shall wither.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:7
verses.text: The paper reeds by the brooks, by the mouth of the brooks, and every thing sown by the brooks, shall wither, be driven away, and be no <hi type="italic">more</hi>.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:8
verses.text: The fishers also shall mourn, and all they that cast angle into the brooks shall lament, and they that spread nets upon the waters shall languish.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:9
verses.text: Moreover they that work in fine flax, and they that weave networks, shall be confounded.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:10
verses.text: And they shall be broken in the purposes thereof, all that make sluices <hi type="italic">and</hi> ponds for fish.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:11
verses.text: ¶ Surely the princes of Zoan <hi type="italic">are</hi> fools, the counsel of the wise counsellers of Pharaoh is become brutish: how say ye unto Pharaoh, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?

verses.name: Isaiah 19:12
verses.text: Where <hi type="italic">are</hi> they? where <hi type="italic">are</hi> thy wise <hi type="italic">men?</hi> and let them tell thee now, and let them know what the Lord of hosts hath purposed upon Egypt.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:13
verses.text: The princes of Zoan are become fools, the princes of Noph are deceived; they have also seduced Egypt, <hi type="italic">even they that are</hi> the stay of the tribes thereof.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:14
verses.text: The Lord hath mingled a perverse spirit in the midst thereof: and they have caused Egypt to err in every work thereof, as a drunken <hi type="italic">man</hi> staggereth in his vomit.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:15
verses.text: Neither shall there be <hi type="italic">any</hi> work for Egypt, which the head or tail, branch or rush, may do.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:16
verses.text: In that day shall Egypt be like unto women: and it shall be afraid and fear because of the shaking of the hand of the Lord of hosts, which he shaketh over it.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:17
verses.text: And the land of Judah shall be a terror unto Egypt, every one that maketh mention thereof shall be afraid in himself, because of the counsel of the Lord of hosts, which he hath determined against it.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:18
verses.text: ¶ In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the Lord of hosts; one shall be called, The city of destruction.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:19
verses.text: In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to the Lord.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:20
verses.text: And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:21
verses.text: And the Lord shall be known to Egypt, and the Egyptians shall know the Lord in that day, and shall do sacrifice and oblation; yea, they shall vow a vow unto the Lord, and perform <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:22
verses.text: And the Lord shall smite Egypt: he shall smite and heal <hi type="italic">it:</hi> and they shall return <hi type="italic">even</hi> to the Lord, and he shall be intreated of them, and shall heal them.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:23
verses.text: ¶ In that day shall there be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria, and the Assyrian shall come into Egypt, and the Egyptian into Assyria, and the Egyptians shall serve with the Assyrians.

verses.name: Isaiah 19:24
verses.text: In that day shall Israel be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, <hi type="italic">even</hi> a blessing in the midst of the land:

verses.name: Isaiah 19:25
verses.text: Whom the Lord of hosts shall bless, saying, Blessed <hi type="italic">be</hi> Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance.  <chapter eID="Isa.19"/><div eID="gen765" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 20:1
verses.text: IN the year that Tartan came unto Ashdod, (when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him,) and fought against Ashdod, and took it;

verses.name: Isaiah 20:2
verses.text: At the same time spake the Lord by Isaiah the son of Amoz, saying, Go and loose the sackcloth from off thy loins, and put off thy shoe from thy foot. And he did so, walking naked and barefoot.

verses.name: Isaiah 20:3
verses.text: And the Lord said, Like as my servant Isaiah hath walked naked and barefoot three years <hi type="italic">for</hi> a sign and wonder upon Egypt and upon Ethiopia;

verses.name: Isaiah 20:4
verses.text: So shall the king of Assyria lead away the Egyptians prisoners, and the Ethiopians captives, young and old, naked and barefoot, even with <hi type="italic">their</hi> buttocks uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.

verses.name: Isaiah 20:5
verses.text: And they shall be afraid and ashamed of Ethiopia their expectation, and of Egypt their glory.

verses.name: Isaiah 20:6
verses.text: And the inhabitant of this isle shall say in that day, Behold, such <hi type="italic">is</hi> our expectation, whither we flee for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria: and how shall we escape?  <chapter eID="Isa.20"/><div eID="gen766" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 21:1
verses.text: THE burden of the desert of the sea. As whirlwinds in the south pass through; <hi type="italic">so</hi> it cometh from the desert, from a terrible land.

verses.name: Isaiah 21:2
verses.text: A grievous vision is declared unto me; the treacherous dealer dealeth treacherously, and the spoiler spoileth. Go up, O Elam: besiege, O Media; all the sighing thereof have I made to cease.

verses.name: Isaiah 21:3
verses.text: Therefore are my loins filled with pain: pangs have taken hold upon me, as the pangs of a woman that travaileth: I was bowed down at the hearing <hi type="italic">of it;</hi> I was dismayed at the seeing <hi type="italic">of it</hi>.

verses.name: Isaiah 21:4
verses.text: My heart panted, fearfulness affrighted me: the night of my pleasure hath he turned into fear unto me.

verses.name: Isaiah 21:5
verses.text: Prepare the table, watch in the watchtower, eat, drink: arise, ye princes, <hi type="italic">and</hi> anoint the shield.

verses.name: Isaiah 21:6
verses.text: For thus hath the Lord said unto me, Go, set a watchman, let him declare what he seeth.

verses.name: Isaiah 21:7
verses.text: And he saw a chariot <hi type="italic">with</hi> a couple of horsemen, a chariot of asses, <hi type="italic">and</hi> a chariot of camels; and he hearkened diligently with much heed:

verses.name: Isaiah 21:8
verses.text: And he cried, A lion: My lord, I stand continually upon the watchtower in the daytime, and I am set in my ward whole nights:

verses.name: Isaiah 21:9
verses.text: And, behold, here cometh a chariot of men, <hi type="italic">with</hi> a couple of horsemen. And he answered and said, Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all the graven images of her gods he hath broken unto the ground.

verses.name: Isaiah 21:10
verses.text: O my threshing, and the corn of my floor: that which I have heard of the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, have I declared unto you.

verses.name: Isaiah 21:11
verses.text: ¶ The burden of Dumah. He calleth to me out of Seir, Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?

verses.name: Isaiah 21:12
verses.text: The watchman said, The morning cometh, and also the night: if ye will inquire, inquire ye: return, come.

verses.name: Isaiah 21:13
verses.text: ¶ The burden upon Arabia. In the forest in Arabia shall ye lodge, O ye travelling companies of Dedanim.

verses.name: Isaiah 21:14
verses.text: The inhabitants of the land of Tema brought water to him that was thirsty, they prevented with their bread him that fled.

verses.name: Isaiah 21:15
verses.text: For they fled from the swords, from the drawn sword, and from the bent bow, and from the grievousness of war.

verses.name: Isaiah 21:16
verses.text: For thus hath the Lord said unto me, Within a year, according to the years of an hireling, and all the glory of Kedar shall fail:

verses.name: Isaiah 21:17
verses.text: And the residue of the number of archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar, shall be diminished: for the Lord God of Israel hath spoken <hi type="italic">it</hi>.  <chapter eID="Isa.21"/><div eID="gen767" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 22:1
verses.text: THE burden of the valley of vision. What aileth thee now, that thou art wholly gone up to the housetops?

verses.name: Isaiah 22:2
verses.text: Thou that art full of stirs, a tumultuous city, a joyous city: thy slain <hi type="italic">men are</hi> not slain with the sword, nor dead in battle.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:3
verses.text: All thy rulers are fled together, they are bound by the archers: all that are found in thee are bound together, <hi type="italic">which</hi> have fled from far.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:4
verses.text: Therefore said I, Look away from me; I will weep bitterly, labour not to comfort me, because of the spoiling of the daughter of my people.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:5
verses.text: For <hi type="italic">it is</hi> a day of trouble, and of treading down, and of perplexity by the Lord God of hosts in the valley of vision, breaking down the walls, and of crying to the mountains.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:6
verses.text: And Elam bare the quiver with chariots of men <hi type="italic">and</hi> horsemen, and Kir uncovered the shield.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:7
verses.text: And it shall come to pass, <hi type="italic">that</hi> thy choicest valleys shall be full of chariots, and the horsemen shall set themselves in array at the gate.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:8
verses.text: ¶ And he discovered the covering of Judah, and thou didst look in that day to the armour of the house of the forest.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:9
verses.text: Ye have seen also the breaches of the city of David, that they are many: and ye gathered together the waters of the lower pool.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:10
verses.text: And ye have numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and the houses have ye broken down to fortify the wall.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:11
verses.text: Ye made also a ditch between the two walls for the water of the old pool: but ye have not looked unto the maker thereof, neither had respect unto him that fashioned it long ago.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:12
verses.text: And in that day did the Lord God of hosts call to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to girding with sackcloth:

verses.name: Isaiah 22:13
verses.text: And behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen, and killing sheep, eating flesh, and drinking wine: let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:14
verses.text: And it was revealed in mine ears by the Lord of hosts, Surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till ye die, saith the Lord God of hosts.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:15
verses.text: ¶ Thus saith the Lord God of hosts, Go, get thee unto this treasurer, <hi type="italic">even</hi> unto Shebna, which <hi type="italic">is</hi> over the house, <hi type="italic">and say</hi>,

verses.name: Isaiah 22:16
verses.text: What hast thou here? and whom hast thou here, that thou hast hewed thee out a sepulchre here, <hi type="italic">as</hi> he that heweth him out a sepulchre on high, <hi type="italic">and</hi> that graveth an habitation for himself in a rock?

verses.name: Isaiah 22:17
verses.text: Behold, the Lord will carry thee away with a mighty captivity, and will surely cover thee.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:18
verses.text: He will surely violently turn and toss thee <hi type="italic">like</hi> a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die, and there the chariots of thy glory <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> the shame of thy lord’s house.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:19
verses.text: And I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall he pull thee down.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:20
verses.text: ¶ And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah:

verses.name: Isaiah 22:21
verses.text: And I will clothe him with thy robe, and strengthen him with thy girdle, and I will commit thy government into his hand: and he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:22
verses.text: And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:23
verses.text: And I will fasten him <hi type="italic">as</hi> a nail in a sure place; and he shall be for a glorious throne to his father’s house.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:24
verses.text: And they shall hang upon him all the glory of his father’s house, the offspring and the issue, all vessels of small quantity, from the vessels of cups, even to all the vessels of flagons.

verses.name: Isaiah 22:25
verses.text: In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, shall the nail that is fastened in the sure place be removed, and be cut down, and fall; and the burden that <hi type="italic">was</hi> upon it shall be cut off: for the Lord hath spoken <hi type="italic">it</hi>.  <chapter eID="Isa.22"/><div eID="gen768" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Isaiah 23:1
verses.text: THE burden of Tyre. Howl, ye ships of Tarshish; for it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in: from the land of Chittim it is revealed to them.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:2
verses.text: Be still, ye inhabitants of the isle; thou whom the merchants of Zidon, that pass over the sea, have replenished.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:3
verses.text: And by great waters the seed of Sihor, the harvest of the river, <hi type="italic">is</hi> her revenue; and she is a mart of nations.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:4
verses.text: Be thou ashamed, O Zidon: for the sea hath spoken, <hi type="italic">even</hi> the strength of the sea, saying, I travail not, nor bring forth children, neither do I nourish up young men, <hi type="italic">nor</hi> bring up virgins.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:5
verses.text: As at the report concerning Egypt, <hi type="italic">so</hi> shall they be sorely pained at the report of Tyre.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:6
verses.text: Pass ye over to Tarshish; howl, ye inhabitants of the isle.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:7
verses.text: <hi type="italic">Is</hi> this your joyous <hi type="italic">city</hi>, whose antiquity <hi type="italic">is</hi> of ancient days? her own feet shall carry her afar off to sojourn.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:8
verses.text: Who hath taken this counsel against Tyre, the crowning <hi type="italic">city</hi>, whose merchants <hi type="italic">are</hi> princes, whose traffickers <hi type="italic">are</hi> the honourable of the earth?

verses.name: Isaiah 23:9
verses.text: The Lord of hosts hath purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory, <hi type="italic">and</hi> to bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:10
verses.text: Pass through thy land as a river, O daughter of Tarshish: <hi type="italic">there is</hi> no more strength.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:11
verses.text: He stretched out his hand over the sea, he shook the kingdoms: the Lord hath given a commandment against the merchant <hi type="italic">city</hi>, to destroy the strong holds thereof.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:12
verses.text: And he said, Thou shalt no more rejoice, O thou oppressed virgin, daughter of Zidon: arise, pass over to Chittim; there also shalt thou have no rest.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:13
verses.text: Behold the land of the Chaldeans; this people was not, <hi type="italic">till</hi> the Assyrian founded it for them that dwell in the wilderness: they set up the towers thereof, they raised up the palaces thereof; <hi type="italic">and</hi> he brought it to ruin.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:14
verses.text: Howl, ye ships of Tarshish: for your strength is laid waste.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:15
verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king: after the end of seventy years shall Tyre sing as an harlot.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:16
verses.text: Take an harp, go about the city, thou harlot that hast been forgotten; make sweet melody, sing many songs, that thou mayest be remembered.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:17
verses.text: ¶ And it shall come to pass after the end of seventy years, that the Lord will visit Tyre, and she shall turn to her hire, and shall commit fornication with all the kingdoms of the world upon the face of the earth.

verses.name: Isaiah 23:18
