verses.text: The violence done to me and to my flesh <hi type="italic">be</hi> upon Babylon, shall the inhabitant of Zion say; and my blood upon the inhabitants of Chaldea, shall Jerusalem say.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:36
verses.text: Therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will plead thy cause, and take vengeance for thee; and I will dry up her sea, and make her springs dry.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:37
verses.text: And Babylon shall become heaps, a dwellingplace for dragons, an astonishment, and an hissing, without an inhabitant.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:38
verses.text: They shall roar together like lions: they shall yell as lions’ whelps.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:39
verses.text: In their heat I will make their feasts, and I will make them drunken, that they may rejoice, and sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake, saith the Lord.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:40
verses.text: I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with he goats.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:41
verses.text: How is Sheshach taken! and how is the praise of the whole earth surprised! how is Babylon become an astonishment among the nations!

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:42
verses.text: The sea is come up upon Babylon: she is covered with the multitude of the waves thereof.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:43
verses.text: Her cities are a desolation, a dry land, and a wilderness, a land wherein no man dwelleth, neither doth <hi type="italic">any</hi> son of man pass thereby.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:44
verses.text: And I will punish Bel in Babylon, and I will bring forth out of his mouth that which he hath swallowed up: and the nations shall not flow together any more unto him: yea, the wall of Babylon shall fall.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:45
verses.text: My people, go ye out of the midst of her, and deliver ye every man his soul from the fierce anger of the Lord.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:46
verses.text: And lest your heart faint, and ye fear for the rumour that shall be heard in the land; a rumour shall both come <hi type="italic">one</hi> year, and after that in <hi type="italic">another</hi> year <hi type="italic">shall come</hi> a rumour, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:47
verses.text: Therefore, behold, the days come, that I will do judgment upon the graven images of Babylon: and her whole land shall be confounded, and all her slain shall fall in the midst of her.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:48
verses.text: Then the heaven and the earth, and all that <hi type="italic">is</hi> therein, shall sing for Babylon: for the spoilers shall come unto her from the north, saith the Lord.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:49
verses.text: As Babylon <hi type="italic">hath caused</hi> the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:50
verses.text: Ye that have escaped the sword, go away, stand not still: remember the Lord afar off, and let Jerusalem come into your mind.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:51
verses.text: We are confounded, because we have heard reproach: shame hath covered our faces: for strangers are come into the sanctuaries of the Lord’s house.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:52
verses.text: Wherefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will do judgment upon her graven images: and through all her land the wounded shall groan.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:53
verses.text: Though Babylon should mount up to heaven, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, <hi type="italic">yet</hi> from me shall spoilers come unto her, saith the Lord.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:54
verses.text: A sound of a cry <hi type="italic">cometh</hi> from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans:

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:55
verses.text: Because the Lord hath spoiled Babylon, and destroyed out of her the great voice; when her waves do roar like great waters, a noise of their voice is uttered:

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:56
verses.text: Because the spoiler is come upon her, <hi type="italic">even</hi> upon Babylon, and her mighty men are taken, every one of their bows is broken: for the Lord God of recompences shall surely requite.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:57
verses.text: And I will make drunk her princes, and her wise <hi type="italic">men</hi>, her captains, and her rulers, and her mighty men: and they shall sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake, saith the King, whose name <hi type="italic">is</hi> the Lord of hosts.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:58
verses.text: Thus saith the Lord of hosts; The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken, and her high gates shall be burned with fire; and the people shall labour in vain, and the folk in the fire, and they shall be weary.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:59
verses.text: ¶ The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, when he went with Zedekiah the king of Judah into Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. And <hi type="italic">this</hi> Seraiah <hi type="italic">was</hi> a quiet prince.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:60
verses.text: So Jeremiah wrote in a book all the evil that should come upon Babylon, <hi type="italic">even</hi> all these words that are written against Babylon.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:61
verses.text: And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, When thou comest to Babylon, and shalt see, and shalt read all these words;

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:62
verses.text: Then shalt thou say, O Lord, thou hast spoken against this place, to cut it off, that none shall remain in it, neither man nor beast, but that it shall be desolate for ever.

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:63
verses.text: And it shall be, when thou hast made an end of reading this book, <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou shalt bind a stone to it, and cast it into the midst of Euphrates:

verses.name: Jeremiah 51:64
verses.text: And thou shalt say, Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise from the evil that I will bring upon her: and they shall be weary. Thus far <hi type="italic">are</hi> the words of Jeremiah.  <chapter eID="Jer.51"/><div eID="gen864" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:1
verses.text: ZEDEKIAH <hi type="italic">was</hi> one and twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name <hi type="italic">was</hi> Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:2
verses.text: And he did <hi type="italic">that which was</hi> evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:3
verses.text: For through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, till he had cast them out from his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:4
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the month, <hi type="italic">that</hi> Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and pitched against it, and built forts against it round about.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:5
verses.text: So the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:6
verses.text: And in the fourth month, in the ninth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the month, the famine was sore in the city, so that there was no bread for the people of the land.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:7
verses.text: Then the city was broken up, and all the men of war fled, and went forth out of the city by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, which <hi type="italic">was</hi> by the king’s garden; (now the Chaldeans <hi type="italic">were</hi> by the city round about:) and they went by the way of the plain.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:8
verses.text: ¶ But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:9
verses.text: Then they took the king, and carried him up unto the king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath; where he gave judgment upon him.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:10
verses.text: And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes: he slew also all the princes of Judah in Riblah.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:11
verses.text: Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in chains, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:12
verses.text: ¶ Now in the fifth month, in the tenth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the month, which <hi type="italic">was</hi> the nineteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzar-adan, captain of the guard, <hi type="italic">which</hi> served the king of Babylon, into Jerusalem,

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:13
verses.text: And burned the house of the Lord, and the king’s house; and all the houses of Jerusalem, and all the houses of the great <hi type="italic">men</hi>, burned he with fire:

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:14
verses.text: And all the army of the Chaldeans, that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with the captain of the guard, brake down all the walls of Jerusalem round about.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:15
verses.text: Then Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard carried away captive <hi type="italic">certain</hi> of the poor of the people, and the residue of the people that remained in the city, and those that fell away, that fell to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:16
verses.text: But Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard left <hi type="italic">certain</hi> of the poor of the land for vinedressers and for husbandmen.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:17
verses.text: Also the pillars of brass that <hi type="italic">were</hi> in the house of the Lord, and the bases, and the brasen sea that <hi type="italic">was</hi> in the house of the Lord, the Chaldeans brake, and carried all the brass of them to Babylon.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:18
verses.text: The caldrons also, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the bowls, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered, took they away.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:19
verses.text: And the basons, and the firepans, and the bowls, and the caldrons, and the candlesticks, and the spoons, and the cups; <hi type="italic">that</hi> which <hi type="italic">was</hi> of gold <hi type="italic">in</hi> gold, and <hi type="italic">that</hi> which <hi type="italic">was</hi> of silver <hi type="italic">in</hi> silver, took the captain of the guard away.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:20
verses.text: The two pillars, one sea, and twelve brasen bulls that <hi type="italic">were</hi> under the bases, which king Solomon had made in the house of the Lord: the brass of all these vessels was without weight.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:21
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">concerning</hi> the pillars, the height of one pillar <hi type="italic">was</hi> eighteen cubits; and a fillet of twelve cubits did compass it; and the thickness thereof <hi type="italic">was</hi> four fingers: <hi type="italic">it was</hi> hollow.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:22
verses.text: And a chapiter of brass <hi type="italic">was</hi> upon it; and the height of one chapiter <hi type="italic">was</hi> five cubits, with network and pomegranates upon the chapiters round about, all <hi type="italic">of</hi> brass. The second pillar also and the pomegranates <hi type="italic">were</hi> like unto these.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:23
verses.text: And there were ninety and six pomegranates on a side; <hi type="italic">and</hi> all the pomegranates upon the network <hi type="italic">were</hi> an hundred round about.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:24
verses.text: ¶ And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door:

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:25
verses.text: He took also out of the city an eunuch, which had the charge of the men of war; and seven men of them that were near the king’s person, which were found in the city; and the principal scribe of the host, who mustered the people of the land; and threescore men of the people of the land, that were found in the midst of the city.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:26
verses.text: So Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:27
verses.text: And the king of Babylon smote them, and put them to death in Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away captive out of his own land.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:28
verses.text: This <hi type="italic">is</hi> the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year three thousand Jews and three and twenty:

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:29
verses.text: In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar he carried away captive from Jerusalem eight hundred thirty and two persons:

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:30
verses.text: In the three and twentieth year of Nebuchadrezzar Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred forty and five persons: all the persons <hi type="italic">were</hi> four thousand and six hundred.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:31
verses.text: ¶ And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the five and twentieth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the month, <hi type="italic">that</hi> Evil-merodach king of Babylon in the <hi type="italic">first</hi> year of his reign lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and brought him forth out of prison,

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:32
verses.text: And spake kindly unto him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that <hi type="italic">were</hi> with him in Babylon,

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:33
verses.text: And changed his prison garments: and he did continually eat bread before him all the days of his life.

verses.name: Jeremiah 52:34
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">for</hi> his diet, there was a continual diet given him of the king of Babylon, every day a portion until the day of his death, all the days of his life.  <chapter eID="Jer.52"/><div eID="gen865" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen813" osisID="Jer" type="book"/>

verses.name: Lamentations 1:1
verses.text: HOW doth the city sit solitary, <hi type="italic">that was</hi> full of people! <hi type="italic">how</hi> is she become as a widow! she <hi type="italic">that was</hi> great among the nations, <hi type="italic">and</hi> princess among the provinces, <hi type="italic">how</hi> is she become tributary!

verses.name: Lamentations 1:2
verses.text: She weepeth sore in the night, and her tears <hi type="italic">are</hi> on her cheeks: among all her lovers she hath none to comfort <hi type="italic">her:</hi> all her friends have dealt treacherously with her, they are become her enemies.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:3
verses.text: Judah is gone into captivity because of affliction, and because of great servitude: she dwelleth among the heathen, she findeth no rest: all her persecutors overtook her between the straits.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:4
verses.text: The ways of Zion do mourn, because none come to the solemn feasts: all her gates are desolate: her priests sigh, her virgins are afflicted, and she <hi type="italic">is</hi> in bitterness.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:5
verses.text: Her adversaries are the chief, her enemies prosper; for the Lord hath afflicted her for the multitude of her transgressions: her children are gone into captivity before the enemy.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:6
verses.text: And from the daughter of Zion all her beauty is departed: her princes are become like harts <hi type="italic">that</hi> find no pasture, and they are gone without strength before the pursuer.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:7
verses.text: Jerusalem remembered in the days of her affliction and of her miseries all her pleasant things that she had in the days of old, when her people fell into the hand of the enemy, and none did help her: the adversaries saw her, <hi type="italic">and</hi> did mock at her sabbaths.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:8
verses.text: Jerusalem hath grievously sinned; therefore she is removed: all that honoured her despise her, because they have seen her nakedness: yea, she sigheth, and turneth backward.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:9
verses.text: Her filthiness <hi type="italic">is</hi> in her skirts; she remembereth not her last end; therefore she came down wonderfully: she had no comforter. O Lord, behold my affliction: for the enemy hath magnified <hi type="italic">himself</hi>.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:10
verses.text: The adversary hath spread out his hand upon all her pleasant things: for she hath seen <hi type="italic">that</hi> the heathen entered into her sanctuary, whom thou didst command <hi type="italic">that</hi> they should not enter into thy congregation.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:11
verses.text: All her people sigh, they seek bread; they have given their pleasant things for meat to relieve the soul: see, O Lord, and consider; for I am become vile.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:12
verses.text: ¶ <hi type="italic">Is it</hi> nothing to you, all ye that pass by? behold, and see if there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow, which is done unto me, wherewith the Lord hath afflicted <hi type="italic">me</hi> in the day of his fierce anger.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:13
verses.text: From above hath he sent fire into my bones, and it prevaileth against them: he hath spread a net for my feet, he hath turned me back: he hath made me desolate <hi type="italic">and</hi> faint all the day.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:14
verses.text: The yoke of my transgressions is bound by his hand: they are wreathed, <hi type="italic">and</hi> come up upon my neck: he hath made my strength to fall, the Lord hath delivered me into <hi type="italic">their</hi> hands, <hi type="italic">from whom</hi> I am not able to rise up.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:15
verses.text: The Lord hath trodden under foot all my mighty <hi type="italic">men</hi> in the midst of me: he hath called an assembly against me to crush my young men: the Lord hath trodden the virgin, the daughter of Judah, <hi type="italic">as</hi> in a winepress.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:16
verses.text: For these <hi type="italic">things</hi> I weep; mine eye, mine eye runneth down with water, because the comforter that should relieve my soul is far from me: my children are desolate, because the enemy prevailed.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:17
verses.text: Zion spreadeth forth her hands, <hi type="italic">and there is</hi> none to comfort her: the Lord hath commanded concerning Jacob, <hi type="italic">that</hi> his adversaries <hi type="italic">should be</hi> round about him: Jerusalem is as a menstruous woman among them.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:18
verses.text: ¶ The Lord is righteous; for I have rebelled against his commandment: hear, I pray you, all people, and behold my sorrow: my virgins and my young men are gone into captivity.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:19
verses.text: I called for my lovers, <hi type="italic">but</hi> they deceived me: my priests and mine elders gave up the ghost in the city, while they sought their meat to relieve their souls.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:20
verses.text: Behold, O Lord; for I <hi type="italic">am</hi> in distress: my bowels are troubled; mine heart is turned within me; for I have grievously rebelled: abroad the sword bereaveth, at home <hi type="italic">there is</hi> as death.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:21
verses.text: They have heard that I sigh: <hi type="italic">there is</hi> none to comfort me: all mine enemies have heard of my trouble; they are glad that thou hast done <hi type="italic">it:</hi> thou wilt bring the day <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou hast called, and they shall be like unto me.

verses.name: Lamentations 1:22
verses.text: Let all their wickedness come before thee; and do unto them, as thou hast done unto me for all my transgressions: for my sighs <hi type="italic">are</hi> many, and my heart <hi type="italic">is</hi> faint.  <chapter eID="Lam.1"/><div eID="gen867" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Lamentations 2:1
verses.text: HOW hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, <hi type="italic">and</hi> cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger!

verses.name: Lamentations 2:2
verses.text: The Lord hath swallowed up all the habitations of Jacob, and hath not pitied: he hath thrown down in his wrath the strong holds of the daughter of Judah; he hath brought <hi type="italic">them</hi> down to the ground: he hath polluted the kingdom and the princes thereof.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:3
verses.text: He hath cut off in <hi type="italic">his</hi> fierce anger all the horn of Israel: he hath drawn back his right hand from before the enemy, and he burned against Jacob like a flaming fire, <hi type="italic">which</hi> devoureth round about.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:4
verses.text: He hath bent his bow like an enemy: he stood with his right hand as an adversary, and slew all <hi type="italic">that were</hi> pleasant to the eye in the tabernacle of the daughter of Zion: he poured out his fury like fire.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:5
verses.text: The Lord was as an enemy: he hath swallowed up Israel, he hath swallowed up all her palaces: he hath destroyed his strong holds, and hath increased in the daughter of Judah mourning and lamentation.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:6
verses.text: And he hath violently taken away his tabernacle, as <hi type="italic">if it were of</hi> a garden: he hath destroyed his places of the assembly: the Lord hath caused the solemn feasts and sabbaths to be forgotten in Zion, and hath despised in the indignation of his anger the king and the priest.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:7
verses.text: The Lord hath cast off his altar, he hath abhorred his sanctuary, he hath given up into the hand of the enemy the walls of her palaces; they have made a noise in the house of the Lord, as in the day of a solemn feast.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:8
verses.text: The Lord hath purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion: he hath stretched out a line, he hath not withdrawn his hand from destroying: therefore he made the rampart and the wall to lament; they languished together.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:9
verses.text: Her gates are sunk into the ground; he hath destroyed and broken her bars: her king and her princes <hi type="italic">are</hi> among the Gentiles: the law <hi type="italic">is</hi> no <hi type="italic">more;</hi> her prophets also find no vision from the Lord.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:10
verses.text: The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground, <hi type="italic">and</hi> keep silence: they have cast up dust upon their heads; they have girded themselves with sackcloth: the virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:11
verses.text: Mine eyes do fail with tears, my bowels are troubled, my liver is poured upon the earth, for the destruction of the daughter of my people; because the children and the sucklings swoon in the streets of the city.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:12
verses.text: They say to their mothers, Where <hi type="italic">is</hi> corn and wine? when they swooned as the wounded in the streets of the city, when their soul was poured out into their mothers’ bosom.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:13
verses.text: What thing shall I take to witness for thee? what thing shall I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? what shall I equal to thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Zion? for thy breach <hi type="italic">is</hi> great like the sea: who can heal thee?

verses.name: Lamentations 2:14
verses.text: Thy prophets have seen vain and foolish things for thee: and they have not discovered thine iniquity, to turn away thy captivity; but have seen for thee false burdens and causes of banishment.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:15
verses.text: All that pass by clap <hi type="italic">their</hi> hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, <hi type="italic">Is</hi> this the city that <hi type="italic">men</hi> call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?

verses.name: Lamentations 2:16
verses.text: All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they hiss and gnash the teeth: they say, We have swallowed <hi type="italic">her</hi> up: certainly this <hi type="italic">is</hi> the day that we looked for; we have found, we have seen <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:17
verses.text: The Lord hath done <hi type="italic">that</hi> which he had devised; he hath fulfilled his word that he had commanded in the days of old: he hath thrown down, and hath not pitied: and he hath caused <hi type="italic">thine</hi> enemy to rejoice over thee, he hath set up the horn of thine adversaries.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:18
verses.text: Their heart cried unto the Lord, O wall of the daughter of Zion, let tears run down like a river day and night: give thyself no rest; let not the apple of thine eye cease.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:19
verses.text: Arise, cry out in the night: in the beginning of the watches pour out thine heart like water before the face of the Lord: lift up thy hands toward him for the life of thy young children, that faint for hunger in the top of every street.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:20
verses.text: ¶ Behold, O Lord, and consider to whom thou hast done this. Shall the women eat their fruit, <hi type="italic">and</hi> children of a span long? shall the priest and the prophet be slain in the sanctuary of the Lord?

verses.name: Lamentations 2:21
verses.text: The young and the old lie on the ground in the streets: my virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword; thou hast slain <hi type="italic">them</hi> in the day of thine anger; thou hast killed, <hi type="italic">and</hi> not pitied.

verses.name: Lamentations 2:22
verses.text: Thou hast called as in a solemn day my terrors round about, so that in the day of the Lord’s anger none escaped nor remained: those that I have swaddled and brought up hath mine enemy consumed.  <chapter eID="Lam.2"/><div eID="gen868" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Lamentations 3:1
verses.text: I <hi type="italic">AM</hi> the man <hi type="italic">that</hi> hath seen affliction by the rod of his wrath.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:2
verses.text: He hath led me, and brought <hi type="italic">me into</hi> darkness, but not <hi type="italic">into</hi> light.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:3
verses.text: Surely against me is he turned; he turneth his hand <hi type="italic">against me</hi> all the day.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:4
verses.text: My flesh and my skin hath he made old; he hath broken my bones.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:5
verses.text: He hath builded against me, and compassed <hi type="italic">me</hi> with gall and travail.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:6
verses.text: He hath set me in dark places, as <hi type="italic">they that be</hi> dead of old.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:7
verses.text: He hath hedged me about, that I cannot get out: he hath made my chain heavy.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:8
verses.text: Also when I cry and shout, he shutteth out my prayer.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:9
verses.text: He hath inclosed my ways with hewn stone, he hath made my paths crooked.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:10
verses.text: He <hi type="italic">was</hi> unto me <hi type="italic">as</hi> a bear lying in wait, <hi type="italic">and as</hi> a lion in secret places.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:11
verses.text: He hath turned aside my ways, and pulled me in pieces: he hath made me desolate.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:12
verses.text: He hath bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:13
verses.text: He hath caused the arrows of his quiver to enter into my reins.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:14
verses.text: I was a derision to all my people; <hi type="italic">and</hi> their song all the day.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:15
verses.text: He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:16
verses.text: He hath also broken my teeth with gravel stones, he hath covered me with ashes.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:17
verses.text: And thou hast removed my soul far off from peace: I forgat prosperity.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:18
verses.text: And I said, My strength and my hope is perished from the Lord:

verses.name: Lamentations 3:19
verses.text: Remembering mine affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the gall.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:20
verses.text: My soul hath <hi type="italic">them</hi> still in remembrance, and is humbled in me.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:21
verses.text: This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:22
verses.text: ¶ <hi type="italic">It is of</hi> the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:23
verses.text: <hi type="italic">They are</hi> new every morning: great <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy faithfulness.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:24
verses.text: The Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:25
verses.text: The Lord <hi type="italic">is</hi> good unto them that wait for him, to the soul <hi type="italic">that</hi> seeketh him.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:26
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> good that <hi type="italic">a man</hi> should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:27
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:28
verses.text: He sitteth alone and keepeth silence, because he hath borne <hi type="italic">it</hi> upon him.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:29
verses.text: He putteth his mouth in the dust; if so be there may be hope.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:30
verses.text: He giveth <hi type="italic">his</hi> cheek to him that smiteth him: he is filled full with reproach.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:31
verses.text: For the Lord will not cast off for ever:

verses.name: Lamentations 3:32
verses.text: But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:33
verses.text: For he doth not afflict willingly nor grieve the children of men.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:34
verses.text: To crush under his feet all the prisoners of the earth,

verses.name: Lamentations 3:35
verses.text: To turn aside the right of a man before the face of the most High,

verses.name: Lamentations 3:36
verses.text: To subvert a man in his cause, the Lord approveth not.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:37
verses.text: ¶ Who <hi type="italic">is</hi> he <hi type="italic">that</hi> saith, and it cometh to pass, <hi type="italic">when</hi> the Lord commandeth <hi type="italic">it</hi> not?

verses.name: Lamentations 3:38
verses.text: Out of the mouth of the most High proceedeth not evil and good?

verses.name: Lamentations 3:39
verses.text: Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?

verses.name: Lamentations 3:40
verses.text: Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:41
verses.text: Let us lift up our heart with <hi type="italic">our</hi> hands unto God in the heavens.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:42
verses.text: We have transgressed and have rebelled: thou hast not pardoned.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:43
verses.text: Thou hast covered with anger, and persecuted us: thou hast slain, thou hast not pitied.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:44
verses.text: Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that <hi type="italic">our</hi> prayer should not pass through.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:45
verses.text: Thou hast made us <hi type="italic">as</hi> the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:46
verses.text: All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:47
verses.text: Fear and a snare is come upon us, desolation and destruction.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:48
verses.text: Mine eye runneth down with rivers of water for the destruction of the daughter of my people.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:49
verses.text: Mine eye trickleth down, and ceaseth not, without any intermission,

verses.name: Lamentations 3:50
verses.text: Till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:51
verses.text: Mine eye affecteth mine heart because of all the daughters of my city.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:52
verses.text: Mine enemies chased me sore, like a bird, without cause.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:53
verses.text: They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:54
verses.text: Waters flowed over mine head; <hi type="italic">then</hi> I said, I am cut off.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:55
verses.text: ¶ I called upon thy name, O Lord, out of the low dungeon.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:56
verses.text: Thou hast heard my voice: hide not thine ear at my breathing, at my cry.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:57
verses.text: Thou drewest near in the day <hi type="italic">that</hi> I called upon thee: thou saidst, Fear not.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:58
verses.text: O Lord, thou hast pleaded the causes of my soul; thou hast redeemed my life.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:59
verses.text: O Lord, thou hast seen my wrong: judge thou my cause.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:60
verses.text: Thou hast seen all their vengeance <hi type="italic">and</hi> all their imaginations against me.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:61
verses.text: Thou hast heard their reproach, O Lord, <hi type="italic">and</hi> all their imaginations against me;

verses.name: Lamentations 3:62
verses.text: The lips of those that rose up against me, and their device against me all the day.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:63
verses.text: Behold their sitting down, and their rising up; I <hi type="italic">am</hi> their musick.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:64
verses.text: ¶ Render unto them a recompence, O Lord, according to the work of their hands.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:65
verses.text: Give them sorrow of heart, thy curse unto them.

verses.name: Lamentations 3:66
verses.text: Persecute and destroy them in anger from under the heavens of the Lord.  <chapter eID="Lam.3"/><div eID="gen869" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Lamentations 4:1
verses.text: HOW is the gold become dim! <hi type="italic">how</hi> is the most fine gold changed! the stones of the sanctuary are poured out in the top of every street.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:2
verses.text: The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, how are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!

verses.name: Lamentations 4:3
verses.text: Even the sea monsters draw out the breast, they give suck to their young ones: the daughter of my people <hi type="italic">is become</hi> cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:4
verses.text: The tongue of the sucking child cleaveth to the roof of his mouth for thirst: the young children ask bread, <hi type="italic">and</hi> no man breaketh <hi type="italic">it</hi> unto them.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:5
verses.text: They that did feed delicately are desolate in the streets: they that were brought up in scarlet embrace dunghills.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:6
verses.text: For the punishment of the iniquity of the daughter of my people is greater than the punishment of the sin of Sodom, that was overthrown as in a moment, and no hands stayed on her.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:7
verses.text: Her Nazarites were purer than snow, they were whiter than milk, they were more ruddy in body than rubies, their polishing <hi type="italic">was</hi> of sapphire:

verses.name: Lamentations 4:8
verses.text: Their visage is blacker than a coal; they are not known in the streets: their skin cleaveth to their bones; it is withered, it is become like a stick.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:9
verses.text: <hi type="italic">They that be</hi> slain with the sword are better than <hi type="italic">they that be</hi> slain with hunger: for these pine away, stricken through for <hi type="italic">want of</hi> the fruits of the field.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:10
verses.text: The hands of the pitiful women have sodden their own children: they were their meat in the destruction of the daughter of my people.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:11
verses.text: The Lord hath accomplished his fury; he hath poured out his fierce anger, and hath kindled a fire in Zion, and it hath devoured the foundations thereof.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:12
verses.text: The kings of the earth, and all the inhabitants of the world, would not have believed that the adversary and the enemy should have entered into the gates of Jerusalem.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:13
verses.text: ¶ For the sins of her prophets, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the iniquities of her priests, that have shed the blood of the just in the midst of her,

verses.name: Lamentations 4:14
verses.text: They have wandered <hi type="italic">as</hi> blind <hi type="italic">men</hi> in the streets, they have polluted themselves with blood, so that men could not touch their garments.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:15
verses.text: They cried unto them, Depart ye; <hi type="italic">it is</hi> unclean; depart, depart, touch not: when they fled away and wandered, they said among the heathen, They shall no more sojourn <hi type="italic">there</hi>.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:16
verses.text: The anger of the Lord hath divided them; he will no more regard them: they respected not the persons of the priests, they favoured not the elders.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:17
verses.text: As for us, our eyes as yet failed for our vain help: in our watching we have watched for a nation <hi type="italic">that</hi> could not save <hi type="italic">us</hi>.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:18
verses.text: They hunt our steps, that we cannot go in our streets: our end is near, our days are fulfilled; for our end is come.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:19
verses.text: Our persecutors are swifter than the eagles of the heaven: they pursued us upon the mountains, they laid wait for us in the wilderness.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:20
verses.text: The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the Lord, was taken in their pits, of whom we said, Under his shadow we shall live among the heathen.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:21
verses.text: ¶ Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, that dwellest in the land of Uz; the cup also shall pass through unto thee: thou shalt be drunken, and shalt make thyself naked.

verses.name: Lamentations 4:22
verses.text: ¶ The punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion; he will no more carry thee away into captivity: he will visit thine iniquity, O daughter of Edom; he will discover thy sins.  <chapter eID="Lam.4"/><div eID="gen870" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Lamentations 5:1
verses.text: REMEMBER, O Lord, what is come upon us: consider, and behold our reproach.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:2
verses.text: Our inheritance is turned to strangers, our houses to aliens.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:3
verses.text: We are orphans and fatherless, our mothers <hi type="italic">are</hi> as widows.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:4
verses.text: We have drunken our water for money; our wood is sold unto us.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:5
verses.text: Our necks <hi type="italic">are</hi> under persecution: we labour, <hi type="italic">and</hi> have no rest.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:6
verses.text: We have given the hand <hi type="italic">to</hi> the Egyptians, <hi type="italic">and to</hi> the Assyrians, to be satisfied with bread.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:7
verses.text: Our fathers have sinned, <hi type="italic">and are</hi> not; and we have borne their iniquities.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:8
verses.text: Servants have ruled over us: <hi type="italic">there is</hi> none that doth deliver <hi type="italic">us</hi> out of their hand.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:9
verses.text: We gat our bread with <hi type="italic">the peril of</hi> our lives because of the sword of the wilderness.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:10
verses.text: Our skin was black like an oven because of the terrible famine.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:11
verses.text: They ravished the women in Zion, <hi type="italic">and</hi> the maids in the cities of Judah.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:12
verses.text: Princes are hanged up by their hand: the faces of elders were not honoured.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:13
verses.text: They took the young men to grind, and the children fell under the wood.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:14
verses.text: The elders have ceased from the gate, the young men from their musick.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:15
verses.text: The joy of our heart is ceased; our dance is turned into mourning.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:16
verses.text: The crown is fallen <hi type="italic">from</hi> our head: woe unto us, that we have sinned!

verses.name: Lamentations 5:17
verses.text: For this our heart is faint; for these <hi type="italic">things</hi> our eyes are dim.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:18
verses.text: Because of the mountain of Zion, which is desolate, the foxes walk upon it.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:19
verses.text: Thou, O Lord, remainest for ever; thy throne from generation to generation.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:20
verses.text: Wherefore dost thou forget us for ever, <hi type="italic">and</hi> forsake us so long time?

verses.name: Lamentations 5:21
verses.text: Turn thou us unto thee, O Lord, and we shall be turned; renew our days as of old.

verses.name: Lamentations 5:22
verses.text: But thou hast utterly rejected us; thou art very wroth against us.  <chapter eID="Lam.5"/><div eID="gen871" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen866" osisID="Lam" type="book"/>

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:1
verses.text: NOW it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth <hi type="italic">month</hi>, in the fifth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the month, as I <hi type="italic">was</hi> among the captives by the river of Chebar, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:2
verses.text: In the fifth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the month, which <hi type="italic">was</hi> the fifth year of king Jehoiachin’s captivity,

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:3
verses.text: The word of the Lord came expressly unto Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the Lord was there upon him.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:4
verses.text: ¶ And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness <hi type="italic">was</hi> about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:5
verses.text: Also out of the midst thereof <hi type="italic">came</hi> the likeness of four living creatures. And this <hi type="italic">was</hi> their appearance; they had the likeness of a man.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:6
verses.text: And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:7
verses.text: And their feet <hi type="italic">were</hi> straight feet; and the sole of their feet <hi type="italic">was</hi> like the sole of a calf’s foot: and they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:8
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">they had</hi> the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and they four had their faces and their wings.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:9
verses.text: Their wings <hi type="italic">were</hi> joined one to another; they turned not when they went; they went every one straight forward.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:10
verses.text: As for the likeness of their faces, they four had the face of a man, and the face of a lion, on the right side: and they four had the face of an ox on the left side; they four also had the face of an eagle.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:11
verses.text: Thus <hi type="italic">were</hi> their faces: and their wings <hi type="italic">were</hi> stretched upward; two <hi type="italic">wings</hi> of every one <hi type="italic">were</hi> joined one to another, and two covered their bodies.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:12
verses.text: And they went every one straight forward: whither the spirit was to go, they went; <hi type="italic">and</hi> they turned not when they went.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:13
verses.text: As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance <hi type="italic">was</hi> like burning coals of fire, <hi type="italic">and</hi> like the appearance of lamps: it went up and down among the living creatures; and the fire was bright, and out of the fire went forth lightning.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:14
verses.text: And the living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:15
verses.text: ¶ Now as I beheld the living creatures, behold one wheel upon the earth by the living creatures, with his four faces.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:16
verses.text: The appearance of the wheels and their work <hi type="italic">was</hi> like unto the colour of a beryl: and they four had one likeness: and their appearance and their work <hi type="italic">was</hi> as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:17
verses.text: When they went, they went upon their four sides: <hi type="italic">and</hi> they turned not when they went.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:18
verses.text: As for their rings, they were so high that they were dreadful; and their rings <hi type="italic">were</hi> full of eyes round about them four.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:19
verses.text: And when the living creatures went, the wheels went by them: and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:20
verses.text: Whithersoever the spirit was to go, they went, thither <hi type="italic">was their</hi> spirit to go; and the wheels were lifted up over against them: for the spirit of the living creature <hi type="italic">was</hi> in the wheels.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:21
verses.text: When those went, <hi type="italic">these</hi> went; and when those stood, <hi type="italic">these</hi> stood; and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up over against them: for the spirit of the living creature <hi type="italic">was</hi> in the wheels.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:22
verses.text: And the likeness of the firmament upon the heads of the living creature <hi type="italic">was</hi> as the colour of the terrible crystal, stretched forth over their heads above.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:23
verses.text: And under the firmament <hi type="italic">were</hi> their wings straight, the one toward the other: every one had two, which covered on this side, and every one had two, which covered on that side, their bodies.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:24
verses.text: And when they went, I heard the noise of their wings, like the noise of great waters, as the voice of the Almighty, the voice of speech, as the noise of an host: when they stood, they let down their wings.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:25
verses.text: And there was a voice from the firmament that <hi type="italic">was</hi> over their heads, when they stood, <hi type="italic">and</hi> had let down their wings.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:26
verses.text: ¶ And above the firmament that <hi type="italic">was</hi> over their heads <hi type="italic">was</hi> the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone: and upon the likeness of the throne <hi type="italic">was</hi> the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:27
verses.text: And I saw as the colour of amber, as the appearance of fire round about within it, from the appearance of his loins even upward, and from the appearance of his loins even downward, I saw as it were the appearance of fire, and it had brightness round about.

verses.name: Ezekiel 1:28
verses.text: As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so <hi type="italic">was</hi> the appearance of the brightness round about. This <hi type="italic">was</hi> the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. And when I saw <hi type="italic">it</hi>, I fell upon my face, and I heard a voice of one that spake.  <chapter eID="Ezek.1"/><div eID="gen873" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezekiel 2:1
verses.text: AND he said unto me, Son of man, stand upon thy feet, and I will speak unto thee.

verses.name: Ezekiel 2:2
verses.text: And the spirit entered into me when he spake unto me, and set me upon my feet, that I heard him that spake unto me.

verses.name: Ezekiel 2:3
verses.text: And he said unto me, Son of man, I send thee to the children of Israel, to a rebellious nation that hath rebelled against me: they and their fathers have transgressed against me, <hi type="italic">even</hi> unto this very day.

verses.name: Ezekiel 2:4
verses.text: For <hi type="italic">they are</hi> impudent children and stiffhearted. I do send thee unto them; and thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God.

verses.name: Ezekiel 2:5
verses.text: And they, whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear, (for they <hi type="italic">are</hi> a rebellious house,) yet shall know that there hath been a prophet among them.

verses.name: Ezekiel 2:6
verses.text: ¶ And thou, son of man, be not afraid of them, neither be afraid of their words, though briers and thorns <hi type="italic">be</hi> with thee, and thou dost dwell among scorpions: be not afraid of their words, nor be dismayed at their looks, though they <hi type="italic">be</hi> a rebellious house.

verses.name: Ezekiel 2:7
verses.text: And thou shalt speak my words unto them, whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear: for they <hi type="italic">are</hi> most rebellious.

verses.name: Ezekiel 2:8
verses.text: But thou, son of man, hear what I say unto thee; Be not thou rebellious like that rebellious house: open thy mouth, and eat that I give thee.

verses.name: Ezekiel 2:9
verses.text: ¶ And when I looked, behold, an hand <hi type="italic">was</hi> sent unto me; and, lo, a roll of a book <hi type="italic">was</hi> therein;

verses.name: Ezekiel 2:10
verses.text: And he spread it before me; and it <hi type="italic">was</hi> written within and without: and <hi type="italic">there was</hi> written therein lamentations, and mourning, and woe.  <chapter eID="Ezek.2"/><div eID="gen874" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:1
verses.text: MOREOVER he said unto me, Son of man, eat that thou findest; eat this roll, and go speak unto the house of Israel.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:2
verses.text: So I opened my mouth, and he caused me to eat that roll.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:3
verses.text: And he said unto me, Son of man, cause thy belly to eat, and fill thy bowels with this roll that I give thee. Then did I eat <hi type="italic">it;</hi> and it was in my mouth as honey for sweetness.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:4
verses.text: ¶ And he said unto me, Son of man, go, get thee unto the house of Israel, and speak with my words unto them.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:5
verses.text: For thou <hi type="italic">art</hi> not sent to a people of a strange speech and of an hard language, <hi type="italic">but</hi> to the house of Israel;

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:6
verses.text: Not to many people of a strange speech and of an hard language, whose words thou canst not understand. Surely, had I sent thee to them, they would have hearkened unto thee.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:7
verses.text: But the house of Israel will not hearken unto thee; for they will not hearken unto me: for all the house of Israel <hi type="italic">are</hi> impudent and hardhearted.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:8
verses.text: Behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces, and thy forehead strong against their foreheads.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:9
verses.text: As an adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead: fear them not, neither be dismayed at their looks, though they <hi type="italic">be</hi> a rebellious house.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:10
verses.text: Moreover he said unto me, Son of man, all my words that I shall speak unto thee receive in thine heart, and hear with thine ears.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:11
verses.text: And go, get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:12
verses.text: Then the spirit took me up, and I heard behind me a voice of a great rushing, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, Blessed <hi type="italic">be</hi> the glory of the Lord from his place.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:13
verses.text: <hi type="italic">I heard</hi> also the noise of the wings of the living creatures that touched one another, and the noise of the wheels over against them, and a noise of a great rushing.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:14
verses.text: So the spirit lifted me up, and took me away, and I went in bitterness, in the heat of my spirit; but the hand of the Lord was strong upon me.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:15
verses.text: ¶ Then I came to them of the captivity at Tel-abib, that dwelt by the river of Chebar, and I sat where they sat, and remained there astonished among them seven days.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:16
verses.text: And it came to pass at the end of seven days, that the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:17
verses.text: Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:18
verses.text: When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked <hi type="italic">man</hi> shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:19
verses.text: Yet if thou warn the wicked, and he turn not from his wickedness, nor from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity; but thou hast delivered thy soul.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:20
verses.text: Again, When a righteous <hi type="italic">man</hi> doth turn from his righteousness, and commit iniquity, and I lay a stumblingblock before him, he shall die: because thou hast not given him warning, he shall die in his sin, and his righteousness which he hath done shall not be remembered; but his blood will I require at thine hand.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:21
verses.text: Nevertheless if thou warn the righteous <hi type="italic">man</hi>, that the righteous sin not, and he doth not sin, he shall surely live, because he is warned; also thou hast delivered thy soul.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:22
verses.text: ¶ And the hand of the Lord was there upon me; and he said unto me, Arise, go forth into the plain, and I will there talk with thee.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:23
verses.text: Then I arose, and went forth into the plain: and, behold, the glory of the Lord stood there, as the glory which I saw by the river of Chebar: and I fell on my face.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:24
verses.text: Then the spirit entered into me, and set me upon my feet, and spake with me, and said unto me, Go, shut thyself within thine house.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:25
verses.text: But thou, O son of man, behold, they shall put bands upon thee, and shall bind thee with them, and thou shalt not go out among them:

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:26
verses.text: And I will make thy tongue cleave to the roof of thy mouth, that thou shalt be dumb, and shalt not be to them a reprover: for they <hi type="italic">are</hi> a rebellious house.

verses.name: Ezekiel 3:27
verses.text: But when I speak with thee, I will open thy mouth, and thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God; He that heareth, let him hear; and he that forbeareth, let him forbear: for they <hi type="italic">are</hi> a rebellious house.  <chapter eID="Ezek.3"/><div eID="gen875" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:1
verses.text: THOU also, son of man, take thee a tile, and lay it before thee, and pourtray upon it the city, <hi type="italic">even</hi> Jerusalem:

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:2
verses.text: And lay siege against it, and build a fort against it, and cast a mount against it; set the camp also against it, and set <hi type="italic">battering</hi> rams against it round about.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:3
verses.text: Moreover take thou unto thee an iron pan, and set it <hi type="italic">for</hi> a wall of iron between thee and the city: and set thy face against it, and it shall be besieged, and thou shalt lay siege against it. This <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> a sign to the house of Israel.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:4
verses.text: Lie thou also upon thy left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it: <hi type="italic">according</hi> to the number of the days that thou shalt lie upon it thou shalt bear their iniquity.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:5
verses.text: For I have laid upon thee the years of their iniquity, according to the number of the days, three hundred and ninety days: so shalt thou bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:6
verses.text: And when thou hast accomplished them, lie again on thy right side, and thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days: I have appointed thee each day for a year.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:7
verses.text: Therefore thou shalt set thy face toward the siege of Jerusalem, and thine arm <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> uncovered, and thou shalt prophesy against it.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:8
verses.text: And, behold, I will lay bands upon thee, and thou shalt not turn thee from one side to another, till thou hast ended the days of thy siege.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:9
verses.text: ¶ Take thou also unto thee wheat, and barley, and beans, and lentiles, and millet, and fitches, and put them in one vessel, and make thee bread thereof, <hi type="italic">according</hi> to the number of the days that thou shalt lie upon thy side, three hundred and ninety days shalt thou eat thereof.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:10
verses.text: And thy meat which thou shalt eat <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> by weight, twenty shekels a day: from time to time shalt thou eat it.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:11
verses.text: Thou shalt drink also water by measure, the sixth part of an hin: from time to time shalt thou drink.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:12
verses.text: And thou shalt eat it <hi type="italic">as</hi> barley cakes, and thou shalt bake it with dung that cometh out of man, in their sight.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:13
verses.text: And the Lord said, Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:14
verses.text: Then said I, Ah Lord God! behold, my soul hath not been polluted: for from my youth up even till now have I not eaten of that which dieth of itself, or is torn in pieces; neither came there abominable flesh into my mouth.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:15
verses.text: Then he said unto me, Lo, I have given thee cow’s dung for man’s dung, and thou shalt prepare thy bread therewith.

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:16
verses.text: Moreover he said unto me, Son of man, behold, I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem: and they shall eat bread by weight, and with care; and they shall drink water by measure, and with astonishment:

verses.name: Ezekiel 4:17
verses.text: That they may want bread and water, and be astonied one with another, and consume away for their iniquity.  <chapter eID="Ezek.4"/><div eID="gen876" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:1
verses.text: AND thou, son of man, take thee a sharp knife, take thee a barber’s rasor, and cause <hi type="italic">it</hi> to pass upon thine head and upon thy beard: then take thee balances to weigh, and divide the <hi type="italic">hair</hi>.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:2
verses.text: Thou shalt burn with fire a third part in the midst of the city, when the days of the siege are fulfilled: and thou shalt take a third part, <hi type="italic">and</hi> smite about it with a knife: and a third part thou shalt scatter in the wind; and I will draw out a sword after them.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:3
verses.text: Thou shalt also take thereof a few in number, and bind them in thy skirts.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:4
verses.text: Then take of them again, and cast them into the midst of the fire, and burn them in the fire; <hi type="italic">for</hi> thereof shall a fire come forth into all the house of Israel.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:5
verses.text: ¶ Thus saith the Lord God; This <hi type="italic">is</hi> Jerusalem: I have set it in the midst of the nations and countries <hi type="italic">that are</hi> round about her.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:6
verses.text: And she hath changed my judgments into wickedness more than the nations, and my statutes more than the countries that <hi type="italic">are</hi> round about her: for they have refused my judgments and my statutes, they have not walked in them.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:7
verses.text: Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Because ye multiplied more than the nations that <hi type="italic">are</hi> round about you, <hi type="italic">and</hi> have not walked in my statutes, neither have kept my judgments, neither have done according to the judgments of the nations that <hi type="italic">are</hi> round about you;

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:8
verses.text: Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I, even I, <hi type="italic">am</hi> against thee, and will execute judgments in the midst of thee in the sight of the nations.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:9
verses.text: And I will do in thee that which I have not done, and whereunto I will not do any more the like, because of all thine abominations.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:10
verses.text: Therefore the fathers shall eat the sons in the midst of thee, and the sons shall eat their fathers; and I will execute judgments in thee, and the whole remnant of thee will I scatter into all the winds.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:11
verses.text: Wherefore, <hi type="italic">as</hi> I live, saith the Lord God; Surely, because thou hast defiled my sanctuary with all thy detestable things, and with all thine abominations, therefore will I also diminish <hi type="italic">thee;</hi> neither shall mine eye spare, neither will I have any pity.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:12
verses.text: ¶ A third part of thee shall die with the pestilence, and with famine shall they be consumed in the midst of thee: and a third part shall fall by the sword round about thee; and I will scatter a third part into all the winds, and I will draw out a sword after them.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:13
verses.text: Thus shall mine anger be accomplished, and I will cause my fury to rest upon them, and I will be comforted: and they shall know that I the Lord have spoken <hi type="italic">it</hi> in my zeal, when I have accomplished my fury in them.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:14
verses.text: Moreover I will make thee waste, and a reproach among the nations that <hi type="italic">are</hi> round about thee, in the sight of all that pass by.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:15
verses.text: So it shall be a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment unto the nations that <hi type="italic">are</hi> round about thee, when I shall execute judgments in thee in anger and in fury and in furious rebukes. I the Lord have spoken <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:16
verses.text: When I shall send upon them the evil arrows of famine, which shall be for <hi type="italic">their</hi> destruction, <hi type="italic">and</hi> which I will send to destroy you: and I will increase the famine upon you, and will break your staff of bread:

verses.name: Ezekiel 5:17
verses.text: So will I send upon you famine and evil beasts, and they shall bereave thee; and pestilence and blood shall pass through thee; and I will bring the sword upon thee. I the Lord have spoken <hi type="italic">it</hi>.  <chapter eID="Ezek.5"/><div eID="gen877" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:1
verses.text: AND the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:2
verses.text: Son of man, set thy face toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them,

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:3
verses.text: And say, Ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God; Thus saith the Lord God to the mountains, and to the hills, to the rivers, and to the valleys; Behold, I, <hi type="italic">even</hi> I, will bring a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places.

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:4
verses.text: And your altars shall be desolate, and your images shall be broken: and I will cast down your slain <hi type="italic">men</hi> before your idols.

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:5
verses.text: And I will lay the dead carcases of the children of Israel before their idols; and I will scatter your bones round about your altars.

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:6
verses.text: In all your dwellingplaces the cities shall be laid waste, and the high places shall be desolate; that your altars may be laid waste and made desolate, and your idols may be broken and cease, and your images may be cut down, and your works may be abolished.

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:7
verses.text: And the slain shall fall in the midst of you, and ye shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord.

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:8
verses.text: ¶ Yet will I leave a remnant, that ye may have <hi type="italic">some</hi> that shall escape the sword among the nations, when ye shall be scattered through the countries.

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:9
verses.text: And they that escape of you shall remember me among the nations whither they shall be carried captives, because I am broken with their whorish heart, which hath departed from me, and with their eyes, which go a whoring after their idols: and they shall lothe themselves for the evils which they have committed in all their abominations.

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:10
verses.text: And they shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord, <hi type="italic">and that</hi> I have not said in vain that I would do this evil unto them.

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:11
verses.text: ¶ Thus saith the Lord God; Smite with thine hand, and stamp with thy foot, and say, Alas for all the evil abominations of the house of Israel! for they shall fall by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence.

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:12
verses.text: He that is far off shall die of the pestilence; and he that is near shall fall by the sword; and he that remaineth and is besieged shall die by the famine: thus will I accomplish my fury upon them.

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:13
verses.text: Then shall ye know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord, when their slain <hi type="italic">men</hi> shall be among their idols round about their altars, upon every high hill, in all the tops of the mountains, and under every green tree, and under every thick oak, the place where they did offer sweet savour to all their idols.

verses.name: Ezekiel 6:14
verses.text: So will I stretch out my hand upon them, and make the land desolate, yea, more desolate than the wilderness toward Diblath, in all their habitations: and they shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord.  <chapter eID="Ezek.6"/><div eID="gen878" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:1
verses.text: MOREOVER the word of the Lord came unto me, saying,

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:2
verses.text: Also, thou son of man, thus saith the Lord God unto the land of Israel; An end, the end is come upon the four corners of the land.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:3
verses.text: Now <hi type="italic">is</hi> the end <hi type="italic">come</hi> upon thee, and I will send mine anger upon thee, and will judge thee according to thy ways, and will recompense upon thee all thine abominations.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:4
verses.text: And mine eye shall not spare thee, neither will I have pity: but I will recompense thy ways upon thee, and thine abominations shall be in the midst of thee: and ye shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:5
verses.text: Thus saith the Lord God; An evil, an only evil, behold, is come.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:6
verses.text: An end is come, the end is come: it watcheth for thee; behold, it is come.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:7
verses.text: The morning is come unto thee, O thou that dwellest in the land: the time is come, the day of trouble <hi type="italic">is</hi> near, and not the sounding again of the mountains.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:8
verses.text: Now will I shortly pour out my fury upon thee, and accomplish mine anger upon thee: and I will judge thee according to thy ways, and will recompense thee for all thine abominations.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:9
verses.text: And mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity: I will recompense thee according to thy ways and thine abominations <hi type="italic">that</hi> are in the midst of thee; and ye shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord that smiteth.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:10
verses.text: Behold the day, behold, it is come: the morning is gone forth; the rod hath blossomed, pride hath budded.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:11
verses.text: Violence is risen up into a rod of wickedness: none of them <hi type="italic">shall remain</hi>, nor of their multitude, nor of any of theirs: neither <hi type="italic">shall there be</hi> wailing for them.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:12
verses.text: The time is come, the day draweth near: let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn: for wrath <hi type="italic">is</hi> upon all the multitude thereof.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:13
verses.text: For the seller shall not return to that which is sold, although they were yet alive: for the vision <hi type="italic">is</hi> touching the whole multitude thereof, <hi type="italic">which</hi> shall not return; neither shall any strengthen himself in the iniquity of his life.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:14
verses.text: They have blown the trumpet, even to make all ready; but none goeth to the battle: for my wrath <hi type="italic">is</hi> upon all the multitude thereof.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:15
verses.text: The sword <hi type="italic">is</hi> without, and the pestilence and the famine within: he that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the field shall die with the sword; and he that <hi type="italic">is</hi> in the city, famine and pestilence shall devour him.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:16
verses.text: ¶ But they that escape of them shall escape, and shall be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them mourning, every one for his iniquity.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:17
verses.text: All hands shall be feeble, and all knees shall be weak <hi type="italic">as</hi> water.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:18
verses.text: They shall also gird <hi type="italic">themselves</hi> with sackcloth, and horror shall cover them; and shame <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> upon all faces, and baldness upon all their heads.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:19
verses.text: They shall cast their silver in the streets, and their gold shall be removed: their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord: they shall not satisfy their souls, neither fill their bowels: because it is the stumblingblock of their iniquity.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:20
verses.text: ¶ As for the beauty of his ornament, he set it in majesty: but they made the images of their abominations <hi type="italic">and</hi> of their detestable things therein: therefore have I set it far from them.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:21
verses.text: And I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a spoil; and they shall pollute it.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:22
verses.text: My face will I turn also from them, and they shall pollute my secret <hi type="italic">place:</hi> for the robbers shall enter into it, and defile it.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:23
verses.text: ¶ Make a chain: for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:24
verses.text: Wherefore I will bring the worst of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses: I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease; and their holy places shall be defiled.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:25
verses.text: Destruction cometh; and they shall seek peace, and <hi type="italic">there shall be</hi> none.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:26
verses.text: Mischief shall come upon mischief, and rumour shall be upon rumour; then shall they seek a vision of the prophet; but the law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the ancients.

verses.name: Ezekiel 7:27
verses.text: The king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with desolation, and the hands of the people of the land shall be troubled: I will do unto them after their way, and according to their deserts will I judge them; and they shall know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the Lord.  <chapter eID="Ezek.7"/><div eID="gen879" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass in the sixth year, in the sixth <hi type="italic">month</hi>, in the fifth <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the month, <hi type="italic">as</hi> I sat in mine house, and the elders of Judah sat before me, that the hand of the Lord God fell there upon me.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:2
verses.text: Then I beheld, and lo a likeness as the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his loins even downward, fire; and from his loins even upward, as the appearance of brightness, as the colour of amber.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:3
verses.text: And he put forth the form of an hand, and took me by a lock of mine head; and the spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the inner gate that looketh toward the north; where <hi type="italic">was</hi> the seat of the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:4
verses.text: And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel <hi type="italic">was</hi> there, according to the vision that I saw in the plain.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:5
verses.text: ¶ Then said he unto me, Son of man, lift up thine eyes now the way toward the north. So I lifted up mine eyes the way toward the north, and behold northward at the gate of the altar this image of jealousy in the entry.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:6
verses.text: He said furthermore unto me, Son of man, seest thou what they do? <hi type="italic">even</hi> the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary? but turn thee yet again, <hi type="italic">and</hi> thou shalt see greater abominations.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:7
verses.text: ¶ And he brought me to the door of the court; and when I looked, behold a hole in the wall.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:8
verses.text: Then said he unto me, Son of man, dig now in the wall: and when I had digged in the wall, behold a door.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:9
verses.text: And he said unto me, Go in, and behold the wicked abominations that they do here.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:10
verses.text: So I went in and saw; and behold every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:11
verses.text: And there stood before them seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel, and in the midst of them stood Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan, with every man his censer in his hand; and a thick cloud of incense went up.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:12
verses.text: Then said he unto me, Son of man, hast thou seen what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:13
verses.text: ¶ He said also unto me, Turn thee yet again, <hi type="italic">and</hi> thou shalt see greater abominations that they do.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:14
verses.text: Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the Lord’s house which <hi type="italic">was</hi> toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:15
verses.text: ¶ Then said he unto me, Hast thou seen <hi type="italic">this</hi>, O son of man? turn thee yet again, <hi type="italic">and</hi> thou shalt see greater abominations than these.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:16
verses.text: And he brought me into the inner court of the Lord’s house, and, behold, at the door of the temple of the Lord, between the porch and the altar, <hi type="italic">were</hi> about five and twenty men, with their backs toward the temple of the Lord, and their faces toward the east; and they worshipped the sun toward the east.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:17
verses.text: ¶ Then he said unto me, Hast thou seen <hi type="italic">this</hi>, O son of man? Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they commit the abominations which they commit here? for they have filled the land with violence, and have returned to provoke me to anger: and, lo, they put the branch to their nose.

verses.name: Ezekiel 8:18
verses.text: Therefore will I also deal in fury: mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity: and though they cry in mine ears with a loud voice, <hi type="italic">yet</hi> will I not hear them.  <chapter eID="Ezek.8"/><div eID="gen880" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Ezekiel 9:1
verses.text: HE cried also in mine ears with a loud voice, saying, Cause them that have charge over the city to draw near, even every man <hi type="italic">with</hi> his destroying weapon in his hand.

verses.name: Ezekiel 9:2
verses.text: And, behold, six men came from the way of the higher gate, which lieth toward the north, and every man a slaughter weapon in his hand; and one man among them <hi type="italic">was</hi> clothed with linen, with a writer’s inkhorn by his side: and they went in, and stood beside the brasen altar.

verses.name: Ezekiel 9:3
verses.text: And the glory of the God of Israel was gone up from the cherub, whereupon he was, to the threshold of the house. And he called to the man clothed with linen, which <hi type="italic">had</hi> the writer’s inkhorn by his side;

verses.name: Ezekiel 9:4
verses.text: And the Lord said unto him, Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof.

verses.name: Ezekiel 9:5
verses.text: ¶ And to the others he said in mine hearing, Go ye after him through the city, and smite: let not your eye spare, neither have ye pity:

verses.name: Ezekiel 9:6
verses.text: Slay utterly old <hi type="italic">and</hi> young, both maids, and little children, and women: but come not near any man upon whom <hi type="italic">is</hi> the mark; and begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the ancient men which <hi type="italic">were</hi> before the house.

verses.name: Ezekiel 9:7
verses.text: And he said unto them, Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain: go ye forth. And they went forth, and slew in the city.

verses.name: Ezekiel 9:8
