verses.text: Jesus saith unto him, Thou hast said: nevertheless I say unto you, Hereafter shall ye see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.

verses.name: Matthew 26:65
verses.text: Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He hath spoken blasphemy; what further need have we of witnesses? behold, now ye have heard his blasphemy.

verses.name: Matthew 26:66
verses.text: What think ye? They answered and said, He is guilty of death.

verses.name: Matthew 26:67
verses.text: Then did they spit in his face, and buffeted him; and others smote <hi type="italic">him</hi> with the palms of their hands,

verses.name: Matthew 26:68
verses.text: Saying, Prophesy unto us, thou Christ, Who is he that smote thee?

verses.name: Matthew 26:69
verses.text: ¶ Now Peter sat without in the palace: and a damsel came unto him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galilee.

verses.name: Matthew 26:70
verses.text: But he denied before <hi type="italic">them</hi> all, saying, I know not what thou sayest.

verses.name: Matthew 26:71
verses.text: And when he was gone out into the porch, another <hi type="italic">maid</hi> saw him, and said unto them that were there, This <hi type="italic">fellow</hi> was also with Jesus of Nazareth.

verses.name: Matthew 26:72
verses.text: And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.

verses.name: Matthew 26:73
verses.text: And after a while came unto <hi type="italic">him</hi> they that stood by, and said to Peter, Surely thou also art <hi type="italic">one</hi> of them; for thy speech bewrayeth thee.

verses.name: Matthew 26:74
verses.text: Then began he to curse and to swear, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew.

verses.name: Matthew 26:75
verses.text: And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.  <chapter eID="Matt.26"/><div eID="gen1039" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 27:1
verses.text: WHEN the morning was come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death:

verses.name: Matthew 27:2
verses.text: And when they had bound him, they led <hi type="italic">him</hi> away, and delivered him to Pontius Pilate the governor.

verses.name: Matthew 27:3
verses.text: ¶ Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,

verses.name: Matthew 27:4
verses.text: Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What <hi type="italic">is that</hi> to us? see thou <hi type="italic">to that</hi>.

verses.name: Matthew 27:5
verses.text: And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.

verses.name: Matthew 27:6
verses.text: And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.

verses.name: Matthew 27:7
verses.text: And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter’s field, to bury strangers in.

verses.name: Matthew 27:8
verses.text: Wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day.

verses.name: Matthew 27:9
verses.text: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued, whom they of the children of Israel did value;

verses.name: Matthew 27:10
verses.text: And gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord appointed me.

verses.name: Matthew 27:11
verses.text: And Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And Jesus said unto him, Thou sayest.

verses.name: Matthew 27:12
verses.text: And when he was accused of the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.

verses.name: Matthew 27:13
verses.text: Then said Pilate unto him, Hearest thou not how many things they witness against thee?

verses.name: Matthew 27:14
verses.text: And he answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.

verses.name: Matthew 27:15
verses.text: Now at <hi type="italic">that</hi> feast the governor was wont to release unto the people a prisoner, whom they would.

verses.name: Matthew 27:16
verses.text: And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.

verses.name: Matthew 27:17
verses.text: Therefore when they were gathered together, Pilate said unto them, Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ?

verses.name: Matthew 27:18
verses.text: For he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

verses.name: Matthew 27:19
verses.text: ¶ When he was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.

verses.name: Matthew 27:20
verses.text: But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude that they should ask Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.

verses.name: Matthew 27:21
verses.text: The governor answered and said unto them, Whether of the twain will ye that I release unto you? They said, Barabbas.

verses.name: Matthew 27:22
verses.text: Pilate saith unto them, What shall I do then with Jesus which is called Christ? <hi type="italic">They</hi> all say unto him, Let him be crucified.

verses.name: Matthew 27:23
verses.text: And the governor said, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out the more, saying, Let him be crucified.

verses.name: Matthew 27:24
verses.text: ¶ When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but <hi type="italic">that</hi> rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed <hi type="italic">his</hi> hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye <hi type="italic">to it</hi>.

verses.name: Matthew 27:25
verses.text: Then answered all the people, and said, His blood <hi type="italic">be</hi> on us, and on our children.

verses.name: Matthew 27:26
verses.text: ¶ Then released he Barabbas unto them: and when he had scourged Jesus, he delivered <hi type="italic">him</hi> to be crucified.

verses.name: Matthew 27:27
verses.text: Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the common hall, and gathered unto him the whole band <hi type="italic">of soldiers</hi>.

verses.name: Matthew 27:28
verses.text: And they stripped him, and put on him a scarlet robe.

verses.name: Matthew 27:29
verses.text: ¶ And when they had platted a crown of thorns, they put <hi type="italic">it</hi> upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!

verses.name: Matthew 27:30
verses.text: And they spit upon him, and took the reed, and smote him on the head.

verses.name: Matthew 27:31
verses.text: And after that they had mocked him, they took the robe off from him, and put his own raiment on him, and led him away to crucify <hi type="italic">him</hi>.

verses.name: Matthew 27:32
verses.text: And as they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name: him they compelled to bear his cross.

verses.name: Matthew 27:33
verses.text: And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull,

verses.name: Matthew 27:34
verses.text: ¶ They gave him vinegar to drink mingled with gall: and when he had tasted <hi type="italic">thereof</hi>, he would not drink.

verses.name: Matthew 27:35
verses.text: And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.

verses.name: Matthew 27:36
verses.text: And sitting down they watched him there;

verses.name: Matthew 27:37
verses.text: And set up over his head his accusation written, THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

verses.name: Matthew 27:38
verses.text: Then were there two thieves crucified with him, one on the right hand, and another on the left.

verses.name: Matthew 27:39
verses.text: ¶ And they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads,

verses.name: Matthew 27:40
verses.text: And saying, Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest <hi type="italic">it</hi> in three days, save thyself. If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.

verses.name: Matthew 27:41
verses.text: Likewise also the chief priests mocking <hi type="italic">him</hi>, with the scribes and elders, said,

verses.name: Matthew 27:42
verses.text: He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him.

verses.name: Matthew 27:43
verses.text: He trusted in God; let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of God.

verses.name: Matthew 27:44
verses.text: The thieves also, which were crucified with him, cast the same in his teeth.

verses.name: Matthew 27:45
verses.text: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.

verses.name: Matthew 27:46
verses.text: And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

verses.name: Matthew 27:47
verses.text: Some of them that stood there, when they heard <hi type="italic">that</hi>, said, This <hi type="italic">man</hi> calleth for Elias.

verses.name: Matthew 27:48
verses.text: And straightway one of them ran, and took a spunge, and filled <hi type="italic">it</hi> with vinegar, and put <hi type="italic">it</hi> on a reed, and gave him to drink.

verses.name: Matthew 27:49
verses.text: The rest said, Let be, let us see whether Elias will come to save him.

verses.name: Matthew 27:50
verses.text: ¶ Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.

verses.name: Matthew 27:51
verses.text: And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;

verses.name: Matthew 27:52
verses.text: And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,

verses.name: Matthew 27:53
verses.text: And came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many.

verses.name: Matthew 27:54
verses.text: Now when the centurion, and they that were with him, watching Jesus, saw the earthquake, and those things that were done, they feared greatly, saying, Truly this was the Son of God.

verses.name: Matthew 27:55
verses.text: And many women were there beholding afar off, which followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering unto him:

verses.name: Matthew 27:56
verses.text: Among which was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee’s children.

verses.name: Matthew 27:57
verses.text: When the even was come, there came a rich man of Arimathæa, named Joseph, who also himself was Jesus’ disciple:

verses.name: Matthew 27:58
verses.text: He went to Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded the body to be delivered.

verses.name: Matthew 27:59
verses.text: And when Joseph had taken the body, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,

verses.name: Matthew 27:60
verses.text: And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed.

verses.name: Matthew 27:61
verses.text: And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre.

verses.name: Matthew 27:62
verses.text: ¶ Now the next day, that followed the day of the preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees came together unto Pilate,

verses.name: Matthew 27:63
verses.text: Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again.

verses.name: Matthew 27:64
verses.text: Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away, and say unto the people, He is risen from the dead: so the last error shall be worse than the first.

verses.name: Matthew 27:65
verses.text: Pilate said unto them, Ye have a watch: go your way, make <hi type="italic">it</hi> as sure as ye can.

verses.name: Matthew 27:66
verses.text: So they went, and made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch.  <chapter eID="Matt.27"/><div eID="gen1040" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Matthew 28:1
verses.text: IN the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.

verses.name: Matthew 28:2
verses.text: And, behold, there was a great earthquake: for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it.

verses.name: Matthew 28:3
verses.text: His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow:

verses.name: Matthew 28:4
verses.text: And for fear of him the keepers did shake, and became as dead <hi type="italic">men</hi>.

verses.name: Matthew 28:5
verses.text: And the angel answered and said unto the women, Fear not ye: for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified.

verses.name: Matthew 28:6
verses.text: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.

verses.name: Matthew 28:7
verses.text: And go quickly, and tell his disciples that he is risen from the dead; and, behold, he goeth before you into Galilee; there shall ye see him: lo, I have told you.

verses.name: Matthew 28:8
verses.text: And they departed quickly from the sepulchre with fear and great joy; and did run to bring his disciples word.

verses.name: Matthew 28:9
verses.text: ¶ And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.

verses.name: Matthew 28:10
verses.text: Then said Jesus unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.

verses.name: Matthew 28:11
verses.text: ¶ Now when they were going, behold, some of the watch came into the city, and shewed unto the chief priests all the things that were done.

verses.name: Matthew 28:12
verses.text: And when they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave large money unto the soldiers,

verses.name: Matthew 28:13
verses.text: Saying, Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him <hi type="italic">away</hi> while we slept.

verses.name: Matthew 28:14
verses.text: And if this come to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him, and secure you.

verses.name: Matthew 28:15
verses.text: So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying is commonly reported among the Jews until this day.

verses.name: Matthew 28:16
verses.text: ¶ Then the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, into a mountain where Jesus had appointed them.

verses.name: Matthew 28:17
verses.text: And when they saw him, they worshipped him: but some doubted.

verses.name: Matthew 28:18
verses.text: And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.

verses.name: Matthew 28:19
verses.text: ¶ Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:

verses.name: Matthew 28:20
verses.text: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, <hi type="italic">even</hi> unto the end of the world. Amen.  <chapter eID="Matt.28"/><div eID="gen1041" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen1013" osisID="Matt" type="book"/>

verses.name: Mark 1:1
verses.text: THE beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God;

verses.name: Mark 1:2
verses.text: As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.

verses.name: Mark 1:3
verses.text: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.

verses.name: Mark 1:4
verses.text: John did baptize in the wilderness, and preach the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.

verses.name: Mark 1:5
verses.text: And there went out unto him all the land of Judæa, and they of Jerusalem, and were all baptized of him in the river of Jordan, confessing their sins.

verses.name: Mark 1:6
verses.text: And John was clothed with camel’s hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey;

verses.name: Mark 1:7
verses.text: And preached, saying, There cometh one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose.

verses.name: Mark 1:8
verses.text: I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Mark 1:9
verses.text: And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized of John in Jordan.

verses.name: Mark 1:10
verses.text: And straightway coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him:

verses.name: Mark 1:11
verses.text: And there came a voice from heaven, <hi type="italic">saying</hi>, Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

verses.name: Mark 1:12
verses.text: And immediately the Spirit driveth him into the wilderness.

verses.name: Mark 1:13
verses.text: And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him.

verses.name: Mark 1:14
verses.text: Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God,

verses.name: Mark 1:15
verses.text: And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.

verses.name: Mark 1:16
verses.text: Now as he walked by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.

verses.name: Mark 1:17
verses.text: And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.

verses.name: Mark 1:18
verses.text: And straightway they forsook their nets, and followed him.

verses.name: Mark 1:19
verses.text: And when he had gone a little further thence, he saw James the <hi type="italic">son</hi> of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets.

verses.name: Mark 1:20
verses.text: And straightway he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants, and went after him.

verses.name: Mark 1:21
verses.text: And they went into Capernaum; and straightway on the sabbath day he entered into the synagogue, and taught.

verses.name: Mark 1:22
verses.text: And they were astonished at his doctrine: for he taught them as one that had authority, and not as the scribes.

verses.name: Mark 1:23
verses.text: And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit; and he cried out,

verses.name: Mark 1:24
verses.text: Saying, Let <hi type="italic">us</hi> alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.

verses.name: Mark 1:25
verses.text: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him.

verses.name: Mark 1:26
verses.text: And when the unclean spirit had torn him, and cried with a loud voice, he came out of him.

verses.name: Mark 1:27
verses.text: And they were all amazed, insomuch that they questioned among themselves, saying, What thing is this? what new doctrine <hi type="italic">is</hi> this? for with authority commandeth he even the unclean spirits, and they do obey him.

verses.name: Mark 1:28
verses.text: And immediately his fame spread abroad throughout all the region round about Galilee.

verses.name: Mark 1:29
verses.text: And forthwith, when they were come out of the synagogue, they entered into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.

verses.name: Mark 1:30
verses.text: But Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick of a fever, and anon they tell him of her.

verses.name: Mark 1:31
verses.text: And he came and took her by the hand, and lifted her up; and immediately the fever left her, and she ministered unto them.

verses.name: Mark 1:32
verses.text: And at even, when the sun did set, they brought unto him all that were diseased, and them that were possessed with devils.

verses.name: Mark 1:33
verses.text: And all the city was gathered together at the door.

verses.name: Mark 1:34
verses.text: And he healed many that were sick of divers diseases, and cast out many devils; and suffered not the devils to speak, because they knew him.

verses.name: Mark 1:35
verses.text: And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.

verses.name: Mark 1:36
verses.text: And Simon and they that were with him followed after him.

verses.name: Mark 1:37
verses.text: And when they had found him, they said unto him, All <hi type="italic">men</hi> seek for thee.

verses.name: Mark 1:38
verses.text: And he said unto them, Let us go into the next towns, that I may preach there also: for therefore came I forth.

verses.name: Mark 1:39
verses.text: And he preached in their synagogues throughout all Galilee, and cast out devils.

verses.name: Mark 1:40
verses.text: And there came a leper to him, beseeching him, and kneeling down to him, and saying unto him, If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

verses.name: Mark 1:41
verses.text: And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth <hi type="italic">his</hi> hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean.

verses.name: Mark 1:42
verses.text: And as soon as he had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.

verses.name: Mark 1:43
verses.text: And he straitly charged him, and forthwith sent him away;

verses.name: Mark 1:44
verses.text: And saith unto him, See thou say nothing to any man: but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing those things which Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

verses.name: Mark 1:45
verses.text: But he went out, and began to publish <hi type="italic">it</hi> much, and to blaze abroad the matter, insomuch that Jesus could no more openly enter into the city, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from every quarter.  <chapter eID="Mark.1"/><div eID="gen1043" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 2:1
verses.text: AND again he entered into Capernaum, after <hi type="italic">some</hi> days; and it was noised that he was in the house.

verses.name: Mark 2:2
verses.text: And straightway many were gathered together, insomuch that there was no room to receive <hi type="italic">them</hi>, no, not so much as about the door: and he preached the word unto them.

verses.name: Mark 2:3
verses.text: And they come unto him, bringing one sick of the palsy, which was borne of four.

verses.name: Mark 2:4
verses.text: And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken <hi type="italic">it</hi> up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.

verses.name: Mark 2:5
verses.text: When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.

verses.name: Mark 2:6
verses.text: But there were certain of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,

verses.name: Mark 2:7
verses.text: Why doth this <hi type="italic">man</hi> thus speak blasphemies? who can forgive sins but God only?

verses.name: Mark 2:8
verses.text: And immediately when Jesus perceived in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, he said unto them, Why reason ye these things in your hearts?

verses.name: Mark 2:9
verses.text: Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, <hi type="italic">Thy</hi> sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?

verses.name: Mark 2:10
verses.text: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (he saith to the sick of the palsy,)

verses.name: Mark 2:11
verses.text: I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house.

verses.name: Mark 2:12
verses.text: And immediately he arose, took up the bed, and went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.

verses.name: Mark 2:13
verses.text: And he went forth again by the sea side; and all the multitude resorted unto him, and he taught them.

verses.name: Mark 2:14
verses.text: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the <hi type="italic">son</hi> of Alphæus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.

verses.name: Mark 2:15
verses.text: And it came to pass, that, as Jesus sat at meat in his house, many publicans and sinners sat also together with Jesus and his disciples: for there were many, and they followed him.

verses.name: Mark 2:16
verses.text: And when the scribes and Pharisees saw him eat with publicans and sinners, they said unto his disciples, How is it that he eateth and drinketh with publicans and sinners?

verses.name: Mark 2:17
verses.text: When Jesus heard <hi type="italic">it</hi>, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

verses.name: Mark 2:18
verses.text: And the disciples of John and of the Pharisees used to fast: and they come and say unto him, Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but thy disciples fast not?

verses.name: Mark 2:19
verses.text: And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

verses.name: Mark 2:20
verses.text: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.

verses.name: Mark 2:21
verses.text: No man also seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment: else the new piece that filled it up taketh away from the old, and the rent is made worse.

verses.name: Mark 2:22
verses.text: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles: else the new wine doth burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be marred: but new wine must be put into new bottles.

verses.name: Mark 2:23
verses.text: And it came to pass, that he went through the corn fields on the sabbath day; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of corn.

verses.name: Mark 2:24
verses.text: And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful?

verses.name: Mark 2:25
verses.text: And he said unto them, Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him?

verses.name: Mark 2:26
verses.text: How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?

verses.name: Mark 2:27
verses.text: And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:

verses.name: Mark 2:28
verses.text: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.  <chapter eID="Mark.2"/><div eID="gen1044" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 3:1
verses.text: AND he entered again into the synagogue; and there was a man there which had a withered hand.

verses.name: Mark 3:2
verses.text: And they watched him, whether he would heal him on the sabbath day; that they might accuse him.

verses.name: Mark 3:3
verses.text: And he saith unto the man which had the withered hand, Stand forth.

verses.name: Mark 3:4
verses.text: And he saith unto them, Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? to save life, or to kill? But they held their peace.

verses.name: Mark 3:5
verses.text: And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, he saith unto the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched <hi type="italic">it</hi> out: and his hand was restored whole as the other.

verses.name: Mark 3:6
verses.text: And the Pharisees went forth, and straightway took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.

verses.name: Mark 3:7
verses.text: But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judæa,

verses.name: Mark 3:8
verses.text: And from Jerusalem, and from Idumæa, and <hi type="italic">from</hi> beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him.

verses.name: Mark 3:9
verses.text: And he spake to his disciples, that a small ship should wait on him because of the multitude, lest they should throng him.

verses.name: Mark 3:10
verses.text: For he had healed many; insomuch that they pressed upon him for to touch him, as many as had plagues.

verses.name: Mark 3:11
verses.text: And unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God.

verses.name: Mark 3:12
verses.text: And he straitly charged them that they should not make him known.

verses.name: Mark 3:13
verses.text: And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth <hi type="italic">unto him</hi> whom he would: and they came unto him.

verses.name: Mark 3:14
verses.text: And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,

verses.name: Mark 3:15
verses.text: And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:

verses.name: Mark 3:16
verses.text: And Simon he surnamed Peter;

verses.name: Mark 3:17
verses.text: And James the <hi type="italic">son</hi> of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:

verses.name: Mark 3:18
verses.text: And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the <hi type="italic">son</hi> of Alphæus, and Thaddæus, and Simon the Canaanite,

verses.name: Mark 3:19
verses.text: And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.

verses.name: Mark 3:20
verses.text: And the multitude cometh together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.

verses.name: Mark 3:21
verses.text: And when his friends heard <hi type="italic">of it</hi>, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself.

verses.name: Mark 3:22
verses.text: ¶ And the scribes which came down from Jerusalem said, He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.

verses.name: Mark 3:23
verses.text: And he called them <hi type="italic">unto him</hi>, and said unto them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?

verses.name: Mark 3:24
verses.text: And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.

verses.name: Mark 3:25
verses.text: And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.

verses.name: Mark 3:26
verses.text: And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.

verses.name: Mark 3:27
verses.text: No man can enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he will first bind the strong man; and then he will spoil his house.

verses.name: Mark 3:28
verses.text: Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:

verses.name: Mark 3:29
verses.text: But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation:

verses.name: Mark 3:30
verses.text: Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.

verses.name: Mark 3:31
verses.text: ¶ There came then his brethren and his mother, and, standing without, sent unto him, calling him.

verses.name: Mark 3:32
verses.text: And the multitude sat about him, and they said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren without seek for thee.

verses.name: Mark 3:33
verses.text: And he answered them, saying, Who is my mother, or my brethren?

verses.name: Mark 3:34
verses.text: And he looked round about on them which sat about him, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren!

verses.name: Mark 3:35
verses.text: For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.  <chapter eID="Mark.3"/><div eID="gen1045" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 4:1
verses.text: AND he began again to teach by the sea side: and there was gathered unto him a great multitude, so that he entered into a ship, and sat in the sea; and the whole multitude was by the sea on the land.

verses.name: Mark 4:2
verses.text: And he taught them many things by parables, and said unto them in his doctrine,

verses.name: Mark 4:3
verses.text: Hearken; Behold, there went out a sower to sow:

verses.name: Mark 4:4
verses.text: And it came to pass, as he sowed, some fell by the way side, and the fowls of the air came and devoured it up.

verses.name: Mark 4:5
verses.text: And some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth:

verses.name: Mark 4:6
verses.text: But when the sun was up, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.

verses.name: Mark 4:7
verses.text: And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.

verses.name: Mark 4:8
verses.text: And other fell on good ground, and did yield fruit that sprang up and increased; and brought forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred.

verses.name: Mark 4:9
verses.text: And he said unto them, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

verses.name: Mark 4:10
verses.text: And when he was alone, they that were about him with the twelve asked of him the parable.

verses.name: Mark 4:11
verses.text: And he said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all <hi type="italic">these</hi> things are done in parables:

verses.name: Mark 4:12
verses.text: That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and <hi type="italic">their</hi> sins should be forgiven them.

verses.name: Mark 4:13
verses.text: And he said unto them, Know ye not this parable? and how then will ye know all parables?

verses.name: Mark 4:14
verses.text: ¶ The sower soweth the word.

verses.name: Mark 4:15
verses.text: And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.

verses.name: Mark 4:16
verses.text: And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness;

verses.name: Mark 4:17
verses.text: And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.

verses.name: Mark 4:18
verses.text: And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word,

verses.name: Mark 4:19
verses.text: And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.

verses.name: Mark 4:20
verses.text: And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive <hi type="italic">it</hi>, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.

verses.name: Mark 4:21
verses.text: ¶ And he said unto them, Is a candle brought to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick?

verses.name: Mark 4:22
verses.text: For there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested; neither was any thing kept secret, but that it should come abroad.

verses.name: Mark 4:23
verses.text: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.

verses.name: Mark 4:24
verses.text: And he said unto them, Take heed what ye hear: with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given.

verses.name: Mark 4:25
verses.text: For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he hath.

verses.name: Mark 4:26
verses.text: ¶ And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground;

verses.name: Mark 4:27
verses.text: And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how.

verses.name: Mark 4:28
verses.text: For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.

verses.name: Mark 4:29
verses.text: But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come.

verses.name: Mark 4:30
verses.text: ¶ And he said, Whereunto shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it?

verses.name: Mark 4:31
verses.text: <hi type="italic">It is</hi> like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, is less than all the seeds that be in the earth:

verses.name: Mark 4:32
verses.text: But when it is sown, it groweth up, and becometh greater than all herbs, and shooteth out great branches; so that the fowls of the air may lodge under the shadow of it.

verses.name: Mark 4:33
verses.text: And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Mark 4:34
verses.text: But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.

verses.name: Mark 4:35
verses.text: And the same day, when the even was come, he saith unto them, Let us pass over unto the other side.

verses.name: Mark 4:36
verses.text: And when they had sent away the multitude, they took him even as he was in the ship. And there were also with him other little ships.

verses.name: Mark 4:37
verses.text: And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full.

verses.name: Mark 4:38
verses.text: And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?

verses.name: Mark 4:39
verses.text: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

verses.name: Mark 4:40
verses.text: And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?

verses.name: Mark 4:41
verses.text: And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?  <chapter eID="Mark.4"/><div eID="gen1046" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 5:1
verses.text: AND they came over unto the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.

verses.name: Mark 5:2
verses.text: And when he was come out of the ship, immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,

verses.name: Mark 5:3
verses.text: Who had <hi type="italic">his</hi> dwelling among the tombs; and no man could bind him, no, not with chains:

verses.name: Mark 5:4
verses.text: Because that he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been plucked asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: neither could any <hi type="italic">man</hi> tame him.

verses.name: Mark 5:5
verses.text: And always, night and day, he was in the mountains, and in the tombs, crying, and cutting himself with stones.

verses.name: Mark 5:6
verses.text: But when he saw Jesus afar off, he ran and worshipped him,

verses.name: Mark 5:7
verses.text: And cried with a loud voice, and said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, <hi type="italic">thou</hi> Son of the most high God? I adjure thee by God, that thou torment me not.

verses.name: Mark 5:8
verses.text: For he said unto him, Come out of the man, <hi type="italic">thou</hi> unclean spirit.

verses.name: Mark 5:9
verses.text: And he asked him, What <hi type="italic">is</hi> thy name? And he answered, saying, My name <hi type="italic">is</hi> Legion: for we are many.

verses.name: Mark 5:10
verses.text: And he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country.

verses.name: Mark 5:11
verses.text: Now there was there nigh unto the mountains a great herd of swine feeding.

verses.name: Mark 5:12
verses.text: And all the devils besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them.

verses.name: Mark 5:13
verses.text: And forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea.

verses.name: Mark 5:14
verses.text: And they that fed the swine fled, and told <hi type="italic">it</hi> in the city, and in the country. And they went out to see what it was that was done.

verses.name: Mark 5:15
verses.text: And they come to Jesus, and see him that was possessed with the devil, and had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.

verses.name: Mark 5:16
verses.text: And they that saw <hi type="italic">it</hi> told them how it befell to him that was possessed with the devil, and <hi type="italic">also</hi> concerning the swine.

verses.name: Mark 5:17
verses.text: And they began to pray him to depart out of their coasts.

verses.name: Mark 5:18
verses.text: And when he was come into the ship, he that had been possessed with the devil prayed him that he might be with him.

verses.name: Mark 5:19
verses.text: Howbeit Jesus suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.

verses.name: Mark 5:20
verses.text: And he departed, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him: and all <hi type="italic">men</hi> did marvel.

verses.name: Mark 5:21
verses.text: And when Jesus was passed over again by ship unto the other side, much people gathered unto him: and he was nigh unto the sea.

verses.name: Mark 5:22
verses.text: And, behold, there cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name; and when he saw him, he fell at his feet,

verses.name: Mark 5:23
verses.text: And besought him greatly, saying, My little daughter lieth at the point of death: <hi type="italic">I pray thee</hi>, come and lay thy hands on her, that she may be healed; and she shall live.

verses.name: Mark 5:24
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">Jesus</hi> went with him; and much people followed him, and thronged him.

verses.name: Mark 5:25
verses.text: And a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years,

verses.name: Mark 5:26
verses.text: And had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse,

verses.name: Mark 5:27
verses.text: When she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment.

verses.name: Mark 5:28
verses.text: For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.

verses.name: Mark 5:29
verses.text: And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in <hi type="italic">her</hi> body that she was healed of that plague.

verses.name: Mark 5:30
verses.text: And Jesus, immediately knowing in himself that virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in the press, and said, Who touched my clothes?

verses.name: Mark 5:31
verses.text: And his disciples said unto him, Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?

verses.name: Mark 5:32
verses.text: And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing.

verses.name: Mark 5:33
verses.text: But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.

verses.name: Mark 5:34
verses.text: And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.

verses.name: Mark 5:35
verses.text: While he yet spake, there came from the ruler of the synagogue’s <hi type="italic">house certain</hi> which said, Thy daughter is dead: why troublest thou the Master any further?

verses.name: Mark 5:36
verses.text: As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe.

verses.name: Mark 5:37
verses.text: And he suffered no man to follow him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.

verses.name: Mark 5:38
verses.text: And he cometh to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and seeth the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly.

verses.name: Mark 5:39
verses.text: And when he was come in, he saith unto them, Why make ye this ado, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth.

verses.name: Mark 5:40
verses.text: And they laughed him to scorn. But when he had put them all out, he taketh the father and the mother of the damsel, and them that were with him, and entereth in where the damsel was lying.

verses.name: Mark 5:41
verses.text: And he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.

verses.name: Mark 5:42
verses.text: And straightway the damsel arose, and walked; for she was <hi type="italic">of the age</hi> of twelve years. And they were astonished with a great astonishment.

verses.name: Mark 5:43
verses.text: And he charged them straitly that no man should know it; and commanded that something should be given her to eat.  <chapter eID="Mark.5"/><div eID="gen1047" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 6:1
verses.text: AND he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him.

verses.name: Mark 6:2
verses.text: And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing <hi type="italic">him</hi> were astonished, saying, From whence hath this <hi type="italic">man</hi> these things? and what wisdom <hi type="italic">is</hi> this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands?

verses.name: Mark 6:3
verses.text: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.

verses.name: Mark 6:4
verses.text: But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.

verses.name: Mark 6:5
verses.text: And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed <hi type="italic">them</hi>.

verses.name: Mark 6:6
verses.text: And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching.

verses.name: Mark 6:7
verses.text: ¶ And he called <hi type="italic">unto him</hi> the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and gave them power over unclean spirits;

verses.name: Mark 6:8
verses.text: And commanded them that they should take nothing for <hi type="italic">their</hi> journey, save a staff only; no scrip, no bread, no money in <hi type="italic">their</hi> purse:

verses.name: Mark 6:9
verses.text: But <hi type="italic">be</hi> shod with sandals; and not put on two coats.

verses.name: Mark 6:10
verses.text: And he said unto them, In what place soever ye enter into an house, there abide till ye depart from that place.

verses.name: Mark 6:11
verses.text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when ye depart thence, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.

verses.name: Mark 6:12
verses.text: And they went out, and preached that men should repent.

verses.name: Mark 6:13
verses.text: And they cast out many devils, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed <hi type="italic">them</hi>.

verses.name: Mark 6:14
verses.text: And king Herod heard <hi type="italic">of him;</hi> (for his name was spread abroad:) and he said, That John the Baptist was risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works do shew forth themselves in him.

verses.name: Mark 6:15
verses.text: Others said, That it is Elias. And others said, That it is a prophet, or as one of the prophets.

verses.name: Mark 6:16
verses.text: But when Herod heard <hi type="italic">thereof</hi>, he said, It is John, whom I beheaded: he is risen from the dead.

verses.name: Mark 6:17
verses.text: For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife: for he had married her.

verses.name: Mark 6:18
verses.text: For John had said unto Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother’s wife.

verses.name: Mark 6:19
verses.text: Therefore Herodias had a quarrel against him, and would have killed him; but she could not:

verses.name: Mark 6:20
verses.text: For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just man and an holy, and observed him; and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly.

verses.name: Mark 6:21
verses.text: And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief <hi type="italic">estates</hi> of Galilee;

verses.name: Mark 6:22
verses.text: And when the daughter of the said Herodias came in, and danced, and pleased Herod and them that sat with him, the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever thou wilt, and I will give <hi type="italic">it</hi> thee.

verses.name: Mark 6:23
verses.text: And he sware unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I will give <hi type="italic">it</hi> thee, unto the half of my kingdom.

verses.name: Mark 6:24
verses.text: And she went forth, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptist.

verses.name: Mark 6:25
verses.text: And she came in straightway with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou give me by and by in a charger the head of John the Baptist.

verses.name: Mark 6:26
verses.text: And the king was exceeding sorry; <hi type="italic">yet</hi> for his oath’s sake, and for their sakes which sat with him, he would not reject her.

verses.name: Mark 6:27
verses.text: And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,

verses.name: Mark 6:28
verses.text: And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.

verses.name: Mark 6:29
verses.text: And when his disciples heard <hi type="italic">of it</hi>, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.

verses.name: Mark 6:30
verses.text: And the apostles gathered themselves together unto Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught.

verses.name: Mark 6:31
verses.text: And he said unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.

verses.name: Mark 6:32
verses.text: And they departed into a desert place by ship privately.

verses.name: Mark 6:33
verses.text: And the people saw them departing, and many knew him, and ran afoot thither out of all cities, and outwent them, and came together unto him.

verses.name: Mark 6:34
verses.text: And Jesus, when he came out, saw much people, and was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things.

verses.name: Mark 6:35
verses.text: And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him, and said, This is a desert place, and now the time <hi type="italic">is</hi> far passed:

verses.name: Mark 6:36
verses.text: Send them away, that they may go into the country round about, and into the villages, and buy themselves bread: for they have nothing to eat.

verses.name: Mark 6:37
verses.text: He answered and said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they say unto him, Shall we go and buy two hundred pennyworth of bread, and give them to eat?

verses.name: Mark 6:38
verses.text: He saith unto them, How many loaves have ye? go and see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes.

verses.name: Mark 6:39
verses.text: And he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass.

verses.name: Mark 6:40
verses.text: And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties.

verses.name: Mark 6:41
verses.text: And when he had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves, and gave <hi type="italic">them</hi> to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all.

verses.name: Mark 6:42
verses.text: And they did all eat, and were filled.

verses.name: Mark 6:43
verses.text: And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes.

verses.name: Mark 6:44
verses.text: And they that did eat of the loaves were about five thousand men.

verses.name: Mark 6:45
verses.text: And straightway he constrained his disciples to get into the ship, and to go to the other side before unto Bethsaida, while he sent away the people.

verses.name: Mark 6:46
verses.text: And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.

verses.name: Mark 6:47
verses.text: And when even was come, the ship was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land.

verses.name: Mark 6:48
verses.text: And he saw them toiling in rowing; for the wind was contrary unto them: and about the fourth watch of the night he cometh unto them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them.

verses.name: Mark 6:49
verses.text: But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out:

verses.name: Mark 6:50
verses.text: For they all saw him, and were troubled. And immediately he talked with them, and saith unto them, Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid.

verses.name: Mark 6:51
verses.text: And he went up unto them into the ship; and the wind ceased: and they were sore amazed in themselves beyond measure, and wondered.

verses.name: Mark 6:52
verses.text: For they considered not <hi type="italic">the miracle</hi> of the loaves: for their heart was hardened.

verses.name: Mark 6:53
verses.text: And when they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore.

verses.name: Mark 6:54
verses.text: And when they were come out of the ship, straightway they knew him,

verses.name: Mark 6:55
verses.text: And ran through that whole region round about, and began to carry about in beds those that were sick, where they heard he was.

verses.name: Mark 6:56
verses.text: And whithersoever he entered, into villages, or cities, or country, they laid the sick in the streets, and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him were made whole.  <chapter eID="Mark.6"/><div eID="gen1048" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 7:1
verses.text: THEN came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.

verses.name: Mark 7:2
verses.text: And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is to say, with unwashen, hands, they found fault.

verses.name: Mark 7:3
verses.text: For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash <hi type="italic">their</hi> hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders.

verses.name: Mark 7:4
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">when they come</hi> from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there be, which they have received to hold, <hi type="italic">as</hi> the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels, and of tables.

verses.name: Mark 7:5
verses.text: Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?

verses.name: Mark 7:6
verses.text: He answered and said unto them, Well hath Esaias prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth me with <hi type="italic">their</hi> lips, but their heart is far from me.

verses.name: Mark 7:7
verses.text: Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching <hi type="italic">for</hi> doctrines the commandments of men.

verses.name: Mark 7:8
verses.text: For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, <hi type="italic">as</hi> the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.

verses.name: Mark 7:9
verses.text: And he said unto them, Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition.

verses.name: Mark 7:10
verses.text: For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:

verses.name: Mark 7:11
verses.text: But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, <hi type="italic">It is</hi> Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; <hi type="italic">he shall be free</hi>.

verses.name: Mark 7:12
verses.text: And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;

verses.name: Mark 7:13
verses.text: Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.

verses.name: Mark 7:14
verses.text: ¶ And when he had called all the people <hi type="italic">unto him</hi>, he said unto them, Hearken unto me every one <hi type="italic">of you</hi>, and understand:

verses.name: Mark 7:15
verses.text: There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man.

verses.name: Mark 7:16
verses.text: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.

verses.name: Mark 7:17
verses.text: And when he was entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.

verses.name: Mark 7:18
verses.text: And he saith unto them, Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, <hi type="italic">it</hi> cannot defile him;

verses.name: Mark 7:19
verses.text: Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?

verses.name: Mark 7:20
verses.text: And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.

verses.name: Mark 7:21
verses.text: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,

verses.name: Mark 7:22
verses.text: Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:

verses.name: Mark 7:23
verses.text: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.

verses.name: Mark 7:24
verses.text: ¶ And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know <hi type="italic">it:</hi> but he could not be hid.

verses.name: Mark 7:25
verses.text: For a <hi type="italic">certain</hi> woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet:

verses.name: Mark 7:26
verses.text: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.

verses.name: Mark 7:27
verses.text: But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast <hi type="italic">it</hi> unto the dogs.

verses.name: Mark 7:28
verses.text: And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.

verses.name: Mark 7:29
verses.text: And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.

verses.name: Mark 7:30
verses.text: And when she was come to her house, she found the devil gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed.

verses.name: Mark 7:31
verses.text: ¶ And again, departing from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the coasts of Decapolis.

verses.name: Mark 7:32
verses.text: And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to put his hand upon him.

verses.name: Mark 7:33
verses.text: And he took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spit, and touched his tongue;

verses.name: Mark 7:34
verses.text: And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.

verses.name: Mark 7:35
verses.text: And straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.

verses.name: Mark 7:36
verses.text: And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published <hi type="italic">it;</hi>

verses.name: Mark 7:37
verses.text: And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.  <chapter eID="Mark.7"/><div eID="gen1049" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 8:1
verses.text: IN those days the multitude being very great, and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples <hi type="italic">unto him</hi>, and saith unto them,

verses.name: Mark 8:2
verses.text: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with me three days, and have nothing to eat:

verses.name: Mark 8:3
verses.text: And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way: for divers of them came from far.

verses.name: Mark 8:4
verses.text: And his disciples answered him, From whence can a man satisfy these <hi type="italic">men</hi> with bread here in the wilderness?

verses.name: Mark 8:5
verses.text: And he asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.

verses.name: Mark 8:6
verses.text: And he commanded the people to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and gave thanks, and brake, and gave to his disciples to set before <hi type="italic">them;</hi> and they did set <hi type="italic">them</hi> before the people.

verses.name: Mark 8:7
verses.text: And they had a few small fishes: and he blessed, and commanded to set them also before <hi type="italic">them</hi>.

verses.name: Mark 8:8
verses.text: So they did eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken <hi type="italic">meat</hi> that was left seven baskets.

verses.name: Mark 8:9
verses.text: And they that had eaten were about four thousand: and he sent them away.

verses.name: Mark 8:10
verses.text: ¶ And straightway he entered into a ship with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.

verses.name: Mark 8:11
verses.text: And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, tempting him.

verses.name: Mark 8:12
verses.text: And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek after a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.

verses.name: Mark 8:13
verses.text: And he left them, and entering into the ship again departed to the other side.

verses.name: Mark 8:14
verses.text: ¶ Now <hi type="italic">the disciples</hi> had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the ship with them more than one loaf.

verses.name: Mark 8:15
verses.text: And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and <hi type="italic">of</hi> the leaven of Herod.

verses.name: Mark 8:16
verses.text: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, <hi type="italic">It is</hi> because we have no bread.

verses.name: Mark 8:17
verses.text: And when Jesus knew <hi type="italic">it</hi>, he saith unto them, Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened?

verses.name: Mark 8:18
verses.text: Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?

verses.name: Mark 8:19
verses.text: When I brake the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? They say unto him, Twelve.

verses.name: Mark 8:20
verses.text: And when the seven among four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? And they said, Seven.

verses.name: Mark 8:21
verses.text: And he said unto them, How is it that ye do not understand?

verses.name: Mark 8:22
verses.text: ¶ And he cometh to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man unto him, and besought him to touch him.

verses.name: Mark 8:23
verses.text: And he took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town; and when he had spit on his eyes, and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw ought.

verses.name: Mark 8:24
verses.text: And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.

verses.name: Mark 8:25
verses.text: After that he put <hi type="italic">his</hi> hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.

verses.name: Mark 8:26
verses.text: And he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither go into the town, nor tell <hi type="italic">it</hi> to any in the town.

verses.name: Mark 8:27
verses.text: ¶ And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Cæsarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?

verses.name: Mark 8:28
verses.text: And they answered, John the Baptist: but some <hi type="italic">say</hi>, Elias; and others, One of the prophets.

verses.name: Mark 8:29
verses.text: And he saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.

verses.name: Mark 8:30
verses.text: And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.

verses.name: Mark 8:31
verses.text: And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and <hi type="italic">of</hi> the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.

verses.name: Mark 8:32
verses.text: And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.

verses.name: Mark 8:33
verses.text: But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.

verses.name: Mark 8:34
verses.text: ¶ And when he had called the people <hi type="italic">unto him</hi> with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

verses.name: Mark 8:35
verses.text: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it.

verses.name: Mark 8:36
verses.text: For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?

verses.name: Mark 8:37
verses.text: Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?

verses.name: Mark 8:38
verses.text: Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.  <chapter eID="Mark.8"/><div eID="gen1050" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 9:1
verses.text: AND he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.

verses.name: Mark 9:2
verses.text: ¶ And after six days Jesus taketh <hi type="italic">with him</hi> Peter, and James, and John, and leadeth them up into an high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them.

verses.name: Mark 9:3
verses.text: And his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can white them.

verses.name: Mark 9:4
verses.text: And there appeared unto them Elias with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.

verses.name: Mark 9:5
verses.text: And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

verses.name: Mark 9:6
verses.text: For he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid.

verses.name: Mark 9:7
verses.text: And there was a cloud that overshadowed them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.

verses.name: Mark 9:8
verses.text: And suddenly, when they had looked round about, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves.

verses.name: Mark 9:9
verses.text: And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, till the Son of man were risen from the dead.

verses.name: Mark 9:10
verses.text: And they kept that saying with themselves, questioning one with another what the rising from the dead should mean.

verses.name: Mark 9:11
verses.text: ¶ And they asked him, saying, Why say the scribes that Elias must first come?

verses.name: Mark 9:12
verses.text: And he answered and told them, Elias verily cometh first, and restoreth all things; and how it is written of the Son of man, that he must suffer many things, and be set at nought.

verses.name: Mark 9:13
verses.text: But I say unto you, That Elias is indeed come, and they have done unto him whatsoever they listed, as it is written of him.

verses.name: Mark 9:14
verses.text: ¶ And when he came to <hi type="italic">his</hi> disciples, he saw a great multitude about them, and the scribes questioning with them.

verses.name: Mark 9:15
verses.text: And straightway all the people, when they beheld him, were greatly amazed, and running to <hi type="italic">him</hi> saluted him.

verses.name: Mark 9:16
verses.text: And he asked the scribes, What question ye with them?

verses.name: Mark 9:17
verses.text: And one of the multitude answered and said, Master, I have brought unto thee my son, which hath a dumb spirit;

verses.name: Mark 9:18
verses.text: And wheresoever he taketh him, he teareth him: and he foameth, and gnasheth with his teeth, and pineth away: and I spake to thy disciples that they should cast him out; and they could not.

verses.name: Mark 9:19
verses.text: He answereth him, and saith, O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him unto me.

verses.name: Mark 9:20
verses.text: And they brought him unto him: and when he saw him, straightway the spirit tare him; and he fell on the ground, and wallowed foaming.

verses.name: Mark 9:21
verses.text: And he asked his father, How long is it ago since this came unto him? And he said, Of a child.

verses.name: Mark 9:22
verses.text: And ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him: but if thou canst do any thing, have compassion on us, and help us.

verses.name: Mark 9:23
verses.text: Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe, all things <hi type="italic">are</hi> possible to him that believeth.

verses.name: Mark 9:24
verses.text: And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.

verses.name: Mark 9:25
verses.text: When Jesus saw that the people came running together, he rebuked the foul spirit, saying unto him, <hi type="italic">Thou</hi> dumb and deaf spirit, I charge thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.

verses.name: Mark 9:26
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">the spirit</hi> cried, and rent him sore, and came out of him: and he was as one dead; insomuch that many said, He is dead.

verses.name: Mark 9:27
verses.text: But Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up; and he arose.

verses.name: Mark 9:28
verses.text: And when he was come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, Why could not we cast him out?

verses.name: Mark 9:29
verses.text: And he said unto them, This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.

verses.name: Mark 9:30
verses.text: ¶ And they departed thence, and passed through Galilee; and he would not that any man should know <hi type="italic">it</hi>.

verses.name: Mark 9:31
verses.text: For he taught his disciples, and said unto them, The Son of man is delivered into the hands of men, and they shall kill him; and after that he is killed, he shall rise the third day.

verses.name: Mark 9:32
verses.text: But they understood not that saying, and were afraid to ask him.

verses.name: Mark 9:33
verses.text: ¶ And he came to Capernaum: and being in the house he asked them, What was it that ye disputed among yourselves by the way?

verses.name: Mark 9:34
verses.text: But they held their peace: for by the way they had disputed among themselves, who <hi type="italic">should be</hi> the greatest.

verses.name: Mark 9:35
verses.text: And he sat down, and called the twelve, and saith unto them, If any man desire to be first, <hi type="italic">the same</hi> shall be last of all, and servant of all.

verses.name: Mark 9:36
verses.text: And he took a child, and set him in the midst of them: and when he had taken him in his arms, he said unto them,

verses.name: Mark 9:37
verses.text: Whosoever shall receive one of such children in my name, receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.

verses.name: Mark 9:38
verses.text: ¶ And John answered him, saying, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name, and he followeth not us: and we forbad him, because he followeth not us.

verses.name: Mark 9:39
verses.text: But Jesus said, Forbid him not: for there is no man which shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me.

verses.name: Mark 9:40
verses.text: For he that is not against us is on our part.

verses.name: Mark 9:41
verses.text: For whosoever shall give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because ye belong to Christ, verily I say unto you, he shall not lose his reward.

verses.name: Mark 9:42
verses.text: And whosoever shall offend one of <hi type="italic">these</hi> little ones that believe in me, it is better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea.

verses.name: Mark 9:43
verses.text: And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:

verses.name: Mark 9:44
verses.text: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

verses.name: Mark 9:45
verses.text: And if thy foot offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter halt into life, than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:

verses.name: Mark 9:46
verses.text: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

verses.name: Mark 9:47
verses.text: And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out: it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire:

verses.name: Mark 9:48
verses.text: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

verses.name: Mark 9:49
verses.text: For every one shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt.

verses.name: Mark 9:50
verses.text: Salt <hi type="italic">is</hi> good: but if the salt have lost his saltness, wherewith will ye season it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace one with another.  <chapter eID="Mark.9"/><div eID="gen1051" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Mark 10:1
verses.text: AND he arose from thence, and cometh into the coasts of Judæa by the farther side of Jordan: and the people resort unto him again; and, as he was wont, he taught them again.

verses.name: Mark 10:2
verses.text: ¶ And the Pharisees came to him, and asked him, Is it lawful for a man to put away <hi type="italic">his</hi> wife? tempting him.

verses.name: Mark 10:3
verses.text: And he answered and said unto them, What did Moses command you?

verses.name: Mark 10:4
verses.text: And they said, Moses suffered to write a bill of divorcement, and to put <hi type="italic">her</hi> away.

verses.name: Mark 10:5
verses.text: And Jesus answered and said unto them, For the hardness of your heart he wrote you this precept.

verses.name: Mark 10:6
verses.text: But from the beginning of the creation God made them male and female.

verses.name: Mark 10:7
verses.text: For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife;

verses.name: Mark 10:8
verses.text: And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh.

verses.name: Mark 10:9
verses.text: What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

verses.name: Mark 10:10
verses.text: And in the house his disciples asked him again of the same <hi type="italic">matter</hi>.

verses.name: Mark 10:11
verses.text: And he saith unto them, Whosoever shall put away his wife, and marry another, committeth adultery against her.

verses.name: Mark 10:12
verses.text: And if a woman shall put away her husband, and be married to another, she committeth adultery.

verses.name: Mark 10:13
verses.text: ¶ And they brought young children to him, that he should touch them: and <hi type="italic">his</hi> disciples rebuked those that brought <hi type="italic">them</hi>.

verses.name: Mark 10:14
verses.text: But when Jesus saw <hi type="italic">it</hi>, he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Mark 10:15
verses.text: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein.

verses.name: Mark 10:16
verses.text: And he took them up in his arms, put <hi type="italic">his</hi> hands upon them, and blessed them.

verses.name: Mark 10:17
verses.text: ¶ And when he was gone forth into the way, there came one running, and kneeled to him, and asked him, Good Master, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?

verses.name: Mark 10:18
verses.text: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? <hi type="italic">there is</hi> none good but one, <hi type="italic">that is</hi>, God.

verses.name: Mark 10:19
verses.text: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Defraud not, Honour thy father and mother.

verses.name: Mark 10:20
verses.text: And he answered and said unto him, Master, all these have I observed from my youth.

verses.name: Mark 10:21
verses.text: Then Jesus beholding him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me.

verses.name: Mark 10:22
verses.text: And he was sad at that saying, and went away grieved: for he had great possessions.

verses.name: Mark 10:23
verses.text: ¶ And Jesus looked round about, and saith unto his disciples, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!

verses.name: Mark 10:24
verses.text: And the disciples were astonished at his words. But Jesus answereth again, and saith unto them, Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God!

verses.name: Mark 10:25
verses.text: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Mark 10:26
verses.text: And they were astonished out of measure, saying among themselves, Who then can be saved?

verses.name: Mark 10:27
verses.text: And Jesus looking upon them saith, With men <hi type="italic">it is</hi> impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible.

verses.name: Mark 10:28
