verses.text: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.

verses.name: Acts 17:12
verses.text: Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.

verses.name: Acts 17:13
verses.text: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.

verses.name: Acts 17:14
verses.text: And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.

verses.name: Acts 17:15
verses.text: And they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed.

verses.name: Acts 17:16
verses.text: ¶ Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry.

verses.name: Acts 17:17
verses.text: Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him.

verses.name: Acts 17:18
verses.text: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection.

verses.name: Acts 17:19
verses.text: And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, <hi type="italic">is?</hi>

verses.name: Acts 17:20
verses.text: For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears: we would know therefore what these things mean.

verses.name: Acts 17:21
verses.text: (For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.)

verses.name: Acts 17:22
verses.text: ¶ Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars’ hill, and said, <hi type="italic">Ye</hi> men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.

verses.name: Acts 17:23
verses.text: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you.

verses.name: Acts 17:24
verses.text: God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands;

verses.name: Acts 17:25
verses.text: Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things;

verses.name: Acts 17:26
verses.text: And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;

verses.name: Acts 17:27
verses.text: That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us:

verses.name: Acts 17:28
verses.text: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.

verses.name: Acts 17:29
verses.text: Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device.

verses.name: Acts 17:30
verses.text: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:

verses.name: Acts 17:31
verses.text: Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by <hi type="italic">that</hi> man whom he hath ordained; <hi type="italic">whereof</hi> he hath given assurance unto all <hi type="italic">men</hi>, in that he hath raised him from the dead.

verses.name: Acts 17:32
verses.text: ¶ And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear thee again of this <hi type="italic">matter</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 17:33
verses.text: So Paul departed from among them.

verses.name: Acts 17:34
verses.text: Howbeit certain men clave unto him, and believed: among the which <hi type="italic">was</hi> Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.  <chapter eID="Acts.17"/><div eID="gen1123" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 18:1
verses.text: AFTER these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;

verses.name: Acts 18:2
verses.text: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them.

verses.name: Acts 18:3
verses.text: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.

verses.name: Acts 18:4
verses.text: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.

verses.name: Acts 18:5
verses.text: And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit, and testified to the Jews <hi type="italic">that</hi> Jesus <hi type="italic">was</hi> Christ.

verses.name: Acts 18:6
verses.text: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook <hi type="italic">his</hi> raiment, and said unto them, Your blood <hi type="italic">be</hi> upon your own heads; I <hi type="italic">am</hi> clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.

verses.name: Acts 18:7
verses.text: ¶ And he departed thence, and entered into a certain <hi type="italic">man</hi>’<hi type="italic">s</hi> house, named Justus, <hi type="italic">one</hi> that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue.

verses.name: Acts 18:8
verses.text: And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.

verses.name: Acts 18:9
verses.text: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:

verses.name: Acts 18:10
verses.text: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.

verses.name: Acts 18:11
verses.text: And he continued <hi type="italic">there</hi> a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.

verses.name: Acts 18:12
verses.text: ¶ And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,

verses.name: Acts 18:13
verses.text: Saying, This <hi type="italic">fellow</hi> persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.

verses.name: Acts 18:14
verses.text: And when Paul was now about to open <hi type="italic">his</hi> mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O <hi type="italic">ye</hi> Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:

verses.name: Acts 18:15
verses.text: But if it be a question of words and names, and <hi type="italic">of</hi> your law, look ye <hi type="italic">to it;</hi> for I will be no judge of such <hi type="italic">matters</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 18:16
verses.text: And he drave them from the judgment seat.

verses.name: Acts 18:17
verses.text: Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat <hi type="italic">him</hi> before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.

verses.name: Acts 18:18
verses.text: ¶ And Paul <hi type="italic">after this</hi> tarried <hi type="italic">there</hi> yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn <hi type="italic">his</hi> head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.

verses.name: Acts 18:19
verses.text: And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.

verses.name: Acts 18:20
verses.text: When they desired <hi type="italic">him</hi> to tarry longer time with them, he consented not;

verses.name: Acts 18:21
verses.text: But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I will return again unto you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus.

verses.name: Acts 18:22
verses.text: And when he had landed at Cæsarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.

verses.name: Acts 18:23
verses.text: And after he had spent some time <hi type="italic">there</hi>, he departed, and went over <hi type="italic">all</hi> the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.

verses.name: Acts 18:24
verses.text: ¶ And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, <hi type="italic">and</hi> mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.

verses.name: Acts 18:25
verses.text: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.

verses.name: Acts 18:26
verses.text: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto <hi type="italic">them</hi>, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.

verses.name: Acts 18:27
verses.text: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:

verses.name: Acts 18:28
verses.text: For he mightily convinced the Jews, <hi type="italic">and that</hi> publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.  <chapter eID="Acts.18"/><div eID="gen1124" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 19:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,

verses.name: Acts 19:2
verses.text: He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.

verses.name: Acts 19:3
verses.text: And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John’s baptism.

verses.name: Acts 19:4
verses.text: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 19:5
verses.text: When they heard <hi type="italic">this</hi>, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 19:6
verses.text: And when Paul had laid <hi type="italic">his</hi> hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.

verses.name: Acts 19:7
verses.text: And all the men were about twelve.

verses.name: Acts 19:8
verses.text: And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.

verses.name: Acts 19:9
verses.text: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.

verses.name: Acts 19:10
verses.text: And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.

verses.name: Acts 19:11
verses.text: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:

verses.name: Acts 19:12
verses.text: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.

verses.name: Acts 19:13
verses.text: ¶ Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.

verses.name: Acts 19:14
verses.text: And there were seven sons of <hi type="italic">one</hi> Sceva, a Jew, <hi type="italic">and</hi> chief of the priests, which did so.

verses.name: Acts 19:15
verses.text: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?

verses.name: Acts 19:16
verses.text: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.

verses.name: Acts 19:17
verses.text: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

verses.name: Acts 19:18
verses.text: And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.

verses.name: Acts 19:19
verses.text: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all <hi type="italic">men:</hi> and they counted the price of them, and found <hi type="italic">it</hi> fifty thousand <hi type="italic">pieces</hi> of silver.

verses.name: Acts 19:20
verses.text: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.

verses.name: Acts 19:21
verses.text: ¶ After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.

verses.name: Acts 19:22
verses.text: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.

verses.name: Acts 19:23
verses.text: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.

verses.name: Acts 19:24
verses.text: For a certain <hi type="italic">man</hi> named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;

verses.name: Acts 19:25
verses.text: Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.

verses.name: Acts 19:26
verses.text: Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:

verses.name: Acts 19:27
verses.text: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.

verses.name: Acts 19:28
verses.text: And when they heard <hi type="italic">these sayings</hi>, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great <hi type="italic">is</hi> Diana of the Ephesians.

verses.name: Acts 19:29
verses.text: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.

verses.name: Acts 19:30
verses.text: And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.

verses.name: Acts 19:31
verses.text: And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring <hi type="italic">him</hi> that he would not adventure himself into the theatre.

verses.name: Acts 19:32
verses.text: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.

verses.name: Acts 19:33
verses.text: And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.

verses.name: Acts 19:34
verses.text: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great <hi type="italic">is</hi> Diana of the Ephesians.

verses.name: Acts 19:35
verses.text: And when the townclerk had appeased the people, he said, <hi type="italic">Ye</hi> men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the <hi type="italic">image</hi> which fell down from Jupiter?

verses.name: Acts 19:36
verses.text: Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.

verses.name: Acts 19:37
verses.text: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.

verses.name: Acts 19:38
verses.text: Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.

verses.name: Acts 19:39
verses.text: But if ye inquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.

verses.name: Acts 19:40
verses.text: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day’s uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.

verses.name: Acts 19:41
verses.text: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.  <chapter eID="Acts.19"/><div eID="gen1125" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 20:1
verses.text: AND after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto <hi type="italic">him</hi> the disciples, and embraced <hi type="italic">them</hi>, and departed for to go into Macedonia.

verses.name: Acts 20:2
verses.text: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,

verses.name: Acts 20:3
verses.text: And <hi type="italic">there</hi> abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.

verses.name: Acts 20:4
verses.text: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.

verses.name: Acts 20:5
verses.text: These going before tarried for us at Troas.

verses.name: Acts 20:6
verses.text: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.

verses.name: Acts 20:7
verses.text: And upon the first <hi type="italic">day</hi> of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.

verses.name: Acts 20:8
verses.text: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.

verses.name: Acts 20:9
verses.text: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.

verses.name: Acts 20:10
verses.text: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing <hi type="italic">him</hi> said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.

verses.name: Acts 20:11
verses.text: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.

verses.name: Acts 20:12
verses.text: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.

verses.name: Acts 20:13
verses.text: ¶ And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.

verses.name: Acts 20:14
verses.text: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.

verses.name: Acts 20:15
verses.text: And we sailed thence, and came the next <hi type="italic">day</hi> over against Chios; and the next <hi type="italic">day</hi> we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next <hi type="italic">day</hi> we came to Miletus.

verses.name: Acts 20:16
verses.text: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.

verses.name: Acts 20:17
verses.text: ¶ And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.

verses.name: Acts 20:18
verses.text: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,

verses.name: Acts 20:19
verses.text: Serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:

verses.name: Acts 20:20
verses.text: <hi type="italic">And</hi> how I kept back nothing that was profitable <hi type="italic">unto you</hi>, but have shewed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,

verses.name: Acts 20:21
verses.text: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Acts 20:22
verses.text: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:

verses.name: Acts 20:23
verses.text: Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.

verses.name: Acts 20:24
verses.text: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.

verses.name: Acts 20:25
verses.text: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.

verses.name: Acts 20:26
verses.text: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> pure from the blood of all <hi type="italic">men</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 20:27
verses.text: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.

verses.name: Acts 20:28
verses.text: ¶ Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.

verses.name: Acts 20:29
verses.text: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.

verses.name: Acts 20:30
verses.text: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.

verses.name: Acts 20:31
verses.text: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.

verses.name: Acts 20:32
verses.text: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.

verses.name: Acts 20:33
verses.text: I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.

verses.name: Acts 20:34
verses.text: Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.

verses.name: Acts 20:35
verses.text: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

verses.name: Acts 20:36
verses.text: ¶ And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.

verses.name: Acts 20:37
verses.text: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul’s neck, and kissed him,

verses.name: Acts 20:38
verses.text: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.  <chapter eID="Acts.20"/><div eID="gen1126" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 21:1
verses.text: AND it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the <hi type="italic">day</hi> following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:

verses.name: Acts 21:2
verses.text: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.

verses.name: Acts 21:3
verses.text: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.

verses.name: Acts 21:4
verses.text: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 21:5
verses.text: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till <hi type="italic">we were</hi> out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.

verses.name: Acts 21:6
verses.text: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.

verses.name: Acts 21:7
verses.text: And when we had finished <hi type="italic">our</hi> course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.

verses.name: Acts 21:8
verses.text: And the next <hi type="italic">day</hi> we that were of Paul’s company departed, and came unto Cæsarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was <hi type="italic">one</hi> of the seven; and abode with him.

verses.name: Acts 21:9
verses.text: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.

verses.name: Acts 21:10
verses.text: And as we tarried <hi type="italic">there</hi> many days, there came down from Judæa a certain prophet, named Agabus.

verses.name: Acts 21:11
verses.text: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver <hi type="italic">him</hi> into the hands of the Gentiles.

verses.name: Acts 21:12
verses.text: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 21:13
verses.text: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.name: Acts 21:14
verses.text: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.

verses.name: Acts 21:15
verses.text: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 21:16
verses.text: There went with us also <hi type="italic">certain</hi> of the disciples of Cæsarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.

verses.name: Acts 21:17
verses.text: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.

verses.name: Acts 21:18
verses.text: And the <hi type="italic">day</hi> following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.

verses.name: Acts 21:19
verses.text: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.

verses.name: Acts 21:20
verses.text: And when they heard <hi type="italic">it</hi>, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:

verses.name: Acts 21:21
verses.text: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise <hi type="italic">their</hi> children, neither to walk after the customs.

verses.name: Acts 21:22
verses.text: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.

verses.name: Acts 21:23
verses.text: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them;

verses.name: Acts 21:24
verses.text: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave <hi type="italic">their</hi> heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but <hi type="italic">that</hi> thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.

verses.name: Acts 21:25
verses.text: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written <hi type="italic">and</hi> concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from <hi type="italic">things</hi> offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.

verses.name: Acts 21:26
verses.text: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.

verses.name: Acts 21:27
verses.text: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,

verses.name: Acts 21:28
verses.text: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all <hi type="italic">men</hi> every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.

verses.name: Acts 21:29
verses.text: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)

verses.name: Acts 21:30
verses.text: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.

verses.name: Acts 21:31
verses.text: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

verses.name: Acts 21:32
verses.text: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.

verses.name: Acts 21:33
verses.text: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded <hi type="italic">him</hi> to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.

verses.name: Acts 21:34
verses.text: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.

verses.name: Acts 21:35
verses.text: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.

verses.name: Acts 21:36
verses.text: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.

verses.name: Acts 21:37
verses.text: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?

verses.name: Acts 21:38
verses.text: Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?

verses.name: Acts 21:39
verses.text: But Paul said, I am a man <hi type="italic">which am</hi> a Jew of Tarsus, <hi type="italic">a city</hi> in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.

verses.name: Acts 21:40
verses.text: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto <hi type="italic">them</hi> in the Hebrew tongue, saying,  <chapter eID="Acts.21"/><div eID="gen1127" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 22:1
verses.text: MEN, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence <hi type="italic">which I make</hi> now unto you.

verses.name: Acts 22:2
verses.text: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)

verses.name: Acts 22:3
verses.text: I am verily a man <hi type="italic">which am</hi> a Jew, born in Tarsus, <hi type="italic">a city</hi> in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, <hi type="italic">and</hi> taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.

verses.name: Acts 22:4
verses.text: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.

verses.name: Acts 22:5
verses.text: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.

verses.name: Acts 22:6
verses.text: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.

verses.name: Acts 22:7
verses.text: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

verses.name: Acts 22:8
verses.text: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.

verses.name: Acts 22:9
verses.text: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.

verses.name: Acts 22:10
verses.text: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.

verses.name: Acts 22:11
verses.text: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.

verses.name: Acts 22:12
verses.text: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt <hi type="italic">there</hi>,

verses.name: Acts 22:13
verses.text: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.

verses.name: Acts 22:14
verses.text: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.

verses.name: Acts 22:15
verses.text: For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.

verses.name: Acts 22:16
verses.text: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.

verses.name: Acts 22:17
verses.text: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;

verses.name: Acts 22:18
verses.text: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.

verses.name: Acts 22:19
verses.text: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:

verses.name: Acts 22:20
verses.text: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.

verses.name: Acts 22:21
verses.text: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.

verses.name: Acts 22:22
verses.text: And they gave him audience unto this word, and <hi type="italic">then</hi> lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a <hi type="italic">fellow</hi> from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.

verses.name: Acts 22:23
verses.text: And as they cried out, and cast off <hi type="italic">their</hi> clothes, and threw dust into the air,

verses.name: Acts 22:24
verses.text: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.

verses.name: Acts 22:25
verses.text: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?

verses.name: Acts 22:26
verses.text: When the centurion heard <hi type="italic">that</hi>, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.

verses.name: Acts 22:27
verses.text: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.

verses.name: Acts 22:28
verses.text: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was <hi type="italic">free</hi> born.

verses.name: Acts 22:29
verses.text: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.

verses.name: Acts 22:30
verses.text: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from <hi type="italic">his</hi> bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.  <chapter eID="Acts.22"/><div eID="gen1128" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 23:1
verses.text: AND Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men <hi type="italic">and</hi> brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.

verses.name: Acts 23:2
verses.text: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.

verses.name: Acts 23:3
verses.text: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, <hi type="italic">thou</hi> whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?

verses.name: Acts 23:4
verses.text: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?

verses.name: Acts 23:5
verses.text: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.

verses.name: Acts 23:6
verses.text: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men <hi type="italic">and</hi> brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.

verses.name: Acts 23:7
verses.text: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.

verses.name: Acts 23:8
verses.text: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.

verses.name: Acts 23:9
verses.text: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes <hi type="italic">that were</hi> of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.

verses.name: Acts 23:10
verses.text: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring <hi type="italic">him</hi> into the castle.

verses.name: Acts 23:11
verses.text: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.

verses.name: Acts 23:12
verses.text: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.

verses.name: Acts 23:13
verses.text: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.

verses.name: Acts 23:14
verses.text: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.

verses.name: Acts 23:15
verses.text: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would inquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.

verses.name: Acts 23:16
verses.text: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.

verses.name: Acts 23:17
verses.text: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto <hi type="italic">him</hi>, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.

verses.name: Acts 23:18
verses.text: So he took him, and brought <hi type="italic">him</hi> to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto <hi type="italic">him</hi>, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.

verses.name: Acts 23:19
verses.text: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went <hi type="italic">with him</hi> aside privately, and asked <hi type="italic">him</hi>, What is that thou hast to tell me?

verses.name: Acts 23:20
verses.text: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would inquire somewhat of him more perfectly.

verses.name: Acts 23:21
verses.text: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.

verses.name: Acts 23:22
verses.text: So the chief captain <hi type="italic">then</hi> let the young man depart, and charged <hi type="italic">him</hi>, <hi type="italic">See thou</hi> tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.

verses.name: Acts 23:23
verses.text: And he called unto <hi type="italic">him</hi> two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Cæsarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;

verses.name: Acts 23:24
verses.text: And provide <hi type="italic">them</hi> beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring <hi type="italic">him</hi> safe unto Felix the governor.

verses.name: Acts 23:25
verses.text: And he wrote a letter after this manner:

verses.name: Acts 23:26
verses.text: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix <hi type="italic">sendeth</hi> greeting.

verses.name: Acts 23:27
verses.text: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.

verses.name: Acts 23:28
verses.text: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:

verses.name: Acts 23:29
verses.text: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.

verses.name: Acts 23:30
verses.text: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what <hi type="italic">they had</hi> against him. Farewell.

verses.name: Acts 23:31
verses.text: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought <hi type="italic">him</hi> by night to Antipatris.

verses.name: Acts 23:32
verses.text: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:

verses.name: Acts 23:33
verses.text: Who, when they came to Cæsarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.

verses.name: Acts 23:34
verses.text: And when the governor had read <hi type="italic">the letter</hi>, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that <hi type="italic">he was</hi> of Cilicia;

verses.name: Acts 23:35
verses.text: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.  <chapter eID="Acts.23"/><div eID="gen1129" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 24:1
verses.text: AND after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and <hi type="italic">with</hi> a certain orator <hi type="italic">named</hi> Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.

verses.name: Acts 24:2
verses.text: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse <hi type="italic">him</hi>, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,

verses.name: Acts 24:3
verses.text: We accept <hi type="italic">it</hi> always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.

verses.name: Acts 24:4
verses.text: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.

verses.name: Acts 24:5
verses.text: For we have found this man <hi type="italic">a</hi> pestilent <hi type="italic">fellow</hi>, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:

verses.name: Acts 24:6
verses.text: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.

verses.name: Acts 24:7
verses.text: But the chief captain Lysias came <hi type="italic">upon us</hi>, and with great violence took <hi type="italic">him</hi> away out of our hands,

verses.name: Acts 24:8
verses.text: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.

verses.name: Acts 24:9
verses.text: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.

verses.name: Acts 24:10
verses.text: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:

verses.name: Acts 24:11
verses.text: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.

verses.name: Acts 24:12
verses.text: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:

verses.name: Acts 24:13
verses.text: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.

verses.name: Acts 24:14
verses.text: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:

verses.name: Acts 24:15
verses.text: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

verses.name: Acts 24:16
verses.text: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and <hi type="italic">toward</hi> men.

verses.name: Acts 24:17
verses.text: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.

verses.name: Acts 24:18
verses.text: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.

verses.name: Acts 24:19
verses.text: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.

verses.name: Acts 24:20
verses.text: Or else let these same <hi type="italic">here</hi> say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,

verses.name: Acts 24:21
verses.text: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.

verses.name: Acts 24:22
verses.text: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of <hi type="italic">that</hi> way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.

verses.name: Acts 24:23
verses.text: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let <hi type="italic">him</hi> have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.

verses.name: Acts 24:24
verses.text: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.

verses.name: Acts 24:25
verses.text: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.

verses.name: Acts 24:26
verses.text: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.

verses.name: Acts 24:27
verses.text: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix’ room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.  <chapter eID="Acts.24"/><div eID="gen1130" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 25:1
verses.text: NOW when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Cæsarea to Jerusalem.

verses.name: Acts 25:2
verses.text: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,

verses.name: Acts 25:3
verses.text: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.

verses.name: Acts 25:4
verses.text: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Cæsarea, and that he himself would depart shortly <hi type="italic">thither</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 25:5
verses.text: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with <hi type="italic">me</hi>, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.

verses.name: Acts 25:6
verses.text: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Cæsarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.

verses.name: Acts 25:7
verses.text: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.

verses.name: Acts 25:8
verses.text: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Cæsar, have I offended any thing at all.

verses.name: Acts 25:9
verses.text: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?

verses.name: Acts 25:10
verses.text: Then said Paul, I stand at Cæsar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.

verses.name: Acts 25:11
verses.text: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Cæsar.

verses.name: Acts 25:12
verses.text: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Cæsar? unto Cæsar shalt thou go.

verses.name: Acts 25:13
verses.text: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Cæsarea to salute Festus.

verses.name: Acts 25:14
verses.text: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul’s cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:

verses.name: Acts 25:15
verses.text: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed <hi type="italic">me</hi>, desiring <hi type="italic">to have</hi> judgment against him.

verses.name: Acts 25:16
verses.text: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.

verses.name: Acts 25:17
verses.text: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.

verses.name: Acts 25:18
verses.text: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:

verses.name: Acts 25:19
verses.text: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

verses.name: Acts 25:20
verses.text: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked <hi type="italic">him</hi> whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.

verses.name: Acts 25:21
verses.text: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Cæsar.

verses.name: Acts 25:22
verses.text: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.

verses.name: Acts 25:23
verses.text: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment Paul was brought forth.

verses.name: Acts 25:24
verses.text: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and <hi type="italic">also</hi> here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

verses.name: Acts 25:25
verses.text: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.

verses.name: Acts 25:26
verses.text: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.

verses.name: Acts 25:27
verses.text: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes <hi type="italic">laid</hi> against him.  <chapter eID="Acts.25"/><div eID="gen1131" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 26:1
verses.text: THEN Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:

verses.name: Acts 26:2
verses.text: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:

verses.name: Acts 26:3
verses.text: Especially <hi type="italic">because I know</hi> thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.

verses.name: Acts 26:4
verses.text: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;

verses.name: Acts 26:5
verses.text: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

verses.name: Acts 26:6
verses.text: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:

verses.name: Acts 26:7
verses.text: Unto which <hi type="italic">promise</hi> our twelve tribes, instantly serving <hi type="italic">God</hi> day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.

verses.name: Acts 26:8
verses.text: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?

verses.name: Acts 26:9
verses.text: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

verses.name: Acts 26:10
verses.text: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against <hi type="italic">them</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 26:11
verses.text: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled <hi type="italic">them</hi> to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted <hi type="italic">them</hi> even unto strange cities.

verses.name: Acts 26:12
verses.text: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,

verses.name: Acts 26:13
verses.text: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.

verses.name: Acts 26:14
verses.text: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? <hi type="italic">it is</hi> hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

verses.name: Acts 26:15
verses.text: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.

verses.name: Acts 26:16
verses.text: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;

verses.name: Acts 26:17
verses.text: Delivering thee from the people, and <hi type="italic">from</hi> the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,

verses.name: Acts 26:18
verses.text: To open their eyes, <hi type="italic">and</hi> to turn <hi type="italic">them</hi> from darkness to light, and <hi type="italic">from</hi> the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.

verses.name: Acts 26:19
verses.text: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:

verses.name: Acts 26:20
verses.text: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judæa, and <hi type="italic">then</hi> to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.

verses.name: Acts 26:21
verses.text: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill <hi type="italic">me</hi>.

verses.name: Acts 26:22
verses.text: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:

verses.name: Acts 26:23
verses.text: That Christ should suffer, <hi type="italic">and</hi> that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.

verses.name: Acts 26:24
verses.text: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.

verses.name: Acts 26:25
verses.text: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.

verses.name: Acts 26:26
verses.text: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.

verses.name: Acts 26:27
verses.text: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.

verses.name: Acts 26:28
verses.text: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.

verses.name: Acts 26:29
verses.text: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.

verses.name: Acts 26:30
verses.text: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:

verses.name: Acts 26:31
verses.text: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

verses.name: Acts 26:32
verses.text: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Cæsar.  <chapter eID="Acts.26"/><div eID="gen1132" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 27:1
verses.text: AND when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto <hi type="italic">one</hi> named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.

verses.name: Acts 27:2
verses.text: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; <hi type="italic">one</hi> Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

verses.name: Acts 27:3
verses.text: And the next <hi type="italic">day</hi> we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave <hi type="italic">him</hi> liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.

verses.name: Acts 27:4
verses.text: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

verses.name: Acts 27:5
verses.text: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, <hi type="italic">a city</hi> of Lycia.

verses.name: Acts 27:6
verses.text: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.

verses.name: Acts 27:7
verses.text: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;

verses.name: Acts 27:8
verses.text: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city <hi type="italic">of</hi> Lasea.

verses.name: Acts 27:9
verses.text: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished <hi type="italic">them</hi>,

verses.name: Acts 27:10
verses.text: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.

verses.name: Acts 27:11
verses.text: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.

verses.name: Acts 27:12
verses.text: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, <hi type="italic">and there</hi> to winter; <hi type="italic">which is</hi> an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.

verses.name: Acts 27:13
verses.text: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained <hi type="italic">their</hi> purpose, loosing <hi type="italic">thence</hi>, they sailed close by Crete.

verses.name: Acts 27:14
verses.text: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.

verses.name: Acts 27:15
verses.text: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let <hi type="italic">her</hi> drive.

verses.name: Acts 27:16
verses.text: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:

verses.name: Acts 27:17
verses.text: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.

verses.name: Acts 27:18
verses.text: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next <hi type="italic">day</hi> they lightened the ship;

verses.name: Acts 27:19
verses.text: And the third <hi type="italic">day</hi> we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.

verses.name: Acts 27:20
verses.text: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on <hi type="italic">us</hi>, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.

verses.name: Acts 27:21
verses.text: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.

verses.name: Acts 27:22
verses.text: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of <hi type="italic">any man</hi>’<hi type="italic">s</hi> life among you, but of the ship.

verses.name: Acts 27:23
verses.text: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,

verses.name: Acts 27:24
verses.text: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Cæsar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

verses.name: Acts 27:25
verses.text: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.

verses.name: Acts 27:26
verses.text: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.

verses.name: Acts 27:27
verses.text: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;

verses.name: Acts 27:28
verses.text: And sounded, and found <hi type="italic">it</hi> twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found <hi type="italic">it</hi> fifteen fathoms.

verses.name: Acts 27:29
verses.text: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

verses.name: Acts 27:30
verses.text: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,

verses.name: Acts 27:31
verses.text: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.

verses.name: Acts 27:32
verses.text: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

verses.name: Acts 27:33
verses.text: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought <hi type="italic">them</hi> all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.

verses.name: Acts 27:34
verses.text: Wherefore I pray you to take <hi type="italic">some</hi> meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.

verses.name: Acts 27:35
verses.text: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken <hi type="italic">it</hi>, he began to eat.

verses.name: Acts 27:36
verses.text: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took <hi type="italic">some</hi> meat.

verses.name: Acts 27:37
verses.text: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.

verses.name: Acts 27:38
verses.text: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.

verses.name: Acts 27:39
verses.text: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.

verses.name: Acts 27:40
verses.text: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed <hi type="italic">themselves</hi> unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.

verses.name: Acts 27:41
verses.text: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.

verses.name: Acts 27:42
verses.text: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

verses.name: Acts 27:43
verses.text: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from <hi type="italic">their</hi> purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast <hi type="italic">themselves</hi> first <hi type="italic">into the sea</hi>, and get to land:

verses.name: Acts 27:44
verses.text: And the rest, some on boards, and some on <hi type="italic">broken pieces</hi> of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.  <chapter eID="Acts.27"/><div eID="gen1133" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Acts 28:1
verses.text: AND when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.

verses.name: Acts 28:2
verses.text: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

verses.name: Acts 28:3
verses.text: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid <hi type="italic">them</hi> on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

verses.name: Acts 28:4
verses.text: And when the barbarians saw the <hi type="italic">venomous</hi> beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.

verses.name: Acts 28:5
verses.text: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.

verses.name: Acts 28:6
verses.text: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

verses.name: Acts 28:7
verses.text: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.

verses.name: Acts 28:8
verses.text: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.

verses.name: Acts 28:9
verses.text: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:

verses.name: Acts 28:10
verses.text: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded <hi type="italic">us</hi> with such things as were necessary.

verses.name: Acts 28:11
verses.text: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.

verses.name: Acts 28:12
verses.text: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried <hi type="italic">there</hi> three days.

verses.name: Acts 28:13
verses.text: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:

verses.name: Acts 28:14
verses.text: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.

verses.name: Acts 28:15
verses.text: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.

verses.name: Acts 28:16
verses.text: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.

verses.name: Acts 28:17
verses.text: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men <hi type="italic">and</hi> brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.

verses.name: Acts 28:18
verses.text: Who, when they had examined me, would have let <hi type="italic">me</hi> go, because there was no cause of death in me.

verses.name: Acts 28:19
verses.text: But when the Jews spake against <hi type="italic">it</hi>, I was constrained to appeal unto Cæsar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.

verses.name: Acts 28:20
verses.text: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see <hi type="italic">you</hi>, and to speak with <hi type="italic">you:</hi> because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.

verses.name: Acts 28:21
verses.text: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judæa concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.

verses.name: Acts 28:22
verses.text: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.

verses.name: Acts 28:23
verses.text: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into <hi type="italic">his</hi> lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and <hi type="italic">out of</hi> the prophets, from morning till evening.

verses.name: Acts 28:24
verses.text: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.

verses.name: Acts 28:25
verses.text: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,

verses.name: Acts 28:26
verses.text: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:

verses.name: Acts 28:27
verses.text: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with <hi type="italic">their</hi> eyes, and hear with <hi type="italic">their</hi> ears, and understand with <hi type="italic">their</hi> heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.

verses.name: Acts 28:28
verses.text: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and <hi type="italic">that</hi> they will hear it.

verses.name: Acts 28:29
verses.text: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.

verses.name: Acts 28:30
verses.text: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,

verses.name: Acts 28:31
verses.text: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.  <chapter eID="Acts.28"/><div eID="gen1134" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen1106" osisID="Acts" type="book"/>

verses.name: Romans 1:1
verses.text: PAUL, a servant of Jesus Christ, called <hi type="italic">to be</hi> an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,

verses.name: Romans 1:2
verses.text: (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)

verses.name: Romans 1:3
verses.text: Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;

verses.name: Romans 1:4
verses.text: And declared <hi type="italic">to be</hi> the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:

verses.name: Romans 1:5
verses.text: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name:

verses.name: Romans 1:6
verses.text: Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ:

verses.name: Romans 1:7
verses.text: To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called <hi type="italic">to be</hi> saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.name: Romans 1:8
verses.text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.

verses.name: Romans 1:9
verses.text: For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers;

verses.name: Romans 1:10
verses.text: Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto you.

verses.name: Romans 1:11
verses.text: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;

verses.name: Romans 1:12
verses.text: That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.

verses.name: Romans 1:13
verses.text: Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you, (but was let hitherto,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.

verses.name: Romans 1:14
verses.text: I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise.

verses.name: Romans 1:15
verses.text: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.

verses.name: Romans 1:16
verses.text: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

verses.name: Romans 1:17
verses.text: For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.

verses.name: Romans 1:18
verses.text: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;

verses.name: Romans 1:19
verses.text: Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed <hi type="italic">it</hi> unto them.

verses.name: Romans 1:20
verses.text: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, <hi type="italic">even</hi> his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

verses.name: Romans 1:21
verses.text: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified <hi type="italic">him</hi> not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.

verses.name: Romans 1:22
verses.text: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

verses.name: Romans 1:23
verses.text: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

verses.name: Romans 1:24
verses.text: Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:

verses.name: Romans 1:25
verses.text: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

verses.name: Romans 1:26
verses.text: For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature:

verses.name: Romans 1:27
verses.text: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.

verses.name: Romans 1:28
verses.text: And even as they did not like to retain God in <hi type="italic">their</hi> knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient;

verses.name: Romans 1:29
verses.text: Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers,

verses.name: Romans 1:30
verses.text: Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,

verses.name: Romans 1:31
verses.text: Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:

verses.name: Romans 1:32
verses.text: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.  <chapter eID="Rom.1"/><div eID="gen1136" type="x-p"/>

verses.name: Romans 2:1
verses.text: THEREFORE thou art inexcusable, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things.

verses.name: Romans 2:2
verses.text: But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things.

verses.name: Romans 2:3
verses.text: And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them which do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?

verses.name: Romans 2:4
verses.text: Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?

verses.name: Romans 2:5
verses.text: But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God;

verses.name: Romans 2:6
verses.text: Who will render to every man according to his deeds:

verses.name: Romans 2:7
verses.text: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life:

verses.name: Romans 2:8
verses.text: But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath,

verses.name: Romans 2:9
verses.text: Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile;

verses.name: Romans 2:10
